title: [Issue-2438] Rework checks to trigger peer sync
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/PegaSysEng/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Rework logic to trigger peer sync:
* Add some sanity checks to make sure peers aren't broadcasting a chain state from the future
* Be more consistent wrt how head slot / finalized epoch triggers sync: 
  * A peer's finalized epoch must now be > 1 epoch ahead, in line with the head slot check which only triggers a sync if the peer's head slot is > 1 epoch ahead.

The change to the finalized epoch trigger helps us avoid triggering a sync too aggressively in the following scenario:
* Our local node is missing a very recent block at an epoch boundary that will cause our finalized block to advance
* A peer has this additional block, causing us to see that the peer's finalized epoch is ahead of our node

title: Fix race condition when committing changes to fork choice votes
body:
## PR Description
Fixes race conditions in fork choice because while changes to votes were made within a read/write lock, the store transaction they were changed in was committed outside of that lock and so may wind up overwriting conflicting changes.

Also fixes access to `Store.votes` to ensure it only occurs inside the store's read lock.

ie:
When we process attestations, we start a StoreTransaction then take the votes write lock, update the votes with next nextRoot and nextEpoch, release the write lock and then commit the transaction.
When we update head, we start a StoreTransaction , take the votes write lock, apply deltas and set the vote current root to next root, release the write lock and then commit the transaction.
Trouble is we might interleave those like:
Attestation - start transaction
Attestation - take write lock, update nextRoot, release write lock
Update Head - start transaction
Update Head - take write lock, apply deltas, update current root, release write lock
Update Head - commit transaction
Attestation - commit transaction, overwriting the vote changes that Update Head made.

With this change we likely have more locks than we actually need.  `ForkChoice` has been moved to use a `ReentrantLock` instead of `synchronized` so that it can use futures safely and still ensure the lock is held for the duration of the action and guaranteed to be released at the end.  But since all it's access to `ProtoArrayForkChoiceStrategy` is now controlled by that lock, we likely don't need as many locks in `ProtoArrayForkChoiceStrategy`. It may be better to make `ProtoArrayForkChoiceStrategy` not thread safe and control access entirely through `ForkChoice` but will leave that for further investigation later once we confirm this fixes the immediate issue.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #2562

## Documentation

title: Use a single threaded executor instead of locks for fork choice
body:
## PR Description
There can be a lot of tasks submitted to fork choice so use a single threaded executor to ensure they are only performed one at a time instead of locks.  Using locks prevented concurrent access but also blocked the thread while it waited to acquire the lock.  Due to the number of incoming tasks and unfair queuing leaving a potential for starvation, it was possible for all threads in the thread pool to be blocked waiting to acquire the fork choice lock.  This could lead to a deadlock as the result of committing the transaction in fork choice was sent on the same thread pool but could never get executed as all threads were already busy.

In the new model, once any prerequisite data is retrieved, the task is executed by `ForkChoiceExecutor` - which in production is implemented by `SingleThreadedForkChoiceExecutor`.  No locks are used, but the task is submitted to a single threaded executor and `.join()` used to ensure the single fork choice thread is blocked until the task completes.  Thus it is guaranteed that only one task can be in progress at a time but the only thread that ever blocks is the fork choice thread.

Re-entrancy is not supported (ie fork choice operations cannot call to other fork choice operations without causing a deadlock) but that was true with the previous `Semaphore` based lock as well.

## Documentation

## PR Description
Rework how hot states are selected for persistence when the persistence frequency is greater than 1 to better handle skipped epochs.  

Rather than persisting states only if they are within a targeted epoch, we should persist any state that spans a targeted epoch. This means we will store states at a more regular cadence even if some epochs are skipped altogether.  For example, say that frequency = 2 (every other epoch) and we completely skip epochs 2,4,6, etc.  For the epoch 2 boundary, in this case we should persist the first state in epoch 3.  For the epoch 4 boundary, we should save the first state in epoch 5, etc.

body:
## PR Description
- Options for starting only a Validator Node (connecting to a Beacon Node).

Here is an example of how to run a minimum beacon node and a validator client:

**Beacon Node**
```
teku --network minimal --data-path=/Users/lucas/Library/teku-beacon/data --Xinterop-enabled --rest-api-enabled --Xremote-validator-api-enabled
```

**Validator Client**
```
teku validator-client --network minimal --data-path=/Users/lucas/Library/teku-validator/data --log-include-validator-duties-enabled --Xinterop-enabled --Xinterop-owned-validator-count=64
```

## New Properties

**Beacon Node** new properties:
- `--Xremote-validator-api-enabled`
    - Enables the WebSocket server that the remote validator client can connect to in order to receive Beacon Node events (default: `false`)
- `--Xremote-validator-api-port <port>` 
    - The port that should be used to accept connection in the WebSocket server (default: `9999`)
- `--Xremote-validator-api-interface <interface>` 
    - The network interface that the WebSocket service should bind to (default: `127.0.0.1`)
- `--Xremote-validator-api-max-subscribers <integer>`
    - The maximum number of remote validators that can connect to the Beacon Node (default: `1,000`)

**Validator Client**

For the validator client, we have created a new subcommand `validator-client`. This subcommand has the following options:
- `--Xbeacon-node-api-endpoint <endpoint>`
    - The endpoint of the Rest API service of the Beacon Node (default: `http://127.0.0.1:5051`)
- `--Xbeacon-node-events-endpoint <endpoint>`
    - The endpoint of the WebSocket service of the Beacon Node (default: `ws://127.0.0.1:9999`)

title: Avoid performing duplicate tasks when they are rebased
body:
## PR Description
Previously when a task was rebased, it was only added to the pending tasks list once the task it was being rebased onto completed. If duplicate tasks were requested before the dependent task completed, they would all be scheduled to execute after it.  This resulted in duplicate work being performed and a `NullPointerException` when later tasks completed and found the result future had already been removed.

Now the result future is added to pending tasks immediately regardless of whether the task is rebased or immediately added to the queue. Duplicates then simply return the existing pending result and are not executed themselves.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #2685 
fixes #2686

title: Start new sync by tracking available chains
body:
## PR Description
Starts to build a `MultipeerSyncService` which will be the new sync algorithm. At this point it only tracks peer statuses to build a set of target chains that we might want to sync to.

Since there are a lot of events coming from different sources and reasonably complex data structures will be required to track sync status, this also introduces the `EventThread` class which enables delegating tasks to a single thread for execution so code can be written without worrying about concurrent access except to ensure that any events coming from other threads are dispatched to the event thread.  This is very similar to the thread model used by `ForkChoice` and `EventChannel` but `EventThread` is a bit more formalised and includes the ability to assert that the current thread is the event thread to detect violations.

If this thread model does prove useful, we should be able to apply it to `ForkChoice` and should consider using it in more places.  One big advantage is that its lock free so has no risk of deadlocking because the thread pool is full of threads waiting to acquire a lock, preventing the task which would release the lock from acquiring a thread to execute which we've seen in other situations in the past.

## Fixed Issue(s)
Part of #1844

title: Prevent the fork choice head from going backwards when updating chain head
body:
## PR Description
When chain head is updated as a result of importing a block, it doesn't have the node slot to provide as the `currentSlot` to `updateHead` which can result in "forgetting" empty slots which had previously been considered the head and so missing reorgs when those empty slots are filled in.  In turn that can lead to validator duties being scheduled incorrectly.

To prevent this from happening under any circumstances, never allow the fork choice head to move backwards.

Also added the common ancestor slot to reorg logs to make these issues easier to debug in future.

title: Reduce reorg noise during sync
body:
## PR Description
This is a "quick fix" approach to avoid logging a reorg message for every block we import during sync. When we're more than 2 epochs behind, we skip updating the chain head for every block imported and only do it once per slot, and when we're syncing (ie printing "Sync Event") we suppress the reorg log message (but the event is still fired to be completely safe).  Notably for the last 2 epochs of the sync there'll still be a heap of reorg events printed so would be nice to do better.

 It's still worth investigating better changes as this feels overly specific but it significantly improves the user experience while syncing so we can take the time required to design a better solution.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#2773

title: Deliver sync event notifications off the event thread
body:
## PR Description
To ensure that the sync event thread is not blocked by subscribers, deliver syncing status change notifications via an `AsyncRunner`.  

Introduces `OrderedAsyncRunner` to ensure that the events are still delivered in the correct order. While a separate `AsyncRunner` with a single thread could be used, that thread would mostly sit idle and require a lot of extra wiring, whereas with `OrderedAsyncRunner` the existing thread pool can be used, along with it's queue limits, monitoring etc.

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/PegaSysEng/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Add a new CLI option allowing users to pass in a weak subjectivity checkpoint.  This new option is hidden while this functionality is under development.

This PR also includes a refactor of our configuration system:
* The current low-level global configuration object has been deprecated and renamed to `GlobalConfiguration`.
* A new high-level `TekuConfiguration` object has been added to the top-level `teku` package.
* The new weakSubjectivity config has been added to the new `TekuConfiguration` to show how we can organize our config objects going forward.

Advantages of this config refactor:
* We can now use domain-specific concepts and objects in `TekuConfiguration`
* Config is more modular - we have a hierarchy of types rather than a flat list of all global properties
* We can use module-specific logic to parse and validate CLI arguments
* Code is more cohesive - most module-specific logic is either in the module or in the module-specific CLI `Options` object
* This refactor is incremental - we can slowly move to the new model over time

## Fixed Issue(s)
Part of #2273

title: Add batches concept as part of new sync strategy
body:
## PR Description
Provides the concept of a `Batch` which is a block range that can be requested from a peer as part of syncing.  The range can be confirmed when it forms a chain with previous or later batches or contested if it doesn't fit into the expected chain.

The `BatchDataRequester` class manages the chain of batches, requesting additional blocks for them and creating new batches as needed to maintain a pipeline of blocks ready to import.

Also changes `Sync` to return a result for the sync when it completes instead of `SafeFuture<Void>`.

title: Handle event thread exiting and being replaced
body:
## PR Description
If the event thread is idle long enough, it may exit and a new thread created when the next event occurs. This still gives the memory guarantees of a single thread that we need, but because `AsyncRunnerEventThread` only recorded the thread ID once at startup, calls to `checkOnEventThread` would incorrectly fail because the new thread ID didn't match.

Fix by recording the event thread ID prior to each task.  After the task completes the ID is reset again to avoid any risk of reused thread IDs conflicting.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#1844

title: Support syncing to non-finalised chains
body:
## PR Description
Updates SyncController to consider non-finalised chains as sync targets once finalised chains have been sync'd.

Fixes an issue where `StackOverflowException` was thrown when the last peer disconnected because the disconnected event would be queued to get onto the event thread, but the current task being executed would be in a tight loop repeatedly trying to request blocks from the disconnected peer which synchronously failed.  Most likely to happen when peers wind up disconnecting us due to throttling.

Also ensures that when a chain fails to sync, any pending batches are cleared so the next sync that starts has a clean slate.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#1844

title: [Issue-2848] Don't look up validator index when logging errors
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/PegaSysEng/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
When a sent attestation fails validation we log an error that involves calculating committee information for the failed attestation.  In some cases to properly calculate committee information we need to pull / derive a checkpoint state that is processed through to a more recent slot.  We're not currently doing the work to pull such a checkpoint state, so if the head state has lagged a few epochs behind the current epoch, we end up throwing an `IllegalArgumentException` because we're trying to derive committee information using a state that is too old.

This PR just cuts out the committee-related calculations, as we added that at one point to debug an issue that has already been solved.  And it seems suboptimal to have to potentially perform state processing in order to log an error message.

## Fixed Issue(s)
Fixes #2848

title: Avoid switching to a new chain until the current import completes
body:
## PR Description
When multipeer sync discovers that a new target chain doesn't extend the current one, it currently restarts the import from the latest finalized block.  If there's an import from the previous target chain in progress, that import might finalise a new block which would cause the first block imported after the reset to fail with `UNKNOWN_PARENT` because the store has been pruned.

To avoid this, when restarting the sync, wait until the current import is complete before selecting the new common ancestor.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#1844

title: Database V6: store all in a single Rocks DB instance by default
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/PegaSysEng/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

RocksDB appears pretty hungry of native memory and creating 2 database instances it very expensive: this just doubles native memory consumption. 

This PR bumps the DB version to `6` and stores both Hot and Finalized in a single RocksDB instance. However there is an option in `VersionedDatabaseFactory` to specify a separate data dir for Finalized data and in this case the second RocksDB instance would be created.

This should reduce native memory consumption by ~500Mb

I'm not sure if we need the CLI option to set archive DB path to another location at the moment. Please let me know if you think this is a wanted feature and I will add it then.

## Fixed Issue(s)
Relates to #2303

title: Reveal the validator command CLI options
body:
## PR Description
Unhides and removes the `--X` prefix from the external Validator Client options.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #2741 

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `documentation` label to this PR if updates are required.

To run the Validator Client as a separate process:
1. Be very, very certain that you've removed the validator keys from the beacon node and restarted it so that it is not still running them.  Never, specify the same validator keys on both the beacon node and Validator Client - only the validator client needs them.
2. Run the beacon node as usual (minus any validator key options) and ensure the REST API is enabled e.g. `teku --network medalla --rest-api-enabled`
3. Run the validator client and pass the URL to the beacon node REST API e.g. `teku validator-client --network medalla --beacon-rest-api-endpoint "http://localhost:5051" --validator-keys keys:passwords`.  The default rest api endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:5051` so the option can be omitted if running the two processes on one machine.   It is important to specify the `--network` option (though we may be able to load the network from the beacon node in future).

The default log file for the Validator Client is same directory as the beacon node but called `teku-validator.log` so on Mac it defaults to `~/Library/teku/logs/teku-validator.log`.

title: Migrate directory layout to clearly separate beacon node and validator client
body:
## PR Description
Introduces a clearer directory layout under `--data-path` to clearly separate the beacon node data from the validator data. This is a draft to get feedback on the changes - more testing will be required and potentially include logs in the default layout as described below.

Up until now the default layout was:

```
~/Library/teku
├── data
│   ├── archive
│   │   ├── <rocksdb stuff>
│   ├── db
│   │   ├── <rocksdb stuff>
│   ├── db.version
│   ├── kvstore
│   │   ├── generated-node-key.dat
│   │   └── local-enr-seqno.dat
│   ├── metadata.yml
│   ├── network.yml
│   └── validators
│       └── slashprotection
│           └── b89bebc699769726a318c8e9971bd3171297c61aea4a6578a7a4f94b547dcba5bac16a89108b6b6a1fe3695d1a874a0b.yml
└── logs
    └── teku.log
```

When you set `--data-path` the files under `data` move, but `logs` are left in the default location.  The validator's slashing protection storage is intermingled with the various parts of beacon chain storage. This has a few problems:

 * When users want to resync the chain, they are likely to delete the entire `data` directory, deleting the validator slashing protection records which should be kept
 * When users move to using an external Validator Client, to reuse the slashing protection database they wound need to set `data-path` to the same directory as the beacon chain uses, but intuition is that this would cause conflicts.
 * Docker users are likely to use `--data-path` to change the location of data to be on a volume, but forget to move the log file and thus lose access to their logs.

If we just added a separate option to specify the slashing protection location, it's highly likely that docker users would fail to set it and lose their slashing protection records after every restart.

With this PR the `data-path` moves to being explicitly the base directory that each service then has its own subdirectory to store things in.  The resulting layout becomes:

```
~/Library/teku
├── beacon
│   ├── archive
│   │   ├── <rocksdb stuff>
│   ├── db
│   │   ├── <rocksdb stuff>
│   ├── db.version
│   ├── kvstore
│   │   ├── generated-node-key.dat
│   │   └── local-enr-seqno.dat
│   ├── metadata.yml
│   └── network.yml
├── logs
│   └── teku.log
└── validator
    └── slashprotection
        └── b89bebc699769726a318c8e9971bd3171297c61aea4a6578a7a4f94b547dcba5bac16a89108b6b6a1fe3695d1a874a0b.yml
```

The default value for `--data-path` has changed from (on MacOS) `~/Library/teku/data` to `~/Library/teku`. Most of the files that were under the `data-path` directly are now under a `beacon` subdirectory which is the root of storage for the beacon node.  The slashing protection has moved from being under `validators/slashprotection` to `validator/slashprotection` so the top level of `data-path` is now just `beacon`, `validator`, `logs`, giving a clear separation of storage between services.

Not implemented yet in this PR, but I think is worth doing, is to also have the default `--log-file` location be under `--data-path` so when a user specifies a custom `--data-path` the whole directory structure above moves under it.  `--data-path` is then the one-stop-shop for moving all data, and we can provide more specific CLI options to move override the location of other items. i.e. the existing `--log-file` would take precedence and we'd add (hopefully better named) `--data-beacon-path` and `--data-validator-path` options to move the beacon and validator directories respectively to a custom location.

We could potentially rename `--data-path` to `--data-base-path` (keeping an alias for `--data-path` for backwards compatibility) to make this structure clearer.


Note: more testing is required on this PR, plus updates to CLI descriptions and adding the new options to specify a different beacon or validator storage dir. The aim of the code at this point is really just to prove the concept can work and the migration is sane.

title: Avoid loading states from disk unless it is significantly better

## PR Description
If a state regeneration has an in-memory state that is almost as good as the one it could load from disk, prefer the in-memory state to reduce memory usage.

The tolerance is set to be equal to the number of epochs that states are stored on disk - so by default if the in-memory state is within two epochs of the one on disk we use the in-memory state.

Also adds the very handy `minusMinZero` method to `UInt64` which performs a minus but returns zero if it would have underflowed avoiding a lot of `x.isGreaterThan(y) ? x.minus(y) : ZERO` conditionals.

title: Track peer reputation score during sync
body:
## PR Description
Track a reputation score for peers which is adjusted by the multipeer sync process.  Peers are rewarded for providing batches that form part of the chain and penalised for batches that don't match up or are invalid.

A small reward is applied for each confirmed batch, with a cap on the maximum reputation score a peer can have. This allows peers to build up a limited amount of "good behaviour credit" to reduce the likelihood that they will be disconnected because of actions which are unhelpful to us but may result from an honest node's behaviour.

A small penalty is applied for each batch that is contested - ie when the batch on either side doesn't form a chain with the batch supplied by the peer. The penalty is only small because this could be the honest peer and the other batch was incorrect. From the initial zero score it would take 4 such penalties to be disconnected and 7 small penalties to be disconnected from the maximum reputation cap.  

A large penalty is applied when the peer is known to have provided an invalid batch (e.g. providing a block that fails to import).  From the initial score of zero a single large penalty will disconnect the peer, but two large penalties are required before being disconnected from any positive score.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#1844

title: Update head on new blocks even when syncing
body:
## PR Description
Now that head update and reorg events are coalesced, move the logging of reorg events into the `CoalescingChainHeadUpdateChannel` which already knows whether sync is in progress or not and re-enable automatically updating the fork choice head on block import even if the block is more than two epochs behind the current node slot.

Previously this was disabled because it caused too much noise in the logs and too much unnecessary work as different components responded to the reorg events. Those events and logs are now suppressed during sync so we may as well get the benefit of the head block being updated more smoothly and not just once per epoch.

Note that the log about chain reorgs is not printed when syncing finishes even if there were reorgs. That just creates a lot of noise and it's not particularly surprising to users that things changed around during a sync so no point in the extra logging.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #2773

body:

<!-- https://github.com/PegaSysEng/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Optimize roughly x20 `BeaconState` SSZ serialization performance
- SSZ serialize based solely on `backing tree` and `ViewType`s 
- Serialize to a bytes 'stream' i.e. with appending bytes only (via `Consumer<Bytes>`)

- Relying on the fact that a `List/Vector` of fixed type elements (that is `validators` and `balances`) flattened with `LeafNode.data` is equal to SSZ serialization. (see https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/pull/3062/commits/9ad32fd194fff75711919fef4bbe3c1a36e9483b commit)

## PR Description
Draft PR to provide an overall guide of how to move the ProtoArray into the Store and not store a separate BlockTree.

There are a few TODOs scattered through here that will need to be cleaned up.  The biggest issue is that storing the protoarray is still out of sync with Store transactions. title: Migrate away from protoarray snapshots
body:
## PR Description
As a first step towards moving the protoarray into `Store` rather than maintaining a separate `BlockTree`, rebuild the protoarray entirely based off of the stored hot blocks.  The justified epoch and finalized epoch information is now stored for each block, along with the block itself.  This information was already available as part of importing the block.

One first run, the protoarray is loaded from snapshot as usual, regenerating states for any blocks in the store but not the snapshot.  The checkpoint epochs are then stored for each hot block.  As blocks are added the checkpoint epochs are stored along with the new block.

On subsequent loads, the database iterates through hot blocks and loads the block metadata that is required for each protoarray node (slot, root, parentRoot, stateRoot, justifiedEpoch, finalizedEpoch) instead of just (slot, root, parentRoot) which was required to create the store.  `Maps.transformValues` is used to provide a view of the block metadata map in the form the current store creation requires (root->parentRoot and root->slot) without having to copy the entire map.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#2832

<!-- https://github.com/PegaSysEng/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Drop initial block argument, and accept initial weak subjectivity state alone.  

Update logic that currently assumes the latest finalized block will be available:
* `RocksDbDatabase`
  * When building the `Store`: 
      * Don't require the latest finalized block to be present
      * If the initial block is missing, pull block metadata from the initial state
  * Update finalization logic to tolerate missing finalized block if it is the initial block
* `WeakSubjectivityInitializer`
  * When validating the initial state CLI argument against an existing database:
      * If the corresponding block is unavailable, try to look up the corresponding state for verification
      * If both the corresponding state and block are missing, just log a warning indicating the initial state argument couldn't be verified against the local chain data
* ForkChoice
  * When initializing at startup, process all available states without requiring the associated block to be available
* State regeneration
  * Look up base states available from the `Store` even if the corresponding block is unavailable
* `PeerChainValidator`
  * Validate peers against local finalized `AnchorPoint` which is kept in memory, avoiding a look up of the latest finalized block

## Fixed Issue(s)

title: Limit size of range used when requesting deposit logs
body:
## PR Description
Infura has a limit of 10,000 log events that it will return from a single call and ETH1 nodes may struggle to respond to requests over a very large range of blocks.  To handle this, `DepositFetcher` now limits the number of blocks requested in each batch and if the request times out or is rejected by Infura, the batch size is halved.

To avoid the batch size being reduced to a very small number because of a busy period and then making a lot of extra requests for the rest of the chain, the batch size increases slightly after each successful request.  The batch size deliberately grows much slower than it shrinks to avoid bouncing around too much.

title: Implement v1.0.0 message ID calculation
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/PegaSysEng/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Implements the Gossip `message-id` calculation based on uncompressed payload ([spec](https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/v1.0.0-rc.0/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#topics-and-messages))

The naive approach could be just change the Gossip `messageIdGenerator` which uncompressed the Snappy-compressed message payload and calculates the ID. However this approach would require uncompressing the message content twice: 
- on id calculation 
- on message decoding

To handle this from the Libp2p side the following features were implemented: https://github.com/libp2p/jvm-libp2p/pull/155
From Teku side the `GossipEncoding.decode` method was split onto
- `prepareMessage` which creates an abstract preprocessed `PreparedGossipMessage` instance which decompresses the payload lazily and caches decompressed payload
- `decodeMessage` which consumes preprocessed `PreparedGossipMessage` instance and makes use of cached decompressed payload 

The similar modification was made for `TopicHandler` interface

Depends on publishing `0.6.0` release: https://github.com/libp2p/jvm-libp2p/pull/156

## Fixed Issue(s)
Fix #3088
Fix #2951 (this PR is the last part of spec v1.0.0-rc0 upgrade)

title: add a command line interface to send voluntary exits for a validator.
body:
The option is hidden,
`teku voluntary-exit --beacon-node-api-endpoint URL --validator-keys KEY:PASS --epoch EPOCH`

The validator key and password file are used to load the validator, so that the exit can be signed.

Care should be taken, if the entire validator keys folder and password folder is passed, exits will be generated for all keys.

If the validation from the remote host fails, the failure message is too generic to be useful currently, so the program only reports that the exit submission failed.

Note: the epoch must be the current or a previous epoch, or a validation error will be received, and the exit won't be processed.

fixes #2461

title: Add CLI option to disable built-in slashing protection for external signers
body:
## PR Description
Adds the `--validators-external-signer-slashing-protection-enabled` CLI option to disable the built-in slashing protection Teku provides for external signers.  Internal signers always use slashing protection regardless of this option.

The idea is that if you have advanced slashing protection with something like Web3Signer, you don't want Teku using its simpler slashing protection and refusing to even send requests to the external signer because it violates the more simple checks.

Also fixes `ExternalSigner` so that it uses a single `HttpClient` instance across all validators so resources can be optimally shared instead of creating a `HttpClient` instance for every validator.

title: make voluntary exit CLI visible.
body:
`voluntary-exit` is now listed with subcommands for teku:

```
Commands:
  voluntary-exit        Create and sign a voluntary exit for a specified
                          validator.
```

and it has help specific to the subcommand:

```
teku voluntary-exit [OPTIONS]

Description:

Create and sign a voluntary exit for a specified validator.

Options:
      --beacon-node-api-endpoint=<ENDPOINT>
                        Endpoint of the Beacon Node REST API
  -c, --config-file=<FILENAME>
                        Path/filename of the yaml config file (default: none)
      --epoch=<EPOCH>   Earliest epoch that the voluntary exit can be processed.
  -h, --help            Show this help message and exit.
  -V, --version         Print version information and exit.
      --validator-keys=<KEY_DIR>:<PASS_DIR> | <KEY_FILE>:<PASS_FILE>[,<KEY_DIR>:
        <PASS_DIR> | <KEY_FILE>:<PASS_FILE>...]...
                        <KEY_DIR>:<PASS_DIR> will find <KEY_DIR>/**.json, and
                          expect to find <PASS_DIR>/**.txt.
                        <KEY_FILE>:<PASS_FILE> will expect that the file
                          <KEY_FILE> exists, and the file containing the
                          password for it is <PASS_FILE>.
                        The path separator is operating system dependent, and
                          should be ';' in windows rather than ':'.
      --validators-external-signer-public-keys[=<STRINGS>[,<STRINGS>...]...]
                        The list of external signer public keys
      --validators-external-signer-timeout=<INTEGER>
                        Timeout (in milliseconds) for the external signing
                          service
      --validators-external-signer-url=<NETWORK>
                        URL for the external signing service

Teku is licensed under the Apache License 2.0
```

Confirmation is requested before sending exits to the beacon node. Any validator keys passed to the command will have an exit generated on confirmation at the prompt.

The ` --beacon-node-api-endpoint` is required, and needs to have the http api running so that it is able to receive requests.

Any specified validator needs to be active at the specified epoch, and the epoch has to be a valid epoch on the network, specifying a future epoch will result in failure.

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/PegaSysEng/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Merge `--Xws-initial-state` weak subjectivity state argument with existing `--initial-state` argument. 

This modifies the startup behavior in a few ways:
* We'll now always parse the initial state if it is supplied.  When spinning up an existing database, we check it is consistent with the initial state.  We also use the initial state to modify weak subjectivity options.  
* Since we're always running validation against the initial state, when overriding the initial state for custom networks users will have to supply the initial state argument at each startup. 

Other changes:
* Parse `NetworkDefinition` in `NetworkOptions` to simplify access to the parsed value.

## Fixed Issue(s)
Part of #3063 

## Documentation
This PR expands the purpose of the `--initial-state` flag:  users can pass a genesis state as before, or a more recent state from which to sync.

title: Avoid repeatedly processing epoch transitions
body:
## PR Description
When creating the first block of an epoch, Teku winds up processing the epoch transition four times:
* Computing proposer duties
* `BlockFactory` creates the state at the block slot to use when getting operations to include in the block
* `BlockProposalUtil` recreates the state at the block slot as part of applying the block to get the resulting state
* `ForkChoiceUtil` reprocesses the block when it imports it

The first three of those can all be modified to reuse the same cached state.  This is done by changing our `Checkpoint` based state cache to a `SlotAndBlockRoot` based so it can cache states from arbitrary slots rather than only epoch boundaries.  Computing proposer duties looks up the state at the epoch start slot. This includes applying any empty slots if needed.
Both `BlockFactory` and `BlockProposalUtil` are invoked as a result of the same validator client call to create the unsigned block - the state from the new block's slot can be retrieved from cache then passed in to both of them to reuse.

Note that the caching works out correctly even when we request a state at the first slot of an epoch prior to importing the block because that's cached under `(start_slot, previous_block_root)` and then if a block is later imported for that slot it's cached under `(start_slot, new_block_root)` so we can't pollute the cache by looking a state for a slot too early.

## Documentation

title: Reuse pre-block state to avoid slot and epoch processing
body:
## PR Description
When generating new blocks, reuse the state generated at the block slot by `BlockFactory` in `BlockProposalUtil` instead of reprocessing empty slots again. While empty slots are fairly cheap, an epoch transition can be quite expensive and increase the risk of the first block in the slot being orphaned.

Note that this means we don't use `StateTransition.initiate` when creating a block, just `process_block`.  The empty slot processing and epoch transitions are already done.  The interim state listener is a no-op as is the block validator so those actions in `initiate` aren't required.

## Fixed Issue(s)
Low hanging fruit for #3262

The validator client needs to differentiate between validator indices not being available because the public keys are unknown and when the state has not yet been set after startup. In both cases once the exception is received its logged at debug level and the validator client retries loading validators on the next slot (but crucially continues waiting to schedule the duties for the epoch until a successful validator index response is received).

title: Always use a state from the current epoch when creating attestations
body:
## PR Description
This ensures the latest justified checkpoint is used if the attestation slot is in a new epoch and the last block is from the previous epoch.

This fixes a corner case where the wrong source checkpoint would be used.  It occurs when an attestation is created for slot in epoch 10, but the most recent block is from epoch 9 *and* epoch 9 had enough attestations to trigger justification.  During epoch processing to go from epoch 9 to 10, the state would be updated with the new checkpoint.  Teku however was only checking that the state from the last block was recent enough to calculate duties (ie anywhere in epoch 9) and then took the justified checkpoint from that old state as the source.

Now it ensures the checkpoint is from the same epoch as the attestation, which guarantees any required epoch processing is complete and the justified checkpoint is updated.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #3328

title: Heap optimize: reduce BeaconState.Validators backing tree memory consumption
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

This change optimizes `BeaconState` backing binary tree memory consumption. For 100K validators the memory footprint for backing tree drops from ~66Mb to ~14Mb. 

The general idea is to merge 'low-level' subtree nodes into a single `TreeNode` structure (`SszSuperNode`) with a backing storage of ssz serialized bytes for this subtree. Updates to this structure (as well as hashTreeRoot recalculation) is more expensive in favor of memory effectiveness. This is well suited for `BeaconState.validators` list as it changes pretty rarely but takes over 95% of the whole state. 

This PR applies `SszSuperNode` to sequences of 256 validators backing subtrees. 

## Fixed Issue(s)

title: Move minimum randomly selected peers config out of P2PConfig and into P2POptions
body:
## PR Description

According to the comment in PeerPools.java some proportion of the peer pool should be randomly selected in order to provide Sybil resistance.

This change was initiated from the observation that the Math.min/max logic was back to front for the 'minimum number of randomly generated peers' config in P2PConfig.

`Math.min(1, p2pPeerLowerBound * 2 / 10);`
should have read
`Math.max(1, p2pPeerLowerBound * 2 / 10);`

In order to explicitly test this behaviour (defaulting to 20% of the lower target bound should be randomly selected) I've moved the logic out of P2PConfig and into P2POptions.

The value is implemented as a --X param and marked hidden - `--Xp2p-minimum-randomly-selected-peer-count` - this may need further discussion.

title: Avoid BigInteger multiplication when calculating base rewards
body:
## PR Description
Previously UInt64.times switched to using BigInteger to perform multiplication when either multiplicand is bigger than the square root of UInt64.MAX_VALUE to provide overflow protection.
Epoch transition multiplies the sum of effective balances by 64 and the effective balances were greater than the square root value, causing the more expensive path to be taken.
Add an additional check that if one multiplicand is 64 or less and the other is less than MAX_VALUE / 64, use the fast path as the result is known to not overflow.

Not a huge performance gain but simple enough.

## Documentation

title: Use cached pre-states when importing blocks
body:
## PR Description
When importing blocks, get the state at the block's slot (prior to applying the block) via `Store.retrieveStateAtSlot` so it benefits from any cached states that performed the required slot and epoch processing.

Note that the `SSZTransitionRecorder` no longer captures the pre-state because we don't have the state at the previous block anymore - however it is still recorded as the post state for the previous block.

State roots are now captured from the state roots vector in the state rather than while processing slots as if the value came from cache we won't have done the slot processing.  If there are more than `SLOTS_PER_HISTORICAL_ROOT` empty slots in a row, we may not record some state roots, but this just matches the behaviour in `RocksDbDatabase` for finalized states.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#3262

title: Decouple in-memory storage updates from on-disk storage updates
body:
## PR Description
Adds the ability to apply updates to the in-memory store without first waiting for the on-disk store to be updated.  The on-disk storage will now continually retry updates if they fail to prevent it from winding up in an inconsistent state.  If the error isn't recoverable the event channel will eventually back up and block any further progress - we will likely need to treat too many repeated failures as a fatal error and shutdown to avoid these stalls.

When using archive mode, there is now potentially a period where finalized blocks have been removed from the in-memory store but are not yet available from the on-disk store.  We'll need to resolve that before this can be toggled on by default.

Change is feature toggled off by default.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#1934

title: Moving all SSZ containers to backing structures (part 2)
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Following up and on top of #3425 

- Refactor all the SSZ containers to backing tree structures using type-safe generated `ContainerN` classes
- Since there is a concern regarding performance of new structures comparing to old POJO classes - create JMH benchmarks for some containers with basic usage scenarios 
- Make a number of optimizations in core ssz classes which speeds up the `benchDeserializeAndIterate` scenario ~3x for the most heavy `BeaconBlockBody` container
- For optimization add custom caches (per each container individually) for heavy structures like `BLSSignature, BLSPublicKey, Bitlist`
- Remove `SimpleOffsetSerializable` and `HashTreeUtils` functionality. 
- Add type-safe child type getters to generated `ContainerTypeN` classes 

There is some stuff left to remove, but I'm planning to address this in the next PR #3512 to not make this PR even more noisy

To make container types more 'readable' added the following `namedType`. This also gives `toString()` 'for free': 
```java
      super(
          "AggregateAndProof",
          namedType("index", BasicViewTypes.UINT64_TYPE),
          namedType("aggregate", Attestation.TYPE),
          namedType("selection_proof", ComplexViewTypes.BYTES_96_TYPE));
```
instead of just
```java
      super(BasicViewTypes.UINT64_TYPE, Attestation.TYPE, ComplexViewTypes.BYTES_96_TYPE);
```

## Benchmarks 
(Measured in microseconds per operation: the lower the better)

- `benchCreate` : just constructing a container instance with its fields members 
- `benchIterate`: iterates all the members recursively. Worth to mention that subsequent iterations are very cheap due to View caches and are nearly as fast as POJO fields access 
- `benchCreateAndIterate` two above combined
- `benchCreateAndSerialize`: `benchCreate` + SSZ serialize. New code is basically faster due to serialization is ~2x faster. 
- `benchSerialize`: just serialize existing instance
- `benchDeserialize`: deserializing from SSZ. Can be faster than `benchCreate`
- `benchDeserializeAndIterate`: I believe the most basic scenario for our structures other than `BeaconState`
- `benchDeserializeAndSerialize`: another scenario which seems to be very common

title: Validator client independently triggers attestation creation
body:
## PR Description
With the move to using dependent roots to detect reorgs we eventually want to be able to stop publishing a new head event 4 seconds into every block (and only publish them when new blocks are actually received).  To ensure the validator client still publishes attestations on time, set up an independent timer to trigger attestation creation.

Only enabled when using dependent roots which is off by default.

Note that currently we still get the head event at 4s but that's no different to when we get a block early - whichever of the events fires first causes attestation creation and the others are ignored.  We might create attestations prior to running the full fork choice but completing but that's not a big deal because we automatically make the first child of our current head the new head so don't need to run full fork choice to have the latest head - we just might take one more slot before switching forks.  When we no longer publish the `head` event we can move running fork choice to just before the start of a slot so it can process all the aggregates received from the slot and ensure we're on the right fork in time to create the next block.

This sets the cache size without using constants to the mainnet size (160) to avoid the problem.

title: Increase read timeout for event stream
body:
## PR Description
The read timeout for the validator client reading from the event stream was set to 2 * `SECONDS_PER_SLOT` which would be enough when a head event is published every slot, but isn't necessarily when using dependent roots as head events are only published when blocks are received.  In addition, it was accessing the `SECONDS_PER_SLOT` constant prior to the constants actually being set so wound up using the minimal config which is only 6 second slots - only just enough when receiving head events every slot.

Switched it to use spec provider to get the seconds per slot so it has the right value and when using dependent roots to allow 5 slots between events before considering it timed out.  While that limit may still be reached, its not particularly common to miss 5 slots in a row and having it be too long risks missing events if the connection drops but in a way that isn't detected (a common issue with these kinds of long poll mechanisms).

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #3469

title: Avoid requesting recent blocks that will be discarded
body:
## PR Description
While a forward sync is in progress, skip requesting parents of pending blocks. If we're far enough behind to need to sync, we're unlikely to be able to follow the ancestors back far enough to be able to import the blocks anyway.

After the forward sync completes, request parents for any pending blocks we didn't wind up getting as part of the forward sync.

Note that we still collect blocks received via gossip so the pending pool is still primed and ready to go when the forward sync completes, we just don't try to backfill any missing blocks while forward sync is in action.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #1890

title: Log fatal errors as well as printing to System.err
body:
## PR Description
When teku exits at startup (e.g because the validator keys can't be loaded), print the error message to both the log and to `System.err` to maximise the chance of it being seen by users. Note that the message sent to the log is only seen by a console user if `--log-destination CONSOLE` is set, so normally users still get nice clean console output.  Even with CONSOLE destination, the simple clear error is the last thing printed with the more verbose log output above it.

The one exception to this is when the parsing of CLI options fails because we are then unable to configure the logging system correctly. The error message in that case is only printed to System.err (previously it was incorrectly printed to System.out even though it's an error message).

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #3481

title: [Issue 3504] Prototype datastructure versioning
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
This PR is a prototype that illustrates how our codebase might be organized in order to support versioned data structures and versioned core logic that operates on versioned data structures.  This is probably easiest to review in an IDE where the organization is clearer.

Highlights:
* The `schema` package has several new sub-packages:
  * A `datastructures` package has been added.  It contains several interfaces to represent common `BeaconState` fields as well as variable fields.  The common `BeaconState` interface sits in the `state` package, while version-specific interfaces and implementations are in versioned sub-packages (`genesis`, `hf1`)
  * A `schemas` package has been added, which contains logic for generating versioned `SszSchema`'s
  * Some sample versioned logic has been added to `statetransition`.
* `BeaconStateRocksDbSerializer` (not currently compiling) shows how we might be able to handle serialization with the existing database schema by just passing the `SpecProvider` down to the serializer.

## Fixed Issue(s)

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

`SszListImpl` internally uses the `SszContainer[SszVector, UInt64]` to keep its data and size node. It was intended to simplify and abstract the implementation but it actually makes the things more complex and periodically causes inconveniences during refactor. It also likely adds performance overhead. 

This PR eliminates complexities with `SszContainer` and makes the things simplier:
- Remove `Ssz[Mutable]List` internal `SszContainer`
- Created `AbstractSsz[Mutable]Collection` where common methods of List/Vector were pulled up 
- `equals()/hashCode()` were pulled up to `AbstractSszComposite`

title: Apply votes to store independently of disk storage
body:
## PR Description
Fork choice works using two pieces of data - the `ProtoArray` tracking blocks and current weightings and the votes recording what each validator is voting for.  It's important that these stay in sync with each other because the `ProtoArray` is updated by applying deltas calculated from which votes have changed.

The `ProtoArray` is updated in memory immediately whereas votes are updated via a transaction mechanism.  Previously, the vote changes would have to be recorded to disk before those changes were applied in memory so if the disk store failed the vote data wouldn't be applied in memory and the two structures would be out of sync.

This PR changes that so that votes are applied in memory first and then the changes are sent to disk. This ensures that the in-memory store stays in sync even if the disk storage encounters a problem.  At startup, the weightings in `ProtoArray` are rebuilt from the stored votes so even if some updates to votes fail to store to disk, when reloaded the `ProtoArray` is still guaranteed to be in sync with them.

A transaction mechanism is still used to support sending the transactions to disk. This doesn't increase the risk of the two structures getting out of sync because the process of applying deltas has to be done in two passes anyway, so if an error occurs part way through updating the `ProtoArray` the data will be left out of sync regardless of whether vote updates have already been applied. 

Also important to note is that when adding a block, the store transaction to record that block is still committed to disk prior to updating the votes for attestations in that block.  This guarantees that all recorded votes are for a block that's already present in the store, even though the two are not recorded together. The vote handling already deals with votes pointing to finalized blocks which have been removed from the store.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#3533

title: Reduce time required to load validator keys at startup
body:
## PR Description
Reduce time required to load validator keys at startup.  Previously the password was checked first, then the keystore decrypted but decryption will fail if the password is invalid and checking the password is expensive so we can skip it and detect invalid passwords purely based on decryption failing.

Also separates loading the public key from decrypting the keystore for local validators.

title: Migrate all SSZ collections from old SSZ* classes
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

- Add the following primitive collection hierarchy (immutable/mutable/schema interfaces, implementations):
```
SszPrimitiveCollection
  |  SszPrimitiveList
  |  SszPrimitiveVector
    |  SszBytes32Vector
    |  SszUInt64List
    |  SszByteVector
      |  SszPublicKey  // ethereum module
      |  SszSignature  // ethereum module
```
- Replace all old `SSZVector/SSZList<SszContainer>` with the corresponding new types
- Replace `SSZVector<Bytes32>` with `SszBytes32Vector`
- Replace `SSZList<UInt64>` with `SszUInt64List`
- Replace all other `SSZList/Vector<Primitive>` with `SszPrimitiveList/Vector` (with 2 type parameters unfortunately)
- Replace `BLSPublicKey` & `BLSSignature` (represented by `SSZVector<Byte>`) with corresponding `SszPublicKey` & `SszSignature`
- Remove all custom caches for `SSZList/Vector` in ssz containers
- Remove `SSZTypes.*` classes except of `Bytes4`
- Add unit tests hierarchy 

Specialized primitive collections (`SszBytes32Vector` and `SszUInt64List`) were added for frequently used types. For others we are using `SszPrimitiveList/Vector` which occurred a bit more verbose than was expected:
e.g.
```java
SszPrimitiveList<Bytes32, SszBytes32>
```
Here `SszBytes32` implies `Bytes32` (extends `AbstractSszPrimitive<Bytes32, SszBytes32>`), but Java doesn't allow declaring kind of 'implicit types inference' for classes. The similar thing however is available for methods.

title: Fix wrong ConnectionClosedException from RcpHandler.sendRequest()
body:
## PR Description

#### Reason

https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/cc98b7230126985e92f3ed4136e6012a74e762a5/networking/p2p/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/networking/p2p/libp2p/rpc/RpcHandler.java#L75-L76

The exception is thrown from `createStream()` method.

The `createStream()` is called when the `Connection` was just closed but when passing `SafeFuture.notInterrupted(closeInterruptor)` right before the `Connection.closeFuture` was not yet complete

#### Fix

Add the `RcpHandler.sendRequest()` async chain with analog of 
```java
try {
  ...
} catch (ConnectionClosedException e) {
  throw new PeerDisconnectedException(e);
}
```

## Fixed Issue(s)

Fix #3548

body:
## PR Description
Support building Teku from a shallow git clone where `git describe` doesn't find any tags. The version will be reported as "UNKNOWN+g<commit hash>".

e.g.
```
git init
git fetch --depth 1 https://github.com/ajsutton/teku.git 3f3e260079046c38c2082f0c5ec265f99aa356a2
git checkout --detach "FETCH_HEAD"
./gradlew printVersion
```

Gives:
```
Specific version: UNKNOWN+g3f3e260  Publish version: develop
```

title: Load the deposit contract from constants if it hasn't been set
body:
If the network configuration is missing a deposit contract address, attempt to load it from the constants.

Because all constants files have deposit contract set, the test for not having contract address has been removed, but the error has been left in case someone specifies a custom constants file that has the contract missing.

### Documentation
Deposit contract address can be loaded from constants, basically if the deposit contract isn't specified in the network configuration, it will be loaded from constants now. previously the doc stated it could be loaded from `--initial-state` or `--network`, which should continue to hold true, but now if it's not defined on startup by the network, then it will load from the defined constants.

fixes #3723

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

## PR Description

This is follow up to #3623 which had introduced some performance regressions (`TransitionBenchmark.Epoch` was especially hard to see)

Include the following optimizations: 
- (likely the major regression reason) Optimize `AbstractSszMutableCollection.set()` value schema check: f330a50
- Don't recreate schemas in `SchemaDefinitions.get*()`: 77b0a57 
- Get rid of sub-optimal `Stream` usages in critical places
- Optimize `SszType.sszGetFixedPartSize()` implementations: just memorizing per-type static values: fe7f535
- Optimizations for `getVariablePartSize()`: 5693317 
- Optimize `SszMutableListImpl.checkIndex`: 8e8aa20 
- Add `SSzSchema.updateBackingNode` batched variant. Optimize it for `UINT64_SCHEMA`
- Optimize `AbstractSszMutableCollection.packChanges` (several commits)
- Cache size for `Ssz*Collection.asList`: 3a8f71e 
- Cache element schema in `SszMutablePrimitive*` collections: e333660 
- Optimization for `AbstractEpochProcessor.applyDeltas`: take `state.getValidators().size()` out of the loop: e352b2d
- Optimize `AbstractSszMutableComposite` - get rid of several `HashMap` queries leaving the only `HashMap` tracking all the changes: b8d1379 
-  Precache schema for `AbstractSszMutableComposite`: e211481 
-  Optimize `SszMutablePrimitiveList/VectorImpl.set()` : no need to check value schema there: ca0e9c0

Also add:
- `EpochTransitionBenchmark` with some isolated transition steps
- `CustomRunner` to easily profile separate benchmarks from `main` method
- Extend `SszMutableCompositeTestBase.set_shouldMatchGet()` test

title: Introduce altair block body schema
body:
## PR Description
Introduces the schema for Altair `BeaconBlockBody`.  This is done slightly differently to how the two `BeaconState` variants are handled.  Unlike `BeaconState`, `BeaconBlockBody` is always immutable and can very simply use the base `Container8` classes to handle most things.  So instead of using a common base class for the `BeaconBlockBody` variants, they are just separate with one extending `Container8` and the new one extending `Container9` to add the new field.  I'm pretty sure this winds up being a lot less code than having to introduce the whole `MutableBeaconBlockBody` pattern.

The block production factory setup doesn't currently provide the information required for the new `SyncAggregate` field so it's always set to the empty value where no committee members are available. The infinite signature is explicitly used for this in the spec.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#3648

title: Update --ws-checkpoint to accept a URL
body:
`--ws-checkpoint` now accepts either root:epoch, or a URL containing key `ws_checkpoint` (formatted as root:epoch) as part of a json payload.

If the checkpoint passed starts with '0x', then it will be loaded as a literal checkpoint reference, otherwise it will attempt to load from url.

If the checkpoint doesn't start in 0x, and it doesnt load from URL, teku will fail with a CLI error.

Fixes #3531

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

### Documentation

ws_checkpoint now accepts a URL (or file) containing JSON, and will read `ws_checkpoint` from that JSON to populate the ws_checkpoint.

title: Adapt block creation for Altair
body:
## PR Description
Adapt the block creation process to allow for setting the `SyncAggregate` field in Altair blocks.  Currently the sync committee logic isn't implemented so it's not being set but wanting to get a sense of whether this approach to supporting the setting of different fields works.

The key question is whether we should go this way and keep `BeaconBlockBody` as immutable or should follow the approach of `BeaconState` and introduce a `MutableBeaconBlockBody` and that mechanism for building blocks.  The key challenge being that while the `spec` module contains the block data structures and `BlockFactory`, it doesn't have access to the `OperationPool` and other sources of information that go into a block, so code outside the spec needs to adjust based on whether the block needs a `SyncAggregate` or not.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#3648

title: Optimize TransitionCaches
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Two closely related changes in this optimization 
- `apache.commons` `Pair` we are currently using inherently (from `java.util.Map.Entry`) has a weak `hashCode()` implementation (`getLeft.hashCode() ^ getRight().hashCode()`) and `beaconCommittee` cache key `Pair<UInt64, UInt64>` (`slot + committee index`) with max size `64 * 64` effectively results in just `64` different `hashCode`s (instead of expected `4096`) which significantly degrades cache operations performance. So the new `TekuPair` was added to address this issue 
- The Guava caches which we had switched to in #2613 indeed showed better performance than `LinkedHashMap` with the weak `hashCode()` mentioned. However returning back to `Collections.synchronizedMap(new LinkedHashMap())` with using `TekuPair` gives significant performance boost. 

As for potential concurrency issue mentioned in #2613 for the `synchronizedMap` I created the concurrency unit test `LRUCacheTest.concurrencyTest` which I ran (on pre #2613 commit) in a loop for ~1hour but it didn't failed. I also didn't find any potential breeches with using `synchronizedMap`. I have no ideas how the `maxCapacity` could potentially be exceeded.

Worth mentioning that the above concurrency test fails with Guava `Cache` cause it supports 'weak' iterators and during `copy()` operation the underlying cache could still be modified. So from this perspective Guava `Cache` doesn't look safe as well. 

I'm really not sure if we should merge this PR assuming the potential risk of #2613 regression. 
@ajsutton what do you think on this?

## Benchmarks: 
#### Block import
Blocks import benchmark (I'm testing with `ProfilingRun` now with block average time (~1.5K blocks)): 
- Before: `21.2` ms/block
- After: `18.6` ms/block 

So import performance increases by ~13%

#### `TransitionCaches`
`Score new Guava` : results with with `TekuPair` and existing Guava backed caches
`Score new`: results with with `TekuPair` and `Collections.synchronizedMap(new LinkedHashMap())` as a cache backing store 

| Benchmark                                               | Score old   | Score new Guava | Score new | Units | Error      |
|---------------------------------------------------------|-------------|-----------------|-------------------|-------|------------|
| TransitionCachesBenchmark.copyBeaconCommitteeCacheBench | 628.384     | 1082.437        | 6045.371          | ops/s | 30.325     |
| TransitionCachesBenchmark.copyCachesBench               | 399.757     | 527.279         | 3485.584          | ops/s | 19.602     |
| TransitionCachesBenchmark.getCommitteeHitBench          | 8469235.624 | 7110180.289     | 25037230.61       | ops/s | 162202.922 |
| TransitionCachesBenchmark.getCommitteeMissBench         | 3199395.978 | 2831232.99      | 9695682.27        | ops/s | 351200.873 |

## Fixed Issue(s)

Related PR #2613

title: Avoid exception when importing block that updates justified checkpoint
body:
## PR Description
Avoid an exception that the best head is not valid when importing a block that causes the justified checkpoint to change and is not the child of the current head block.

In that case `ForkChoice` can't automatically make the new block head, so has to use `ProtoArray.findHead` but `ProtoArray.findHead` doesn't yet know about the updated justified epoch because that would normally be updated by running `applyScoreChanges` first, but we don't want to apply all pending votes as part of importing each block.

The fix is to update the justified and finalized epoch in ProtoArray if necessary as part of running `findHead`. While such an update is somewhat expensive, it's very unusual for it to be required and we do want to switch to the new block because if it caused a new justified checkpoint to be adopted then it must be the new head block (as all others have an earlier justified checkpoint so are not valid heads).

In terms of performance impact this extra update to checkpoints can only happen at most once per epoch. Further, during sync we'd be following a single chain so once the update is done once (if necessary at all), the rest of the block will build on the current head and not need any further updated.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #3793

## PR Description
Adds a `GossipForkSubscriptionsAltair` as the basis for Altair specific gossip code.  Currently it only has the same topics as for Phase0, but the update block body schema winds up being automatically used.

Also introduces a more foundational `Spec.getEnabledMilestones()` which gives a list of `Fork` instances along with an enum identifying which milestone the fork actually is (Phase0 or Altair) to make it easier for things like the gossip code to select the right implementations based on which fork applies.  Some things to ponder about this:

 * I would have expected this to be in `ForkManifest` but it doesn't actually have anyway to get the spec config and so can't work out which milestone a fork actually maps to (it only knows the fork ID). So it wound up in spec which is ok, but is there a better place?
 * What's the right name for `Milestone`? `Phase` is another option but feels overloaded and `Fork` is already used.  Could be `ForkVersion`? Or even just `ForkName`?
 * Not sure the package structure is right, suggestions welcome.

title: [Issue 3732] Refactor RPC interfaces to prep for versioning
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Start reworking RPC API's to prepare for versioned eth2 RPC methods:
* Create a new `eth2.rpc.methods` package and reorganize `Eth2RpcMethod` logic to allow us to have implementations that handle a single protocol (just a v1 version) as well as implementations that handle multiple protocols (v1 and v2).  This logic is now organized across:
  * A new `Eth2RpcMethod` interface
  * A base class: `AbstractEth2RcpMethod`
  * A primary implementation: `SingleProtocolEth2RpcMethod`
  * A versioned implementation: `VersionedEth2RpcMethod`
* In order to support RPC methods that handle multiple versions, some lower-level RPC interfaces had to be reworked so that we can pass the negotiated protocol to the right places to determine what logic to run:
  * `Eth2RpcMethod.createOutgoingRequestHandler` can't be called directly in `DefaultEth2Peer` when a request is initiated because we don't yet know what protocol has been negotiated.  So, a lot of logic was moved from the higher level `eth` package down into the `p2p.rpc` package, and some new interfaces and API's were added to support this. 
  * `ResponseStreamListener ` became a lower-level `RpcResponseListener`
  * Logic to configure response expectations was moved from `ResponseStream` to `Eth2RpcResponseHandler`
    * This logic was modified slightly, so that now we're more strict if a peer returns too many responses unexpectedly
* Start implementing versioning for blocksByRoot to give in idea of where we're heading in `BeaconChainMethods`
* Request serialization was pushed down into `RpcHandler` from `DefaultEth2Peer`

## Fixed Issue(s)
Part of #3732

title: Reveal new --eth1-endpoints option
body:
## PR Description
Thanks to @tbenr 's excellent work, the support for multiple eth1 endpoints is now ready to move to supported status (it has just missed the 21.4.1 release so this will first go out in 21.5.0).

Documentation wise - the `--eth1-endpoint` option can now be specified as either `--eth1-endpoint` or `--eth1-endpoints` (plural) and both versions accept a list of Eth1 endpoints.  Endpoints are tried in the order they're specified.  Typically that means users would specify `--eth1-endpoint <local eth1 url> <infura url>` to automatically fallback to Infura.  As usual with our options that take a list value can be either space or comma separated or the value can be specified multiple times.  So all of the following work:

* `teku --eth1-endpoints http://localhost:8545 https://infura.io/`
* `teku --eth1-endpoints http://localhost:8545,https://infura.io/`
* `teku --eth1-endpoints http://localhost:8545  --eth1-endpoints https://infura.io/`
* `teku --eth1-endpoint http://localhost:8545  --eth1-endpoint https://infura.io/`

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #3327

title: Ensure the state used to calculate duties for an epoch is after the fork slot
body:
## PR Description
The Altair fork slot is not necessarily the first slot of a sync committee period and sync committees can't be calculated until the fork actually happens. This requires two updates:

1. The validator client can't always use the first epoch of the sync committee period to request duties. This switches it to use the last epoch of the duties. That's always after the fork slot but also the most likely epoch to not be finalized and in memory.
2. The beacon node should consider the head state unsuitable for calculating sync committee duties if it isn't an Altair state.

## Fixed Issue(s)

fixes #3945

title: Adds error detection in web3j responses from eth1 endpoint
body:
## PR Description

Currently we are not checking if web3j responses from eth1 endpoints contain an error.

example:

**eth_chainId** call:
```
curl --header "Content-Type: application/json" -X POST --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"eth_chainId","params":[],"id":83}' http://localhost:8545

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":83,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"chain not synced beyond EIP-155 replay-protection fork block"}}
```
Since we are not checking if response contains an error we later fail trying to parse the response:

`Endpoint localhost:8545 [1] is INVALID | Value must be in format 0x[1-9]+[0-9] or 0x0`

Solution:
always check if response contains an error and, if yes throw and actual exception with corresponding error message.

title: Retrieve the hashTreeRoot from the immutable preState to fully benefit from caching
body:
## PR Description
When processing slots, the previous state root has to be added to the historical roots.  Previously we would get a mutable version of the state and immediately calculate it's hash tree root to get that value.  This changes it so we get the hash tree root of the immutable preState instead so that we can utilise a precalculated hash if one already exists.  It's only a minor improvement since the hash tree root of each SSZ node is cached and we benefit from the next level down, but it is a small saving.

title: Update remote validator client to handle altair block creation
body:
Use spec milestone of Altair enabled to direct the validator client to use `eth/v2/validator/blocks/:slot`, so that the version field in the response can be used to determine which type of block should be deserialized.

The `eth/v1/validator/blocks/:slot` endpoint does return an altair block but its less simple to decode, which ultimately stopped the remote validator from participating in block production.

The block production v2 endpoint is part of the standard spec, but we need to be careful switching to it, so for now this option is hidden and disabled by default.

For deserialization to work, a custom deserializer has been added for the GetNewBlockResponseV2 object.

it appears theres still functionality broken for remote validators, but this is a good start.

fixes #3974

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

title: [DO NOT MERGE] Delay attestation creation when using independent timers by 1 second
body:
Just creating PR to make experimental builds more accessible.

Context for anyone looking on.  With dependent roots disabled (the default) the beacon node produces a head event, 4 seconds into every slot and that's used to trigger creation of attestations.  With dependent roots enabled, that event is gone and attestations are produced using an independent timer in the validator client. Given they're on the same machine and even in the same process, clock skew or load doesn't make a difference but there seems to be a tiny difference in results.

The head event produced, happens on the fork choice thread, after running the full fork choice selection, which means if a block is still being processed while it happens, the event will be slightly delayed until the block imports and is always slightly delayed because of the time taken to run fork choice and then propagate the event.  So this tests what happens to rewards if we artificially delay attestation creation. It's delayed by a full second which is more than the event would be delayed, but is a quick way to see if this is possibly the problem (if the rewards don't improve, it definitely isn't timing, if they do we need to establish if the head event is delayed by enough to actually matter).


To be very clear, producing attestations 1 second late is dishonest validator behaviour and is definitely not something we intend to actually do in the real Teku.  This is just an experiment to gather data.

title: Cache public key group membership status
body:
## PR Description
Group membership checks for elliptic curve points (public keys and signatures) are very  expensive and we want to do them as little as possible, ideally checking each point we use in verification exactly once.

When aggregating public keys using Blst's `blst.P1.aggregate()` method, the keys' group membership is [always checked](https://github.com/supranational/blst/blob/dc79d429fa4c63a53f4b1f8cb01d90cb9c2eccf0/bindings/blst.hpp#L164), even if it was checked previously. With this PR, we lazily check a public key's group membership and cache the result. We can then avoid the repeated group membership checks by using `blst.P1.add()` instead of `aggregate()`.

Remarks:
  - This only helps if `BLSPublicKey` objects are well-cached and not created anew: we lose the cached group check status in that case.
  - By design, the aggregated public key will be in the group. Nevertheless Blst's `core_verify()` still checks group membership of the aggregated key. Not a lot we can do about that.
  - As for signatures, we don't expect to be seeing the same signature time and time again, so there is likely little to be gained by applying the group membership caching to signatures.

Closes #4032

title: CLI to allow conversion between database versions
body:
Implemented migrate-data subcommand to create a new database version.

The `--network` context is needed. It's probably easiest to specify `--config-file` as part of the CLI like normal, then execute the migrate-data subcommand, so the path, eth1 contract etc can be read from the config file while the new database is being created.

 - cannot create a database instance of the same type currently.

 - prints status updates every 100k records, and also a count of rows moved for each column.

 - no data validation is performed, byte data is literally copied. This makes the move fairly fast.

 - if an existing beacon.old is found, the program will abort. Beacon.old is theoretically a real database that was working, so removing it might be dangerous.

 - if there's an existing beacon.new, it's cleaned up at the start of the process - this was likely an incomplete conversion.

 - if the subcommand completes successfully, the 'beacon' folder will be the new database type. 'beacon.old' will be the original database, and will need to be manually cleaned up by the user.  It shouldn't be cleaned up until the new database is verified to be ok.

 - the 'beacon' folder is impacted by this subcommand, but other folders (eg. validator are not touched).

fixes #3882

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

title: Fix potential race condition in DefaultPerformanceTracker
body:
## PR Description
start is called from a different thread to onSlot so need to ensure a consistent view of nodeStartEpoch. Most of the time we'd get away with it but sometimes it's possible for the method to start on one CPU and pass the `nodeStartEpoch.isEmpty` check and enter the main logic in the method but to then wind up on a different core and see an empty value for `nodeStartEpoch` (no memory barrier means no ordering guarantees).

Making `nodeStartEpoch` volatile and using a consistent immutable reference to it inserts the required memory barriers and avoids the race condition.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #4200
