## PR Description
SignedContributionAndProofValidator was incorrectly rejecting contribution gossip if the chain head state slot was greater than the contribution slot. This check could fail because of a race condition when contributions were received right at the end of the slot.

Now that there's no requirement for the block to be known, it doesn't make sense to try and check the referenced block root's slot.

title: Make use of abstract unit tests for BLST implementation
body:
## PR Description

Turned out that there are 3 BLST abstract unit tests which were formerly derived just by the Mikuli implementation tests, but were actually intended to test BLST implementation as well. 


- Remove `succeedsWhenPassingEmptyListToAggregatePublicKeysDoesNotThrowException` : aggregating empty set of public keys should formerly return 'infinite point' public key. Don't think this is a case any more as the spec now explicitly prohibits 'infinite points' 
- Return 'true' for `batchVerify` with empty batches list
- ~~`aggregateVerifyDuplicateMessages`: for some reasons in Mikuli we prohibited duplicate messages when doing `aggregateVerify`. That [condition](https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/pull/1100/files?file-filters%5B%5D=.java&hide-deleted-files=true#diff-43cbcb21d01ad4a2e674e5d30fcf4533e4d9460ea0d4ee83b875bc73d10f609bR101-R106) was added in #1100. @benjaminion could you please check this if you by any chance remember what was the reason behind this check?~~
- fix `BatchSignatureVerifierTest#shouldRaiseExceptionIfNoValidPublicKeys`: throwing `IndexOutOfBoundsException` was just a side effect. Returning `false` from `batchVerify()` is the expected behavior 
- Prohibit duplicate messages for `aggregateVerify` as per [BLS spec](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-irtf-cfrg-bls-signature-04#section-3.1.1).

## Fixed Issue(s)

Fix #4240

title: Switch jdk16 docker image to use eclipse-temurin
body:
## PR Description
The jdk16 docker image (which is the default) is now built from eclipse-temurin.

eclipse-temurin doesn't provide a JRE only build so we now use jlink to build one from the JDK. On the plus side, this gives us an even smaller image and we now control the base OS our images use.

There isn't a java 14 or 15 for eclipse-tumerin so they have switched back to OpenJDK, but also use jlink to build a JRE then use ubuntu:latest as the base OS.

Have added a note that the jdk14 and jdk15 images will be removed in a future release. Those JDK versions aren't being supported anymore so there's no reason anyone should be using them.

## Fixed Issue(s)

title: Optimise voted validator iteration
body:
## PR Description
Store the highest index of any validator that has attested to avoid copying the entire set of indices. Since nearly every validator has voted at some point and we can quickly identify validators that haven't voted there's no benefit to iterating over the specific list, and copying it for thread safety creates a significant amount of garbage.

## PR Description

title: Verify SSZ bit is padded to byte boundary with zeros
body:
## PR Description
Verify SSZ bit is padded to byte boundary with zeros when deserializing.

SSZ bits, when not packed as part of a list or vector, should be either 0x00 or 0x01 but Teku previously wasn't verifying the leading bits padding out the byte were all zero.

This is really just future proofing as the only place a bit is used outside a list or vector currently is in `BeaconState.Validator.slashed` and we use the `SszSuperNode` optimisation for validators so don't parse individual field during deserialisation.  However this change ensures that if a bit is ever added to something transferred over the network that our parsing will be compatible with other clients.

title: Fix gossip validation around a network upgrade
body:
## PR Description
Remove get_domain variants that get the fork from the state and explicitly pass in the fork to use instead.
Resolves an issue where attestations (and potentially other types) from after the fork are published by a node that did not follow the fork, but validated against a state from prior to the fork.  The older state may be used either because it is within the look-ahead period for attestation committees or because there were empty slots immediately after the fork epoch. The old state does not contain info on the fork as it only contains previous and current fork info, so the gossiped signature verifies even though it is incorrectly from the old fork.

More complete write up at https://hackmd.io/n54L4BRoTP2l3OVrrSXszg

Starting the test-network with `launch.sh` Grafana stops with the following error:

title: Retrieve network information for external validator from beacon node endpoint
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Currently, when running a remote validator client (typically using the `teku vc ...` subcommand), a `--network` option needs to be specified. The value provided to this option can either be the name of one of a set of defined networks (mainnet, prater, etc.), or a path to a configuration file, in the case of a custom network. This information is used to load the relevant network presets and constants that a VC will need. 
However, because a beacon node already exposes some of this information through its config API (/eth/v1/config/spec), a VC can technically fetch these details directly, without requiring the cli option. 
This PR enables this feature through a new option value, `auto`, added to the `--network` option of a `validator-client` subcommand. All other values to the `--network` option values have been deprecated in favor of this value.  

Example: `teku validator-client --network=auto`

## Fixed Issue(s)
This PR fixes #3530

title: Don't assume all MatchingDataAttestationGroup instances have a known shuffling seed
body:
## PR Description
Fixes an `IllegalStateException` during block production in a particular corner case. Specifically:

 * A block is imported to the canonical chain containing an attestation with `AttestationData` that has never been seen via gossip.
 * Then an attestation with that same `AttestationData` is received via gossip with a subset of the already included validators.
 * Block production is requested before any attestations with not-included validators are received for that `AttestationData`.

It was assumed that all `MatchingDataAttestationPool` instances held would have, at some point, had an attestation added to them from which the committee shuffling seed could be retrieved.  As part of filtering for inclusion in the block the group is checked to ensure that stored seed matches one of the valid seeds for the block.  In this corner case the seed has never been stored and so an `IllegalStateException` is thrown.

The fix is to consider any `MatchingDataAttestationPool` that doesn't have a stored seed as not matching and simply skip over it (it won't have any attestations in it anyway).

title: Simplify handling of invalid signatures
body:
The previous implementation used a flag to track whether a signature was valid or invalid. An example of an invalid signature was one that encodes a point not in the G2 group.

This led to oddities like having both valid and invalid infinity signatures. It also led to ambiguity about whether we check the G2 group membership at deserialisation or on usage of a signature. In batch verification we ended up doing both (but not explicitly checking the signature's validity in the calling code). This was all a bit messy and hard to maintain.

In this PR we explicitly delegate the group membership check to the Blst library, and we _do not_ perform the group membership check at deserialisation of the signature. This ought to slightly speed things up (due to no longer duplicating the check in batch verification) and should make things more maintainable.

The risk is that if Blst behaviour changes, or we swap in a different library in future, we could inadvertantly end up without the group membership check. I have added some tests to guard against this.

As a bonus, this closes #4111.

title: Extend readiness check with peer count
body:
## PR Description
Extend readiness check with peer count:
- get target peer count from request parameters optionally
- return unavailable when peer target not reached
- return bad request when cannot parse parameter
- add tests to cover new scenarios
- fix typos

## Fixed Issue(s)
This new feature aims to improve teku load balancing in Kubernetes.
Currently a beacon is considered ready to accept traffic when is already initialised but this not necessarily means that I connected to a sufficient number of peers. 
Therefore beacon would start receiving traffic from validators but unable to include all the attestations received. 

## Documentation
Readiness probe is enriched with peer count check optionally.
If target peer count is passed as a parameter, then readiness check would return unavailable until target count is reached.
Therefore beacon would be in better position to receive traffic with a target number of peers connected.

body:
## PR Description
Fixes some corner cases which could lead to exceptions when importing, exporting or repairing slashing protection records.

* `NullPointerException` when importing a slashing protection record that contained a genesis validators root over an existing record that did not (e.g after performing a repair)
* Generated an invalid export for validators that had never signed an attestation - should have had an empty list of attestations but actually had a single, empty object as the signed attestation
* `NullPointerException` when importing an invalid export with an empty object as signed attestation
* `NullPointerException` when repairing the slashing protection record for a validator that had never attested

Generally makes code much more defensive to `null` values.

## PR Description

A lot of API compatibility issues fixed

With these changes Teku works with [Geth EE ](https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/23607), successfully produces and imports blocks with `ExecutionPayload` composed by Geth EE

### Run instructions

1. Build and start Geth EE as described [here](https://notes.ethereum.org/@9AeMAlpyQYaAAyuj47BzRw/rkwW3ceVY)

  --Xnetwork-altair-fork-epoch=0 \

  --eth1-endpoints=http://localhost:8545 \

title: Publish to multiple endpoints for validator duties
body:
To improve participation rates in the network, allow multiple endpoints to be configured to send production duties.

The CLI `--Xvalidators-publish-to-additional-nodes` will allow the user to configure multiple URI's to use to send validator produced items. Each produced object (attestations, aggregations, blocks, contributions, aggregate and proofs) will be sent to all endpoints rather than to just the primary beacon node configured. This will be usable by either validator-client or full beacon node mode.

I've used URI which did simplify configuration, but will need some extra testing as it's a fair amount more permissive than URL objects.

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

title: [Merge] Draft implementation of Optimistic sync with Execution Layer
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Based on top of #4456 

Kind of quick fix to support the Optimistic syncing: 
- Assume all 'old' blocks  (`block.slot  < currentSlot - 128`) as 'finalized' which need no `executionPayload` and `checkOnTerminalPowBlockConditions` validation
- Validating all the 'recent' blocks as per spec

The general idea of production implementation is to queue those validations while syncing, drop validations for blocks which become finalized, execute the remaining validations when the sync completes. Probably makes sense to update the head upon EL validations pass

Related  Lighthouse PRs:
- https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/pull/2686
- https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/pull/2683

Related doc: https://notes.ethereum.org/@djrtwo/BJxKBaqNF

Good description here as well: https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/issues/2691

title: Increase delay between pinging bootnodes
body:
## PR Description
Ensures that the delay between pings is longer than the session timeout from discovery so previously failed ping attempts are forgotten and we retry from a clean slate. This is a quick fix, ultimately the session management in discovery needs to be adjusted to drop sessions that are non-responsive faster when they are in the initial handshake phase.

Without this the first ping to the bootnode moves the state to `RANDOM_PACKET_SENT` and so subsequent ping attempts wait for that handshake complete, but each ping attempt is incorrectly extending the session timeout.

## Fixed Issue(s)
work around for #4482. This has identified a weakness in discovery session management that will need to be properly fixed.

title: Add windows sanity check build
body:
## PR Description
Adds a basic windows build. This runs `./gradlew.bat` on a fresh checkout to confirm building and running unit tests works on Windows.  The unit tests include coverage of blst, leveldb and rocksdb (all our native components) to give good confirmation of whether they will or won't work on a pretty normal windows install.

Currently LevelDB is not supported on recent windows so tests have been updated to add assumptions that LevelDB is supported before they try to run. We can remove these assumptions when we have update LevelDB.

Ideally we'd run this only on master post-merge since it's fairly expensive and most changes aren't Windows specific so running it on every commit to a PR is excessive.  However the slack notification orb doesn't currently work on Windows boxes so we have no way of notifying of failures.  Until that's fixed we'll need to run it as part of pre-merge checks.

## Fixed Issue(s)

title: Move defaults and calculations from CLI `*Options` to `*Config` [part 1]
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

This is a part of effort to introduce Java API: easy node spinning up with `TekuConfiguration`

The aim is to make `TekuConfiguration` (and its members) the primary source of config values and leave CLI `*Options` as a simple facade for command line parsing. The `TekuConfiguration` created either with CLI or with a builder should be the same when the same options are specified. 

I.e. that simple test should work:
```java
public class TekuConfigurationTest extends AbstractBeaconNodeCommandTest {
  @Test
  void test() {
    TekuConfiguration cliConfig = getTekuConfigurationFromArguments();
    TekuConfiguration config = TekuConfiguration.builder().build();
    Assertions.assertThat(config).usingRecursiveComparison().isEqualTo(cliConfig);
  }
}
```

Currently a lot of default option values resides in the `*Options` classes while `*Config` values are either nulls or duplicate default values. The same relates to computable default value s: the most of the logic is handled by the `*Options` classes 

This PR addresses most simple cases and moves defaults (either constant or computed) from `*Options` to `*Config`s:
- Move default config constants from `MetricsOptions` to `MetricsConfig`
- Move default config constants from `BeaconRestApiOptions` to `BeaconRestApiConfig`
- Move default config constants from `InteropOptions` to `InteropConfig`
-  Move default constant and computable values from `P2POptions` and `Eth2NetworkOptions` to `P2PConfig`, `DiscoveryConfig`, `NetworkConfig`, `StorageConfiguration`, `PowchainConfiguration`, `SyncConfig`
- To handle computed default values - add a number of `*Config.Builder` methods `<someOption>Default()` which sets the option value if it's not set explicitly yet

title: Publish multi-arch docker images
body:
## PR Description
Configure CircleCI to publish multi-arch docker images. This isn't the ideal approach but it threads the needle between significant limitations in Docker's multi-arch support and CircleCI's support for ARM docker instances.

We want to be able to build the docker images locally, test them and then publish, but Docker can't make multi-arch images locally, it has to publish the single-arch versions to a repo then create a multi-arch manifest pointing at them. And while we can use the docker buildx plugin to build multi-arch images it isn't capable of loading the multi-arch image back into the local docker - it can only do that for single-arch images. So we have to do the multi-arch build and publish them in the dockerUpload step.

To ensure the docker build process used for testing is as similar as possible to the final build we publish, we install and use the `buildx` plugin when building the single-arch docker image for ATs, even though it doesn't strictly need buildx.

Also removes the separate `docker` step to the build and just lets the docker images be built as part of the acceptance test step. Looking at the logs for previous runs, only the base layers for the built docker images were being reused anyway with the Teku specific steps still executing again as part of the acceptance test step. Plus the acceptance test step runs on the same machine_executor type as the final publish so building the images there brings the two build setups closer.


Testing-wise it's obviously hard to check how this works in CircleCI since the upload step only runs once merged. So testing has been done in two ways:
1. Initially the buildx multi-arch build ran as part of the `docker` step which confirmed it does work and builds images successfully (though they don't get published anywhere)
2. I've been testing the publish by running locally and publishing under a different alias (https://hub.docker.com/repository/docker/ajsutton/tekua/tags). From there I can confirm that I can run the images on both intel and arm devices and it pulls the right image. I've since deleted the repo but have also run tests of building when there is a release tag for that commit to check it publishes under the right release versions still.


fixes #4062

title: Filter out invalid nodes in ProtoArray.contains
body:
## PR Description
Modify ProtoArray.contains to return false when the requested node is invalid.

As with blocks discarded because they no longer descend from the finalized checkpoint, the `ProtoNode` remains but the block root to node index lookup is removed which effectively makes the node inaccessible but doesn't require creating a copy of the protoarray with the actual node removed.

As a result of removing this lookup, if the justified block is found to be invalid we are no longer able to determine the head since the fork choice algorithm starts from the justified block and the valid head must agree with that justified block. Since getting to this point requires 2/3rd of validators to have attested to an invalid block it has the same kind of "oh this is really bad" setup as finalizing an invalid block and requiring user intervention makes sense.

title: [Merge] Add execution payload block hash to protoarray
body:
## PR Description
Stores the execution payload block hash for each block in protoarray so it can be accessed efficiently.  Since we have a protoarray node for every non-finalised block we need to minimise memory usage of them so are using `Bytes32.ZERO` for all blocks prior to the merge fork to avoid the additional overhead of an `Optional` instance.  `ZERO` is also the default value for a block that doesn't include an execution payload because TTD hasn't been reached so it makes compatibility with earlier forks easy as they simply appear as pre-TTD.

No database schema migration is required because we load the protoarray data from the actual blocks so we are already storing the full execution payload when there is one.  There is an older storage layout we still support migrating from `ProtoArraySnapshot` which does not have this information but since we stopped writing to that format well before we started supporting merge blocks there can't be any databases with merge blocks in them that are still using `ProtoArraySnapshot`.

title: Reject create block and attestation requests when chain head is optimistic
body:
## PR Description
It is not safe for validators to produce blocks on top of or attest to blocks that have only been optimistically synced. So if the referenced block is not fully validated, return a node syncing response rather than creating the block/attestation. Node syncing is used because the execution engine is still syncing and unable to verify the payload.

Since blocks and attestations use the chain head which is normally not optimistic block production and attestation creation can continue while there are some optimistically sync'd blocks, as long as we still have a fully validated block close enough to use as our chain head and build on. If we've optimistically finalized, we will cease block and attestation production.

We don't prevent creating aggregates because the validator client will only create aggregates for attestations they produced, so if they managed to produce the attestation it must have been validated (though potentially by a different beacon node).

title: [Java API] Allow to customize `BeaconChainController` construction
body:
## PR Description

This is the follow PR up to #4601 

Currently Teku is pretty solid in terms of substituting/tweaking various components. 
Trying to address this, the initial change I'd like to discuss is to make `BeaconChainController` construction more customizable. 

- Add `BeaconChainControllerFactory` to the `TekuConfiguration`
- Make `BeaconChainController` extensible with making all its members protected. 

I guess the latter change is a bit controversial to common Teku patterns. I.e. altering behavior via inheritance is generally not too good practice. 

However overriding specific `BeaconChainController` methods looks like the easiest way to tweak the logic and replace components without much support burden for Teku maintainers and without duplicating a lot of code for Teku clients 

Java API is not official and declared as unstable so Teku would still not provide any guarantees that overridden client `BeaconChainController` is not broken after any commit.

title: Perform state transition for blocks off the fork choice thread
body:
## PR Description
Since state transition does not require a mutable store, it can be performed off the fork choice thread, then once the post-state is complete, adding the block to the store and protoarray can happen on the fork choice thread.

This simplifies execution of post-merge payloads as the executePayload request is sent to the EL from off the fork choice thread and the CL can then wait for a response prior to switching to the fork choice thread. Thus when the EL is online, blocks are imported as valid immediately and optimistic sync is only used when the EL is actually syncing.

This also has the benefit of allowing multithreaded processing of blocks received via gossip if they are from different forks such as when a block is a full slot late and arrives at the same time as the block for the next slot.

title: DiscoveryConfig: correctly handle the case when maxPeers == 0
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Was experimenting with a node config and found that even when `maxPeers == 0`  a `ConnectionManager` still tries to connect. 

The first reason was that even when `maxPeers == 0` the config still initializes `minRandomlySelectedPeers` default value to `1`. That's why `Eth2PeerSelectionStrategy` still yields one candidate to connect to. 

This PR fixes the reason above by bounding `minRandomlySelectedPeers` with `maxPeers`

The second issue with `maxPeers == 0` is that `Eth2PeerSelectionStrategy` still yields peers to connect due to `PeersSubnetSubscriptions` (related PR #2543): https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/48aa4d6ec85e68a14b7270f0851550ba12e7ade0/networking/eth2/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/networking/eth2/peers/Eth2PeerSelectionStrategy.java#L77

I'm not sure I get the logic why `getSubscribersRequired()` returns `2` while there are no subnet subscriptions. Here is the unit test checking that:https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/9aeda7b8e270b04ed6f9720c9cb1c980dd81d21d/networking/eth2/src/test/java/tech/pegasys/teku/networking/eth2/gossip/subnets/PeerSubnetSubscriptionsTest.java#L116-L121

The issue could be worked around by specifying `--Xp2p-target-subnet-subscriber-count` option though I'd like to make sure the `peerSubnetSubscriptions.getSubscribersRequired()` logic works as expected

title: Optimise sha256 calls
body:
## PR Description
Avoid using Bytes.concatenate to combine byte arrays when calculating sha256. Bytes.concatenate copies the content of the values passed to it. Even Bytes.wrap which doesn't copy initially will copy the data when toArrayUnsafe() is called to create a unified view.  By providing versions of Hash.sha256 that accept multiple arguments the calculation can be done without copying the data. 

Additionally the `Bytes.update(MessageDigest)`  method is used instead of `toArrayUnsafe()` because `toArrayUnsafe()` may create a copy of the data if the `Bytes` instance is a view into a subset of the underlying bytes array, for example when using `.slice` to extract a portion of a larger `Bytes` instance.

These changes also provide a significant reduction in the number of object allocations required.

Added a benchmark to confirm the difference which shows about a 15% speed up per hash operation.

title: Rename merge to bellatrix
body:
## PR Description
Inline with the changes in the spec 1.1.8 release rename the `MERGE` fork to `BELLATRIX`. Note that the fork is called `BELLATRIX` but the point later when total terminal difficulty is reached and the two chains combine is still called the merge - hence references to things like "merge block" remain valid.  Otherwise a whole heap of `merge` got renamed to `bellatrix`.

Public API effects of this:
 * Network config files now use the new config names (e.g. `BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH`)
 * Beacon REST API now sets the `version` field for blocks and states to `bellatrix` instead of `merge` (only affects networks where bellatrix fork has activated).

title: Validator id parameters should not be rejected for bytes48 not on g2 curve
body:
If a bytes48 key is provided that can't be validated on the curve, treat it as a missed key, not an invalid request. In a large list of bytes48 a single key will otherwise reject the entire request, where we could instead just process the rest of the request.

Internally we still need to map keys to the curve to be able to search for the key, so for any valid bytes48 we will still end up having to map to the curve to find the key.

0x hex with invalid length will still be rejected as a bad request.

fixes #4787

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

title: Add authentication to validator rest api.
body:
On startup, the server will create a file in `validator/validator-api-bearer` with a random password.

If the password is "xyz", that is what is in that file, and then the Authorization header is expected to be `Bearer xyz`

The first line of the file is read and then uri encoded to remove any invalid data. For example, ` ` gets encoded to `+`.

Users and roles are possible but not implemented in this version, as we're keeping it simple.

The password is read at startup, so changing password would currently require a restart.

Because of the clear text nature of the password in the header, it's going to need to be changed to https transport.

Signed-off-by: Paul Harris <paul.harris@consensys.net>

title: Add support for multiple fee recipients
body:
## PR Description

The PR introduces two new params for validator client:

- `--Xvalidators-proposer-config`: allows to specify a file path or a URL from which retrieve the configuration

- `--Xvalidators-proposer-config-refresh-enabled`: enables reload of the config every time VC is about to call `prepare_beacon_proposer` API (which currently happen at the beginning of each epoch)

the config is an extensible json file which allows to specify:

- a _**proposer configuration**_ for multiple validator public key.
- a default _**proposer configuration**_ for validator public keys not included in the previous mapping.

_**proposer configuration**_ currently contains only `fee_recipient`. It can be extended to include other information (ie block builder URL)

### behaviour details

- if `--Xvalidators-proposer-config` is specified,  VC during initialisation will try to load the configuration. If fails (or the json config is invalid\incorrect) VC will fail start up
- if `--Xvalidators-proposer-config-refresh-enabled` is activated, if config reload fails, the last valid configuration will be used.

### config json structure

```json
{
  "proposer_config": {
    "0xa057816155ad77931185101128655c0191bd0214c201ca48ed887f6c4c6adf334070efcd75140eada5ac83a92506dd7a": {
      "fee_recipient": "0x50155530FCE8a85ec7055A5F8b2bE214B3DaeFd3",
    }
  },
  "default_config": {
    "fee_recipient": "0x6e35733c5af9B61374A128e6F85f553aF09ff89A"
  }
}
```

`proposer_config` is optional
`default_config` is mandatory
`fee_recipient` is mandatory in each config

### How fee recipient will be actually chosen

- when `--Xvalidators-proposer-config` is used in VC
  - `fee_recipient` from a specific validator in the config
  - otherwise, `fee_recipient` from `default_config` in the config
  - otherwise, `--Xvalidator-proposer-default-fee-recipient` at beacon node

- when `--Xvalidators-proposer-default-fee-recipient`  is used in VC
  - `fee_recipient` from `--Xvalidators-proposer-default-fee-recipient` in VC
  - otherwise, `--Xvalidator-proposer-default-fee-recipient` at beacon node

### additional notes

currently, IO is blocking (file access as well as URL access). We have 5 threads on `validator` runner, to be evaluated if it is enough for the moment. It can be improved by migrating to async IO.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #4850

title: Add value checks for some configuration options
body:
This PR begins to add simple validation checks to configuration options. This is still a work-in-progress. I expect to make more commits to this PR before it is approved. I'm just want to start the process now so that I know I'm going down the right path.

To identify options that needed checks, I used the following regex. This finds function signatures that return a `Builder` object and have an `int`, `long`, `OptionalInt`, or `Duration` in the parameter list. These types allow negative values but generally negative values are not wanted.

```
ag "public \w*Builder .*\(.*(\(|\s)(int|long|OptionalInt|Duration) "
```

There are lots of other configuration options that could probably use better validation. We can deal with those later. I only modified options that were clearly not meant to be zero/negative.

I throw `IllegalArgumentException` instead of `InvalidConfigurationException` because I ran into some circular dependency issues early on. I can work on fixing those problems or we might want to change these checks to `com.google.common.base.Preconditions.checkArgument` as I see that used a lot.

This is for issue #4906.

title: Move exception handlers to `:infrastructure:async`
body:
`:infrastructure:execeptions` had a dependency on `:infrastructure:async` that would cause a circular dependency in some situations. For example, if `:infrastructure:metrics` included `:infrastructure:exceptions`:

```
Circular dependency between the following tasks:
:infrastructure:async:compileJava
\--- :infrastructure:metrics:compileJava
     \--- :infrastructure:exceptions:compileJava
          \--- :infrastructure:async:compileJava (*)
```

To resolve this problem, this commit moves the two exception handlers that used `async.SafeFuture` from `:infrastructure:execeptions:ExceptionUtil` to `:infrastructure:async:ExceptionHandlers`.

Also, the `:infrastructure:async` dependency has been removed from `:infrastructure:execeptions` as it is no longer required.

Related to issue #4906. This PR must be merged before #4909 can be completed.

title: Fixes BatchSync when EL offline
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
When `BatchSync` is trying to import batch and `BatchImport` unables to verify it because it contains `ExecutionPayload` and Execution Client is offline, `BatchSync` is paused for 5 seconds to retry the same action afterwards. Before PR `BatchSync` marked batches as invalid and penalized peers in the same case.

I called event `BatchImportResult.SERVICE_OFFLINE` because I'm not sure we should disclose EL on this level, though logs are not a part of code and could be helpful for users, so I mentioned it there. 

I don't like the way I did logging in `Web3JExecutionEngineClient` but I want good UX for users who looks at node after 2 hours of stall. I discarded `EVENT_LOG` in `BatchSync` option, where similar message repeats,  because during normal block-by-block sync `BatchSync` is not used and EL could gone offline too. Any advices how could I make this better are appreciated.

Also I'm not sure peers are not penalized during normal sync at the head of the chain when importing fresh blocks. My home chain have not synchronized yet, will check tomorrow and update.

title: Block gossip optimization by early reject and ignore in `BlockValidator`
body:
## PR Description

- changed `invalidBlockRoots` from a `Set` to a `Map` holding INVALID import result
- new `executionFailedBlockRoots` `Set` of blockroots of blocks failed with `FAILED_EXECUTION_PAYLOAD_EXECUTION`

- new failure reasons:
  - `FAILED_DESCENDANT_OF_INVALID_BLOCK`: whenever `BlockManager` tries to import a block child of a block contained in `invalidBlockRoots`, it immediately returns this result.
  - if the imported block is contained `invalidBlockRoots`, we immediately return with its previous invalid reason.

- in gossip import (`validateAndImportBlock`) if block is in `invalidBlockRoots` (or is a child of one of those blocks) we immediately reject with `Block (or its parent) previously marked as invalid`. 

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #4920 by closing the last nice to have task

title: Convert some collections to use fastutil collections
body:
Converted several `Map<Integer, ?>` to `Int2ObjectMap<?>` and `Set<Integer>` to `IntSet`. These new collections are faster and more memory efficient because they use built-in types and not `Integer` objects. There were a few collections I did not convert because it just didn't make sense too.

* In two instances, I had to move `iterator.remove()` after entry references. The tests were throwing an index out of bounds exceptions. I'm unsure why using `ObjectIterator` behaves differently.
* Needed to add some `contains()` checks prior to `remove()` because in `Map` and `Set` the remove method will just return null if the value did not exist. The fastutil collections will throw an error instead.
* On the same though, converted from `get(key)` to `getDefault(key, null)` to have the same behavior.

title: Print Syncing messages during optimistic sync and initial startup
body:
## PR Description
Change `SlotProcessor` to use a `SyncStateProvider` (which is ultimately backed by `SyncStateTracker`) to determine if the node is syncing or not.  This means that it will stay in syncing mode while waiting for the EL to finish validating blocks after optimistic sync reaches the beacon chain head.

It will also now be in syncing mode immediately after startup until either sufficient peers are reached or the timeout is reached (ie while the node is in the initial startup mode).  Other components like the REST API and `ValidatorApiHandler` always used this sync state so their behaviour is unchanged, but now the console messages accurately reflect the sync state.

Also fixed a minor oversight where the p2p network wasn't informed of epoch changes during sync. It uses those events to ensure it subscribes to the right fork gossip topics. Mostly gossip is disabled during sync anyway but with some particularly unlucky timings Teku may have wound up not subscribed to the right fork gossip until the epoch after sync completed.

title: sync-aware `TerminalPowBlockMonitor`
body:
Let `TerminalPowBlockMonitor` do its checks when the node is full in Sync (CL and EL in sync)

The basic idea is that, even if the Terminal Block detection depends only by EL sync status only, if CL is syncing the knowledge of Terminal Block is useless.

Lowered the gravity and rephrased the TTD validation log from `error` to `warning` in the case when the EL has progressed beyond the Terminal Block, which means that it's likely that we were syncing around that time and we missed it.

Also removed `AtomicBoolean` usage, not needed since all important methods are `synchronized`

title: Remove use dependent roots feature toggle.
body:
## PR Description
Remove feature toggle for dependent roots. We've been using dependent roots for a long time so no need to maintain the old approach.

There's a couple of differently named things this toggle controlled (which makes sense in their specific contexts):

* `useDependentRoots` - now always `true` - duties are invalidated based on the `dependent_root` metadata
* `updateHeadForEmptySlots` - now always `false` (we don't send a re-org event if an empty slot is filled)
* `useIndependentAttestationTiming` - now always `true` - the validator now handles timing independently and doesn't expect a `head` event every slot

title: Feature: Websockets and IPC connection to execution engine
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Added support of Websockets connection to execution engine. There are several notes regarding this PR:
- `Files.readString(filePath).strip()` in `JwtSecretKeyLoader`. Similar code appears in several parts of the project, I'd add it to some `Utils` to be consistent over the codebase, but haven't found any `Utils`.
- Errors are handled too broad both with websockets and http as execution client being offline. Not semantically correct, but user see errors like this not too deep. Pretty sure `ConnectException` is not the only type for execution client connection issues, so not forcing fix.
```
13:12:49.893 ERROR - Execution Client is offline java.lang.Error: -32601: the method engine_exchangeTransitionConfigurationV1 does not exist/is not available (See log file for full stack trace)
```
- We may need to support TLS in the future for both type of connections. Besu already supports it. Shouldn't be an epic issue for `https`, but for `wss` it could. Check more below regarding implementation limitations.


There are several constraints due to limited support of websockets (comparing to http) by `web3j` library:
- we couldn't have something like log interceptor for http, though in `TRACE` logging `web3j` logs incoming and outgoing messages by itself
- `WebSocketService` which we should use with `web3j` ignores connection exception, so it may be difficult to debug for the user. For example, with wrong JWT tokem on http you see in console "403 wrong token" or something like this, but inside `WebSocketService` there is dummy thrower
```
   if (!connected) {
            throw new ConnectException("Failed to connect to WebSocket");
        }
```
- Websockets implementation in `web3j` doesn't support TLS which could be an issue in future
- I don't see simple way to plug something from 3rd party into `web3j` for Websockets

title: Migrate GetIdentity REST API to new framework
body:
## PR Description
As a starting point to migrate the Beacon REST API over to the new framework used by the validator REST API, convert the GetIdentity function over.

We can't combine the two approaches to OpenAPI generation so while the migrated endpoints can generate OpenAPI from their type definitions, the OpenAPI continues to come from the annotations. An integration test has been setup to check the OpenAPI generated from type definitions is what we expect so that when we do finish switching over the new OpenAPI is in good shape.

The legacy OpenAPI plugin detects the annotations on any method called `handle` so the new framework `handle` method had to be renamed `handleRequest`.

Builds on #5072

title: Remove EventChannel indirection for time tick events
body:
## PR Description
Moves control of the TimerService into BeaconChainController so that it can call the onTick method directly rather than going via an event channel. This removes the queue of events and allows the quartz scheduler to manage back pressure if events aren't processed fast enough. It does this by skipping forward, making it less likely (though still possible) for the beacon chain's view of time to fall behind.

The scheduler has also been better configured to only use a single thread (matching the thread model of the event channel), consider an execution failed if it's delayed long enough that the next one is due and be explicit about some important defaults.

## Fixed Issue(s)
Should make #5131 less common, though long term the full solution is to remove the use of time tick events entirely and just schedule actions at the particular time they're required (and use plain system time for the clock).

title: Introduce strategy to select states for attestation validation
body:
## PR Description
Previously attestations were validated using the state for the block they attested to (applying slots if required). That requires holding or generating the state for any block we receive an attestation for.

We can reduce the number of states required by being more intelligent about the state we select. Since we hold strong references to the finalised and head states, those are our preferred options. If neither of those are suitable then we use the state from the earliest slot that would have the required committees (on the same fork as the attestation's block).

In typical network conditions this means we use three states:

1. The chain head for anything attesting to a canonical block in the current epoch
2. The finalised state for anything attesting to a block 2 epochs after the finalised state
3. The justified state for pretty much everything in between. The exception being blocks that don't descend from our justified checkpoint and are in the current epoch but that's quite unusual.

In periods of non-finalisation we may need more states to cover the different forks but will be able to use at most one state per fork per epoch which is still a 32x reduction in required states.

The other advantage this has is that it causes the justified state to be used frequently and so makes it far more likely to be available in memory when the finalised checkpoint updates and the next finalised checkpoint is most likely going to be the current justified checkpoint.

title: SSZ improvements in `MessageDigest` handling
body: This pr improves `MessageDigest` handling in 2 ways - by reusing it when possible (which avoids several objects creations) and passing around between nodes. - leveraging "delegation" feature above, in `SimpleLeafNode`, to avoid allocating new trailing zeros. Receiving the MessageDigest from the branch node we can update it in 2 steps: adding Data and static zeros borrowed from `ZERO_LEAVES` to reach the needed 32 bytes. New version: Reuse `MessageDigest` almost everywhere ## BeaconStateBenchmark Test case I used to compare profiles (from `BeaconStateBenchmark`): ```java private static final BLSPublicKey pubkey = BLSTestUtil.randomPublicKey(0); private static final DataStructureUtil dataStructureUtil = new DataStructureUtil(0).withPubKeyGenerator(() -> pubkey); private static final BeaconState beaconState = dataStructureUtil.randomBeaconState(32 * 1024); public static void main(String[] args) { IntStream.range(0, 2000) .forEach( __ -> { BeaconState stateW = beaconState.updated( state -> { int size = state.getBalances().size(); UInt64 balance = UInt64.valueOf(777); for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) { state.getBalances().setElement(i, balance); } }); stateW.hashTreeRoot(); }); } ``` ### CPU usage reduction initial version: 4% -->> new version: 7.5% ### Memory allocation reduction initial version: 46% -->> new version: 85% due to: initial version: -->> new version: (not even detected) initial version: -->> new version: -->> new version (more pressure on Bytes32 as expected) ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15999009/161274264-79b94866-6613-4646-937e-bf148819e637.png) ## Mainnet state transition but in a real world scenario, profiling by applying state transition on mainnet state at 3378209, to 3378508 (about 300 blocks) ### CPU usage increase initial version: -1.6% (worse) -->> new version: 0.5% ### Memory allocation reduction initial version: 12% -->> new version: 23% ## Documentation - [ ] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required. ## Changelog - [ ] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

title: Enable deprecation check & fix/suppress warnings
body:
## PR Description

Doing some spring cleaning. In this PR I enable deprecation checks (`-Xlint:deprecation`) and either fix the warnings or suppress them via a `SuppressWarnings` annotations. Enabling this deprecation check could potentially prevent some bugs.

Most of these are passing a spec to `DataStructureUtil`.

### Some Notes

In some of the asserts, I needed to add `ignoringFields` with some field names. I only added the ones that were different (ie caused the test to fail). If any of these look like they should match, maybe we will need to alter the test.

Some resources to explain the recommended changes I made:

* [hasFailed](https://www.javadoc.io/static/org.assertj/assertj-core/3.18.1/org/assertj/core/api/AbstractCompletableFutureAssert.html#hasFailed())
* [isEqualToComparingFieldByField](https://www.javadoc.io/static/org.assertj/assertj-core/3.18.1/org/assertj/core/api/AbstractObjectAssert.html#isEqualToComparingFieldByField(java.lang.Object))
* [isEqualToIgnoringGivenFields](https://www.javadoc.io/static/org.assertj/assertj-core/3.18.1/org/assertj/core/api/AbstractObjectAssert.html#isEqualToIgnoringGivenFields(java.lang.Object,java.lang.String...))

---

It's not that straight-forward to replace `BeaconChainUtil` with `ChainBuilder`.

I tried to replace `networkConfig.getConstants()` with `networkConfig.getSpec().getGenesisConfig().getRawConfig().get(field)` but I was having some problems. For example, sometimes the configuration wouldn't have a network name field; `rawConfig.get("NETWORK_NAME")` would be null.

---

I would like to replace this deprecated `com.google.common.io.Files#createTempDir` call with `java.nio.file.Files#createTempDirectory` but I would need to handle the `IOException` somehow. Not sure how to propagate that without changing a bunch of stuff; I tried but it got complicated quickly.

https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/516444f5b43ff85530d32e7a3206acc369a8b8fb/teku/src/test/java/tech/pegasys/teku/cli/subcommand/internal/validator/tools/KeyGeneratorTest.java#L69

* https://github.com/trinodb/trino/issues/6908

---

Here we are overloading a deprecated method. This seems sensitive, so I'm hesitant to attempt to fix it. The [API](https://javadoc.io/static/org.web3j/core/4.5.8/org/web3j/tx/gas/ContractGasProvider.html) wants us to use the method that takes a `contractFunc` string.

https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/335a1b7dafb0f65f07e234c94489089b5f36cf61/acceptance-tests/src/testFixtures/java/tech/pegasys/teku/test/acceptance/dsl/tools/deposits/DepositTransactionSender.java#L114-L120

Same with `getGasLimit` which is hardcoded.

body:
This processes a full set of 16 deposits in around 4ms rather than 22ms - over 5x speedup.

Logic:
  - We check signatures of all the block's deposits in a batch.
      - Almost always this will succeed and we can then process all the deposits without checking any individual signatures.
  - If the batch check fails then we fall back to normal deposit processing
     -  This verifies signatures for new validators and ignores the signatures for existing validators as usual.

Resolves #5254.

This replaces `keySet` with `entrySet` for loops that iterate over the whole map.

It is more efficient to use an iterator on the `entrySet` of the map, avoiding the extra `HashMap.get(key)` lookup.

See: https://stackoverflow.com/a/3870093 & https://stackoverflow.com/a/38116169

title: Add stricter limits to attestation pool size
body:
## PR Description
When the total number of attestations in the pool grows too large, start dropping attestations from older slots.  It's expensive to determine exactly how many attestations we could include in a block because that depends on how well they aggregate, but we can set an approximate maximum number that are ever likely to be useful and ensure the pool size stays below that.  For efficiency and simplicity we drop all attestations from the oldest slot we have when the limit is exceeded which is cheap and the oldest attestations are likely to be the least valuable.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #5196

title: Ensure gossip subscription is started when we begin waiting for EL to sync
body:
## PR Description
Previously if the optimistic sync started far enough back that we didn't subscribe to or unsubscribed from gossip, the sync state wouldn't change when the optimistic sync completed until the EL also completed sync. Since the P2P network listens for sync state changes to decide when to subscribe to gossip, Teku didn't subscribe to gossip while waiting for the EL causing to fall behind until long sync kicked in again.

Introducing a new AWAITING_EL sync state ensures a sync state change happens and provides more accurate sync state information for the node to work with.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #5323

title: Optimise epoch transition
body:
## PR Description
Few optimisations in this:

* Fix the EpochTransitionBenchmark and include calculating the hashTreeRoot of the resulting state since that's a fairly big part of the cost
* Use the BeaconState invariant fields to get the field index for slot (and genesis validator root and genesis time). Avoids a map lookup to find the index which is a big win when accessing the state slot in a loop
* Compute baseReward from the validator statuses instead of state. Avoids a bunch of SSZ field accesses for each validator and caches some values that are used for each calculation more efficiently.
* Avoid temporary list creation when updating primitive collections. Avoids needing to iterate through the Stream to create the list, then iterating again to actually do the processing.


Before changes:
EpochTransitionBenchmark.epochTransition              32768  thrpt   10  21.627 ± 0.875  ops/s

After changes:
EpochTransitionBenchmark.epochTransition              32768  thrpt   10  26.840 ± 0.720  ops/s

title: Bellatrix fork + External Signer: Send block_header for block sign request
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
For Bellatrix fork, send `block_header` instead of `block` for external signer block signing request (`BLOCK_V2`). `block_header` contains `body_root` instead of complete beacon block `body` which significantly reduces the traffic between Teku and external signer for block signing request. 

Either `block_header` or `block` can be used to calculate signing root by the external signer. For backward compatibility with PHASE0 and ALTAIR forks, only `block` is sent; for Bellatrix and later forks, only `block_header` is sent.

title: Add time based tolerance before disconnecting event streams
body:
## PR Description
Given that huge numbers of attestations are received at once, a strict queue length based limit on event stream subscribers is too strict as there's no chance to serialize and read all those events. With this change, the event queue can exceed the maximum size for up to one second, ensuring there is time for the messages to be sent if the subscriber is reading. If the subscriber is slow the timeout is still hit quickly without too many events backing up and causing memory issues.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #5399

title: Add propertyTest task
body:
## PR Description

This new task will run all of our Property-Based Testing (PBT) tests. With PBT, you test a certain property by defining constraints and letting the test engine produce randomized inputs; it's a lot like fuzzing. I discovered this concept while looking for an equivalent to [Golang's `go fuzz` feature](https://go.dev/doc/fuzz/), introduced in Go 1.18, that would work with Teku and its dependencies.

These first few property tests are relatively simple. I had a difficult time deciding where to start. I know that this area is already pretty well tested, most of Teku is pretty well tested IMO, but I needed to start somewhere. The plan is to add more PBT tests to existing classes in the near future.

The PBT test engine that I chose was not my first choice. Initially, I evaluated [JQF](https://github.com/rohanpadhye/JQF) which features randomized testing with coverage-guided fuzzing algorithms and the ability to run a certain test indefinitly.  Unfortunately, JQF does not work well with Teku. It requires the JUnit4 "vintage" platform and when we use the newer JUnit5 "jupiter" platform. Also, JQF is pretty tightly integrated with Maven and does not really support Gradle.  There is [a Gradle plugin](https://github.com/mborzenkov/jqf-gradle-plugin) but it's still very much in development; it doesn't support project structures like Teku.

Then, I evaluated `java-quickcheck`, which JQF is based on. As expected, it had the same problems as JQF. It doesn't feature coverage-guidance or anything cool like that but it would have still been useful.

Lastly, I tested `jqwik` which is an alternative PBT test engine that is designed to work for the JUnit5 platform. In my opinion, it has really great documentation (see the [user guide](https://jqwik.net/docs/current/user-guide.html) and [javadoc](https://jqwik.net/docs/1.6.5/javadoc/index.html)) and, from the best I can tell, it has all of the same features as `java-quickcheck`. Another good quality, there's an additional `jqwik-kotlin` module that is supposed to simplify/streamline using `jqwik` in Kotlin projects. This will be useful if we decide to introduce PBT into libp2p in the future as it is primarily written in Kotlin.

title: Implement more memory efficient deposit merkle tree
body:
## PR Description
Switches our merkle tree implementation to a more memory efficient approach that supports smaller snapshots, as per EIP-4881.

Currently storage is unchanged so we aren't taking actually advantage of the snapshot functionality but still benefit from a reduction in memory and likely slightly improved performance when creating a block with deposits (we create the required deposit tree once instead of dynamically restricting the "view" to create the proof for each deposit included in the block.

The old merkle tree implementation has been moved to testFixtures since it's used in tests (and inlined the abstract parent class since it only had one subclass). This provides confirmation that we're getting the same results with the new and old implementation, but in the future we can probably remove it entirely and just use the one implementation.

title: RejectedExecution reporting and health effects
body:
- New metric for rejected execution:
 ```
 # HELP executor_rejected_execution_total Count of rejected executions by task queue
 # TYPE executor_rejected_execution_total counter
 executor_rejected_execution_total{name="p2p",} 12.0
 ```
  this is a counter, so will track from start the number of RejectedExecutionExceptions received.

 - A new counter tracks 10 minutes (5 second polling intervals) of RejectedExecutionExceptions (aggregated across all threads). The counter is pretty generic, it allows to specify the number of polling periods to track, and you'd be responsible for calling 'poll' when the period changes. It's been configured for 120 periods of 5 seconds (10 minutes rolling). The poll function will return the value stored for that period.

 - if the counter is non 0, the GetHealth query will return 503. This means once the first RejectedExecutionException occurs, the health check will start to respond 503. It would take 10 minutes of no RejectedExecutionExceptions for the node to be again marked healthy.

## PR Description

This is because `BLSPubKey.fromHexString` will automatically validate the key:

title: [Mev Boost\Builder] we should be using builder post-merge only
body:
To reduce complexity during the transition, has been decided to start using builder infrastructure post merge only.

I'm introducing a `forceLocalFallback` in `builderGetHeader` to be used by `BlockOperationSelectorFactory` to control the fallback based on current transition state.

to summarize the flows:

blinded flow:
- pre bellatrix: `BlockFactory` transparently passthrough blocks
- post bellatrix:
  - pre transition: `BlockOperationSelectorFactory` will produce `executionHeaderOfDefaultPayload`. The flow completes in `createUnblinderSelector` which generates the corresponding `defaultPayload`
  - transition occurred, not finalized: `BlockOperationSelectorFactory` will force `forceLocalFallback` in `builderGetHeader`. The flow completes in `createUnblinderSelector` which calls `builderGetPayload` that rebuilds the payload from the fallback cache.
  - transition occurred and finalized: `BlockOperationSelectorFactory` will call `builderGetHeader` which eventually fallback. The flow completes in `createUnblinderSelector` which calls `builderGetPayload` that rebuilds the payload by calling  the builder or from the fallback cache.

unblinded flow (standard):
- pre bellatrix:  standard flow
- post bellatrix:
  - pre transition: `BlockOperationSelectorFactory` will produce `defaultPayload`
  - transition occurred, not finalized: `BlockOperationSelectorFactory` will call local `engineGetPayload`
  - transition occurred and finalized: same as above.

related to #5396

title: Optimize primitive SSZ collection iteration
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Essentially optimize `ValidatorStatsAltair.getValidatorStats()` method which currently takes around 250ms which means about 0.5 sec of CPU per slot which looks a bit expensive for metrics gathering. 

The major issue with byte list is that we are traversing the backing tree from the very root node every time a single byte is accessed. 

The main idea to optimize it is to introduce `CachingTreeAccessor` which is capable of caching some internal results of SszList element query to optimize the next list query. 

This PR:
- Adds `ByteListBenchmark`
- Adds basic `CachingTreeAccessor` implementation which just caches the latest accessed tree leaf so any following queries to elements packed in the same leaf would avoid tree search. Utilizes this class in `SszPrimitiveListImpl`
- Precompute `treeDepth` in `AbstractSszCollectionSchema`
- Precompute a couple of frequently used fields in `SszPrimitiveListImpl`
- Adds `SszPrimitiveSchema.createFromPackedNodeUnboxed()` to potentially avoid ssz boxing/unboxing when iterating primitive collections
- Change `SszPrimitiveListSchema` factory method to create specific `SszByteListSchema` class when the list element type is `Byte`

## Benchmarks

### Before changes:

{"@timestamp":"2022-06-03T17:03:12,158","level":"WARN","thread":"ExecutionLayerChannel-0","class":"ExecutionLayerManagerImpl","message":"Blinded block seems not been built via either builder or local engine. Trying to unblind it via builder endpoint anyway.","throwable":""}

full call sequence:

The [InterfaceWithOnlyStatics](http://errorprone.info/bugpattern/InterfaceWithOnlyStatics) check will identify cases where:

The docs provide a little more rationale:

I think this makes sense; I like this check.

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
We have already straightforward happy case in `BellatrixMergeTransitionAcceptanceTest`, this PR adds both possible optimistic sync cases.
Notes about this PR:
- `OptimisticSyncPostMergeAcceptanceTest` verifies accidentally syncing execution layer after the merge, `OptimisticSafeSlotsSyncPostMergeAcceptanceTest` verifies that we could pass even merge slot optimistically after `SAFE_SLOTS_TO_IMPORT_OPTIMISTICALLY` with optimistic import if execution layer is syncing
- I've removed `.withLogConsumer(frame -> LOG.debug(frame.getUtf8String().trim()))` line from `BesuNode` initialization, it duplicates log output, maybe I'm missing something, but there is one already in `Node`
- `getInternalIpAddress()` in `BesuNode` looks ugly, but I have not found any other way to get internal container IP, hosts are not allowed in `enode`
- `OptimisticSafeSlotsSyncPostMergeAcceptanceTest` needs 5 minutes between `StatusMessage` updates in order to resume sync, so this test takes a long time. Some way to disconnect teku nodes connection and then connect  them again could be an alternative, I have tried all ways to do this, but none is working

PS: Starting with draft to do several CI runs to clarify non-flaky

title: Fix payload re-execution
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
We have a bug in re-execution of payload, which prunes block with `FAILED_EXECUTION_PAYLOAD_EXECUTION` in the next slot instead of retrying to execute it in the next slots. Fixing it, test added.

Opened question, do we want to keep 2 slots retrying here?
My guess is that we will try to re-request these blocks via sync after StatusMessage exchange, which is often with, say, 30 peers connected. But it's not often on non-mainnet cases. With one peer connected we will wait for 5 minutes. Same time if it's bad payload which is killing EL, we don't want to continue retrying for a long.

title: Enable guava-beta-checker and fix findings
body:
## PR Description

[`guava-beta-checker`](https://github.com/google/guava-beta-checker) is Google's EP checker that identifies usage of beta Guava APIs. This checker is limited to the main source tree and doesn't produce warnings for test code. There weren't many findings.

> Such APIs should never be used in library code that other projects may depend on; using the Beta Checker can help library projects ensure that they don't use them.

When removing `Streams.zip` I was worried that the new implementation might be slower, so I added a benchmark function for the `BLS.aggregateVerify` method. In the process of adding this, I made a some changes to whole benchmark class; things could be simpler with a setup function.

#### Before

```
Benchmark                              (sigCnt)   Mode  Cnt    Score   Error  Units
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature         1  thrpt   10  926.271 ± 1.448  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature         2  thrpt   10  710.323 ± 1.462  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature         4  thrpt   10  481.074 ± 5.471  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature         8  thrpt   10  295.479 ± 2.709  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature        16  thrpt   10  163.657 ± 1.735  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature        32  thrpt   10   86.401 ± 0.738  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature        64  thrpt   10   44.565 ± 0.155  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature       128  thrpt   10   22.638 ± 0.093  ops/s
```

#### After

```
Benchmark                              (sigCnt)   Mode  Cnt    Score   Error  Units
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature         1  thrpt   10  927.673 ± 1.370  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature         2  thrpt   10  712.032 ± 0.952  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature         4  thrpt   10  485.891 ± 2.164  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature         8  thrpt   10  294.099 ± 1.980  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature        16  thrpt   10  162.698 ± 1.052  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature        32  thrpt   10   86.303 ± 0.847  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature        64  thrpt   10   44.676 ± 0.309  ops/s
BLSBenchmark.aggregateVerifySignature       128  thrpt   10   22.720 ± 0.018  ops/s
```

So things are pretty much the exact same. The new version might actually be a hair faster.

title: Use head state for more attestation validations
body:
## PR Description
Adjust `AttestationStateSelector` to allow using the head state for attestations that are from prior epoch. We can still correctly determine the committees needed to validate the attestation using the randao mix history even if the state is from a later epoch than the attestation.

The head state is guaranteed to be in memory, should give the best cache hit rate and any committees we have to calculate will be added to it's state and then copied when any blocks build on that state making it less likely we'll need to calculate them again.

title: Include SyncCommitteeMessage in Contribution only on received subnet
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
From the [spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/altair/validator.md#construct-sync-committee-contribution), what should we do to create Contribution:
> Collect all of the (valid) `sync_committee_messages: Set[SyncCommitteeMessage]` from the `sync_committee_{subnet_id}` gossip during the selected `slot` with an equivalent `beacon_block_root` to that of the aggregator.

This means that we should count only `SyncCommitteeMessage` as contribution if it was received on particular `subnet_id`, which sounds reasonable, as if one is listening to only one `subnet_id` and message should be distributed to several subnets, he will see it only if it appears on the `subnet_id` he is listening to.
Also this fix clears noisy exception, when we were trying to add same messages to contribution which were received on different subnets, which you could see in `SyncCommitteeGossipAcceptanceTest`. Test `SyncCommitteeMessagePoolTest.shouldCreateCorrespondingContributionsForEqualMessagesFromDifferentSubnets` clarifies that Exception is not thrown anymore.

title: [MEV-Boost\Builder] Unhide hidden params for mev-boost\builder
body:
CLI argument changes changes:

`--eb-endpoint` -> `--builder-endpoint`

`--Xvalidators-registration-default-enabled` -> `--validators-builder-registration-default-enabled`
`--Xvalidators-registration-timestamp-override` -> `--validators-builder-registration-timestamp-override`
`--Xvalidators-proposer-blinded-blocks-enabled` -> `--validators-proposer-blinded-blocks-enabled`

`--Xvalidators-registration-default-gas-limit` -> `--Xvalidators-builder-registration-default-gas-limit`
`--Xvalidators-registration-sending-batch-size` -> `--Xvalidators-builder-registration-sending-batch-size`

Relaxed proposerConfig json rule to allow per pubkey configuration to have empty\null `fee_recipient`.
`default_config` still requires it.

Extended `proposer-config` json referenced by the existing `--validators-proposer-config`

A draft note covering the usage of the changes: https://hackmd.io/@StefanBratanov/BkMlo1RO9 

closes #5396

### Documentation content

#### Intro
When [The Merge](https://docs.teku.consensys.net/en/latest/Concepts/Merge/) completes, Consensus Clients will be responsible for proposing blocks containing an Execution Payload (the Ethereum PoW Block in the context of PoS) obtained from their local Execution Clients via the `Engine API`.
Optionally, instead of building it locally, a Consensus Clients can configure an external “builder” to delegate the Execution Payload construction to.
This new interface is called `Builder API` and has been introduced to standardize the interaction with MEV providers, in the effort of making it easily accessible and  interchangeable.

Teku supports this interface and allows to configure the Beacon Node to a single `builder endpoint` that will be trusted for generating Execution Payload. In case of failures or non timely responses, Teku will use the payload produced by the local Execution Client (the one specified with `ee-endpoint`)

The most common deployment is to run an specialised software (i.e. [mev-boost](https://github.com/flashbots/mev-boost)) and configure it as the `builder endpoint`. This software will be responsible for requesting a payload proposal from several entities (called relays) and selecting the best bid.

__Important Note__
In deployment where Validator Client runs in a separate process and communicate with a Beacon Node via rest API, make sure that the Beacon Node supports the blinded block API.

#### new CLI args

`--builder-endpoint`
Optionally specify the Builder API to delegate the execution payload construction to. 
example(`--builder-endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:18550/`)


`--validators-builder-registration-default-enabled`
When enabled, all validators managed by the validator client will be configured to register to builder endpoint and will use it when proposing a block.

`--validators-builder-registration-timestamp-override`
This parameter allows to specify a timestamp that will be used when registering validators against the builder endpoint. It is only useful in deployments where validator keys are shared between multiple nodes (Obol, SSV or similar)

`--validators-proposer-blinded-blocks-enabled`
This enables blinded blocks flow, a prerequisite for the usage of the builder endpoint. When `--validators-builder-registration-default-enabled` is enabled this option will be enabled automatically. It requires explicit enablement when used in conjunction with `--validators-proposer-config`.


#### CLI args changes
`—validators-proposer-config` 
The specified config file now supports a new `builder` attribute that can be specified in the `default_config` as well as for each public keys.

in `builder`
- `enabled` indicates if the applicable validator key should register to and use the builder endpoint when proposing blocks.
- `gas_limit` is an optional parameter that allows to specify the preferred `gas_limit` that the builder should respect. When not specified the default value `30000000` will be used.

`fee_recipient` attribute becomes optional in a public key config, but remains mandatory in the `default_config`

```jsonc
{
  "proposer_config": {
    "0xa057816155ad77931185101128655c0191bd0214c201ca48ed887f6c4c6adf334070efcd75140eada5ac83a92506dd7a": {
      "fee_recipient": "0x50155530FCE8a85ec7055A5F8b2bE214B3DaeFd3", //optional
      "builder": { //optional
        "enabled": true, //mandatory
        "gas_limit": "12345654321" //optional
      }
    }
  },
  "default_config": {
    "fee_recipient": "0x6e35733c5af9B61374A128e6F85f553aF09ff89A", //mandatory
    "builder": { //optional
      "enabled": false, //mandatory
       "gas_limit": "12345654321" //optional
    }
  }
}
```

title: Optimize `TransitionCaches.committeeShuffle` cache utilization
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

When running Teku with high peers load (around 500-600 connected peers), noticed that `MiscHelpers.shuffleList` takes about 6%  of CPU. Turned out that `MiscHelpers.shuffleList` could be executed up to ~20 times per epoch (when expected just once)

There are 2 issues with the `TransitionCaches.committeeShuffle`:
1. Thread racing: when a number of attestations arrives simultaneously on several network threads the attestation handler  requests corresponding committee in parallel for attestations validation. Since the `LRUCache` is not synchronized (only the underlying `Map` is synchronized) the missed cache entry is calculated on several threads simultaneously. 
2. Too small cache size (2 entries): prior to epoch `N` `EpochCachePrimer` precalculates shufflings for epochs `N` and `N+1`, after that processing older attestations requires back shuffling for the epoch `N-1`. The shuffling for the epoch `N` is thus evicted and then needed to be recalculated again. 
Not 100% sure but it seems sometimes even shuffling for `N-2` is requested for ancient attestatations come with last block in the epoch `N-1`

Solution: 
1. Synchronize `LRUCache` while using non-synchronized underlying map. The synchronization performance impact should be 0
2. Increase `committeeShuffle` cache size from 2 to 4. The memory consumption is expected to increase by ~3Mb per cross-epoch fork (just 3Mb when no forks)

title: Batch vote update storage
body:
## PR Description
Implements batching when storing vote updates. We can get a lot of vote updates in a short period when processing individual attestations and it's significantly more efficient to write them to the database in a single transaction rather than separate transactions for each update.

The batching also ensures that the vote update queue is never filled which would otherwise cause back pressure to block the fork choice thread. Since vote updates are keyed by validator index, the maximum batch size is limited by the total number of active validators (which we already store in a single batch when applying vote changes to protoarray).

Also worth noting that it's not an issue if the last batch isn't written as we regenerate the protoarray based on the stored votes so we just have slightly less information when finding the initial chain head, but will quickly augment that with updated attestations via gossip and importing blocks.

```
VoteUpdateChannelBenchmark.storeVotesDirect   thrpt   10  0.049 ± 0.002  ops/s
VoteUpdateChannelBenchmark.storeVotesBatched  thrpt   10  6.180 ± 0.373  ops/s
```

Also fixes an issue in protoarray where only the justified and finalized epoch was stored instead of the full checkpoint - fixing that gets the last fork choice reference test passing which involves an exceptionally unlikely corner case. Nice to have it working though.

title: Improve execution payload retrying
body:
## PR Description
Replaces `ReexecutingExecutionPayloadBlockManager` with `FailedExecutionPool`. This simplifies the design a bit by using delegation instead of inheritance but also changes the algorithm for retrying:

 * Delay between retries now uses exponential back-off up to a maximum of 30 seconds
 * Only a single block is re-executed at a time instead of all pending blocks
 * The same block is retried on timeout (assuming the EL will complete execution of that payload even though the call timed out and then be able respond from a cached result)
 * A different block is retried on error or syncing to give the best chance of finding a fork we can continue to follow and not get stuck on a side-fork that doesn't have EL data available or that the EL is consistently hitting an error when importing

## Fixed Issue(s)

title: Failover for BN Event Stream from VC
body:
## PR Description

- Move `RemoteValidatorApiChannel` to the remote module and change the endpoint return type to be `HttpUrl`
- Change `EventSourceBeaconChainEventAdapter` to failover with the help of `getSyncingStatus` method
- Removed authentication, since an Auth interceptor will already be configured in the `OkHttpClient`

#### Test Scenarios

##### 1 VC and 2 Beacon Nodes

- Stop primary BN -> VC failovers to the other BN if the other BN is synced, otherwise it keep retrying against the primary BN
- Start primary BN -> VC goes back to the primary BN after sync is complete
- Stop both BN when current event stream BN is the primary one -> VC continues to fail and retries against the primary BN, while at the same time tries to connect to the any of the failover BN
- Stop both BN when current event stream BN is the failover one -> VC continues to fail and retries against the failover BN, while at the same time tries to connect to the primary BN

##### 1 VC and 3 Beacon Nodes
 - Stop primary BN -> VC failovers to the first BN which succeeds a syncing status check
 - Stop one of the failover BN -> VC failovers to the last remaining BN if syncing status check succeeds, otherwise it keeps retrying to connect to the current failover, while also trying to connect to the primary BN

title: Fix incorrect error logged when a newly imported block has an invalid payload
body:
## PR Description
When a block with an invalid payload was imported while the EL was in sync, Teku failed to find the latestValidHash because it wasn't checking the direct parent in this case (the code was originally only dealing with blocks that were imported optimistically and then later found to be invalid).

Teku's behaviour was correct (and there was even a test for it) but in incorrectly logged:

```
2022-07-21 10:53:00.508 ERROR - Could not find latest valid execution payload hash (0xfa87aa1b3ee36c763fb5b083aa3fed49fd037371ffc4949b03f894fcf5c3c099) in the non-finalized chain. Optimistic sync may have finalized an invalid transition block.
```

Now it does not.
