title: Detect ee-endpoint timeouts correctly
body:
## PR Description
Detect correct exception for timeouts when using the execution engine api.  The exception differs because the engine API is the only place we add an overall request timeout to the OkHttpClient configuration.  So when using `--eth1-endpoint` we get a `SocketTimeoutException` if response takes too long from the HTTP level, but the `--ee-endpoint` configures time outs and so triggers an `InterruptedIOException` when the socket is closed by the timeout.

This was causing extra noise in the logs but also the request for deposit logs wasn't being adjusted to reduce the range, which generally meant retrying it led to another timeout until eventually the disk cache was warmed up enough to get the response in time.

title: Remain in optimistic mode if there is no viable head
body:
## PR Description
During optimistic sync it is possible to import blocks that include enough attestations to update the justified checkpoint, but then discover the blocks including those attestations were invalid. This potentially makes the valid chain non-viable because it doesn't (yet) include enough attestations to reach that same justified checkpoint. Note that in this case the justified checkpoint itself is valid and eventually the attestations required to justify will be included in a valid chain.

Until that point though, our node should remain in optimistic mode so that it doesn't create attestations with the source of the updated justified checkpoint which may lead to later being unable to attest without creating a surround vote.

See https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2955 for more details.

title: Perform database updates asynchronously
body:
## PR Description
Applies transactions to the in-memory store immediately, allowing the actual database update to be performed asynchronously. Toggled off by default - lots more testing needed and double check for any unexpected threading implications.

Will also need to handle the case where new block is stored and quickly dropped from in-memory store, then attempts to be loaded from disk again before the database write has happened. Currently updates are on a different channel to requests so a race condition exists where the read could be attempted before the write completes.  One mitigating factor here though is that the database write will hold a hard reference to the data being stored which would prevent it being GC'd and thus it wouldn't be dropped from the in-memory store.  The exception there is when a transaction updates the finalized checkpoints - the hot blocks would be immediately removed from the in-memory store but not yet available from the database.

Simplest solution is to add additional storage for blocks and states in Store using hard references. Any blocks or states sent to the database to be stored are added to those maps as part of updating the in-memory store, then remove once the database update completes. May need to tweak `CombinedChainDataClient` to be able to deal with blocks before the finalized checkpoint possibly only being available from the in-memory store. In most cases it already tries the in-memory store first anyway to avoid race conditions with the finalized checkpoint updating.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#1934

title: Avoid finding min genesis PoW block when genesis state already known
body:
## PR Description

Skip finding the PoW block that first satisfies the minimum genesis time condition when we already have an anchor state.

The min genesis time block is only required as part of the process to generate genesis so if we already have a BeaconState to start from, we don't need to generate the genesis state and thus don't need to find this block.

This improves compatibility with ELs (particularly Nethermind) that may not download all historic blocks or may backfill them after eth_syncing reports the node is in sync.


## Fixed Issue(s)
#6059

body:
## PR Description
It may not have been possible to check the gossip validation rules for an aggregate because of a missing block or the aggregate being from the future. To ensure we don't send invalid gossip, ensure gossip validation is completed before sending the attestation to the network layer if it has been deferred. title: Make it possible to disable BLS verification for everything except Deposits
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

When doing experiments it is sometimes desirable to disable BLS verification globally for performance reasons. However verifying Deposit signature is kind of special case: it is legal for a valid block to contain Deposit with invalid signature. Not being able to handle invalid deposit signature leads to consensus break. 

This PR is still a bit hacky way to handle this: replace `AbstractBlockProcessor.blsVerifyDeposit` static flag with `BLSSignatureVerifier` reference to be able to set the verifier to the working instance even if the BLS verification is globally disabled with `BLSConstants.disableBLSVerification()`. 

BTW this change reminded me that there is still pending BLS refactoring to make BLS code cleaner (also includes this issue #2716). Will try to address this in a separate PR later

title: Verify operation signatures when building blocks
body:
## PR Description
Explicitly verify operation signatures when selecting operations to include in blocks. Simpler and safer than checking the fork indirectly.

Change the fork we use when validating gossip to always use the chain head fork rather than the fork that would be in place at the slot the message is for. This aligns with the behaviour of others clients better and also means we're only accepting gossip that we could then include in the next block.  Potentially some gossip might be rejected that could have been included later after a hard fork activates but that's a pretty rare occurrence.

Reference tests for exits and slashing operations have been updated to not only check the block processing, but also confirm that the block creation filters accept or reject the operations correctly based on their validity.

To ensure we don't keep revalidating the signature of an operation that can no longer be included forever, operations are removed from the pool if they fail validation when creating a block.

title: Improve peer search-connect task on startup
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
The issue is well understandable from these logs:
1st attempt, in milk
```
2022-08-27 17:04:15.403+04:00 | nioEventLoopGroup-2-1 | INFO  | teku-status-log | Listening for connections on: /ip4/127.0.1.1/tcp/9000/p2p/16Uiu2HAkvKzJGsWAgqUEsbJf1botdLqxPzJbX8Bx5B2iBCf1MpuJ
2022-08-27 17:04:15.428+04:00 | nioEventLoopGroup-4-1 | INFO  | ConnectionManager | connectToBestPeers: additionalPeersToConsider of size 0
2022-08-27 17:04:15.435+04:00 | nioEventLoopGroup-4-1 | INFO  | Eth2PeerSelectionStrategy | selectPeersToConnect:tech.pegasys.teku.networking.p2p.libp2p.LibP2PNetwork@1603e783, with 0 size input
```
2nd, immediately after the first, in milk too
```
2022-08-27 17:04:15.436+04:00 | discovery-tasks-1 | INFO  | ConnectionManager | connectToBestPeers: additionalPeersToConsider of size 0
2022-08-27 17:04:15.438+04:00 | discovery-tasks-1 | INFO  | Eth2PeerSelectionStrategy | selectPeersToConnect:tech.pegasys.teku.networking.p2p.libp2p.LibP2PNetwork@1603e783, with 0 size input
```
3rd, +43 seconds, +36 candidates
```
2022-08-27 17:04:58.100+04:00 | discovery-expiration-0 | INFO  | ConnectionManager | connectToBestPeers: additionalPeersToConsider of size 0
2022-08-27 17:04:58.114+04:00 | discovery-expiration-0 | INFO  | Eth2PeerSelectionStrategy | selectPeersToConnect:tech.pegasys.teku.networking.p2p.libp2p.LibP2PNetwork@1603e783, with 36 size input
```

4th, +27 seconds + 14 candidates
```
2022-08-27 17:05:25.618+04:00 | discovery-expiration-0 | INFO  | ConnectionManager | connectToBestPeers: additionalPeersToConsider of size 0
2022-08-27 17:05:25.626+04:00 | discovery-expiration-0 | INFO  | Eth2PeerSelectionStrategy | selectPeersToConnect:tech.pegasys.teku.networking.p2p.libp2p.LibP2PNetwork@1603e783, with 50 size input
```

What's wrong with it:
- we don't have any peers from discovery on the 1st peer search-connect attempt in tthe `ConnectionManager`
- 2nd attempt goes in a few millis after the 1st, looks like a bug
- 3rd attempt is in 30 seconds, finally we are doing something

As a result, we almost always don't have any peers for the first 30 seconds after startup. It's 2.5 slots on Mainnet, which could be critical for real peers on any restart, as we couldn't gossip anything during this. Plus we are failing Hive tests due to these skipped blocks. I'm trying to solve it.

At first I did a code with (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 30, 30, ...) delays of search, but it looked complicated. As discovery call always took some unpredictable time, I think it's not critical to have valuable delay there, just some 1-second delays between discovery calls is ok, just not to throw out whole load immediately by error. So I did it with  (1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 30, 30, ...) delays and removed 2nd attempt, which looked definitely buggy.
Now the same startup looks like this. Please note: we are not getting more peers, but we have some peers earlier than before, it's a goal.
1st attempt

title: Return unmodifiable view for private mutable fields
body:
## PR Description

Sorry, this PR touches a lot of different files. The changes are pretty minor though, hope that makes it okay.

In the spirit of defensive programming, when a public method returns a private field that is mutable (`List`, `Set`, `Map`, etc.), I think we should return an unmodifiable view of that field. My intention is to help prevent the modification of private variables outside of the class. There were a couple instances of this happening in some tests. For example:

```java
storageSystem.chainHeadChannel().getHeadEvents().clear();
```

`getHeadEvents` returns a reference to a private field. To fix this, I created a new method, `clearHeadEvents` with the `@VisibleForTesting` decorator, that clears the clears the events internally.

I chose to use `Collections.unmodifiable*` instead of using immutable objects because immutable objects are a lot slower. The unmodifiable view just ["replaces" the modification methods with `UnsupportedOperationException`](https://stackoverflow.com/a/6604553), therefore the performance penalty will be very minor, if anything. There were two places that I decided to create unmodifiable copies; because the field was a list of lists or list of maps. It would have been possible to modify the entries.

These were identified with a pretty simple error-prone check that I just made:
 * https://github.com/ConsenSys/errorprone-checks/pull/10

## Documentation

title: VC connect to failover event stream if BN is not synced
body:
## PR Description

- Connect to a failover event stream in case `/eth/v1/node/syncing` returns an error or shows that the node is not synced (which is the case if the EL goes down post merge)

The flow is as below:

- VC connects to the primary Beacon Node event stream
- Every 12 seconds (configurable) there is a task, which checks the syncing status of the primary Beacon Node:
- If the node is not synced or there is an error, the VC will try to connect to a failover Beacon Node event stream if failovers are configured
- In case the event stream has already failed over and the syncing status of the primary Beacon Node is back to normal, then a reconnection to the primary Beacon Node event stream will be attempted.

In case of event stream connection errors, the VC will try connecting to a failover as well. (this was the functionality before)


## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #6142

title: Handle known getLogs errors
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
As part of debugging my validator setup, I encountered an [issue along at least a few others](https://github.com/hyperledger/besu/issues/4293) where teku is continually querying besu for a 10k range of deposit logs, causing timeouts.  The fix in https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/pull/6061 does not seem to have actually fixed this issue.  I believe the root cause is that teku is no longer creating a `FallbackAwareEth1Provider` [when PowchainConfiguration is not enabled](https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/feb46ef53a8c8519edde37fbe8bd67d803bf9d9a/services/powchain/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/services/powchain/PowchainService.java#L84). This means no one is throwing `Eth1RequestException` anymore, which is what `DepositFetcher` is using for the auto-adjusting the range.  Meaning the range isn't being auto-adjusted.

The workaround is to change the config so the max range is 1000 (or less), in which besu responds in less than 8s, and all is good.

This is a hacky PR and there is likely a cleaner way to solve this, but I just wanted to expose the problem and a working solution.

title: Preserve ordering of updates and queries when async IO is enabled
body:
## PR Description
Moves storage updates and queries to use the same event channel when async IO is enabled. This ensures that any query sent to the channel after an update only begins executing after the update completes. To avoid updates being delayed by queries, the queries are actually executed on a separate async runner. This means that queries may be delayed by updates but not the other way around. It avoids the need to try and buffer content to deal with updates being asynchronous and finalized data being unavailable until the update completes.

Separate channels are still used when async IO is disabled so there's no impact to current behaviour by default.

## Fixed Issue(s)
#6194

title: Prevent sentry node config being used with beacon-node-api-endpoint
body:
When using sentry nodes, the `duties_provider` node should be used as the "main" beacon node API endpoint. One example of this is when the VC starts up and downloads the spec from the BN.

This change creates the following rules:
1. If `--Xsentry-config-file` AND `--beacon-node-api-endpoint` are not set, we use the default beacon node api endpoint (defined on `ValidatorConfig.DEFAULT_BEACON_NODE_API_ENDPOINTS`).
2. If `--Xsentry-config-file` AND `--beacon-node-api-endpoint` are set, the node fails starting and gives a useful error message.
3. When only `--Xsentry-config-file` is set, the node will use the endpoint for the `duties_provider` (as defined in the sentry config file) as the beacon node api endpoint.

title: Add dedicated lock to votes fields in `Store`
body:
`Store` is updated via `StoreTransaction` and `StoreVoteUpdater`. There is no intersection between the two: they update different fields in the store and they don't relay on the others data to compute the update.

Before this PR, Store locking was done via only one lock, which means both updates systems where locking the entire store.

In particular, `StoreVoteUpdater` updates votes via `applyForkChoiceScoreChanges` which is computational intensive. It means that every time we were processing head and the entire Store were locked including timing getters (`getTimeMillis` and `getGenesisTime`) that are massively used (ie: `onTick`, processing data coming from gossip)


This PR introduces a lock dedicated to votes fields, so we will have two different locks representing the two way of updating the Store. They do not lock eachother out and more importantly the heavy `StoreVoteUpdater` will no longer lock timing getters. Timing getters are still locked by `StoreTransaction` which locks in `applyToStore` (which can be still heavy) and in `putBlock` used to cache blocks.


related to #6016

title: Add Doppelganger Detection Service
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Add a doppelganger detection service which runs for at least 2 epochs and checks the validators indices each 12s.
In order to prevent the service from running indefinitely (If, for some reason, the service is unable to calculate the current epoch) a timeout is configured to stop the service and continue the VC tasks. In that case an error message is logged asking the user to check the previous logs and perform a new check.
The service is started after the validators keys have been loaded and before their duties are scheduled. 
If a doppelganger is detected the VC shuts down completely (This behaviour is still subject to change).
The check is performed at the VC startup. The validators loaded via the keymanager API are not handled yet. The same service can be reused for that use case.

title: Calculate sync committee duties and subscribe at most SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT ahead
body:
## PR Description
Calculate sync committee duties and subscribe at most SYNC_COMMITTEE_SUBNET_COUNT ahead not EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD ahead. Otherwise if the random number of epochs ahead we wind up picking is close to or equal to `EPOCHS_PER_SYNC_COMMITTEE_PERIOD` a reorg or late block may cause the sync committee duties to change.

Since sync committees are very stable, the REST API doesn't provide information on dependentRoots for sync committee duties and the validator client doesn't invalidate them. So in the case where we calculate duties too early and they are affected by a reorg, the validator client will fail to perform the correct duties leading to 0% inclusion rate.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #6212

title: Share type definitions between beacon node and validator api client
body:
## PR Description
First stab at sharing a JSON type definition and supporting data class between the beacon REST API and the validator api client.

Put it in the `:ethereum:json-types` module which seems pretty reasonable, though it could be a module level conceptually between ethereum and beacon/validator but apart from calling it "shared" or "common" I'm not really sure how to name it which suggests it may not need to exist.

The main complication here is that we don't have an internal data structure that can hold the data required for the get genesis API response so a custom wrapper class has to be defined. In this version the wrapper class is also in `:ethereum:json-types` and the type definition is a static field on that class. It works quite neatly for this case but there's a risk that the `:ethereum:json-types` module will get used as a dumping ground for types that are actually used internally and not just in the edges of the REST API and validator API client. There is some resistance to that problem though as `:ethereum:json-types` isn't a widely used dependency so when I initially tried to use the new class more widely I found a lot of compiler errors because it wasn't available. The temptation for overreach is strong however...

title: Use value comparison for validator sync committee indices
body:
## PR Description

So `validatorSyncCommitteeIndices` is an `IntSet` and should be compared with `Objects.equals`, right?

For a little backstory... last week, I noticed this fix:

```diff
-      if (withdrawalCredentials.slice(1)
-           != Hash.sha256(addressChange.getFromBlsPubkey().toBytesCompressed()).slice(1)) {
+       if (!withdrawalCredentials
+           .slice(1)
+           .equals(Hash.sha256(addressChange.getFromBlsPubkey().toBytesCompressed()).slice(1))) {
```

Link: https://github.com/consensys/teku/commit/1292eee92ce1b638ccbfe7b73e1068602a8cffb8#diff-87b45febe4cdb42f6503c505eb76fc3efe53b77caa61d7f8cf578968da70a63cL297-R293

It was a reference comparison when it should have been a value comparison. I would have expected [ErrorProne's ReferenceEquality](http://errorprone.info/bugpattern/ReferenceEquality) bug-pattern to spot this, but it doesn't seem to work the way I would expect. With that in mind, I wrote a new bug-pattern that works as I expect and it found this. I'll publish that soon, still needs some work.

title: `BEACON_BLOCK_AND_BLOBS_SIDECAR` gossip topic
body:
This is the first time we have to unsubscribe to a topic and subscribe to a new one.

`GossipForkSubscriptions` have been refactored to leverage class inheritance but also avoid most of the code duplication when the next fork stop using previously used topics.

Basically each fork exposes methods to add `GossipManager` for all topic that has been introduced by that fork. Than it's up to the forks to call the corresponding `add` method (or delegate to `super` if the fork is a superset of the previous).
To make sure that forks can reenable previously disabled topics, we have to make sure to pass all possible `OperationProcessor`s even if the current doesn't use it. It's the case of `blockProcessor` that may be re-enabled in future forks.

Add missing eip4844 and capella network configuration handling

fixes #6460

title: OperationValidators as a "bag" of validators
body:
## PR Description

This is just an idea of how we could simplify the work of adding a new operation and validation rules.

Basically, we have `OperationValidators` as a sort of bag of validators (those implementing `OperationStateTransitionValidator`). Whenever we want to validate an operation, we let OperationValidators decide what validator to use based on a mapping.

It also has the option to serve the actual validator object by type to support some edge cases.

Pros:
- Less plumbing when adding new operations.

Cons:
- Won't find out that we forgot to "link" a validator to an operation until actually trying to use it (runtime)

Further changes:
- We could introduce a Operation type and stop relying on SszContainer as the only acceptable type of operation.
- Potentially, we could float this change all the way to the Spec object so it only exposes a method like `Optional<OperationInvalidReason> validateOperation(final BeaconState state, final Operation operation)`.

title: Provide default values for all milestone config items
body:
## PR Description
Spec config handling has been adjusted to make sure that some value is always available for each known milestone. This is required for the REST API to access all the types used in the API definitions even if the milestone isn't actually enabled.

If a fork epoch is specified for the milestone, all values for that milestone must be explicitly specified. If no fork epoch is specified, default, roughly MainNet like values are provided for all values and the fork epoch is set to FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH. This ensures that if the milestone is enabled, the config is actually providing all required values.

When loading a remote config, the preset specified (if present, which it should always be) will now be loaded. Values from the remote config still override the preset values though.

This effectively means we're dropping support for network configs that use the old style of all constants in one file with no preset. It's been over a year and two hard forks (I think it even predates mainnet launch), I think that's ok.

title: Reduced time taken to compute expected proposers
body:
Tested on a mainnet state upgraded to capella, ran performance benchmarking on the first selection of state which will initially involve rejecting over 100k validators based on the fact they're not containing eth1 withdrawal credentials.

 - only compare credentials once
 - use single byte compare rather than slicing the string
 - don't touch the balance until the validator is known to have eth1 credentials, as that is surprisingly not a cheap operation. This could get flipped in time, but initially no validators are 0 balance and a lot of validators are not eth1 withdrawals.

 I shelved the benchmark, as it was based on a very specific mainnet state that would be sub-optimal to check in (very large)

title: Do one more duplication check before gossiping BlsToExecutionChange
body:
## PR Description

Noticed a small implementation difference between `SignedBlsToExecutionChangeValidator` and the other message validators. The others would perform a duplication check (for the same validator index) twice, but this one doesn't.

1. When receiving the message but before validation checks.
2. Right before returning `InternalValidationResult.ACCEPT`.

I believe the second one is important if we receive two `SignedBlsToExecutionChange` messages in close succession. If `validateForGossip` is called on both of them at almost the exact same time, the first duplication check most likely will not catch the duplication but the second duplication check would.

For example, `validateForGossip` for voluntary exits (scroll down to see all of it):

https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/22b93cb62e9326abd063d9531433ca138230e889/ethereum/statetransition/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/statetransition/validation/VoluntaryExitValidator.java#L50-L83

title: Use intValue method for uint64 to int conversions
body:
## PR Description

Replace `toIntExact(u64.longValue())` with `u64.intValue()`.

This is just a little nit I noticed when reading over these files. It helps readability and it will fail a bit faster if there's a problem. To be clear, there is nothing wrong with the current way things are done.

These aren't equivalent. The difference is that `intValue()` will throw an `ArithmeticException` if the value is negative, whereas `toIntExact` will not. None of these values should be negative, so I think that's better.

https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/b0b100f786b4f21a3591bfa5e8cfd0a16df722dd/infrastructure/unsigned/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/infrastructure/unsigned/UInt64.java#L466-L472

Also, I added `ArithmeticException` to the handled exceptions in `safelyProcess`. I feel like this should have been there before, but maybe I'm misunderstanding something and this doesn't matter. `toIntExact` throws that too.

title: Optimise finalized block pruning
body:
## PR Description
Adjusts how finalized blocks are pruned in the unblinded database format. We now scan over the full column of blockRoot->slot entries in each batch because while that reads more data, it avoids needing to recalculate the block root for each block to be deleted.  This makes the initial pruning significantly faster and after that the number of entires is limited so scanning the full column is straight forward.

It turns out to still be important to do the deletion in batches or LevelDB chokes on having that much very old data be deleted and the whole node fails to stay in sync for quite a long period while to sorts itself out. 

Switching a fully sync'd mainnet node from `prune` to `minimal` with this version took about 80 minutes or a stock EC2 non-attached storage (not particularly fast). While CPU usage was higher during that period there were no visible impacts on the node performance, block import time etc.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #6576

title: [EIP-4844] Blobs pruning
body:
Blocks and Blobs pruning work slightly different.

Blocks jobs run every 1h and always prune all "prunable" blocks (that's why the first time you switch MINIMAL on, takes a while to complete).

Blobs pruning are designed to run frequently and with an hard cap on the `BlobsSidecar`s that can be pruned. Currently configured to run every minute and prune maximum of 32 blobs. Under finalization, with mainnet config, we are supposed to create 5 BlobsSidecar each minute, so 32 is able to catch up relatively quickly.

The idea is to avoid those pruning jobs to overlap, so we limit the CPU\Disk pressure while node is doing its main work that's why I configured `storagePrunerAsyncRunner` to be single-threaded.

I also lowered down the thread priority.

I added the unconfirmed blobs pruning, which make sure that unconfirmed blobs (blobs its block has been received but never imported (remaining in FutureItems or in PendingPool)) are removed from DB once we finalize those slots. It shares the same prune limit (32)

Improved pruning by adding the ability to stream keys only from the KV store, so value doesn't need to be read\deserialized.

title: Use the local block if its reported value exceed the builder bid
body:
## PR Description
Adjusts the payload selection process to actually consider the block value reported by the local Engine API.  If the local block value is equal to or greater than the block builder's block, the local block is used.

One thing to note with this change is that we now need to wait for both the builder getHeader and the local getPayload call to return before deciding which block to sign, whereas previously we'd only wait for the local EL getPayload if we actually had to fall back to it. There is a 1 second timeout on the local EL getPayload call though so the delay is strictly limited (and that 1 second timeout is in parallel with the call to the builder getHeader).

Changes `BuilderBidValidationException` to be unchecked since the only place it was being caught was using `thenComposeChecked` which just bundles it into a failed future anyway so being checked didn't provide any value anyway.

title: [EIP-4844] Implement BlobsManager
body:
Introduces `BlobsSidecarManager` which is responsible for:
- storing unconfirmed _validated_ BlobsSidecars coming from gossip via `BlockManager`
- storing unconfirmed _non_validated_ BlobsSidecars coming from syncing flows via `BlockManager`
- creating a `blobsSidecarAvailabilityChecker` used in `ForkChoice`
- caching validated blobs to avoid revalidation in `ForkCoiche` for blocks\sidecar coming from gossip. 

Under kvstore and storage:
- rename kvstore method `removeUnconfirmedBlobsSidecar` -> `confirmBlobsSidecar`
- remove two unused blobs methods in `ChainStorage` and related classes
- fix SafeFuture handling on `ChainStorage` fro void returning blobs methods

In `StorageUpdate` and `StoreTransactionUpdates`:
- migrate prunedHotBlockRoots from a `Set<blockRoot>` to `Map<blockRoot,slot>` to support blobs cleanup when hot blocks are pruned

In `BlockValidator` (gossip):
- implements kzg commitments validation against blobsSidecar

In `BlockManager`:
- added `handleBlobs` method in the `doImportBlock` pipeline to store blobsSidecar via `BlobsSidecarManager`. This is done after block validity check (`handleInvalidBlock`) and after checking it is actually a new block not seen before (`handleKnownBlock`). Gossip validation result is considered to allow `BlobsSidecarManager` to know if the availability check needs to be done or not.
- it handles the blobs "discard" conditions when the corresponding block import results in a rejection of the block.


## Additional notes
- we could discard blobs sending them to the BlobsPruner which will gradually delete them from BD without queue the deletions in the storageUpdateChannel which can cause slowdown if many blobs are discarded in sequence (various pending blocks on a fork that turns out to be invalid). We could implement a BlobsDeletionChannel and block BlockPruner will consume it 

- having unconfirmed affects how we handle BlobsSidecarByRange rpc method:
  - for non finalized blobs, we should have a fast way to check if corresponding blocks are in recentChainData (via `containsBlock`)
  - for finalized we should always lookup on the unconfirmed column to filter them out (even in the case we have only one blob per slot, it might be still unconfirmed (a proposed invalid block))

- for the unconfirmed column I found an interesting approach that could make the confirmed-unconfirmed flag more efficient to store and update: https://groups.google.com/g/leveldb/c/qOMWvp7gyxg but would require some changes in our kvstore layer
  - the idea is to have a column key stored like <id, key, attributeId> where `id` is our current _prefix_ and `attributeId`s is a new _postfix_ byte from 0 to number of attributes defined + the actual value we store. The column will have multiple value serializers one for each attributeId. In our case we can have:
    - `<blobsSidecarId, <SlotAndBlockRoot>, 0>` -> `KvStoreSerializer<Boolean>` (confirmed flag)
    - `<blobsSidecarId, <SlotAndBlockRoot>, 1>` -> `KvStoreSerializer<Bytes>` (BlobsSidecar ssz data)
  so when streaming\lookingup blobs we can efficiently filter by unconfirmed flag without even try to deserialize the object if doesn't match the filter.
  This need further investigation for rocksDB.

title: Reference tests cleanup
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Reviewing state of reference tests:
- LightClient tests - we don't support it
- `PowBlock` and `Eth1Block` tests - we don't have these ssz structures and there is no sense to create them for reference tests only because tests will verify only those structures isolated
- `PendingAttestation` for milestones other than Phase0 - I've puzzled to find a way to initialize it for other milestones but had not find it. But structures are used only in Phase0 and there is no real value to run them during other milestones.
- `ssz_generic/uints` we skip uint32 and uint128 tests. Both are not supported by Teku sizes which are not used anywhere in spec. 
- `ssz_generic/basic_vector` we skip vectors with unsupported uint32 and uint128
- `fork/fork` tests - enabled for all milestones, made it in a way we'll get failed tests with new fork
- `transition/core` tests - enabled for all milestones, made it in a way we'll get failed tests with new fork, one test was failing because we didn't update EIP4844 upgrade with historical summaries recently introduced in Capella

No other tests are ignored

title: Allow other users to read the /opt/teku dir when using docker
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

The problem is that if we try to run the teku container with any other user that has a differen uid than `1000`, we won't be able to execute the teku binary due to the permissions of the working dir ( `/opt/teku` ) being too strict 0770. I'm changing the permissions to 0775 so that other users can also read the directory and execute the teku binary.

Example on how this fails currently with other users than 1000

```sh
$ docker pull consensys/teku 
$ docker run --rm -it --entrypoint ls --user=1000 consensys/teku 
LICENSE  bin  lib  licenses  teku.autocomplete.sh
$ docker run --rm -it --entrypoint ls --user=1003 consensys/teku 
ls: cannot open directory '.': Permission denied
```

## Fixed Issue(s)

title: Adds sync committee metrics
body:
`validator_scheduled_sync_committee_duties_current` This new metric is a visualisation to see how many validators are currently assigned to performing sync committee duties.

There were already metrics showing the attestation duties and block production duties, named in the same way, so this was just filling in the gap, although the other duties are accounted in a slightly different way, as they work differently.

This new metric is effectively the number of validators that you have that are in a sync committee currently.

Also added
`validator_current_sync_committee_last_epoch`, which will be the last epoch of the current sync committee.

This will allow validator maintainers to better determine if they are in a sync committee currently, and when the sync committee will be changing.

Fixes #6270

title: Update eventsource
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
The was a major update of the library, trying to applying it to our code. From [release notes](https://github.com/launchdarkly/okhttp-eventsource/releases/tag/4.0.0):
> This release revises the implementation of `EventSource` so that it does not create its own worker threads. The methods for starting and reading a stream now perform synchronous I/O, and the caller is responsible for choosing what thread to start the stream and read the stream on. This makes the core implementation simpler and more efficient, and reduces possibilities for deadlock. If you want to continue using the old asynchronous push model, see the `com.launchdarkly.eventsource.background` package.

So for this PR I've used `com.launchdarkly.eventsource.background` API which also changed but not too much. Do we need to use synchronous API with our own event thread instead? 
Also giving the sensitive part of code this update is touching, I'd better test it on our nodes before merging

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
It's follow-up for the #6242 
How do I see it:
- this one PR: we unhide the feature but left it toggled off to give some time to update it
- before the next release we toggle it to the `false` by default and add appropriate CHANGELOG entry 

```
Syntax: --p2p-discovery-site-local-addresses-enabled[=<BOOLEAN>]
Example: --p2p-discovery-site-local-addresses-enabled=true
Environment variable: P2P_DISCOVERY_SITE_LOCAL_ADDRESSES_ENABLED=true
Configuration file: p2p-discovery-site-local-addresses-enabled: true
```

Whether discovery accepts messages and peer records with site local (RFC1918) addresses. Default is `false`.

Normal Teku operation should not send traffic to local networks (RFC1918) addresses.
```
   The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) has reserved the
   following three blocks of the IP address space for private internets:

 	10.0.0.0    	-   10.255.255.255  (10/8 prefix)
 	172.16.0.0  	-   172.31.255.255  (172.16/12 prefix)
 	192.168.0.0 	-   192.168.255.255 (192.168/16 prefix)
```	 
For some reasons operators may need to enable discovery of local addresses, for example when you run multiple consensus layer nodes in one local network, these nodes are not discovered in public Internet and are advertised with local IPs. Such configurations are usual for test or private networks. When running in such configuration this flag should be toggled (set to true).

title: Add BlobSidecar getters in CombinedChainDataClient
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
There were 3 possible approaches to implement storage for BlobSidecars:
Using  `Slot+BlockRoot+BlobIndex` key, `BlockRoot+BlobIndex` key or `Slot+BlobIndex` key. Currently we have these type of queries:
 - A. By Slot range RPC, Slot query
 - B. By BlockIdentifiers RPC, BlockRoot + BlobIndex query 
 - C. Earliest available epoch query
 - D. By Slot for pruning, similar to `A`

`A` could be used both for recent missed slots and historical sync. `B` is used only for recent slots but we assume it could be changed in the future, because it's very useful to fill several small gaps in one query. `C` is used once per query along with `A`. `D` is happen once in epoch. We could get following breakdown of operation complexity by chosen key type:
  1. `Slot+BlockRoot+BlobIndex` key
  	A+D. For each slot query slot -> Block to get root and indexes
  	B. For each blobsidecar search for a block to get slot
  	C. First element
  2. `BlockRoot+BlobIndex` key
  	A+D. For each slot query slot -> Block to get root and indexes
  	B. No additional queries
  	C. Extra query for a block or we need to use DB variable with some in memory cache for it
  3. `Slot+BlobIndex` key
  	A. No additional queries
  	B. For each blobSidecar search for a block to get slot
  	C+D. First element

For current usage we assume getting a slot for `B` will be very fast as it's memory operation (for recent slots). Plus for `A` and `D` we could use slot order streaming. It makes `1` and `3` preferrable with not much difference between `1` and `3` when using DB streaming. For clarity we choose `Slot+BlockRoot+BlobIndex` key.

We cannot use DB stream in `BlobSidecarsByRangeMessageHandler` because of the application design and strict requirements for stream closing. Also we couldn't pass streams through async interfaces. There are 2 possible approaches to get this around:
  1. Stream keys and collect it before closing. Key weight should be about 16 (object header) + 24 (UInt64) + 48 (Bytes32) + 24 (UInt64) + 8 bytes list reference = 120 bytes per `SlotAndBlockRootAndBlobIndex`. So maximum 61440 bytes for 128 blocks with 4 blobSidecars in each. 16 peers with maximum possible queries will consume under 1Mb memory for it which sounds acceptable for me
  2. Something tricky like `getNextKeyAfter(V value)` will void opportunity of stream by calling for a lot times plus follows to the weird code.

So I've chosen the 1st

Confirmed/unconfirmed logic, `BlobSidecar` persistence and pruning is not covered by this PR.
Also I'm not sure on the placement of `SlotAndBlockRootAndBlobIndex`.

title: Introduces BlobSidecarPool with block-blobs tracking
body:
The basic idea is to have a pool of trackers for each `blockRoot` we see (coming from a block or from a sidecar)

- each tracker have the responsibility to signal when a block-blobs bundle is completed
- the pool is currently responsible of signal to fetchers (block and blobs) to retrieve missing content. This logic is triggered only when dealing with object related to current slot (following the head, content coming from gossip)

- the pool implements a fetch delay logic. There are three constants:
  - `TARGET_WAIT_MILLIS`: ideal delay before fetching (currently set to 1s)
  - `MIN_WAIT_MILLIS`: minimum delay before fetching (currently set to 0.5s). The rationale is that we don't want to issue fetches if we are most probably still receiving block and blobs.
  - `MAX_WAIT_RELATIVE_TO_ATT_DUE_MILLIS`: maximum "distance" from attestation due (4s) when we really want to have block and blobs to process (currently set to 1.5s). The rationale is that, if we are close to attestation due, even if we may still receive something from gossip, we are in rush and we can waste some bandwidth to have more chance to import before the 4s mark (and attest to correct head)

- currently if we try to fetch blobsidecars and we don't have the corresponding block yet, we try to fetch all possible sidecars (considering maxBlobsPerBlock). If we receive the block after fetch occurs, we drop the (eventually) non existing blobs.

fixes #6849

title: Unhide `--deposit-snapshot-enabled`
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Unhides  `--deposit-snapshot-enabled` options. There are some questions with no clear decisions
- We had `--Xdeposit-snapshot-enabled` in testing by some users. As I removed it, Teku will fail to start until flag is updated. If I leave it, we have it in help along with flag without `X`, which I dislike.
- Should we make it default to true immediately? Why not? Why yes? I'm not sure

Doc draft. Will be submitted after `default` decision:


    Syntax: --deposit-snapshot-enabled[=<BOOLEAN>]
    Example: --deposit-snapshot-enabled=false
    Environment variable: TEKU_DEPOSIT_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED=false
    Configuration file: deposit-snapshot-enabled: false

Use bundled deposit contract tree snapshot and persist tree after finalization.

Currently at sync Teku requests all deposit logs from the execution layer up to the head. Next, at each startup Teku loads all deposits from the disk and replays them to recreate the merkle tree. Both operations consumes peer resources and delays node availability on restart. This feature dramatically decreases the time of both operations by bundling deposit tree snapshots in Teku distribution for all major networks including testnets (Mainnet, Gnosis, Goerli, Sepolia) and persisting current tree after finalization. Instead of replaying thousands of deposits on startup, Teku will load bundled tree or a saved one, whichever is the latest.

Security considerations: if a malicious agent changes bundled tree, Teku will throw `InvalidDepositEventsException` on the next deposit received from Execution Layer and will be unable to follow up the chain, so you will not be able to propose with incorrect deposit tree snapshot. Overall, it means network couldn't be attacked with malicious bundle, the consequences will be inability to propose like with any other serious bug in proposal flow.

title: Process attestations when the state from their target block state is available in cache
body:
## PR Description
When selecting a state to use to process attestation gossip, check if the attestations `beaconBlockRoot` state is already available in the cache before deciding if it's worth regenerating a state. This allows us to process significantly more attestations without requiring additional state generations - particularly if attestations are received for blocks we just imported on a long fork.

Also potentially reduces the number of generations we'd do during periods of non-finality by better leveraging what we have in cache.

title: Embed blob sidecars directly under blob_sidecars property in BlockContents
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Remove redundant `blob_sidecars` property name in `BlockContents` container. This means removing the `BlobSidecars` container and its `BlobSidecarsSchema` (Same for the signed and the signed, blinded ones).
Blob sidecars should be represented as an array under the `blob_sidecars` property in `BlockContents`.
In the current implementation there is a redundant `blob_sidecars` property:
`BlockContents`:
```
{
	"beacon_block": {}
	"blob_sidecars": {
		"blob_sidecars": array of BlobSidecar
	}
}
```

These changes fixes it to become:

```
{
	"beacon_block": {}
	"blob_sidecars": array of BlobSidecar
}
```

These changes also fix `SignedBlockContents`, `BlindedBlockContents` and `SignedBlindedBlockContents`

[Spec reference here](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/302)

title: BlobSidecarsByRange send only canonical blobs
body:
This PR makes sure that BlobSidecarsByRange RPC responds only with blobsidecars belonging to canonical chain.

It is implemented with the following logic:

- Splits the range in two logical sub ranges of slots: finalized and non finalized.
  - For the finalized subrange, It assumes the storage is already pruned from non canonical blobs, so we keep them as they are.
  - For non-finalized subrange, it obtains the canonical  `Map<Slot,BlockRoot>` from combinedChainDataClient, and it filters out blobs that do not refer to any of those SlotAndBlockRoot.

fixes #7246

<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->

## PR Description
Draft.
I don't like inconsistency of networking constants among spec:
- Max gossip and max chunk constants are in main config
- Deneb networking constants are in main config
- Bellatrix max gossip and chunk constants are in spec (neither config nor presets)

In our code previously:
- Max gossip and max chunk constants - phase0 preset
- Bellatrix max gossip and max chunk - bellatrix preset

What I think it should be:
- either put all in config, so in spec we will need to include 2 Bellatrix gossip constants in config
- or keep base networking constants in base config, move deneb constants to deneb preset, add bellatrix gossip constants to bellatrix preset

I think ideologically it should be in each preset, but names not clashes and it will be simpler for us to load them all from the main config. In the code I've tried both usage when we need `specVersion` for epoch/milestone and when we could use base config with `getNetworkingConfig()` shortcut to see how it's simpler.

**UPDATE:** Questions are resolved with the following outcome:
- Bellatrix networking constants are abolished, based constants are aligned with its numbers. We will do the same (in separate PR)
- We put Deneb networking constants in main config like it's done in consensus specs

title: Use progressive balances during epoch transition
body:
Also cleaned up some of the processing logic, but only very small tweak.

Basically it's cheap to check if a delta is zero, and if it's zero there's no need to adjust balance. This will occur for every exited validator that has 0 balance, and any exited validator outside of any slashing period, so it's actually about 15% of the validator set, at which point it becomes quite worthwhile to check if the delta is zero, as we save a read+write to the balance set.

This is not a huge speed improvement, but it does round out the progressive balances change.

Fixes #6998

title: Increased the pending pool size for attestations
body:
This pool is used when an attestation is seen for a block we're not yet aware of.

The two main cases this is going to be useful is
 - when we're falling behind and listening to all subnets
 - if clients are attesting on receipt of block

 The pool size, worst case, would need to handle the number of attestations in a slot (all subnets would have to be enabled)

 With 32 slots, there's 32 segments of the validator count, so at 1 million validators, that'd be 31_250 attestations per slot.

 An upcoming testnet will be larger again, will have to re-evaluate if we're hitting the limit at that point, but we're currently hitting the 5k size of this pool on some nodes several times an hour.

 Having some head room on mainnet for a while should give us a good idea of sizing this cache going forward, and it may need to be periodically tweaked.

title: rate limit based on the served objects instead of the requested objects count
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Update objects requests rate limiting based on the served objects count instead of the requested objects count:
`BeaconBlockByRange`, `BeaconBlockByRoot`, `BlobSidecarsByRange` and `BlobSidecarsByRoot` are all rate limited based on the requested objects count (The rate limiter is triggered when the request is received). In most case the real served objects count is lower (For blocks request, some blocks could not be returned and BlobSidecars we estimate the requested objects count by assuming that every block will contains `MAX_BLOB_SIDECARS_BY_BLOCK` Blob Sidecars which is not always/rarely the case).
The proposed solution is to add an object count adjustment to the rate limiter:
- `popBlockRequests` and `popBlobSidecarsRequests` will update the rate limiter with the max estimated objects counts.
- `adjustBlockRequests` and `adjustBlobSidecarsRequests` will adjust the initially estimated objects count and replace it with the served objects count (only if the adjustment happens during the same rate limiting time window).
- `cancelBlockRequests` and `cancelBlobSidecarRequests` will reset the initially estimated objects if the request is cancelled for some reason (mainly errors when serving the requests)

 I decided to go this way to avoid possible breaking changes to people using https URLs relaying on default JVM trusted store. The benefit is also that, since it is a standard API, user doesn't need to specify the full URL.

title: Added epoch state cache configuration
body:
Now that attestations aren't being validated against states so often, we need a cache closer aligned to what we're doing when we need to regenerate - basically we want to avoid regeneration of state if at all possible.

One epoch transition the finalized and sometimes justified state get read, and were causing regenerations, so adding a cache to handle storing those, but leaving it size 0 by default for now.

The idea would be to have the current state cache reduced significantly in size, potentially to about half an epoch or so, and have an epoch cache with a maximum size over 2, and could probably be below 10 by default.

This would mean the vast majority of the time, no state regeneration is required, and our states in memory can drop to a much lower number than currently stored in memory (32 * 5 max by default currently).

Tested in minimal network, needs to be deployed to a more complex setup to see if it behaves well in a real environment.

title: Allow different kinds of validation when publishing blocks
body:
It is the easiest approach I come up with to extract the "consensus validation" stage from the block import process.

In summary:
- `ForkChoice.onBlock` now accepts an optional `SafeFuture` to be completed by the method when state transition and blobs availability check succede
- `BlockManager` implementing `BlockImportChannel` now expose the import method with an optional `BroadcastValidation` param. Based on the value, the import flow behaves so that the returned `SafeFuture` completes when the broadcast can be performed. If `empty` is passed, the `SafeFuture` will resolve when import is fully executed (same flow as today)
- `BlockValidator` (now `BlockGossipValidator`) responsible for performing gossip validation, now:
  - exposes the equivocation check, so that it can be done at the end of the consensus check, if required.
  - `validation` method now expect a `isLocal` parameter to know whenever the equivocation data should only be checked (`isLocal == true`, locally produced) or need to be updated as well (`isLocal == true`, block actually coming from a gossip)
- new `BlockValidator` uses `BlockGossipValidator` and consensus validation result to compose the validation flow.

What I don't like much:
- a safe future as parameter, that needs to be resolved by the method itself
alternatives: 
    - wrapping the return in a class that holds the two stages of resolution. But i feel like there is more impact in the whole code base. 
    - use a subscription pattern to subscribe to a consensus validation result even, but i think it makes the coordination of the flow more complex. 
    - pass a `Consumer` instead of a future, as a callback pattern. 

- New block import `FailureReason`s that are not relevant for the actual block import process. But having both consensus SafeFuture and full block import SafeFuture returning the same type makes the flow easier to handle.

needed for #7349

* The spec has introduced a new helper function `verify_blob_sidecar_signature`.

  * Swapped order of parameters to match spec too.

Reference to checks in the spec:

## PR Description
- I don't like `OwnedValidators.getActiveValidators()` name because it's misleading. I'd rename to exclude word active, but it will lead to changes in several classes, so I skipped it to omit unnecessary changes in this PR and could do a separate PR with this change.
- Cache looks like not an issue. We will not cache not yet active validator. For exited validator we will not receive any duty but once we try to renew registration, it will be filtered out and will not lead to sign attempt. Cache will not be pruned in this case but it doesn't look an issue too. As validator remains in owned, we will try to further attempts anyway.
- What I don't like is that we do everything on the 3rd slot, so if validator becomes active ongoing in this epoch and luckily become a proposer in first 3 slots, it will not use builder registration for it

title: EIP-4844 External Signer integration for blob sidecar and blinded blob sidecar
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->
## PR Description
External signer integration for offloading signing request for blob sidecar and blinded blob sidecar (EIP 4844)

## Summary of changes:
**`tech.pegasys.teku.validator.client.signer`**
- `ExternalSigner`: Implemented `signBlobSidecar` and `signBlindedBlobSidecar`. Both methods send `BlindedBlobSidecar` converted to json. The `BlobSidecar.getBlob().hashTreeRoot()` makes it compatible with
`BlindedBlobSidecar` for the purpose of calculating signature remotely. 
- `SignType`: Introduced `SignType.BLOB_SIDECAR`
- `ExternalSignerDenebIntegrationTest`: Integration test for above methods.

**`tech.pegasys.teku.api.schema`**
- `BlindedBlobSidecar`: To convert internal `BlobSidecar` and `BlindedBlobSidecar` to JSON. Used by `ExternalSigner`.
- `KZGProof`: Used in `BlindedBlobSidecar` class. 

**`tech.pegasys.teku.provider`**
- `JsonProvider` Register KZGProof serializer and deserializer i.e. `KZGProofSerializer` and `KZGProofDeserializer` that helps in de/serializing BlindedBlobSidecar.
 
The resultant JSON request would look like:

title: Decrease block pruning size
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
In case of changing storage mode or min epochs for block requests we get thousands of blocks to remove. Removal may freeze node for a minutes and after that DB compaction starts, which could freeze node even more. To avoid such situation we may want to prune old blocks without hurry, only 1 batch per run. Also added configuration option, so the value could be easily overriden.

Some concerns still on this:

0. Maybe I've over engineered it and we don't need boolean return, it will make all the things way simpler
1. Am I missing the case when it could be empty while finalized blocks are really stored? (see old code)
2. We are not pruning non-canonical blocks, should we?
3. Calculations:
  
  blobs: 48 every 1 minutes
  avg 3 in block => 30 epochs in hour, 3.2 times faster than arrival
  1 year of blobs pruned in 4 months
  
  blocks: 5000 every 15 minutes
  20000 in hour => 625 epochs in hour, 66.6 times faster than arrival
  1 year of blocks pruned in 5.5 days

5.5 days for a year of blocks when you change DB storage mode, for example, looks reliable, though we may consider to run in more often in smaller sets. You keep node performance, which could be production node with validators, not a big issue that disk space will be freed only after few days. We should prioritize node stability in this case.
Regarding the blobs, I understand the difference: most of the nodes will keep only required epochs of blobs, but I think we may need to increase this number.

title: Updated holesky forks and genesis time
body:
We were accepting the current genesis due to some fork checks being skipped during startup, because we detected pre-genesis. I've altered fork checking to always occur, which did mean a few more changes than just holesky configuration.

The upside is we can now configure default initial state to finalized, then genesis, and it'll warn and try the genesis state if the finalized fails, and it'll determine if the forks change (like on holesky) and error. example output:
```
13:56:52.665 INFO  - Loading initial state from https://checkpoint-sync.holesky.ethpandaops.io/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/finalized
13:56:53.006 WARN  - Failed to load initial state from https://checkpoint-sync.holesky.ethpandaops.io/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/finalized
13:56:53.006 INFO  - Loading initial state from https://checkpoint-sync.holesky.ethpandaops.io/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/genesis
13:57:11.233 INFO  - Loaded initial state at epoch 0 (state root = 0x706eeb43c9e44932b312cd26b8d35ef69725f117275ef3dcd67653625b519f16, block root = 0x00af3346d685d33731a476469262112fee02e82b05e60d83c577c649b33ad152, block slot = 0).
The fork from the intial-state (0:0x20017000) does not match the configured fork schedule (0:0x03017000).
Please check that network in configuration matches the loaded state.
```

We could still reference the genesis state from github, but it's not currently merged.

Partially addresses #7517

title: Fix `FAILED_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CHECK_INVALID` handling
body:
If block import fails with `FAILED_DATA_AVAILABILITY_CHECK_INVALID` we mark block as invalid. This is wrong because the block itself isn't invalid. What is invalid is the block's commitments WRT blobs we have received so far.
So if the majority of the network saw the correct blobs and imported the block, then the next proposer will build on top of it. In this case we must be able to recover and redownload block\blobs by root.

We could potentially cache the block somewhere and do a blobSidecar cleanup session (running kzg validation one by one to find out which one is invalid and drop it). So we could avoid re-downloading everything, but it means we should:
1- "cache" the entire block in the `blobSidecarPool` (ATM the tracker stores only the body)
2- implement the blobSidecar cleanup
3- whenever we try to retrieve a block by root via RPC we should check it if it is already in the `blobSidecarPool`, if yes just keep it from there.

This PR just implement the easy way.

title: Updated ProtoArray#nodeLeadsToViableHead to check own node viability before best descendant
body:
## PR Description

When checking the viability of a node, we consider a node to be viable if either itself or its best descendant is viable. The current implementation checks the viability of the best descendant before checking the viability of the current node.

Part of the viability check involves traversing the array, following the node's ancestry (see ProtoArray#hasAncestorAtSlot).

When we need to update descendants, we visit every node and check its viability. Consider a scenario of long non-finality and no forks, where we have n nodes, where n[i].parent = n[i-1]. When we are checking the viability of node n[i] (where i is the index of the node and 0 <= i < n), we are going to traverse the array for its best descendant which is always going to be n[n-1] (the worst case traversing the whole array).

With this change, in those scenarios, we are moving from the worst case towards the best case as we visit the nodes. This change improves the time it takes to perform the operations.

## Fixed Issue(s)
related to #7570

title: Implemented isFinalizedRootOrDescendant
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

When checking if a node is viable as head (`ProtoArray#nodeIsViableForHead`), we were navigating backwards the nodes to check if the node was a descendant of a finalized checkpoint.

This change adds a sort of "shortcut" (ProtoArray#isFinalizedRootOrDescendant) to this check, by using the head-candidate node's `BlockCheckpoints`, checking if either of these is true:
- Does the node's finalized epoch and finalized root match the ProtoArray view of the finalized epoch and root?
- Does the node's justified epoch and justified root match the ProtoArray view of the finalized epoch and root?
- Does the node's unrealized finalized epoch and finalized root match the ProtoArray view of the finalized epoch and root?
- Does the node's unrealized justified epoch and finalized root match the ProtoArray view of finalized epoch and root?

If none of these are true, we fall back into the old traverse of the hierarchy until we find the finalized checkpoint for that head candidate.

## Fixed Issue(s)
related to #7570

title: Add block arrival time in metrics at the earliest possible point
body:
## PR Description There are 2 options how we could get arrival block time earlier than in current `master` branch flow (https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/ethereum/statetransition/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/statetransition/block/BlockManager.java#L150-L158): 1. Less invasive, without changes in libp2p library, the way it's implemented in the current PR. We have early entrypoint for all messages, message factory, where we have full control using libp2p API https://github.com/ConsenSys/teku/blob/f31b239f7788f07d8e9c2b6e7544c5e16b01a259/networking/p2p/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/networking/p2p/libp2p/gossip/LibP2PGossipNetworkBuilder.java#L107. It's called very early in libp2p https://github.com/libp2p/jvm-libp2p/blob/1a5f08d0a05aca80dcef8be5708aebf7b77d8186/libp2p/src/main/kotlin/io/libp2p/pubsub/AbstractRouter.kt#L161-L191 and it's less complicated to implement than the other option. We return `PreparedPubsubMessage` from it which is pretty easy to extend, what I did, putting time there. And here appears the first issue with such improvement: message type is more or less abstract on this stage and we cannot use specific type performance meter there. So the only way I could go is to use the same TimeProvider for time data, which we use in performance metrics. Yet, from the implementation standpoint it's not clear that we have the same time source in this measurement.
The result of measurement of delay between previously measured arrival point, which I renamed to `pre_validate` (not a final name) goes below: ``` Total late block arrivals for ~2 days: ~300 blocks of 15,000 arrival to pre_validate (min, max, avg): 1ms, 101ms, 3.74ms (98% < 10ms) ``` 2. Another way is to extend libp2p, which is not that simple from many points of view: - Libp2p message factory interface is `(Rpc.Message) -> PubsubMessage` where the input is pubsub message type, which we shouldn't extend. As libp2p API is public and is used not only by the Teku, we should not break the API, instead we could introduce something like Experimental Message Factory, do a check in libp2p builder if it's provided and use it in Teku instead of the base factory. - Between message factory and message arrival there are only minor computations. If you look at the pipeline https://github.com/libp2p/jvm-libp2p/blob/1a5f08d0a05aca80dcef8be5708aebf7b77d8186/libp2p/src/main/kotlin/io/libp2p/pubsub/AbstractRouter.kt#L116-L123 (we need only decoders from it for inbound messages) there is `LimitedProtobufVarint32FrameDecoder` which just detects which multiplexer frames belongs to one message and pushes them next. It's safe to say it adds 0ms after last frame. After it we have `ProtobufDecoder` which decodes raw bytes data to actual message, but it's a pretty optimized piece of software and protobuf decoding is fast. So it adds few milliseconds between message factory and last frame of the message. There is little value to count this time in consideration of complexity. Alternatively we could extend wrapper for every frame of the message with it's own timestamp and start measurement from the first frame complete arrival. This way we will measure delay based on badndwidth throughput, it will not measure anything on computation side. - If we do anything with time we should have the same time source as we use in Teku, which should be a pain to implement. Alternatively we could track some delta only inside libp2p with it's own time source and provide only delta which we could safely call something like `transfer_time` because, there is only minor computation before API configured message factory, so it will actually measure message transfer time. - It will still require piece of software (1) to extract this data in experimental message factory and pass in the Teku ## Fixed Issue(s) Fixes #7536 ## Documentation - [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required. ## Changelog - [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

title: Added checkpoint-sync-url CLI option
body:
This PR is introducing the `--checkpoint-sync-url` CLI option. Teku already supports checkpoint sync using `--initial-state` option, but we wanted to be more explicit on the fact that we support checkpoint sync.

The behaviour of using `checkpoint-sync-url` is similar to using `--initial-state` ([docs](https://docs.teku.consensys.net/reference/cli#initial-state)) and `--genesis-state`([docs](https://docs.teku.consensys.net/reference/cli#genesis-state)) together. First, Teku will try to load the latest finalized checkpoint from the beacon node. If it fails, Teku will then try to load the genesis from the beacon node.

Starting a sync from genesis is something we want to discourage and we are exploring the option of not doing it by default (it would require an override flag to allow this behaviour).

fixes #7664

title: teku-5930 Make it the default to not sync from Genesis
body:
## PR Description

One common issue when starting a new node is start synchronizing from genesis, instead of using checkpoint sync. Not only this takes longer to sync, but is riskier (subject to long-range attacks).

By default, Teku won't allow users to sync from an epoch that is too old (out of the weak subjectivity period). This includes trying to sync from genesis on mainnet.

For most users, the best option to start a new node is to use [`--checkpoint-sync-url`](https://docs.teku.consensys.net/development/get-started/checkpoint-start) pointing to a checkpoint sync endpoint in sync with the network. This is going to start their node from the latest finalized checkpoint.

This PR added a CLI option `--ignore-weak-subjectivity-period-enabled` to allow users to opt-out of this behaviour.


## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #5930

title: Don't use FailoverValidatorApiHandler if no failovers configured
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Essentially, if no failovers configured, just use the primary `ValidatorApiChannel` instead of using the `FailoverValidatorApiHandler`.

Also another major change in this PR is removing metrics from the `FailoverValidatorApiHandler` and moving them to the new `RemoteMetricRecordingValidatorApiChannel` which will be attached to every remote channel. This leaves the `FailoverValidatorApiHandler` cleaner and not concerned with metrics.

title: Fix encoding of comma character in query parameters
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

The Teku VC encodes the comma `,` character in its request to the `/validators` endpoint, resulting in a request like this:

`GET /eth/v1/beacon/states/head/validators?id=0x978e96b6b6b474f3f91b705a311906b14a5e2893d15e01f5a0ff210393ace5e0abc8488e844dab00f430364ba4c19b1a%2C0x99f013b0314981b0083e494bdd2989304f9fc9dfd2b0c23b40429d817b02acc78f0b4328e45e745a5c6cc48e8f0e9930 HTTP/1.1`

This is incompatible with Lodestar's BN, which handles it as one long ID containing the `%2C` string, resulting in an empty array of statuses being returned. This in turn results in the Teku VC failing to get the status for its validators (and subsequently not performing validator duties for them):

```
19:14:03.083 WARN  - Unable to retrieve status for validator 978e96b.
19:14:03.083 WARN  - Unable to retrieve status for validator 99f013b.
```

This was discussed in https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/issues/5403 . The conclusion there was the comma character should not be encoded in this case.

The Teku BN API can handle both cases, regardless of whether the comma character is encoded or not, so this change is completely backwards compatible.

Looking forward to hear your thoughts on this.

## Fixed Issue(s)

I have not found an issue for this in this repository.

title: Allow deferred blinded-unblinded schema selection in block body builder
body:
With this PR `BeaconBlockBodyBuilder` doesn't need to be set for blinded or unblinded flow in advance. It is created with both schemas and behaviour changes based on the payload is provided. In `build()` If header has been provided, it will go for blinded block body. If full payload has been provided, unblinded block is created. So it won't expose `isBlinded` method any more.

The blinded-unblinded `BeaconBlock` will be chosen based on the "blindess" of the `BeaconBlockBody`

This PR do not change the fact that we currently return blinded by default. It only moves where the decision is made so that we will be dynamically choose based on the flow on a following up PR. 

fixes #7835

title: Fix rest api bind error message
body:
## PR Description

When Javalin can't bind to a port that is already in use. The Javalin `app` object will not contain a port, it will have it as -1.
Because of this, the error message that we are getting looks like:

```
TCP Port -1 is already in use. You may need to stop another process or change the HTTP port for this process.
```

To fix this, we can use Javalin's `JavalinBindException` message that already has the port. It looks like: 

```
Port already in use. Make sure no other process is using port 5000 and try again.
```

This PR is part 1 of the deposit snapshots changes support for checkpoint sync url.

In this PR, we are breaking the deposit snapshot path option into 3 separate options:

- path from our bundles distributed as part of Teku

title: Don't log error in case storage mode file doesn't exist
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Noticed tests extending `AbstractBeaconNodeCommandTest` (e.g. Eth2NetworkOptionsTest) throw exception such as when the storage mode file doesn't exist:

```java
2024-01-10 14:43:34.307+02:00 | ForkJoinPool-1-worker-1 | ERROR | Builder | Failed to read storage mode from file
java.nio.file.NoSuchFileException: C:\Users\Stefan\AppData\Local\teku\beacon\data-storage-mode.txt
	at java.base/sun.nio.fs.WindowsException.translateToIOException(WindowsException.java:85) ~[?:?]
	at java.base/sun.nio.fs.WindowsException.rethrowAsIOException(WindowsException.java:103) ~[?:?]
	at java.base/sun.nio.fs.WindowsException.rethrowAsIOException(WindowsException.java:108) ~[?:?]
	at java.base/sun.nio.fs.WindowsFileSystemProvider.newByteChannel(WindowsFileSystemProvider.java:236) ~[?:?]
	at java.base/java.nio.file.Files.newByteChannel(Files.java:380) ~[?:?]
	at java.base/java.nio.file.Files.newByteChannel(Files.java:432) ~[?:?]
	at java.base/java.nio.file.Files.readAllBytes(Files.java:3288) ~[?:?]
	at java.base/java.nio.file.Files.readString(Files.java:3366) ~[?:?]
	at java.base/java.nio.file.Files.readString(Files.java:3325) ~[?:?]
	at tech.pegasys.teku.storage.server.StorageConfiguration$Builder.getStorageModeFromPersistedDatabase(StorageConfiguration.java:280) ~[classes/:?]
```

I think in this case, we should just return Optional.empty() and don't log anything, and throw actual `UncheckedIOException` if an error occurs while reading the file, which would indicate some serious issue that should be investigated, so would rather prefer the node not to start in that case.

title: Adds some statistical metrics for `BlobSidecarPool`
body:
Produce metrics like this:

```
# HELP beacon_blobs_pool_stats Blobs pool statistics
# TYPE beacon_blobs_pool_stats counter
beacon_blobs_pool_stats{type="block",subtype="rpc_duplicate",} 0.0
beacon_blobs_pool_stats{type="block",subtype="gossip_duplicate",} 0.0
beacon_blobs_pool_stats{type="block",subtype="rpc_fetch",} 0.0
beacon_blobs_pool_stats{type="blob_sidecar",subtype="rpc",} 0.0
beacon_blobs_pool_stats{type="block",subtype="gossip",} 470.0
beacon_blobs_pool_stats{type="blob_sidecar",subtype="gossip",} 1411.0
beacon_blobs_pool_stats{type="blob_sidecar",subtype="rpc_duplicate",} 0.0
beacon_blobs_pool_stats{type="blob_sidecar",subtype="gossip_duplicate",} 0.0
beacon_blobs_pool_stats{type="block",subtype="rpc",} 0.0
beacon_blobs_pool_stats{type="blob_sidecar",subtype="rpc_fetch",} 5.0
```

- `gossip` subtype counts first-seen (non duplicate) blocks\blob_sidecars that has been received via gossip
- `rpc` subtype counts first-seen blocks\blob_sidecars received via RPC (a recent fetch)
- `gossip_duplicate` counts blocks\blob_sidecars coming from gossip that was already present in the pool (duplicate)
- `rpc_duplicate` counts blocks\blob_sidecars coming from rpc that was already present in the pool (duplicate)
- `rpc_fetch` counts number of requested fetches

I may find a better home for the `RemoteOrigin` enum.

title: Added optional/required deposit tree snapshot resource + fallback
body:
## PR Description

The core idea in this PR is that `DepositSnapshotFileLoader` now has multiple resources to load (instead of a single URL). Each resource can be set as required (can't fail) or optional (can fail).

In our current implementation, when using `--Xdeposit-snapshot` to provide a custom deposit tree snapshot to Teku, we will set it as the only resource, and mark it as required. Therefore, if it fails to load, Teku will exit with an error.

For known networks like Mainnet or Testnets (networks that we have a bundled snapshot of the deposit tree), we will also set the bundled version as a required resource (there is no reason for it to fail).

Last but not least, if the user is using `--checkpoint-sync-url`, we will add an extra optional resource that takes precedence over the bundled resource. If it fails loading, we will fallback into the bundled one.

When configuring `DepositSnapshotFileLoader` through its builder, we keep the order of insertion, what reflects the order we use when evaluating resources.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #7715
