title: Updated RpcHandler with sendRequestWithBodySelector(..) method
body:
## PR Description

This PR is a preparation for a follow-up change where we choose the correct Status message (V1 or V2) depending on the version negotiated by libp2p's multistream-select.

The tricky part is that when we are defining the request or sending the body, we don't know what version will be used. The way to handle this is to define a function that takes a string representing the `protocolId` (version negotiated) and chooses the correct body depending on the version chosen.

Summary of changes:
- Created an interface `RpcRequestBodySelector` and two implementations, one to represent the current behavior where we always use the same body regardless of the version, and a new implementation that uses a map to choose the correct body based on the `protocolId` negotiated by multistream-select.
- Updated `RpcHandler` class with a new method `sendRequestWithBodySelector` that supports this body selector.
- Updated `RpcHandler` existing method `sendRequest` to call the new method `sendRequestWithBodySelector` using a `SingleRpcRequestBodySelector`, basically maintaining the existing behavior.

Next steps: update the logic of sending Status message to choose the correct V1 or V2

## Fixed Issue(s)
partially addresses #9539

title: Make some improvements to `DataColumnSidecarGossipValidator.java`
body:
## PR Description

This PR does three things:

* Renames all instances of `verifyDataColumnSidecarKzgProof` to `verifyDataColumnSidecarKzgProofs`.
  * See: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs
* Fixes punctuation in `DataColumnSidecarGossipValidator.java` messages.
  * Removes punctuation from strings with a single sentence.
  * Adds punctuation to strings with multiple sentences.
* Move up the "The current finalized_checkpoint is an ancestor of the sidecar's block" check.
  * This matches the order we do it in the regular path.

### Regular path

https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/f5f694bf7dad0edbfa5c501cfa4f2e0d4481aeed/ethereum/statetransition/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/statetransition/validation/DataColumnSidecarGossipValidator.java#L276-L290

### Optimized path

https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/f5f694bf7dad0edbfa5c501cfa4f2e0d4481aeed/ethereum/statetransition/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/statetransition/validation/DataColumnSidecarGossipValidator.java#L365-L392

PS: you'll need to scroll a bit.

### Sidenote

I thought about adding the valid inclusion proof to `validInclusionProofInfoSet` immediately after verification, but I believe waiting until after the sidecar is determined to be completely valid (what we currently do) is probably the safest thing. I can imagine a situation in which someone spams sidecars and is somehow able to make this set use a large amount of memory.

Previously, Bytes32Converter only caught NumberFormatException when parsing a hex string to Bytes32. However, Bytes32.fromHexStringStrict can throw IllegalArgumentException for various invalid inputs (e.g., incorrect length, missing 0x prefix).  
This commit updates the converter to catch IllegalArgumentException, ensuring all invalid hex formats are properly handled and reported as a TypeConversionException.

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Updated Rust KZG library to 0.8.0. Run old benchmarks + added new.

Summary for benhmarks: 
- kzgVerify (single) - RustKZG is 40% slower, precompute doesn't affect both Rust and CKZG
- kzgVerifyBatch - RustKZG is 115% slower, precompute doesn't affect both Rust and CKZG. We doesn't user batch verification in code because we expect gossip arrives not in the same time and it's better to verify it immediately in multi-threaded pool not waiting for arritval of others
- reconstruct 100% dataColumnSidecars from 50%: RustKZG is 11-16% faster, depends on precompute.

Overall I think: 
- we should drop precompute default for supernode. It doesn't benefit us but consumes more memory
- we'd better stay with CKZG

title: Add spec references, a mapping of spec to implementation
body:
## PR Description

This PR adds a directory with specification references. These are used to map specification items (configs, presets, functions, etc) to client implementations (code in Teku). This is much less invasive than my original idea of adding spec tags all across the codebase. These specification references are meant to (1) help developers keep track of specification changes and (2) make it easier for third-parties (eg EF Protocol Security) to verify clients adhere to the specifications.

If there's a change (eg a file is moved or a function is renamed) the included CI check will alert developers that something needs to be fixed; fixing issues should be relatively infrequent and easy, probably just updating a filepath or search string. When updating the codebase to be compliant with the next spec version, developers will:

* Bump the version in `specrefs/.ethspecify.yml`.
* Run `ethspecify process --path=specrefs`.
  * This will update the code sections in the spec tags.
* Run `git diff` to see what changes were made.
  * Developers can then make the appropriate changes.
* Run `ethspecify check --path=specrefs` to check for new spec items.
  * For example, a new function is added and is missing from the spec references.
  * The developer will add it to the appropriate spec reference file.

This PR is marked as a draft because I have not completely mapped out all of the functions. This is taking longer than I expected. Opening this now so that I can collect feedback from the team.
 
PS: I got the idea for this from Lodestar!

* https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/7861

title: feat: Make BUILDER_PROPOSAL_DELAY_TOLERANCE Configurable
body:
**Description:** 

Currently, the timeout value for `BUILDER_PROPOSAL_DELAY_TOLERANCE` is hardcoded to `Duration.ofSeconds(1)` in [ethereum/spec/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/spec/config/Constants.java](https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/ethereum/spec/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/spec/config/Constants.java#L67). Allowing this value to be configurable would enable operators to adjust the timeout as needed for different environments or use cases.

**Motivation:** 

In some scenarios, increasing the timeout would allow the builder extra time to gather more transactions or MEV value, potentially improving block value and network efficiency. Making this value configurable allows for experimentation and optimization based on network conditions or operator needs.

**Proposed Solution:**

- Expose BUILDER_PROPOSAL_DELAY_TOLERANCE as a configurable parameter, e.g., via a config file, environment variable, or command-line flag.
- Retain the current `Duration.ofSeconds(1)` as the default if not explicitly set.
- Document the new configuration option for users.

**Benefits:**

- Increase validator's yield
- Greater flexibility for node operators.
- Ability to tune performance for different conditions.
- Supports experimentation and research on the effects of timeout adjustments.

title: Avoid builder validator registration calls potentially delaying calls on critical path
body:
Concurrent batches of validator registration may fill up our throttler and can cause getHeader\getPayload to be queued up.

I think it is better to not throttle critical path calls at all.

Our Teku VC logic sends batches in sequence so it is not causing this issue, but if there are multiple VCs connected to the same teku BN (or a VC sending batches in parallel) we may end up with multiple concurrent batches.

Since we we are not throttling critical calls anymore, we can reduce the number of concurrent non-critical calls to 3 (in practice, we won't send more than 3 registrations concurrently)

It won't affect status calls. We anyway relay on actual status API call timeout\response to decide if builder is alive or not, so if we delay it in the throttler it won't cause any bad effect.

title: Early prepare block production
body:
This is a quick approach to anticipate by 500ms the block production.

Which means we will:
- run `prepareForBlockProduction`
   - advance the time to the beginning of the slot
   - apply deferred attestations
   - process head
     - run late block reorg logic
     - eventually run reorg logic to prepare pools accordingly (upcoming PR)
- retrieve the corresponding state we will use to build the block
   
When VC calls for block production we already have the state to continue the block production (or at least we have the process started and the flow simply attaches to it)

This is faking a bit but we were already tolerating 500ms if beacon API were already called that early.

title: Late block reorg final step
body:
It completes the implementation of our late block reorg feature.

During block preparation we run `processHead` and it can select a head which is late.
During state selection we run late block reorg conditions and we may select the parent, which initiate reorg preparation.
In that case we engage `LateBlockReorgPreparationHandler` which runs the reorging logic in `OperationsReOrgManager`. The state selection will wait the handler to complete before returning the state.

Since there is the extra step of waiting the operation reorg, enabling late block reorg should be done together with `--Xprepare-block-production-enabled` which triggers the block preparation in advance.


BUG FIX on existing reorg logic:
the "non-canonical" flow must be completed before running the "new-canonical". Since the flow are async we could have some new-canonical running after the non-canonical, which can leave the pool dirty when the same operations\attestations are present in both chains.

Two thing worth noting:
 1. when the actual late block reorg happens (we import our produced block) the "operations requeue" of the non canonical block (the actual late block) happens again. We could optimize this by caching what has been already done and skip it
 2. if our block production fails, we will never actually do the reorg. In theory we should run the canonical step again to restore the pools as late block was canonical. It could be done by running a delayed task by the end of the slot if our slot turns out to be empty. It is not a big deal: if we are a proposer of another block we could re-add on chain some operations that were already in.

title: Improve Static peer connection persistence logic
body:
~~I did some tests and appears to me we are only applying reputation on outgoing connection attempt, and we do not check it on incoming connection.~~

~~So without this PR, a peer that get disconnected due to reputation can reconnect immediately without any problems, and all rate limiting trackers will be recreated brand new. We only consider reputation in `Eth2PeerSelectionStrategy` which is outbound.~~

~~There is an interaction with Static peers.~~
~~What I did:~~
~~- if 2 nodes are configured as mutually static, they both consider them trusted and the Reputation never goes down. Thus inbound\outbound connection are always allowed.~~

~~- if static is not mutually configured, the reconnection happens with increasing delay, up to matching the cooldown period. This way the connection is eventually reestablished.~~

~~TLDR: with this PR mutually configured static peers reconnect faster, non-mutual static peers reconnect slower (4 minutes: `(3+9+27+81+120) / 60`)~~

**We decided to make this PR just a static peer handling improvement, as applying reputation to inbound connection requires some additional changes**

title: Add per subnet subscribers target for dynamic peer requirements
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
We have flag and configurable variable:
`--Xp2p-target-subnet-subscriber-count` which currently defaults to 2. It's required by the spec. It's very strange, but it's required by the spec. It checks the number of subnet subscription and if there is any, it will return it's value. So with default 2 it requires 2 total peers for any number of subscriptions. No subscriptions - 0 peers, 1,2,3,100 subnets - 2 peers total.

I've introduced flag `--Xp2p-target-per-subnet-subscriber-count` which is a configuration how many peers are required for each subnet. It's goal is to dynamically require additional peers depending on the node subnet subcriptions. So if say, you are a supernode with 128 subnets, you require 128 peers, if you need 8 custody subscriptiions, you require 8 peers. It's an experimental flag and defaults to unset so it will not affect any current behavior.
## Fixed Issue(s)

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes peer requirement calculation used by peer selection to optionally scale with the number of subscribed subnets, which can affect target peer counts and network connectivity behavior. Default remains unset so existing behavior is preserved unless the new hidden flag is enabled.

> **Overview**
> Introduces a new hidden config/CLI option `--Xp2p-target-per-subnet-subscriber-count` (stored as `OptionalInt` in `P2PConfig`) to optionally specify a *per-subnet* subscriber target.

> Updates `PeerSubnetSubscriptions.getSubscribersRequired()` to account for this per-subnet target by computing total subscriber shortfall across relevant attestation, sync committee, and data column sidecar subnets, and taking the max of that and the existing global/subnet-minimum based requirement.

title: Adding source error as suppressed exception when propagating async
body:
## PR Description

When propagating from future A to future B in a separate thread (using `SafeFuture.propagateToAsync`), failure may occur due to `AsyncRunner` rejecting the execution or for some other unknown reason.

When this happens, future B is completed exceptionally with `cause` related to the error thrown by the `AsyncRunner`. However, if future A also completes exceptionally, we don't propagate that to B.

This change keeps that link by adding A's thrown exception as a suppressed exception of B's cause exception.

enabled via `Xp2p-reworked-sidecar-recovery-enabled: true`

Timeouts drastically changed
 - the checking task is about 3x more common but shouldn't fall on slot boundary very regularly due to the 1/3 second offset.
 - the timeout is 2 minutes rather than 5, and it could potentially be significantly shorter still

primarily more separated and the lifecycle of the recovery process is arguably better defined.

Tried to keep the timeout to the entire process rather than have a timeout that is only part of the process also.

Currently most of the interesting `PendingRecoveryRequest` logging is at debug level, trace gets very noisy.

needs work still, but pushing draft to share the idea.

need to think about how we measure its behaviour through metrics, and what is useful to report on, as well as see the recovery process actually working.

title: Remove earliest available block slot cache
body:
The field become a DB variable, and the cache default config was just making sure there was only 1 inflight request at a time.

If we want to keep this class and have a meaningful impact, we should modify `DEFAULT_EARLIEST_AVAILABLE_BLOCK_SLOT_QUERY_FREQUENCY` to be 1

related to https://github.com/Consensys/teku/pull/9906#issuecomment-3310949410

[eab_queries.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22425785/eab_queries.log)

running with:
```java
  public SafeFuture<Optional<UInt64>> getEarliestAvailableBlockSlot() {
    var start = System.nanoTime();
    return historicalChainData.getEarliestAvailableBlockSlot().thenPeek(__ ->
      LOG.info("Earliest available block {}ms", (System.nanoTime() - start) / 1_000_000));
  }
```

I think, looking at the stats, it is safe to remove.

The timing spikes are because the Splitter queue up all the reads until the DB write (happening on epoch transition) completes

title: fix: assert state root mismatch on root cause
body: Update SanityBlocksTestExecutor to assert error messages on the root cause instead of the top-level RuntimeException. Spec.processBlock throws StateTransitionException which gets wrapped in RuntimeException by applyBlocks; asserting the wrapper’s message is unreliable (often null). Root cause assertions align with repository conventions and correctly detect the state root mismatch message emitted by AbstractBlockProcessor.

title: Fix basic deprecations
body:
## PR Description

Fixed a couple of deprecation warnings that were getting in the way of our build in IntelliJ.

Summary:
- Replaced usages of `assertThat(x).isEqualToComparingFieldByField(y)` with `assertThat(x).usingDefaultComparator().isEqualTo(y)` or `assertThat(x).usingRecursiveComparison().isEqualTo(y)` (depending on need).
- Replaced usages of `NodeManager.create(..)` method that did not have a spec param at index 0.
- Replaced deprecated IntStream.stream()` with `IntStream.intStream().boxed()`.
- Replaced `IntList.add(object)` with `IntList.add(integer)`.
- Replaced `com.google.common.io.Files.createTempDir()` with a variant using `java.nio.file.Files.Files.createTempDirectory(..)`.
- Replaced `assertThat(<FUTURE>).hasFailed()` with `assertThat(<FUTURE>).isCompletedExceptionally().isNotCancelled()`.
- Using import `org.apache.commons.io.IOUtils` instead of `org.apache.commons.compress.utils.IOUtils`
- Object2IntMap.get(k) logic had to be updated due to deprecation.

Also added a few suppressions of our own deprecated code:
- BeaconChainUtil
- Eth2NetworkConfiguration.getConstants()
- MiscHelpersFulu.constructDataColumnSidecarsOld(..)

These supressions are only on testing code.

title: Rework custody/sampling count delivery
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Why it's so complex?

We have `CustodyGroupCountManager` which provides values for custody/synced custody/sampling counts for other components. The issue is that some components are initialized before this manager and some after it. We could play with it a bit probably, do later initializations and other tricks but will eventually hit the wall. This solutions solves this issue: all other components will receive values no matter if they are initialized before or after manager. And it's guaranteed delivery: with channel we had an issue when subscribers didn't recieve first value due to race in creation of channel and subscribed component creation. Current solution is not affected by this bug.

## Fixed Issue(s)

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
This PR refactors the monolithic `BlockGossipValidator` into a more flexible, maintainable, and testable two-stage pipeline architecture. The new design addresses the challenges of adding fork-specific validation logic and improves the clarity of the validation process.

1. Introduced a Two-Stage Pipeline:
**Stateless Pipeline:** Executes fast, preliminary checks (e.g., slot checks, parent known, equivocation peek) without needing the parent state.
**Stateful Pipeline:** Executes slower, state-dependent checks (e.g., signature verification, proposer index) only if the stateless checks pass.
2. Modular Validation Rules:
Each validation check is now a small, single-responsibility class implementing either `StatelessValidationRule` or `StatefulValidationRule` depending on if it needs a parent state access or not.
The new `ForkValidationPipelines` class composes these rules into ordered lists for each consensus fork, making fork-specific logic explicit and easy to manage.

## Fixed Issue(s)
<!-- Please link to fixed issue(s) here using format: fixes #<issue number> -->
<!-- Example: "fixes #2" -->

> [!NOTE]
> Refactors block gossip validation into modular, fork-aware stateless/stateful pipelines with a separate equivocation checker, updating integrations and tests accordingly.
> 
> - **Validation**:
>   - Introduces `StatefulValidationRule` and `StatelessValidationRule` interfaces and per-fork rule sets via `BlockGossipValidationPipelines`.
>   - Replaces monolithic `validation.BlockGossipValidator` with `validation.block.BlockGossipValidator` that executes stateless then stateful pipelines.
>   - Adds `EquivocationChecker` and `SlotAndProposerIndex`; removes old inline equivocation tracking.
>   - Implements fork-specific rules: Phase0/Altair (`FutureSlotRule`, `BlockParent*`, `ExpectedProposerRule`, `ProposerSignatureRule`, etc.), Bellatrix (`ExecutionPayloadTimestampRule`), Deneb (`KzgCommitmentsRule`), and Gloas (`ExecutionPayloadParent*Rule`).

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Last part of #10095 (supernode data column sidecar reconstruction) — the main wiring on top of the already-merged storage/reconstruction/RPC parts.
  
  - **Archiver**: on supernodes the periodic pruner now archives extension data column sidecars (index ≥ NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS/2) down to their KZG proofs — pruning the sidecars while
  persisting the proofs needed to reconstruct them on demand. Wired via `SidecarArchivePrunableChannel` (reconstructor → pruner → `Database.archiveSidecarsProofs`); `halfColumns`
  now derived from spec instead of hardcoded. Full pruning drops the retained proofs too.
- **Reconstruction**. Added queue, so result is capped and stored for reuse not only in single request but for configured amount of time.
  - **Logs**: debug/trace across the reconstruct-and-serve path (both RPC handlers), the archive/prune steps, and the prunable-slot signal, so the flow is observable in logs.
  - **Test coverage**: unit + integration + real-KZG bit-for-bit reconstruction test; RPC by-root/by-range successful-reconstruction serving; `isSidecarPruned` gating;
  prune-removes-proofs; metrics/serializer edges; and a guard test that the archiver is never wired on non-Fulu networks. Log lines asserted via `LogCaptor`.




Speed with 14 blobs on laptop, operation = 1 slot recovery
```
WithPrecomputeBenchmark.reconstructDataColumnSidecarsFromArchive            true             true  thrpt   10  86.109 ± 4.351  ops/s
WithPrecomputeBenchmark.reconstructDataColumnSidecarsFromArchive            true            false  thrpt   10  89.175 ± 4.297  ops/s
WithPrecomputeBenchmark.reconstructDataColumnSidecarsFromArchive           false             true  thrpt   10  81.804 ± 4.506  ops/s
WithPrecomputeBenchmark.reconstructDataColumnSidecarsFromArchive           false            false  thrpt   10  91.047 ± 5.711  ops/s
```

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
After some testing and discussions, if one validator appears more than once in a PTC, we need the signature to be added multiple times when aggregating. Tested on local interop successfully block being processed with multiple attestations.

Also one of the tests wasn't really working since when number of validators is 32, then exactly one validator would be chosen for PTC (since 32 slots in an epoch) and then the `allMatch()` assertion was just asserting on empty bits but was passing.

## Fixed Issue(s)
related to #10041

---

> [!NOTE]
> Fix payload attestation aggregation to align with PTC (including repeated validators) and de-duplicate messages by validator; update tests accordingly.
> 
> - **State transition / payload attestation**:
>   - `MatchingDataPayloadAttestationGroup`
>     - De-duplicates by validator using `Map<Integer, PayloadAttestationMessage>` and rejects repeats in `add(...)`.
>     - Aggregates by iterating PTC positions, setting aggregation bits per PTC index and collecting signatures; supports repeated validators in PTC (signature included per occurrence).
>     - Uses `spec.atSlot(data.getSlot())` when building schemas; simplifies with `IntArrayList` and explicit loops.
> - **Tests**:
>   - `AggregatingPayloadAttestationPoolTest`
>     - Scales to `8192` validators; derives voters from `ptc` (80/20 split); fixes assertions by mapping set bits back through `ptc`; adjusts "not applicable" slot and metric expectations.
>   - `MatchingDataPayloadAttestationGroupTest`
>     - Adds test rejecting duplicate validator index.
>     - Adds test verifying multiple PTC occurrences set multiple bits; retains multi-attestation aggregation test.

## PR Description
Change behavior of `--Xdas-extra-custody-group-count` to `--Xcustody-group-count-override`

title: Sidecar KZG Proofs storage
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Part of #10132, implementing #10095
Implementing only database part: storing, reading, removing KZG Proofs for DataColumnSidecars.

Main concerns:
- Serializing/deserializing location (Spec)
- Serialization choice: lists written one by one, adds `64*4=256 bytes` per slot, which could be shrinked to a single int value, 4 bytes. But both are tiny numbers on the whole scale, say, with 14 target blobs supernode:
  + current storage 508Gb
  + expected: 254Gb + (48*14*64+256)*32*4096 = 254Gb + 5.67Gb = 259.67Gb
  + with 4 bytes instead of 256: 254Gb + (48*14*64+4)*32*4096 = 254Gb + 5.63Gb = 259.63Gb
Anyway I'm happy to apply any solution which looks more elegant than this one.
- Test coverage, what could be added?

body:
This an alternative to `DASCustodySync`.
The class is just introduced and not activated yet. Flags and additional DB variable will be added in subsequent PRs.

title: Allow sampler to reissue RPC requests
body:
If RPC requests issued by the sampler fail (due to timeout or other problems) the sampler stalls and never retries downloads.

This can stall the sync itself, because even in the case `SyncStallDetector` restarts the sync, the sampler will always have the same trackers with RPCFetched marked as `true`. Thus no more attempts on restart.


With this change, multiple calls to `checkDataAvailability` can cause redownloads attempt on incomplete trackers.

related to: #10185


NOTE: A limitation of the current sync design is that the sync has no feedback from the PreSampler, so the only way it has to attempt a recovery is via `SyncStallDetector`, which requires a relatively long timeout.

## Documentation

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> Allows `DasSamplerBasic` to retry RPC data fetches by resetting the scheduled flag and short-circuiting completed trackers; updates tests to cover retry and scheduling behavior.
> 
> - **Statetransition (DAS Sampler)**
>   - In `checkDataAvailability(...)`:
>     - Return early if `completionFuture` is already done.
>     - Atomically schedule RPC fetch with `rpcFetchScheduled().compareAndSet(false, true)`.
>   - In `fetchMissingColumnsViaRPC(...)`:
>     - After completion (success or failure), reset `rpcFetchScheduled` via `.alwaysRun(() -> ...set(false))` to allow retries.
> - **Tests**

title: Run `kzg.loadTrustedSetup` in thread with 8MB stack size
body:
## PR Description

This PR runs `kzg.loadTrustedSetup()` in a separate, temporary, short-lived thread with an 8MB stack.

This was segfaulting with higher precompute values (greater than 10) because the default stack size for java threads is 1MB. It worked just fine in c-kzg-4844 testing because the tests ran on the main thread which is 8MB.

To test this out, you can run the following command before & after the change:

```
./build/install/teku/bin/teku --Xkzg-precompute=15 --ee-endpoint=http://blah --checkpoint-sync-url=https://mainnet.checkpoint.sigp.io
```

You can also test this by setting all threads to be 8MB 😅 

```
JAVA_OPTS="-Xss8m" ./build/install/teku/bin/teku --Xkzg-precompute=15 ...
```

## Fixed Issue(s)

* https://github.com/ethereum/c-kzg-4844/issues/611

title: Fix TOCTOU race condition for duplicate attestations
body:
## PR Description

When validating attestations, the node should not propagate an attestation that was previously seen. In our current implementation, the check if the attestation was seen and the resulting validation was not done atomically, which could lead to a race condition where we check two similar attestations but don't consider them seen.

This fix relies on our synchronised `seenPayloadAttestations` set `add()` function to perform a second check if the attestation has been seen.

## Fixed Issue(s)
N/A

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Makes duplicate payload attestation detection atomic in the gossip validator and adds tests to cover the race scenario.
> 
> - **Validation (PayloadAttestationMessageGossipValidator)**:
>   - Atomically handle duplicates by checking `seenPayloadAttestations.add(key)` post-validation; return `ignore(...)` if already present.
>   - Replace pre-check return with `ignoreAttestationAlreadySeenValidationResult(...)` helper and reuse it after `add(...)`.
>   - Add private helper `ignoreAttestationAlreadySeenValidationResult(...)` to centralize logging and ignore result.
> - **Tests**:
>   - Add `shouldIgnore_whenAlreadySeen_AfterInitialCheck` to simulate concurrent validations and verify ignore-on-second.
>   - Tighten existing tests to verify no further validations on duplicates and behavior when validation fails then succeeds.

title: replace LRUCache with CaffeineCache
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Replace our custom `synchronized` `LRUCache` implementation with `CaffeineCache`, a wrapper around the Caffeine cache library.

The `Cache` interface remains unchanged. The existing test suite has been updated to be compatible with Caffeine's eviction policy.

The existing `LRUCache` implementation presents a significant performance bottleneck under concurrent load due to its reliance on the `synchronized` keyword for all operations.

The primary issue is with the `get` method:
```java
public synchronized V get(final K key, final Function<K, V> fallback) { ... }
```
If one thread experiences a cache miss, it acquires a lock on the entire cache. If the `fallback` function to compute the new value is slow , **all other threads are blocked**, even those trying to access completely different, already-cached keys. This leads to poor scalability and thread contention.

#### How does this PR address the issue?

1.  Caffeine uses sophisticated locking mechanisms. A cache miss and subsequent value computation on one key does not block other threads from reading or writing different keys. This eliminates the primary bottleneck of the old implementation

2.  Superior Eviction Policy (TinyLFU): While `LRUCache` uses a classic LRU policy, Caffeine employs a TinyLFU. This policy offers the same core benefit as LRU (evicting old, unused items) but is smarter, providing a better overall hit rate. TinyLFU combines recency (LRU) with frequency (LFU). It keeps track of not just when an item was last used, but also how often it's used

3.  Caffeine is a mature library known for achieving near optimal hit rates with minimal overhead

title: Add inflight db sidecars
body:
This is just an idea, to be validated in real world, and it could explain why, before #10219, we were actually duplicating download requests instead of just rebuilding the tracker which then completes immediately.

if that's the case, the underlining design problem\bug is that we don't write Columns via `CombinedStorageChannelSplitter`.

`CombinedStorageChannelSplitter` guarantees that reads are happening only after writes.

this approach is beneficial because it does not wait the writes, and can be very useful for quickly serving byRoot RPCs on the block head.

We should probably fix `CombinedStorageChannelSplitter` anyway too.

title: Allow getBlobs API to retrieve required sidecars on demand
body:
Based on an idea by @ajsutton 

Enabling `--get-blobs-api-p2p-sidecars-download-enabled` the get blobs endpoint will attempt to download missing sidecars from the p2p network via RPC, to be able to rebuild the requested blobs.
If the retrieval succede, the columns are also written on DB, so that subsequent calls for the same slot wont trigger RPC anymore.

This allow blobs to be retrieved for nodes that are not configured to do full custody.
Another benefit is that a node could be able to serve blobs even if custody backfill is not yet completed.
The query could even try to get blobs from outside the retention period (`MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS`) after the prune happened. Maybe some nodes on the network still serve that data.

based on my testing on mainnet, once the node starts and manage to get some peers, it is immediately able to successfully retrieve columns.

title: Column sidecar batching and inflight retrievable
body:
supersedes #10233

this PR implements:
1. column sidecar write batching
2. inflight write tracking


Feature 1. reduce the amount of transactions against DB (columns will be batched and written within the same transaction)
Feature 2. allows to immediately respond to getSidecar, so reading classes do not need to wait for the DB write to complete. This addresses some additional latency (100ms) introduced by 1. The inflight will be also considered on the columnId caching functionality

## PR Description
We had documented cases when sidecars are submitted to recovering custody for 2 times in a row. For example with failed sync batch submission, which retries the same range after a while. If there are misses in the second retry, recovering custody will try to recover sidecars which are already in DB. I've added small light cache to `DataColumnSidecarRecoveringCustodyImpl` to avoid such behavior and skip creation of recovery task for the second time. 

Regarding the disabled test: it takes locally om m4 like 10 seconds, so it will take on CI 30+ seconds, which I think is too much for single unit test. If some could suggest a lighter way to check the same, I'd appreciate and will change the test.

> **High Risk**
> Touches core consensus/spec-critical paths for Gloas (SSZ containers, bid/envelope validation, fork upgrade behavior, and withdrawals limits), so mismatches could cause invalid block processing or network incompatibility despite being largely spec-alignment work.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates Teku’s Gloas implementation to consensus-specs `v1.7.0-alpha.2`, most notably changing `ExecutionPayloadBid` to carry full `blob_kzg_commitments` (a list) instead of a single `blob_kzg_commitments_root`, and removing `blob_kzg_commitments` from `ExecutionPayloadEnvelope`. This rewires bid/envelope creation, SSZ schemas, REST API JSON fixtures, signing test vectors, and execution payload validation to derive `versioned_hashes` from the committed bid commitments.
> 
> Aligns Gloas data-column sidecars with the spec by removing the `kzg_commitments` field from the Gloas `DataColumnSidecar` SSZ container (builders treat commitments as a no-op, accessors now throw `UnsupportedOperationException`), and updates sidecar construction utilities accordingly.
> 
> Adjusts Gloas fork/state logic and withdrawals handling: adds onboarding of builders from pending deposits during `GloasStateUpgrade`, adds commitment-count limit checks when processing execution payload bids, tightens withdrawals limit checks (reserve one slot where required) and wraps withdrawals processing in `safelyProcess` in multiple processors. Also updates `MIN_BUILDER_WITHDRAWABILITY_DELAY` (mainnet `4096→64`, minimal `8→2`) and bumps reference-test spec version to `v1.7.0-alpha.2` (including adding Altair `rewards/inactivity_scores`).

title: Use current date when CI triggered manually
body: ## PR Description The `publish-docker` workflow fails when triggered manually with this error: `Error: unmarshal Provenance predicate: parsing time "" as "2006-01-02T15:04:05Z07:00": cannot parse "" as "2006"` Example: https://github.com/Consensys/teku/actions/runs/21670357205 (ci triggered manually for master) This happens because It uses `${{ github.event.head_commit.timestamp }}` for the `buildStartedOn` field and this value is only available in push events but is empty `workflow_dispatch` events (manual runs) resulting in an empty string that cannot be parses as a valid timestamp. This PR adds a fallback mechanism that checks if `BUILD_STARTED_ON` is empty and generates a valid timestamp using `date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"` when the event context doesn't provide one. ## Fixed Issue(s) ## Documentation - [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required. ## Changelog - [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary. --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Low risk workflow-only change that just fills `buildStartedOn` with a valid UTC timestamp when `github.event.head_commit.timestamp` is missing, preventing provenance generation/attestation failures on manual or `workflow_call` triggers. > > **Overview** > Fixes `publish-docker` provenance generation for non-push triggers by **falling back to the current UTC time** when `github.event.head_commit.timestamp` is empty. > > The workflow now writes placeholders into `provenance.json` and `sed`-substitutes both `buildStartedOn` and `buildFinishedOn`, ensuring cosign provenance attestation always has valid timestamps. > > Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit ed3c5a48e232544a7c75176c4f4ed9ec5c64d9f2. body: I run a profiler for ~4min on mainnet and I noticed this We can avoid the serialization/deserialization of the singleAttestationAggregationBits when creating a the electra attestation (aggregated) ## Benchmark Results: SszBitlist Tree Construction Optimization **Environment:** JDK 21.0.6, OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM (Zulu), 1 fork, 5 warmup / 10 measurement iterations @ 1s each ### Throughput (ops/s, higher is better) | Benchmark | Baseline | Optimized | Speedup | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `createBitlistAndSerialize` | 2,573,246 ± 22,197 | 11,401,721 ± 106,930 | **4.43x** | | `createBitlistAndHashTreeRoot` | 2,383,815 ± 33,825 | 8,053,888 ± 37,651 | **3.38x** | | `createBitlistAndOr` | 42,836,426 ± 163,337 | 40,525,583 ± 198,794 | ~1.0x | ### Allocations (B/op, lower is better) | Benchmark | Baseline | Optimized | Reduction | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `createBitlistAndSerialize` | 1,760 B/op | 928 B/op | **-47% (-832 B)** | | `createBitlistAndHashTreeRoot` | 1,720 B/op | 944 B/op | **-45% (-776 B)** | | `createBitlistAndOr` | 392 B/op | 392 B/op | 0% | ### Summary The optimization replaces the serialize/deserialize round-trip in `SszBitlistImpl` with direct tree construction from `BitSet` byte data. Benchmarks that force tree materialization (`sszSerialize()`, `hashTreeRoot()`) show **3.4-4.4x throughput improvement** and **~45-47% allocation reduction**. The `or()` benchmark is unaffected because it operates at the `BitlistImpl` level and defers tree construction (lazy supplier), confirming the optimization is correctly scoped. ## Documentation - [ ] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required. ## Changelog - [ ] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary. --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches SSZ tree construction for bitlists; incorrect byte sizing/padding could change hash tree roots or serialization for edge-case lengths, though new tests cover a range of sizes. > > **Overview** > **Optimizes `SszBitlist` tree materialization.** `SszBitlistImpl` no longer builds its backing tree via SSZ `serialize`/`deserialize`; it now constructs the tree directly from the underlying `BitSet` bytes via a new `SszBitlistSchemaImpl.createTreeFromBitData` path. > > This adds `BitlistImpl.toByteArray()` as the raw bit source, updates tests to validate the new byte extraction and that direct tree construction matches the previous deserialization-based root, and extends JMH benchmarks to measure `create+serialize`, `create+or`, and `create+hashTreeRoot` scenarios. > > Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit 6db4238fcf15820c18fafd6788d0e3f277bbdfe8. This will update automatically on new commits. Configure [here](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot).

title: Optimize getIndexedAttestationFromSingleAttestation
body:
related to: #9035

there is also an hot memory allocation path on `getIndexedAttestationFromSingleAttestation`

## Benchmark Comparison: `SszPrimitiveListSchemaImpl.createTreeFromElements()` Optimization

### UInt64 List (8 bytes/element, 4 elements/chunk)

#### Throughput (ops/us) — higher is better

| listSize | Baseline | Optimized | Speedup  |
|----------|----------|-----------|----------|
| **1**    | 2.756    | **7.164** | **2.60x** |
| 4        | 2.196    | **4.498** | **2.05x** |
| 16       | 0.933    | **1.857** | **1.99x** |
| 64       | 0.231    | **0.581** | **2.52x** |

#### Allocation (gc.alloc.rate.norm, B/op) — lower is better

| listSize | Baseline | Optimized  | Reduction                |
|----------|----------|------------|--------------------------|
| **1**    | 4,952    | **1,624**  | **-67%** (3,328 B saved) |
| 4        | 5,312    | **2,392**  | **-55%** (2,920 B saved) |
| 16       | 7,400    | **5,344**  | **-28%** (2,056 B saved) |
| 64       | 20,640   | **17,696** | **-14%** (2,944 B saved) |

### Byte List (1 byte/element, 32 elements/chunk) — no regression

`SszByteListSchemaImpl` overrides `createFromElements` with its own optimized path
(`fromBytes`), so it does not go through `createTreeFromElements` at all.
These results confirm zero interference from the optimization.

#### Throughput (ops/us) — higher is better

| listSize | Baseline | Optimized | Delta                     |
|----------|----------|-----------|---------------------------|
| **1**    | 8.750    | 8.752     | ~0%                       |
| 4        | 8.644    | 8.476     | ~0% (within error margin) |
| 16       | 7.837    | 8.042     | ~0% (within error margin) |
| 64       | 5.491    | 5.334     | ~0% (within error margin) |

#### Allocation (gc.alloc.rate.norm, B/op) — lower is better

| listSize | Baseline | Optimized | Delta |
|----------|----------|-----------|-------|
| **1**    | 1,320    | 1,320     | 0%    |
| 4        | 1,328    | 1,328     | 0%    |
| 16       | 1,384    | 1,384     | 0%    |
| 64       | 1,840    | 1,840     | 0%    |

### Key Takeaways

- **UInt64 (single-attestation hot path, listSize=1): 2.60x faster, 67% fewer allocations**
- UInt64 lists see ~2x throughput improvement across all sizes with significant allocation reduction.
- **Byte lists show zero regression** — both throughput and allocations are identical within noise.
- The optimization benefits types that go through `SszPrimitiveListSchemaImpl.createTreeFromElements()`,
  replacing the generic writable-copy-then-commit path with direct leaf-node packing.

### JMH Configuration

```
-f 1 -wi 3 -i 5 -bm thrpt -tu us -prof gc
JVM args: -Xmx1g -Xms1g
```


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes low-level SSZ tree construction logic; while covered by new correctness tests, mistakes could impact hash tree roots/serialization across many primitive list types.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Optimizes SSZ primitive list construction** by overriding `SszPrimitiveListSchemaImpl.createTreeFromElements` to build the backing tree directly via packed leaf nodes (for byte-aligned primitive elements), instead of going through the generic writable-copy/commit path.
> 
> Adds a new JMH benchmark (`PrimitiveListCreationBenchmark`) to measure list creation for `UInt64` and `byte` lists, and extends `SszPrimitiveListSchemaTest` with a parameterized check that the optimized tree matches the generic path by comparing hash roots and SSZ serialization.
>

> **Overview**
> Enables *Gloas-aware state selection* in validator block production by introducing `ValidatorApiHandlerGloas` and routing `BeaconChainController` to use it when `SpecMilestone.GLOAS` is supported; the handler can prefer an execution-payload-derived state (regenerated to the target slot) before falling back to the existing `getStateForBlockProduction` path.

title: hashing optimization for epoch transition
body:
## Reduce `ArrayWrappingBytes32` Allocations in SSZ Tree Hashing

  ### JMH Benchmark: `updateEffectiveBalancesAndHash`

  **Scenario:** Update effective balance on 2,000 randomly selected validators (out of 400K), then compute `hashTreeRoot()`.

  **JMH args:** `-f 3 -wi 5 -i 10 -w 2s -r 2s -prof gc`
  **JVM:** JDK 21.0.6, OpenJDK 64-Bit Server VM (Zulu), Compiler Blackhole mode

  | Metric | Before (master) | After (optimized) | Delta |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | **Throughput** | 5.518 ± 0.073 ops/s | 5.725 ± 0.030 ops/s | **+3.7%** |
  | **gc.alloc.rate** | 2707.620 ± 36.025 MB/sec | 1697.425 ± 9.000 MB/sec | **-37.3%** |
  | **gc.alloc.rate.norm** | 514,516,233 B/op | 310,923,036 B/op | **-39.6%** |

  ### Mainnet Profiling: async-profiler `alloc` event

  **Conditions:** Mainnet, checkpoint sync, `--ee-endpoint unsafe-test-stub`, all subnets + all custody subnets, `-Xmx10G`, 1 epoch capture after sync completion.

  | Path | Before (samples) | After (samples) | Delta |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `SszNodeTemplate` → `ArrayWrappingBytes32` | 2,393 | 0 | **-100%** |
  | `SszSuperNode` → `ArrayWrappingBytes32` | 3,945 | 460 | **-88.3%** |
  | `calcHashTreeRoot` / `calculateHashTreeRoot` → `ArrayWrappingBytes32` | 2,530 | 1 | **-99.96%** |
  | `MutableBytes32.create` (right-pad allocs) | 1,046 | 29 | **-97.2%** |

  **Note:** Total alloc samples differ between runs (660K vs 795K) due to network variability. The targeted SSZ hashing paths are deterministic for a given state size, making the
  per-path comparisons reliable.

## Documentation

- [ ] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [ ] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core SSZ Merkle hashing internals to use raw byte arrays and new digest overloads; while aimed at allocation reduction, any subtle hashing/caching bug would affect state roots and consensus behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Optimizes SSZ tree hashing for packed nodes by avoiding repeated `Bytes32`/right-padding allocations: `SszNodeTemplate` and `SszSuperNode` now compute intermediate Merkle hashes as raw `byte[32]` and only wrap to `Bytes32` at the end, reusing a precomputed default leaf hash.
> 
> Extends `Sha256` with a `digest(byte[], byte[])` overload to support the new raw-hash path, and fixes `SimpleLeafNode.hashTreeRoot()` to actually return the cached value instead of re-allocating on every call.
> 
> Adds a new JMH benchmark (`updateEffectiveBalancesAndHash`) and trial `@Setup` to model epoch-transition-like validator effective balance updates and pre-warm hashing.
>

> Touches core forward-sync and forkchoice execution-payload import paths, adds new RPC request/validation logic, and changes failure classification that can affect peer disconnects and sync liveness.

> Adds **Gloas forward-sync support for execution payload envelopes** in both multi-peer and single-peer modes.
> 
> Multi-peer batches now request and track execution payload envelopes (gated by `SpecMilestone.GLOAS`), validate they’re present for “full” blocks, and the `BatchImporter` imports payloads via `ExecutionPayloadManager` after successful block import, mapping payload failures to sync outcomes.

> Single-peer sync now requests payload envelopes alongside blocks/blob sidecars, imports them after block import with new metrics and error handling (`FailedExecutionPayloadImportException`, new `PeerSyncResult` outcomes), and threads `ExecutionPayloadManager` through the sync factories.

> Execution payload import plumbing is expanded: `ExecutionPayloadManager` gains an explicit `importExecutionPayload` API (and NOOP impl), `ExecutionPayloadImportResult` adds `FAILED_EXECUTION_SYNCING` plus helpers to classify execution/data-availability failures, and forkchoice returns this new failure when payload status is “not validated”. title: Reimplement ForkAwareTimeBasedEventAdapter
body:
run an interop from PHASE0 to GLOAS

```
2026-02-18 17:27:07.827 DEBUG  - Scheduling 3 events for Phase0TimeBasedEventAdapter starting at 1771432030000 with period 6000ms, expiry 1771432096000
2026-02-18 17:28:10.008 DEBUG  - Scheduling 5 events for AltairTimeBasedEventAdapter starting at 1771432096000 with period 6000ms, expiry 1771432384000
2026-02-18 17:32:58.007 DEBUG  - Scheduling 6 events for GloasTimeBasedEventAdapter starting at 1771432384000 with period 6000ms, expiry none
```

every TimeBasedEventAdapter will reschedule all events, including the slot one, allowing slot time changes in future forks


## Documentation

- [ ] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core validator timing and async scheduling behavior; incorrect expiry or fork-boundary transitions could delay/skip duty production across forks.
> 
> **Overview**
> Validator time-based duties are reimplemented as a fork-aware scheduler: `ForkAwareTimeBasedEventAdapter` now switches between per-milestone adapters (Phase0/Altair/Gloas) and schedules all slot/duty timers with an explicit expiry at the next timing-changing fork boundary, allowing rescheduling when slot timings change.
> 
> `RepeatingTaskScheduler` is extended to support **expiring repeating tasks** with a one-shot `ExpirationTask` callback, and the validator adapters are refactored into an abstract `TimeBasedEventAdapter` with milestone-specific subclasses and updated tests covering expiry, fork transitions, and non-divisible slot durations.
> 
> Timing tweaks align timeouts/offsets with spec helpers: blob sidecar availability completion timeout now uses `spec.getAttestationDueMillis(slot)`, and slot attestation due documentation is updated to reflect Gloas timing changes.

title: Progressive ssz
body:
fixes: #9772

TODO:
- Implement `TreeNodeStore` related methods
- SuperNode hint
- We also probably need primitive versions using `CachingTreeAccessor`?
- do some benchmarking to evaluate performance impacts

---- 
The following branch
https://github.com/tbenr/teku/tree/progressive_ssz_electra_testing
implements:
- a unified Container\Progressive container, so that we can reuse the same classes but enable progressive mode just by passing the new `active_fields` param.
- introduce "progressive" constructor in `ContainerN` and `ContainerSchemaN`
- fixes progressivebitlist having size in the underlining data structure.
- implements SuperNode **hints** and `CachingTreeAccessor`.
- implements store\load functions
- introduces specialized ProgressiveUInt64List for compatibility.
- Experiment: Modifies Electra with
   1. progressiveBitList in electra attestation (aggregation bits)
   2. beaconState with validators and balances as progressive list


question: is the Unified approach the best or we want to keep Progressive classes well separated, leave common code in Util classes, and have specific `ProgressiveContainerN` and `ProgressiveBeaconState` classes too?

----

general perplexities:

- since PL are unbounded by design, our usage of schema SszLengthBounds will be partially defeated. IE: when introducing in attestation suddenly the attestation schema upperbound will be `Long.MAX_VALUE`. Which means at gossip level we wont be so restrictive anymore and the overall upperbound value we apply (10mb?) becomes applicable to more structures. I see 2 solutions: introduce the ability to "suggest" a reasonable upperbound per on PL, or haveing different limits on gossip (like 10mb for blocks only, 1mb for all the others)

- in beacon state, when upgrading the state to a PL enabled state schema, datastructures needs to be rebuilt.

- we need to be careful in types. we need to make sure we have specialized list schemas that implements the different interfaces we have (ie: `SszProgressiveUInt64ListImpl` implementing `SszUInt64List`) to be able to swap them

title: Fix inconsistency of synced custody group count
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Alternative to #10396. Should fix all potential cases when synced count was incorrect.
Removed synced custody group count at all.
We used it for 2 main consumers:
- `StatusMessage`. `StatusMessage` provides both `earliestAvailableSlot` and `cgc`, so other peers should expect `cgc` custody count starting from `earliestAvailableSlot`, 
which basically means that it doesn't require full backfill since we provide correct `earliestAvailableSlot`, we should use just custody count here. 
- ENR. In spec it's not mentioned whether ENR should advertise synced or non-synced count, which means it's up to the client implementation. As far as 99% peers in network
are already synced, it makes sense to advertise non-synced number here too. In 99% cases other peers are looking for gossip source which doesn't require full backfill.

With changes in this PR Backfiller on start checks earliestAvailableSlot DB custody and compares it to the requirement to find if Backfilling is needed. This should fix also #10039


## Fixed Issue(s)

Closes #10232

> `MetadataMessagesFactory` (and discovery/ENR wiring) now advertises the current custody group count directly, and tests/acceptance expectations are updated accordingly; `MiscHelpersFulu` exposes `getCustodyColumnsPerGroup()` to support the new synced-count calculation.

title: Migrate `EventChannel` to virtual threads (feature flag)
body:
## Summary

  Adds `--Xevent-channel-virtual-threads-enabled` hidden CLI flag to switch `EventChannel.createAsync()` from platform threads (`CachedThreadPool`) to virtual threads (`newThreadPerTaskExecutor`).

  The flag defaults to `false` (original platform thread behavior). When enabled, each async event channel uses virtual threads instead of a cached platform thread pool.

  **Why no lock changes?** [JEP 491](https://openjdk.org/jeps/491) (JDK 24) eliminates `synchronized` pinning of virtual threads, so the `ReentrantLock` conversions from the original PR are
  no longer necessary. JDK 24+ users get full virtual thread benefits without any lock migration.
  
  
## Benefits

  1. Memory savings: ~70 fewer platform threads x ~1MB stack each = ~70MB less committed memory.
  2. Reduced OS scheduling overhead: Fewer platform threads competing for CPU time slices.

(in practice, we can continue subscribing classes to `SlotEventsChannel` and others without the side effect of having a new OS thread for each subscription)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Low risk because the new virtual-thread execution path is guarded by a hidden flag that defaults to `false`, preserving existing cached-thread-pool behavior. Main risk is limited to the opt-in virtual-thread executor choice for event delivery and its operational characteristics.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds an opt-in (hidden) CLI flag `--Xevent-channel-virtual-threads-enabled` to run async `EventChannel` deliveries on virtual threads instead of a cached platform-thread pool.
> 
> Wires the flag through a new `BeaconNodeConfig` into `TekuConfiguration` and `AbstractNode` so `EventChannels`/`EventChannel.createAsync()` select between `Executors.newThreadPerTaskExecutor(Thread.ofVirtual...)` and the existing `newCachedThreadPool`. Includes CLI parsing tests covering default/explicit true/false behavior.
>

title: Javalin7 and virtual threads on REST API
body:
this is on top of the Event Channel virtual threads (#10426)

the Javalin 6->7 migration and Virtual Threads activation is on 78e724202cc4482d9aaa291aebfc526911d91074

fixes #10428


## Context

Virtual threads were introduced in the event channel infrastructure (`EventChannel.createAsync()`). We want to extend this to the REST API layer to make request handling cheaper, especially for SSE long-lived connections and synchronous endpoints.

**Problem:** Unbounded virtual threads could exhaust memory under load spikes via concurrent large response serialization (e.g., `GetState` returning full `BeaconState`). We need bounded concurrency.

**Solution:** Upgrade Javalin 6.7 → 7.x (which brings Jetty 11 → 12). Jetty 12 provides a native `VirtualThreadPool` with `setMaxConcurrentTasks()` — semaphore-bounded virtual threads, no custom code needed.

### Files modified

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `gradle/versions.gradle` | `io.javalin` 6.7.0 → 7.0.0, `javalin-rendering` → `javalin-rendering-thymeleaf` |
| `infrastructure/restapi/build.gradle` | `javalin-rendering` → `javalin-rendering-thymeleaf` |
| `infrastructure/restapi/.../RestApiBuilder.java` | Moved all route/handler/exception registration into `Javalin.create(config)` block; `config.startup.*` for banner/watcher; `config.http.compressionStrategy` assignment; removed Conscrypt; added `VirtualThreadPool` in `modifyJettyServer`; moved password file creation from `RestApi` to `ensurePasswordFile()` |
| `infrastructure/restapi/.../JavalinEndpointAdapter.java` | Made constructor public; removed static `addEndpoint(Javalin, ...)` (endpoint registration now in RestApiBuilder config block) |
| `infrastructure/restapi/.../SwaggerUIBuilder.java` | Replaced `configureDocs(Javalin, OpenApiDocBuilder)` with `buildDocs(OpenApiDocBuilder)` returning docs string only; `SWAGGER_DOCS_PATH` now package-private; removed Javalin import |
| `infrastructure/restapi/.../RestApi.java` | Simplified: removed `passwordPath` field/constructor param, removed `checkAccessFile`, simplified error handling for `jettyServer()` → `app.port()` |
| `data/beaconrestapi/.../StubContext.java` | Updated for Javalin 7 `Context` interface: removed `endpointHandlerPath()`, `handlerType()`, `matchedPath()`; added `endpoints()`, `endpoint()`, `multipartConfig()` |
| `infrastructure/restapi/.../RestApiTest.java` | Updated `RestApi` constructor (2-arg), moved password-file-writability test to call `RestApiBuilder.ensurePasswordFile()` directly |

### Key design decisions
- **Compression**: Left `CompressionStrategy.GZIP` default (1500 byte threshold). The per-request `minSizeForCompression(0)` in `JavalinRestApiRequest` still forces compression on all endpoint responses. The original mixed-content bug is fixed in Javalin 7 via `isCompressionDecisionMade` flag.
- **Virtual threads**: `QueuedThreadPool` stays for accept/selector (platform threads), `VirtualThreadPool.setMaxConcurrentTasks(250)` delegates task execution to bounded virtual threads.
- **Password file**: Creation moved from `RestApi.doStart()` to `RestApiBuilder.build()` so `AuthorizationHandler` can be registered in the Javalin 7 config block.


#### Why this caps large response serialization

With the current `QueuedThreadPool(250)`, at most 250 concurrent `GetState` requests can serialize simultaneously. `VirtualThreadPool.setMaxConcurrentTasks(250)` preserves this exact bound. Tasks beyond the limit are queued (virtual thread parked cheaply on the semaphore) rather than hard-rejected.

#### What improves
- **SSE `/eth/v1/events`** — each connected client holds a virtual thread instead of a platform thread; hundreds of SSE clients become cheap
- **Synchronous endpoints** (~49) — parameter parsing, JSON serialization, data lookups no longer consume platform threads
- **Burst handling** — excess requests park cheaply on the semaphore rather than being rejected by `QueuedThreadPool`
- **Jetty monitoring** — `QueuedThreadPool` metrics still work; `VirtualThreadPool` adds `getMaxConcurrentTasks()` / `getThreads()`

#### Risks
- **`synchronized` audit** — virtual threads pin carrier threads in synchronized blocks. Jetty 12 was designed for virtual threads, but Teku handler code paths should be verified

## Conscrypt removal


The validator REST API TLS was never actually using Conscrypt (#4869)— the dependency was never on the classpath. Jetty 11's SslContextFactory silently caught the
  NoSuchProviderException and fell back to the JDK's default SSL provider. It just produced a debug/info log message about it.

  Removing setProvider("Conscrypt") is correct — it eliminates a dead code path and a misleading log line. The validator API TLS works the same as before, using the JDK's built-in SSL
  provider.

title: Javalin7
body:
## Context

  Upgrade Javalin 6.7 → 7.0.1 (which brings Jetty 11 → 12), following the [Javalin 6→7 migration guide](https://javalin.io/migration-guide-javalin-6-to-7).

  fixes #10428

  ### Files modified

  | File | Change |
  |------|--------|
  | `gradle/versions.gradle` | `io.javalin` 6.7.0 → 7.0.1, `javalin-rendering` → `javalin-rendering-thymeleaf` |
  | `infrastructure/restapi/build.gradle` | `javalin-rendering` → `javalin-rendering-thymeleaf` (required by Swagger UI)|
  | `infrastructure/restapi/.../RestApiBuilder.java` | Moved all route/handler/exception registration into `Javalin.create(config)` block; `config.startup.*` for banner/watcher;
  `config.http.compressionStrategy` assignment; removed Conscrypt; moved password file creation from `RestApi` to `ensurePasswordFile()` |
  | `infrastructure/restapi/.../JavalinEndpointAdapter.java` | Made constructor public; removed static `addEndpoint(Javalin, ...)` (endpoint registration now in RestApiBuilder config block) |
  | `infrastructure/restapi/.../SwaggerUIBuilder.java` | Replaced `configureDocs(Javalin, OpenApiDocBuilder)` with `buildDocs(OpenApiDocBuilder)` returning docs string only; `SWAGGER_DOCS_PATH` now
  package-private; removed Javalin import |
  | `infrastructure/restapi/.../RestApi.java` | Simplified: removed `passwordPath` field/constructor param, removed `checkAccessFile`, simplified error handling for `jettyServer()` → `app.port()` |
  | `data/beaconrestapi/.../StubContext.java` | Updated for Javalin 7 `Context` interface: removed `endpointHandlerPath()`, `handlerType()`, `matchedPath()`; added `endpoints()`, `endpoint()`,
  `multipartConfig()` |
  | `infrastructure/restapi/.../RestApiTest.java` | Updated `RestApi` constructor (2-arg), moved password-file-writability test to call `RestApiBuilder.ensurePasswordFile()` directly |

  ### Key migration changes

  - **Route registration (Javalin 7 requirement)**: All route/handler/exception registration moved from post-`Javalin.create()` into the `config` block via `config.routes.*`.
  - **Startup config**: `config.showJavalinBanner` / `config.startupWatcherEnabled` → `config.startup.showJavalinBanner` / `config.startup.startupWatcherEnabled`.
  - **Compression**: Replaced `config.http.customCompression(strategy)` with `config.http.compressionStrategy = CompressionStrategy.GZIP`. Removed the global `setDefaultMinSizeForCompression(0)`
  workaround — the mixed-content bug is fixed in Javalin 7 via `isCompressionDecisionMade` flag. Per-request `minSizeForCompression(0)` in `JavalinRestApiRequest` still forces compression on all
  endpoint responses.
  - **Password file**: Creation moved from `RestApi.doStart()` to `RestApiBuilder.build()` so `AuthorizationHandler` can be registered in the Javalin 7 config block.
  - **Rendering module**: `javalin-rendering` split into engine-specific modules in Javalin 7; switched to `javalin-rendering-thymeleaf`.

  ### Conscrypt removal

  The validator REST API TLS was never actually using Conscrypt (#4869) — the dependency was never on the classpath. Jetty 11's SslContextFactory silently caught the NoSuchProviderException and fell
  back to the JDK's default SSL provider. It just produced a debug/info log message about it.

  Removing `setProvider("Conscrypt")` is correct — it eliminates a dead code path and a misleading log line. The validator API TLS works the same as before, using the JDK's built-in SSL provider.

## Documentation

- [ ] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [ ] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Medium risk because it upgrades the core REST framework (Javalin/Jetty) and changes how routes, exception handling, Swagger docs, and auth middleware are registered, which could affect request handling and startup behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Upgrades the REST API stack to `io.javalin` `7.0.1` (and switches rendering to `javalin-rendering-thymeleaf`), updating build/dependency configuration accordingly.
> 
> Migrates REST API initialization to Javalin 7 patterns by registering **all routes, filters, and exception handlers inside** the `Javalin.create(config -> ...)` block, including Swagger docs route registration and host-allowlist/auth `beforeMatched` hooks. Password/token file creation is moved to `RestApiBuilder.build()` via `ensurePasswordFile()` (and `RestApi` is simplified accordingly), and tests/stubs are updated for the new Javalin 7 `Context` API.

title: Rest API virtual threads
body:
## Summary

  - Add two experimental CLI flags to enable virtual threads for REST API request handling, disabled by default:
    - `--Xrest-api-virtual-threads-enabled` (boolean, default `false`)
    - `--Xrest-api-virtual-threads-max-threads` (int, default `200`)
  - Uses Jetty 12's native [`VirtualThreads.Configurable`](https://jetty.org/docs/jetty/12/programming-guide/arch/threads.html#virtual-threads) API: acceptors and selectors remain on platform threads,
   only request handling is dispatched to a bounded virtual thread pool

  ## Motivation

  Teku's REST API serves workloads where cheap, plentiful threads improve throughput and reduce latency. Without virtual threads, all workloads share Jetty's default `QueuedThreadPool` of 200 platform threads (~1MB stack each). Under load, thread exhaustion causes request queuing and timeouts. [Virtual threads](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/core/virtual-threads.html) remove this bottleneck — they are lightweight (~few KB vs ~1MB per platform thread) and scheduled by the JVM rather than the OS.

  Two categories of REST API workloads benefit:

  ### Long-lived SSE connections

  `GET /eth/v1/events` holds a connection open per client indefinitely. Each connected client pins a platform thread for the lifetime of the subscription. With many monitoring tools or validator clients subscribed, this directly reduces the thread pool available for other requests. Virtual threads make these long-lived connections essentially free.

  ### Long-running async request handlers

  Several endpoints occupy a handler thread while waiting for an async operation to complete via `SafeFuture`, like state queries triggering regeneration, blob retrieval with P2P download, and even block production (external builder calls).

  In all these cases, the handler thread is held until the future completes. Virtual threads allow many such requests to be in-flight concurrently without exhausting the pool.

  ## Configuration

  The default `maxConcurrentTasks` of 200 matches Jetty's default `QueuedThreadPool` max threads, so enabling virtual threads is a neutral change in terms of max concurrency. Operators can tune it
  higher if needed since virtual threads are cheap.

  --Xrest-api-virtual-threads-enabled        # enables virtual threads (default: false)
  --Xrest-api-virtual-threads-max-threads=200 # max concurrent virtual threads (default: 200)

## Documentation

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**

> **Overview**

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Replay execution payload for Gloas state regeneration:
The state regeneration cache `CachingTaskQueue` uses soft references to cache intermediate states. In practice, the cache usually had a state very close to the target, often just 1 slot away. When only 1 block needs to be replayed, the `latestBlockHash` happens to be correct (it was set by the execution payload that ran right before that state was cached).
A bug surfaces when 2 or more blocks need to be replayed from a cached intermediate state, because the gap between block processing and execution payload processing becomes visible.

title: Fix swagger-ui failing to serve static files from JAR in Docker
body:
Jetty 12 (introduced with the Javalin 7 upgrade) uses URLResourceFactory to verify classpath static file directories via URLConnection.getInputStream(). On Linux, this throws FileNotFoundException for JAR directory entries, causing Teku to fail at startup when swagger UI is enabled in Docker.

Fix by resolving the swagger-ui webjar to a real filesystem path before passing it to Javalin. When running from an unpacked directory (development), the path is used directly. When running from a JAR (Docker), the webjar contents are extracted to a temp directory and served via Location.EXTERNAL, which uses Jetty's PathResourceFactory (NIO) and avoids the URLConnection issue.

Closes #10512

title: remove cache contention
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Remove cache contention by replacing the LRUCache by an Indexed Array cache for validator public keys and an Concurrent Map backed cache for the validator indices.

## Fixed Issue(s)
<!-- Please link to fixed issue(s) here using format: fixes #<issue number> -->
<!-- Example: "fixes #2" -->

## Documentation

- [ ] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [ ] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Swaps core state-transition caches from synchronized `LRUCache` to new non-evicting `ArrayIndexedCache` and `ConcurrentMapCache`, which can change memory growth characteristics and relies on relaxed concurrency semantics (possible extra cache misses). Changes affect frequently-hit validator/builder lookups during state transitions, so regressions would impact performance or correctness assumptions around cached indices.
> 
> **Overview**
> Reduces cache contention in state transition hot paths by replacing large `LRUCache` instances with new cache implementations optimized for concurrency and index-based keys.
> 
> `TransitionCaches` now stores validator/builder public keys in `ArrayIndexedCache` (indexed by `UInt64::intValue`) and uses `ConcurrentMapCache` for builder index lookups; `ValidatorIndexCache` similarly moves from an unbounded synchronized `LRUCache` to a `ConcurrentMapCache`.
> 
> Adds the new `ArrayIndexedCache` and `ConcurrentMapCache` implementations, plus a JMH `CacheContentionBenchmark` and unit tests for `ArrayIndexedCache` (including a stress-style concurrency test).
> 
> <sup>Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit 1d0b4285e33531f9523d3bf64a2c9b666b4621db. This will update automatically on new commits. Configure [here](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot).</sup>

> Introduces **`SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelopeContents`** SSZ/schema and refactors data-column sidecar construction to accept blobs/proofs from either the cache or envelope contents.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds a new persisted data type and KV-store column with associated pruning logic; bugs here could cause envelope loss or DB incompatibilities during finalization/pruning.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Adds persistent storage for Gloas blinded execution payload envelopes.** `StorageUpdate` now carries `blindedExecutionPayloadEnvelopesByBlockRoot` plus an `executionPayloadEnvelopesEnabled` gate, and `StoreTransactionUpdatesFactory` derives envelopes from execution payloads when the spec supports Gloas.

> **Extends the KV-store schema and DB APIs** to read/write `SignedBlindedExecutionPayloadEnvelope`s (new column + serializer) and to delete envelopes when non-canonical blocks are pruned while retaining those for canonical/finalized blocks; includes new integration/unit/property tests and a new SSZ slot-extraction helper (`ExecutionPayloadEnvelopeInvariants`).

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Introduces a new `ptc_window` field and epoch-processing logic that affects Gloas state schema/serialization and PTC duty selection, so spec/state transitions and API duties could change if the cache is incorrect. Also updates test infrastructure defaults (validator counts) which may subtly alter existing test assumptions.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates Teku’s consensus-spec alignment to `v1.7.0-alpha.4`, including bumping reference-test versions and adjusting which reference tests are discovered/run.
> 
> Implements **cached Payload Timeliness Committee selection** for Gloas by adding a new `ptc_window` field to `BeaconStateGloas` (schemas, JSON schema, schema registry, and state builders), initializing it on the Gloas fork upgrade, carrying it through the Heze upgrade, and updating it each epoch via a new `processPtcWindow` hook.
> 
> Refactors PTC computation to separate `computePtc` from `getPtc` (which now reads from `ptc_window`), adjusts committee query bounds (`minSeedLookahead`) and avoids slot-validation during epoch processing, updates `getPtcDuties` messaging/assumptions, and aligns/rewires reference-test executors (notably gossip/networking test packaging and additional SSZ-static ignores).
>

body:

## Documentation

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches fork-choice late-block reorg decision paths and how block timeliness is recorded/queried, so subtle behavioral differences could affect head selection and FCU suppression. Changes are mostly a refactor but now rely on new context/plumbing and a new timeliness tracker.
> 
> **Overview**

title: Add Gossip Beacon Block Reference Test Executor
body:
New file: GossipBeaconBlockTestExecutor.java

  Implements the consensus spec reference tests for networking/gossip_beacon_block. The executor:

  Setup:

  - Loads meta.yaml (topic, blocks, messages, current_time_ms, bls_setting, finalized_checkpoint)
  - Builds an in-memory StorageSystem + RecentChainData initialized from state.ssz_snappy
  - Constructs a full ForkChoice with InlineEventThread, TickProcessor, and a stub execution layer
  - Advances the clock to current_time_ms via forkChoice.onTick()

  Block pre-loading (the blocks[] list):
  - Loads each block from file. Blocks marked failed: true are recorded in failedBlockRoots but not imported — a NOOP BLS verifier would accept them despite invalid signatures, so importing would corrupt the store
  - Valid blocks are imported via forkChoice.onBlock() to build up chain state

  Finalized checkpoint handling (two variants):
  - block field → real block root; committed to the store via StoreTransaction
  - root field → raw hex (possibly fake/non-existent); stored as customFinalizedCheckpoint for executor-level ancestry checks, since StoreTransaction.commit() requires the block to exist in the store

  Message validation loop:
  - Advances clock to current_time_ms + offset_ms per message
  - Two short-circuit rejection paths before calling BlockGossipValidator: a. Parent block is in failedBlockRoots → assert reject (validator would return SAVE_FOR_FUTURE since it can't distinguish "parent not seen" from "parent invalid") b. Custom finalized checkpoint present → replicate the ancestry check using forkChoiceStrategy.getAncestor() and assert reject if the block doesn't descend from the checkpoint
  - Calls blockGossipValidator.validate() and asserts the result matches expected: valid→ACCEPT, reject→REJECT, ignore→IGNORE or SAVE_FOR_FUTURE

  Modified: GossipTests.java
  - Imports GossipBeaconBlockTestExecutor
  - Changes networking/gossip_beacon_block mapping from TestExecutor.IGNORE_TESTS to new GossipBeaconBlockTestExecutor()

title: Bug fix: SlashingProtectedValidatorSource now wraps external signers added via API with slashing protection.
body:
The bug: When a validator key was added via the validator API using an external signer (URL-based), the addValidator(BLSPublicKey, Optional<URL>) override simply delegated to the underlying source without wrapping the returned signer in a SlashingProtectedSigner. This meant no local slashing protection was applied until the node restarted (at which point keys are loaded through the normal path that does wrap them).

  The fix: The addValidator(BLSPublicKey, Optional<URL>) override now delegates to the shared addSlashingProtectedValidator() helper (extracted from the keystore-based addValidator method), so both add paths wrap the returned signer identically.

  Test added: addValidatorWithSignerUrl_shouldWrapWithSlashingProtectedSigner — verifies that the signer returned from the URL-based add path is a SlashingProtectedSigner by confirming the second signBlock call on the same block+fork fails with a slashing violation.

body:
## PR Description

Harden GitHub Actions permissions and reusable workflow calls under restricted repo defaults.

- Add explicit `actions: read` / caller permissions where reusable workflows and artifact downloads require them (`ci.yml`, `publish-release.yml`)
- Remove unnecessary `secrets: inherit` from matrix test workflow calls
- Split Docker publishing from signing/attestation so `id-token: write` is limited to the signing job (`publish-docker.yml`)
- Add explicit `contents: read` defaults to simple read-only workflows
- Restrict the CLA workflow job to PR-related events/comments only

No intended CI behavior change beyond permission scoping, workflow validation fixes, and reduced token/secret exposure.
