title: Avoid quadratic BLS verification onboarding builders at Gloas fork
body:
## Problem

Fixes #11154.

`onboardBuildersFromPendingDeposits` (the one-time builder onboarding at the Gloas fork) calls `isPendingValidator(pendingDeposits, pubkey)` for every builder-credential deposit whose pubkey is not yet a builder. That helper rescans the entire accumulated pending-deposit list and performs a BLS `is_valid_deposit_signature` verification for every entry with a matching pubkey. When one pubkey is repeated across many deposits, this is quadratic in the number of same-pubkey deposits.

The existing `verifiedPendingValidatorPubkeys` cache only memoized **positive** results, so it does not help pubkeys that are *not* pending validators — e.g. spam deposits with invalid signatures — which re-run the full scan on every occurrence.

Observed on `glamsterdam-devnet-8`: the pre-fork pending-deposit queue had ~16k deposits with a single spam pubkey repeated ~5.3k times (with builder withdrawal credentials). Every Teku node pinned a core in this method and never advanced past the fork slot; thread dumps showed one `beaconchain-async` thread runnable in `blst core_verify` ← `isValidDepositSignature` ← `isPendingValidator` ← `onboardBuildersFromPendingDeposits` for 25+ minutes. Downstream this surfaced misleadingly as `Unable to import blocks: DATA_NOT_AVAILABLE` sync failures.

## Fix

Maintain the set of pubkeys that already have a valid-signature deposit in the queue **incrementally**, as deposits are appended, so the pending-validator check becomes an O(1) set lookup instead of an O(queue) rescan-and-verify.

A non-builder-credential deposit is the only kind of append that can newly make its pubkey a pending validator (existing-validator deposits short-circuit earlier; builder-credential deposits are appended only when the pubkey is *already* a pending validator, and are otherwise onboarded or dropped). So its signature is verified exactly once at that point and the pubkey recorded. This is behaviourally equivalent to the previous code — `pendingValidatorPubkeys.contains(pubkey)` returns the same result `isPendingValidator(pendingDeposits, pubkey)` would — while doing at most one BLS verification per non-builder deposit (linear), matching the spec note that implementations SHOULD validate pending-deposit signatures and cache the results.

## Test

Adds `GloasStateUpgradeTest.shouldDropRepeatedBuilderDepositsWithInvalidSignaturesAndKeepEth1Deposits`, which puts 256 builder-credential deposits sharing one pubkey (invalid signatures) plus a few eth1 deposits into the pre-fork queue and asserts the upgrade onboards no builders, drops the invalid builder deposits, and keeps the eth1 deposits. Before this change that scenario triggers the quadratic path.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches Gloas fork-transition deposit handling, which can change which deposits become builders vs stay queued. Intended to be equivalent, but a logic error would affect consensus at the fork.
> 
> **Overview**
> Stops Gloas fork builder onboarding from re-scanning the pending-deposit queue (and re-verifying BLS signatures) for every repeated builder-credential deposit.
> 
> `onboardBuildersFromPendingDeposits` now incrementally records pubkeys that already have a valid-signature non-builder deposit, so the pending-validator check is an O(1) set lookup. Invalid repeated builder deposits are still dropped; ETH1 deposits stay in the queue. A test asserts signature verification stays linear for that spam pattern.
>

> [!NOTE]

> 
> **Overview**
> Multipeer forward sync now **cancels in-flight batch imports** when sync aborts or a batch import future is cancelled, instead of leaving block/payload work running and stacking on retries.
> 
> **BatchImporter** returns a cancellable future that tracks the active block import, execution-payload import, or parent-envelope fetch and cancels that work when the batch is cancelled. > **BatchSync** keeps the current import future and calls `cancel(true)` from `abort()`. **SyncStallDetector** raises import stall thresholds from 180s to 300s to account for heavier post-DA sync work.

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->

## PR Description
We have a duplication of `--Xbuilder-boost-factor` and `--builder-bid-compare-factor` but the new one is VC specific and the other one is BN one. Given from Gloas onwards, VC will configure the builder boost factor entirely, we wouldn't need the old one which is BN specific anyways. For the moment, I made all new ones hidden until we schedule mainnet. Also this change doesn't include proposer config changes, which we will do at a later stage.

**Renames**
  - RequestAuth → BuilderRequestAuth, SignedRequestAuth → SignedBuilderRequestAuth (classes, schemas, tests, JSON
    fixtures) — aligns naming with the spec.

**New signing support**
  - Added signBuilderRequestAuth(BuilderRequestAuth) to Signer and all implementations (LocalSigner, DeletableSigner,
    SlashingProtectedSigner, ExternalSigner, NoOpSigner).
  - Added corresponding signing root to SigningRootUtil and a domain constant in Domain.

**VC-side builder config assembly**
  - New BuilderOptions CLI class exposes --builder-urls, --builder-min-bid, and --builder-boost-factor flags; wired into
    ValidatorOptions and ValidatorConfig.
  - New BuilderConfigProvider: for each configured builder URL, signs a BuilderRequestAuth (keyed to URL bytes + slot)
    using the proposing validator's signer, then assembles a BuilderConfig with signed BuilderEntry objects. Returns
    Optional.empty() for pre-Gloas slots.
  - BlockProductionDuty now fetches the BuilderConfig from BuilderConfigProvider and passes it through to
    createUnsignedBlock, so the BN receives the VC's builder preferences at block creation time.
  - BlockDutyFactory and ValidatorClientService wired up with the new provider.

related to #10822

> **Overview**
> This PR hardens **multi-peer batch sync** and **Fulu data-column availability** so large catch-up imports don’t stall or fail prematurely.
> 
> **Batch import:** `BatchSync` now uses `handleAsync` on batch import futures and routes exceptional completion through `onImportFailed`, which logs, releases importing state, and treats the outcome like `IMPORT_FAILED` so sync can retry instead of hanging. Import pause warnings include batch slot ranges; chain-switch while an import is in flight is covered when the delayed import fails exceptionally.
> 
> **DAS during sync:** `DataColumnSidecarAvailabilityChecker` applies a **5× slot-duration timeout** for blocks more than one epoch behind the current slot (batch sync can pull ~125 slots at once). `DasSamplerBasicImpl` only soft-evicts sampling trackers when eviction is **safe** (failed sampling or sampling complete and the block is already satisfied in chain/store), keeping trackers needed for pending imports.
> 
> **Sidecar retrieval:** `SimpleSidecarRetriever` skips stale matches, cancels in-flight RPC when gossip satisfies the request, and **does not penalize peer scores** for client-side cancellations.
> 
> `SyncConfig` comments clarify the recently-sampled-blocks soft limit vs the sampler hard cap.

title: Remote validator client: use v2 proposer duties endpoint from Fulu
body:
Summary

  The /eth/v2/validator/duties/proposer/{epoch} endpoint was already implemented server-side (GetProposerDutiesV2), but the remote validator client was always calling the deprecated v1 endpoint and ignoring the isFuluCompatible flag.

  At Fulu the dependent root calculation changes: BlockProposalUtilFulu returns previousTargetRoot for current-epoch duties and currentTargetRoot for next-epoch duties, whereas the pre-Fulu logic does the opposite. BlockDutyScheduler uses the
  fork-correct local calculation to check whether fetched duties are still fresh after a head event. If the remote client fetched via v1 (which forces PHASE0 logic server-side), the returned dependent_root would never match the locally computed
  value at Fulu, causing duties to appear stale on every head event.

  Changes

  - ValidatorApiMethod: add GET_PROPOSER_DUTIES_V2 (eth/v2/validator/duties/proposer/:epoch)
  - GetProposerDutiesV2Request: new request handler for the v2 endpoint (mirrors v1 handler)
  - OkHttpValidatorTypeDefClient: expose getProposerDutiesV2(epoch)
  - RemoteValidatorApiHandler: dispatch to v2 when isFuluCompatible=true (which BlockProductionDutyLoader always passes), fall back to v1 otherwise (for the deprecated beacon API v1 path)
  - Tests covering both isFuluCompatible=false (v1) and isFuluCompatible=true (v2) paths

  Note on "required from Gloas"

  The beacon-APIs spec says v2 is only required from Gloas in the sense that other clients aren't obligated to implement it before then. The dependent root semantics change at Fulu, so v2 is needed for correctness from Fulu onwards — restricting it
  to Gloas would cause incorrect dependent roots at Fulu.

  fixes #10092

## Documentation

- [X] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [X] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes which beacon API proposer-duties endpoint remote validators use, affecting dependent_root matching and block proposal scheduling correctness on forked networks.
> 
> **Overview**
> The remote validator client always used **`GET /eth/v1/validator/duties/proposer/{epoch}`**, so **`dependent_root`** from the beacon node could disagree with local Fulu+ duty checks and make proposer duties look stale on every head event.
> 
> This PR wires **`GET /eth/v2/validator/duties/proposer/{epoch}`** through **`ValidatorApiMethod`**, **`GetProposerDutiesV2Request`**, and **`OkHttpValidatorTypeDefClient.getProposerDutiesV2`**. **`RemoteValidatorApiHandler`** takes **`Spec`** and calls v2 when **`spec.isMilestoneSupported(SpecMilestone.GLOAS)`**; otherwise it keeps the v1 path. The **`isFuluCompatible`** argument is still logged on the v1 path but is not used to pick the endpoint.
> 
> Tests update handler construction for the new **`Spec`** parameter and assert that a Gloas-scheduled spec uses v2 and never hits v1.
>

title: Validate custody_group_count in MetaData path to prevent ArithmeticException
body:
Summary:

  MetadataDasPeerCustodyTracker.onPeerMetadataUpdate called UInt64.intValue() (which uses Math.toIntExact) on the peer-advertised custody_group_count without a bounds check. A malicious peer advertising a value greater than Integer.MAX_VALUE would
  cause an ArithmeticException on every ping cycle (~10s), logged at ERROR level, with the peer's custody state silently left at 0.

  The ENR path (NodeRecordConverter.validateAndParseDasCustodyGroupCount) already performs this check. This change brings the MetaData path into line: values exceeding NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS are filtered out before intValue() is called, and the
  peer is treated as minimum-custody — the same outcome as the ENR path.

  MetadataDasPeerCustodyTracker now takes numberOfCustodyGroups in its constructor; BeaconChainController passes the already-computed maxGroups value.


## Documentation

- [X] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [X] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes P2P metadata handling for DAS peer custody counts; low blast radius but affects how malicious or malformed peers are classified for column retrieval.
> 
> **Overview**
> **MetaData peer custody counts are now bounded** before they are stored, matching the existing ENR validation behavior.
> 
> `MetadataDasPeerCustodyTracker` takes the spec’s max custody groups (`maxGroups` from `BeaconChainController`) and **ignores** `custody_group_count` values above that limit instead of calling `UInt64.intValue()` unconditionally. That avoids repeated `ArithmeticException` errors (and ERROR logs on metadata/ping cycles) when a peer advertises an oversized count, and leaves the peer treated as **zero custody** for DAS routing.
> 
> Tests cover the over-max case; wiring passes `maxGroups` into the tracker constructor.
>

title: Enforce StrictNoSign key field in GossipWireValidator
body:
## Summary

- `GossipWireValidator` checked `from`, `signature`, and `seqno` but omitted the `key` field (protobuf field 6).
- A peer sending a gossip message with `key` set would pass Teku's validator; Teku would relay the bytes verbatim to all mesh peers.
- Any strict-enforcing implementation (e.g. go-libp2p-pubsub / Prysm) that receives the forwarded message detects the forbidden field, charges the invalid delivery to Teku, and disconnects.
- Fix: add the missing `hasKey()` arm; update the class javadoc to list all four prohibited fields.

gossipsub spec reference: https://github.com/libp2p/specs/blob/master/pubsub/README.md#signature-policy-options

Fixes #11186


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Small, spec-aligned inbound validation change in P2P gossip with unit tests; reduces risk of relaying non-compliant messages rather than introducing new behavior for valid traffic.
> 
> **Overview**
> Closes a **StrictNoSign** gap in `GossipWireValidator`: inbound gossip protobufs that set the **`key`** field (field 6) were accepted and could be forwarded unchanged, while stricter peers treat that as invalid and may penalize or disconnect the relaying node.
> 
> The validator now rejects messages with **`hasKey()`**, matching the existing checks for **`from`**, **`signature`**, and **`seqno`**, and the class docs list all four forbidden fields. A new **`GossipWireValidatorTest`** covers clean payloads and each prohibited field; **CHANGELOG** records the fix (Fixes #11186).

We have had many instances where “random” potential contributors submit PRs for areas unsolicited and without prior discussion, etc.

title: Embed latest execution payload bid in Gloas genesis block body
body:
## PR Description

Teku fails to start from a Gloas genesis state produced by the ethpandaops genesis generator (e.g. a kurtosis devnet with `gloas_fork_epoch: 0`):

```
FATAL - Teku failed to start
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Genesis block root 0x087b43… does not match genesis state latest block root 0xfce6bd…
```

The Gloas spec does not define `initialize_beacon_state_from_eth1`, so the genesis block body is not spec-defined. The convention used by the ethpandaops genesis generator (`eth-beacon-genesis`), Lighthouse and Lodestar is an empty `BeaconBlockBody` whose (unsigned) `signed_execution_payload_bid.message` is the state's `latest_execution_payload_bid` (parent block hash = EL genesis hash, `execution_requests_root` = root of empty `ExecutionRequests`). Teku hashed a fully empty body instead, both when synthesising the genesis block from a state (`BeaconBlock.fromGenesisState`) and when generating a genesis state itself (`GenesisGenerator`), so `latest_block_header.body_root` never matched.

Changes:
- Add `BeaconBlockBodySchema.createGenesisBody(genesisState)` (empty body by default) and override it for Gloas to embed the state's latest execution payload bid.
- Use it in `BeaconBlock.fromGenesisState` (also fixes the genesis block root used by `BeaconStateUtil.getDutyDependentRoot`) and in `GenesisGenerator`, so Teku-generated Gloas genesis states are consistent with other clients.
- Fix the `AnchorPoint.fromGenesisState` error message, which had the two roots swapped.
- Tests: Gloas `AnchorPoint`/`GenesisGenerator` tests, plus a regression test loading a real `genesis.ssz` + `config.yaml` produced by `ethpandaops/ethereum-genesis-generator:6.2.1` (minimal preset, `GLOAS_FORK_EPOCH: 0`).

Verified with a kurtosis devnet (minimal preset, `gloas_fork_epoch: 0`, besu + this build of Teku): Teku now starts and follows the chain.

title: Reject inclusion lists containing an empty transaction
body:
## PR Description

Follow-up for ethereum/consensus-specs#5576 (issue ethereum/consensus-specs#5575). The spec keeps the raw transaction byte bound (`MAX_TRANSACTIONS_BYTES_PER_INCLUSION_LIST`) and derives the `inclusion_list` gossip message bound from it as the size of a list of one-byte transactions (`MAX_SIGNED_INCLUSION_LIST_SIZE = 41112`); that derivation is only finite if every transaction is non-empty, so the gossip rules gain `[REJECT] every transaction in message.transactions is non-empty`.

This adds that check to `SignedInclusionListValidator` (with a test). Teku has no topic-specific gossip size constant for inclusion lists, so nothing else changes. Lodestar counterpart: ChainSafe/lodestar#9936.

## Fixed Issue(s)

ethereum/consensus-specs#5575

title: Derive the genesis duty dependent root from the state's latest block header
body:
## PR Description

Regression from #11190 when a fork is scheduled **after** genesis (e.g. a kurtosis devnet with `gloas_fork_epoch: 1`): Teku's validators get no attestation duties for the fork epoch.

```
ERROR - Failed to request validator duties for epoch 1. Retrying after delay.
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Expected a Gloas state but got: BeaconStateFuluImpl
  at BeaconStateGloas.required(BeaconStateGloas.java:51)
  at BeaconBlockBodySchemaGloasImpl.createGenesisBody(BeaconBlockBodySchemaGloasImpl.java:181)
  at BeaconBlock.fromGenesisState(BeaconBlock.java:64)
  at BeaconStateUtil.getDutyDependentRoot(BeaconStateUtil.java:217)
  at BeaconStateUtil.getCurrentDutyDependentRoot(BeaconStateUtil.java:81)
  at AttesterDutiesGenerator.getAttesterDutiesFromIndicesAndState(AttesterDutiesGenerator.java:44)
```

The duties of the first epoch after genesis depend on the genesis block root. `BeaconStateUtil.getDutyDependentRoot` rebuilt it with `BeaconBlock.fromGenesisState(schemaDefinitions, state)` using **its own milestone's** body schema — the duties for epoch 1 are computed by `spec.atEpoch(1)`, i.e. Gloas — against the Fulu genesis state. Before #11190 that silently produced a Gloas-empty-body root (wrong, but harmless); now `createGenesisBody` correctly requires a Gloas state and throws. Observed on a 4-node devnet as exactly 50% target/head votes in epoch 1 (both Teku nodes attested at slots 6, 7, 16, 17 and nothing in 8–15); `Failed to publish proposer preferences` fails through the same path.

Fix: derive the root from the state itself — `BeaconBlockHeader.fromState(state).getRoot()` (latest block header with the state root filled in). At genesis that is the genesis block root for whatever the genesis fork is, and for a state at the dependent slot it is the root of that slot's block; no block body schema is involved. The now unused `SchemaDefinitions` is removed from `BeaconStateUtil` and its `SpecLogic*` call sites (ErrorProne `UnusedVariable`).

Tests: new `getCurrentDutyDependentRoot_genesisStateWithForkScheduledAfterGenesis` (Gloas at epoch 1 — throws before, passes after); the existing genesis test now builds a state whose latest block header carries the genesis body root, as a real genesis state does. `BeaconStateUtilTest`, `AnchorPointTest`, `GenesisGeneratorTest`, `ValidatorApiHandlerTest` pass.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Follow-up to #11190.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01YHCg1Q6QaZn8rPjB7za3UB

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core validator duty root calculation used for attestation scheduling; change is narrow and well-tested but affects consensus-adjacent behavior on post-genesis fork boundaries.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes validator attestation duties failing on the **first epoch after genesis** when a later fork (e.g. Gloas at epoch 1) is scheduled. Duty computation for that epoch uses the fork milestone’s `BeaconStateUtil` against the pre-fork genesis state; rebuilding the genesis block via `BeaconBlock.fromGenesisState` with the later fork’s body schema threw `Expected a Gloas state but got: BeaconStateFuluImpl`, so duties never loaded.

title: Replace modulo test sharding with timing-based shard planning
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Modulo-by-name-sort has no idea which test classes are slow, so a shard that happens to draw a couple of heavyweight classes gates the whole suite. I pulled real JUnit XML from a recent CI run and simulated a timing-based bin-pack against the current modulo split: slowest-shard time drops 46% on integrationTests, 38% on propertyTests, 33% on unitTests, 22% on acceptanceTests. referenceTests only gained 10% (~20s) because its ~63k generated spec-test-case classes are already near-uniform in size, so I left it as is.

This replaces the modulo split with a greedy LPT (longest-processing-time-first) bin-pack, fed by per-class timings cached from previous master runs.

### Changes

- `collate-junit-reports` now restores the last cached per-class timings after gathering a run's JUnit XML, merges in this run's durations (a class missing from this run, e.g. because its shard failed, keeps its last known timing instead of being dropped), and caches the merged result under a fresh key. The cache save only runs on `master` pushes, so PR runs read the baseline but never overwrite it.
- `matrix-tests-template.yml` gets a new `planShards` job that runs before the matrix fans out: restores the cached timings, scans the current test classes, and bin-packs them into shards. A class with no cached timing yet (new class, or first run ever) gets the average of known classes as its weight, so it doesn't distort the plan. The plan is uploaded as an artifact; each shard job downloads it and reads its own class list instead of running the modulo split.

Since unitTests, integrationTests, propertyTests, and acceptanceTests all call this same reusable workflow, this covers all four suites with one change. `referenceTests` has its own separate sharding job and isn't touched here, given the measured gain didn't justify duplicating the wiring.

Side effect: one extra small job (`planShards`) per suite on the critical path, ~10-20s of checkout + cache restore + a bin-packing script, in exchange for the 22-46% cut on whichever shard currently gates the suite.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes Consensys/teku-internal#316

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes CI test distribution and caching behavior; mis-sharding or stale timings could skew wall-clock time or leave gaps, but failures in capture are non-blocking and PRs cannot overwrite the master timing baseline.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces **alphabetical modulo sharding** with **greedy LPT bin-packing** across 12 shards for unit, integration, property, and acceptance tests (via `matrix-tests-template.yml`). A new **`planShards`** job restores cached per-class durations, assigns classes to shards by estimated runtime, and uploads `plan.json`; each matrix shard downloads that plan instead of using `(NR-1) % total`.
> 
> Adds **`.github/actions/capture-test-timings`**, which pulls JUnit XML artifacts, aggregates testcase times by `classname`, merges with the previous cache (failed/missing shards keep last-known times), and **writes the cache only on `master`**. **`ci.yml`** wires four standalone post-test jobs (`*CaptureTimings`) with `continue-on-error` so org action-allowlist rules do not abort timing capture alongside report collation.
> 
> **Reference tests** are unchanged and still use modulo sharding.

body:

## PR Description

Numbers before, Macbook M4 Max, Mainnet:
epoch transition: 18-20 seconds
1 slot: 300-400ms

Numbers after part1:
epoch transition: 2 seconds
1 slot: 300-400ms

First part mainly addresses slow epoch transition when we do several runs on the same block inside calculator.
*Speed up fast confirmation with memoization and one-pass chain scoring*

Memoize the per-slot calculator queries (slot committees and ranges,
adversarial weight and safety threshold per balance source, current
target score, honest FFG support, equivocator set) and score a whole
chain segment in a single pass over the active validator set instead of
one pass per block. Add a JMH benchmark covering both scoring paths.


## Fixed Issue(s)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes performance paths in fork-choice fast confirmation (confirmed root and safe block), where correctness bugs could affect execution-layer safe head; behavior is intended to match prior scoring with broad new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Speeds up Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR) work** by cutting repeated per-slot computation and replacing per-block validator scans with a single pass when scoring a linear chain segment.
> 
> `FastConfirmationCalculator` now **memoizes** slot committees, committee unions over slot ranges, adversarial weight, safety thresholds, equivocator indices, current-target FFG score, and honest FFG support for the lifetime of a per-slot calculator instance. **Equivocation scoring** walks only known equivocators instead of building full committees when none exist.
> 
> The main algorithmic change is **`computeChainAttestationScores`**: one active-validator pass buckets votes by the latest chain block they support, then prefix-sums to produce the same attestation scores as repeated `getAttestationScore`. **`findLatestConfirmedDescendant`** and **`isConfirmedChainSafe`** use precomputed scores via `isOneConfirmedWithSupport`, sharing one batch score across both walk phases and avoiding a second ancestor walk.
> 
> Adds a **JMH benchmark** (`FastConfirmationBenchmark`) for the ~2-epoch warm-up catch-up path and batch vs per-block scoring at 100k/1M validators. **`ForkChoiceFastConfirmation`** comments are updated to note batch scoring while keeping the widened warm-up segment timeout. **Unit tests** cover batch equivalence (including Gloas FULL votes), binary-search ancestry on chains with empty slots, and memoization behavior.

title: FCR optimization part2:  Reuse cached checkpoint states and parallelize fast confirmation scoring
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
On top of #11212, which should be merged first:

Reuse cached checkpoint states and parallelize fast confirmation scoring
    
    Load the pulled-up head state through the store's checkpoint-state
    cache instead of replaying the epoch transition, read a flat
    zeroed-balances list instead of materializing validators, resolve each
    distinct latest message once, and chunk the vote scan across the common
    pool. Prefetch the next epoch's balance source off the critical path at
    epoch boundaries.


## Fixed Issue(s)
<!-- Please link to fixed issue(s) here using format: fixes #<issue number> -->
<!-- Example: "fixes #2" -->

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches fork-choice confirmation logic and parallel vote scoring; behavior is guarded by existing parity tests, but incorrect scoring or prefetch timeout handling could affect confirmed-root selection at epoch boundaries.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR speeds up Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR) work by changing **where** states come from and **how** validator weights are scanned, without altering the rule’s semantics.
> 
> **Pulled-up head state** is no longer derived inside `FastConfirmationCalculator` via `process_slots`. `FastConfirmationStateLoader` now supplies `pulledUpHeadState` directly—checkpoint state `(current_epoch, head)` when the head block is before the epoch start, otherwise the head block state—so epoch-boundary work is shared with attestation processing instead of replayed on the FCR runner.
> 
> **Attestation scoring** uses the cached flat `getEffectiveActiveUnslashedBalances` list (zero = skip) instead of walking every `Validator`. `computeChainAttestationScores` parallelizes the vote scan on the common pool, caches distinct latest messages in a `VoteKey` map, and merges per-chunk support buckets. `computeCurrentTargetScore` filters by message epoch first and memoizes checkpoint resolution per voted root to avoid crashes on pruned blocks.
> 
> On the **last slot of each epoch**, `FastConfirmationTracker` fire-and-forgets prefetch of the next epoch’s current balance-source checkpoint state and its scoring balances, with a one-slot timeout on a **copy** of the shared regeneration future so epoch-start slots are not blocked or failed by slow prefetch.
>

title: Fix dropping from SYNCING to IN_SYNC while far behind the head
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

## Issue: how we drop to `IN_SYNC` while far behind

  `SyncStateTracker.updateCurrentState()` chose `IN_SYNC` purely from `!syncActive` — it never
  checked how far behind the head actually was. Forward sync deactivates whenever it has no target
  chain to work on, which includes "all peers dropped" and "stalled, waiting to retry". Both OOM
  logs show exactly that: sync deactivates with the head still 850–1100 slots back, and the node
  logs `Syncing completed` and reports `IN_SYNC`.

  ## What it leads to
  
  `SyncState.isInSync()` → `ForkChoiceNotifier.inSync = true` →
  `ProposersDataManager.calculatePayloadBuildingAttributes` passes its `!inSync` guard and asks for
  the state at `currentSlot + 1` on top of a head ~1000 slots older.
  `StateAtSlotTask.regenerateFromState` replays that gap: ~27–34 epoch transitions, each
  materialising ~1M `Validator` SSZ views plus `ValidatorStatus` objects.

  It also runs many times over:
  
  - fired every slot and on every head change;
  - each new head root is a fresh cache key;
  - `streamIntermediateSteps()` only looks back 640 slots, so a larger gap defeats rebasing and
    deduplication entirely;
  - `CachingTaskQueue` allows `availableProcessors` of them concurrently.
  
  9 GB heap exhausted → `OutOfMemoryError`.

  ## The fix

  Judge behind-ness against **the head our peers report**, not the wall-clock slot.                                                        
  `SyncStateTracker` implements `SlotEventsChannel`, re-evaluates each slot, and holds `SYNCING`
  while our head is more than `slotsPerEpoch * MAX_SEED_LOOKAHEAD` (128 slots) behind the
  peer-reported head from `Eth2Peer.getStatus().getHeadSlot()`.

  | peers | reference head | behind? |
  |---|---|---|
  | 0, `startupTargetPeerCount == 0` | none | no — standalone node, keep proposing |
  | 0, `startupTargetPeerCount > 0` | none | yes — can't trust our own head |
  | 1–2 | highest peer head | distance > 128 |
  | 3+ | 2nd-highest peer head | distance > 128 |

  Requiring two peers to agree once 3+ are connected means one peer overstating its head can't                                             
  wedge us. Sync retry is untouched — a restart just moves the node from held-`SYNCING` to
  active-`SYNCING`.

  Using peer heads rather than the current slot is the load-bearing detail: the obvious version
  (head vs current slot) deadlocks on a chain with >128 consecutive empty slots, because the held
  `SYNCING` makes `ValidatorApiHandler.isSyncActive()` reject every duty, so nobody proposes and the
  head never advances. Peer heads are equally old during such an outage, so the comparison stays
  correct.

## Fixed Issue(s)
<!-- Please link to fixed issue(s) here using format: fixes #<issue number> -->
<!-- Example: "fixes #2" -->

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes when the node reports IN_SYNC, which gates block production and payload/state regeneration; incorrect thresholds could block duties or leave heavy work enabled, though behavior is heavily covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a case where **forward sync stopping** (no peers, stall/retry) still flipped the node to **`IN_SYNC`** even when the local head was hundreds of slots behind the network.
> 
> **`SyncStateTracker`** now treats “behind the known chain head” like active sync: it stays **`SYNCING`** when the head is more than **`MAX_SEED_LOOKAHEAD` epochs** behind a **peer-reported** head (via **`RecentChainData.isHeadCloseToSlot`**), not the wall-clock slot—so long empty-slot runs do not deadlock proposing. With enough peers it uses the **second-highest** peer head; with no peers it only distrusts the local head if the node **expects peers**. It implements **`SlotEventsChannel`** for per-slot re-checks (e.g. gossip catch-up without a sync restart) and tightens **sync start/complete** logging so retries do not spam “Syncing completed”.
> 
> **`EventLogger`** adds one-time warnings for **stopped while behind** and **no peers**. **`DefaultSyncServiceFactory`** wires **`RecentChainData`** and subscribes the tracker to slot events. Changelog documents the **OOM** fix when sync stopped early.
>

title: Compare gossip payload size against the compressed bound
body:
The gossip size gate in `GossipHandler.apply()` runs on `message.getData()`, which is the snappy-compressed payload, but `Eth2TopicHandler.getMaxMessageSize()` returned `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` (10,485,760) — the *uncompressed* bound from the p2p-interface spec. Snappy encoding is not canonical, so a spec-valid, appropriately-sized message can be re-encoded to compress to more than `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` and still be accepted and forwarded by other clients. Teku rejected those as `Invalid` before ever decompressing them, which applies gossipsub's invalid-message-delivery penalty (P4) to the peer that forwarded the message, not to whoever crafted it. Enough of those and Teku prunes that mesh edge and stops taking gossip from an honest peer.

The two limits inside the process already disagreed: `LibP2PParamsFactory` computes `max_compressed_len(MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE)` for the libp2p transport, so the transport happily reassembles messages the application-level gate then rejects.

### Changes

- `Eth2TopicHandler.getMaxMessageSize()` now returns `max_compressed_len(MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE)` = 12,233,418, matching what Prysm, Lighthouse and Grandine enforce, and reuses `LibP2PParamsFactory.maxCompressedLength` rather than duplicating the formula.

- Added `Eth2TopicHandlerTest.getMaxMessageSize_shouldAllowWorstCaseSnappyExpansionOfMaxPayload`, which fails on `master`.

The uncompressed bound is still enforced downstream: `SnappyPreparedGossipMessage.uncompressPayload` passes `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` to `SnappyCompressor`, which validates the declared uncompressed length. That check previously never ran on these messages because the pre-decode gate rejected them first.

Every gossip topic handler extends `Eth2TopicHandler`, so the single fix covers all topics.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes consensus-adjacent block import failure handling; incorrect classification could either accept bad blocks or still reject good ones, but scope is limited to INTERNAL_ERROR paths with explicit allowlist and broad test coverage.
> 
> **Overview**
> Tightens when a failed block import with **`INTERNAL_ERROR`** is cached as permanently invalid. Previously, almost any internal exception (except `RejectedExecutionException`) caused the block and its descendants to be rejected until the invalid-block cache evicted the entry—so transient local failures (OOM, full queues, bugs) could wrongly blacklist canonical chain segments.

> **`BlockManager`** now uses an allowlist (`INVALID_BLOCK_INTERNAL_ERRORS`): only exceptions that clearly reflect bad block content—state transition / block processing failures, malformed SSZ or schema violations, BLS errors, and arithmetic overflow/underflow during processing—trigger `dropInvalidBlock`. Unknown or infrastructure-style errors no longer add the block to `invalidBlockRoots`.
> 
> Tests are expanded into parameterized cases for both “do not mark invalid” (e.g. `RejectedExecutionException`, OOM, `ServiceCapacityExceededException`, generic runtime errors) and “mark invalid” (the allowlisted types, including wrapped causes).

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes global process termination and async error handling; incorrect detection could exit on non-OOM errors or miss edge cases, though behavior is heavily tested and shutdown is idempotent.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a case where Teku could keep running after heap exhaustion because **OutOfMemoryError** was swallowed by async futures, suppressed subscriber/REST callbacks, or only detected via a direct `instanceof` check.
> 
> Adds **`FatalErrorHandler`**, which treats OOM (including wrapped causes and suppressed errors) as fatal, triggers shutdown **once**, and exits via a non-blocking path: graceful **`System.exit`** on a daemon thread plus a **90s watchdog** that **`Runtime.halt`s** if shutdown hooks wedge (e.g. stuck Jetty teardown).
> 
> Wires that handler into **`SafeFuture`** completion/error callbacks, **`TekuDefaultExceptionHandler`**, REST **`DefaultExceptionHandler`**, and **`ObservableValue` / `Subscribers`** when exceptions are suppressed. OOM exits use **`ERROR_EXIT_CODE`** (restart-friendly); existing fatal service/storage paths still use **`FATAL_EXIT_CODE`**. Gradle dependency rules allow **`infrastructure:subscribers`** to depend on **`exceptions`**.

title: Replace EF bootnodes with NodeOps fleet
body:
I am on the Ethereum Foundation's Node Infrastructure team (NodeOps). We run the bootnodes
that ship in this repository as the "EF" entries for mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi. We are
replacing that fleet, and we would like the new records in a release before the Glamsterdam
client releases.

### What changes

- Add five new EF bootnodes per network. Every node serves all three networks.
- Remove the legacy EF entries. The new set is a replacement, not an addition.
- Third-party bootnodes and DNS discovery roots are untouched.

### The new fleet

Five bootnodes, each serving mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi. They are geographically distributed,
multi-cloud, and dual stack (IPv4 + IPv6). Each node runs discv4 and discv5 on the EL port and
discv5 on the CL port, and the fleet spreads across several discovery implementations so one
implementation bug cannot take the whole set down.

### About the records

- The ENRs are generic bootnode records: no `eth2` field, no `tcp`, sequence number 1. Clients
  dial configured bootnodes regardless of fork, and a static list cannot be re-signed every
  fork, so we do not include fork data on purpose.
- Where an EL list accepts ENRs, we list the ENR. It covers discv4 and discv5 and carries the
  IPv6 endpoint. Enodes appear only where a list needs them, in the discovery-only form
  `enode://<pubkey>@<ip>:0?discport=<port>` (no RLPx listener).
- The records are derived from the node keys and are byte-identical across all the client
  PRs. The canonical copies are the eth-clients PRs (`metadata/bootstrap_nodes.yaml` and
  `metadata/enodes.yaml` for mainnet, sepolia and hoodi).

### Verification

- Each node answers discv4 and discv5 pings from the public internet on the advertised ports.
- The relevant tests in this repository pass with the new lists (details below).
- The legacy nodes stay online until client releases with the new records are widely deployed.
  We will announce the shutdown separately.

### Contact

Chase Wright, EF Node Infrastructure. Discord `MysticRyuujin` (ETH R&D and STEEL servers), or
chase.wright@ethereum.org.

### This repository

**Files:** `ethereum/networks/src/main/java/tech/pegasys/teku/networks/Eth2NetworkConfiguration.java`.

**Semantics:** the EF blocks in `applyMainnetNetworkDefaults`, `applySepoliaNetworkDefaults`
and `applyHoodiNetworkDefaults` swap the EF ENRs (4 / 5 / 6) for the five new CL ENRs.

**Tests:** `./gradlew :ethereum:networks:test --tests '*Eth2NetworkConfigurationTest*'` (includes
the byte-exact ENR round-trip); `spotlessCheck` clean.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Bootnode lists drive initial P2P discovery; bad or unreachable ENRs can slow peer join until clients upgrade, though this is a coordinated infra swap with no application logic changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Swaps the **Ethereum Foundation** default **discovery bootnode ENRs** in `Eth2NetworkConfiguration` for **mainnet**, **Sepolia**, and **Hoodi**. Legacy EF records are removed and replaced with **five new shared NodeOps ENRs** per network (not added on top of the old set).
> 
> **Teku**, **Prysm**, **Lighthouse**, **Nimbus**, and other third-party bootnodes in those blocks are unchanged. Only the EF-labeled entries in `applyMainnetNetworkDefaults`, `applySepoliaNetworkDefaults`, and `applyHoodiNetworkDefaults` are updated.
>

title: Enforce progressive-list soft limits at network decode time
body:
Makes sure that limits that are part of the state transition function are applied at message decoding phase (GOSSIP as well as RPC) so we early drop them. REJECT and peer downscore during sync (RPC) are ensured.

The alternative is just reordering the gossip checks so that those limits are checked earlier.
This is more invasive approach, tightening the check to the schema itself, bringing the benefit that we apply it on RPC side too (we don't need to fill a batch, start the import, to find out that some data is invalid)

related to #11228
ref: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5564

Out of scope, DAS column retrieval and other RPC consumers outside forward sync do not penalize malformed responses either; a central hook in `DefaultEth2Peer.sendEth2Request` could cover them later.

title: Updated jvm-libp2p to 1.3.7
body:
Updates relevant to jvm-libp2p 1.3.7 release.

- `maxSubscriptions`, `maxGraftMessages`, `maxPruneMessages` and `maxIWantMessageIds` no longer exist on `GossipParamsBuilder` - the byte budget covers what they covered for allocation safety.
- Subscriptions still need a count, but on the outbound side. We announce every subscribed topic in one RPC when a peer becomes active, and a peer whose limit we exceed drops the whole RPC rather than the surplus. `maxSubscriptionsPerRpc` replaces `maxSubscriptions` there.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches consensus P2P gossip configuration during a libp2p upgrade; behavior should stay equivalent for subscription batching but networking is sensitive to limit mismatches.
> 
> **Overview**
> Bumps **jvm-libp2p** from `1.3.6-RELEASE` to **`1.3.7-RELEASE`** and updates Teku’s gossip parameter wiring for the new API.
> 
> **`LibP2PParamsFactory`** no longer sets removed builder fields (`maxSubscriptions`, graft/prune message caps, `maxIWantMessageIds`); the library now relies on its byte budget for those bounds. Outbound subscription batches are capped with **`maxSubscriptionsPerRpc(200)`**, still tied to **`MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_MESSAGE`**, so Teku does not send more subscriptions per RPC than **`MaxCountTopicSubscriptionFilter`** allows inbound (peers drop the whole RPC if the limit is exceeded).
> 
> Tests were adjusted: RPC limit assertions were trimmed to what still applies, and a dedicated test checks **`maxSubscriptionsPerRpc`**.
>

title: fix: don't penalise the preceding batch's peer when two batches fail to form a chain
body:
Exclude firstBatch from the contested set in checkBatchesFormChain. At the point where the contest is applied, firstBatch is guaranteed non-empty (it came from previousNonEmptyBatch/nextNonEmptyBatch) and complete, so its peer bears no responsibility for the gap. The intermediate empty batches and secondBatch (where the fault actually lies) remain contested.

## Documentation

- [X] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [X] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes peer penalty logic in multipeer beacon sync when batches disagree; incorrect exoneration could leave bad data un-retried, but guards reduce false positives versus blindly contesting the prior batch.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Tightens which batches are marked contested** when two adjacent non-empty batches fail to chain in multipeer forward sync. Instead of always contesting from `firstBatch` through `secondBatch`, `checkBatchesFormChain` now **skips `firstBatch` only when** its last received block reaches `getLastSlot()` **and** its first block is already confirmed on the trusted chain; otherwise `firstBatch` stays in the contested set.
> 
> This addresses cases where a batch is marked complete after an empty follow-up without filling its slot range (possible hidden linking block), or where a full-range batch sits on an unconfirmed fork. **`BatchChain`** gains `batchesBetweenExclusiveStart` to contest intermediates plus `secondBatch` while leaving a verified `firstBatch` out. Tests cover partial ranges, unconfirmed forks, empty batches hiding links, and ordering when later batches arrive first.
>

title: ref test tar gz load optimization
body:
The trigger was me hating to wait ref test expansion when running ref test locally.
instead of expanding thousands of files on FS, they are transformed to a zip file that can be read as an indexed FS by java.



## Read reference test fixtures from zip archives instead of expanding them on disk

### Problem

The consensus-spec reference tests were expanded into `eth-reference-tests/src/referenceTest/resources/consensus-spec-tests/` (4.3 GB, ~332k files, ~80k directories). That tree was the dominant cost around the reference tests rather than the tests themselves:

- `generateReferenceTestClasses` declared the whole tree as an input, so Gradle fingerprinted 332k files on every up-to-date check.
- The tree lived under `src/.../resources`, so a local `./gradlew referenceTest` copied all 4.3 GB into `build/resources` (CI worked around it with `-x processReferenceTestResources`).
- CI cached the tree with `actions/cache` and shipped the whole module, fixtures included, to 8 shards as an uncompressed tar.
- Expanding the tarballs is pure filesystem metadata work (on an M4 Max: 91 s for `minimal`, 70 s of it in the kernel).

### Change

Each downloaded tarball is streamed once into a zip (`build/refTests/<version>/archives/<config>.zip`) and the tests read fixtures straight out of the archive through the JDK's built-in zip filesystem (`jdk.zipfs`). Nothing is expanded on disk anymore.

- **`ReferenceTestArchiveConverter`** (`eth-tests`): streaming tar.gz → zip with no intermediate files. Handles ustar, GNU long names and pax paths; every entry is deflated at the fastest level (mainnet: 963 MB vs 2.8 GB if `.ssz_snappy` were stored as-is). Each zip contains one top-level `<config>/` directory. Unit-tested with a small tar writer.
- **`ReferenceTestRoot`** (`eth-tests`): resolves `<config>` directories from either the archives directory (default; each zip mounted lazily, once per JVM) or a plain directory of vectors via `-Dteku.ref-test.root-dir=<dir>` (e.g. generated from a local consensus-specs checkout).
- **Finders / executors** are now filesystem-provider agnostic: no `Path.toFile()`, no cross-provider `resolve(Path)`. `TestDefinition` carries the relative path as a `/`-separated string; the generated test template passes a string too.
- **Gradle**: per-config `convertRefTests*` tasks with proper inputs/outputs replace `expandRefTests*`. The generator fingerprints 5 zips instead of the tree. The legacy fixture directory is excluded from resources. `referenceTest` gets `maxHeapSize = '2g'` because each fork holds the zip central directories in memory (~170 MB for minimal).
- **CI**: caches `build/refTests/*/archives/` instead of the tree, shards fail fast on a cache miss, `reftests.tar` no longer contains fixtures. The cache key now also covers the BLS / slashing-protection versions and the converter source.

Test discovery is unchanged: generating from the archives and from an expanded directory produces identical class sets (54,840 for `minimal`).

### Measurements

**CI** — baseline is today's green `master` run (a772d43b, warm fixture cache); the PR run (475238174f) had a **cold** cache and includes the one-off download + conversion. Both ran 63,024 reference tests, 3,487 skipped, 0 failures.

| Stage | Baseline (warm cache) | PR run (cold cache) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| `referenceTestsPrep` job | 7m07s | 5m45s | −1m22s despite cold cache (~4m10s expected warm) |
| Prep: fetch fixtures | 0s (cache hit) | 1m33s (download 1.3 GB + convert) | one-off per version bump |
| Prep: compile generated classes | 3m00s | 3m10s | noise |
| Prep: cache save + compress + upload `reftests` | 1m19s | 10s | −1m09s |
| Shard job total (shard 7 / shard 0) | 11m49s / 11m54s | 7m22s / 7m17s | **−4m30s per shard** |
| Shard: restore fixture cache | 25–27s | 6–7s | −20s |
| Shard: download + extract `reftests` | 1m49s–2m08s | 4–5s | −2 min |
| Shard: run tests (Gradle) | 6m18s / 6m35s | 5m49s / 6m04s | ~−30s, within noise |
| Shard: upload JUnit reports | 1m00s–1m16s | 21–23s | −45s |
| Prep start → last shard done | 21m26s | 18m20s | −3m06s cold, ~−4.5 min expected warm |

Runner queueing and the `Download assemble-output` step varied between the runs and are excluded above.

| Sizes | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Fixture cache entry (as stored by `actions/cache`) | 638 MB, 332k files | 956 MB, 5 files |
| `reftests` inter-job artifact | whole module incl. 4.3 GB fixture tree | 12 MB |
| Fixtures on the runner / dev disk | 4.3 GB expanded (+4.3 GB copy in `build/resources` locally) | 1.6 GB of zips |

**Local (M4 Max, `minimal` = 375,940 files)**

| Operation | Expanded tree | Zip archive |
|---|---|---|
| Prepare fixtures | `tar -xzf`: 91 s | convert: 12 s |
| All 5 archives incl. mainnet download + class generation | — | 73 s |
| Full `Files.walk` | 11.0 s | 0.2 s |
| Walk + probe marker file per directory (finder pattern) | 10.4 s | 0.15 s |
| Read 4,000 random fixtures (cold / warm) | 1,005 ms / 171 ms | 43 ms / 26 ms |
| Mount cost per JVM | — | 170 ms, ~170 MB heap |

### Trade-offs

- **Cache entry is +50% larger** (956 MB vs 638 MB): the zips are already deflated so the cache's zstd gains nothing, whereas the raw tree compressed well. Inherent to caching pre-compressed data; deflate level 6 would only shave ~40 MB.
- **~200 MB more heap per test JVM** for the zip indexes (minimal + mainnet), covered by `maxHeapSize = '2g'`.
- **No expanded tree to browse.** Use `unzip -l`, an IDE archive viewer, or unzip and point `-Dteku.ref-test.root-dir` at it.
- Nightly download path and Windows were not exercised; the nightly path uses the same tarball file names as before.

### Unrelated finding

The upstream `general.tar.gz` asset of v1.7.0-beta.0 is 3 KB and contains only two altair BLS suites, so **no `ssz_generic` or `kzg` reference tests are generated at this version on `master` either**. The release has a new `comptests.tar.gz` asset that may hold them. Tracked separately.

### How to use

```bash
./gradlew referenceTest                                   # converts archives on first run, then reads from them
./gradlew referenceTest -Dteku.ref-test.root-dir=/path/to/tests   # plain directory of <config>/ vectors instead
```

Downloaded tarballs are streamed once into per-config zip archives (`build/refTests/<version>/archives/*.zip`) via **`ReferenceTestArchiveConverter`**, and tests read vectors through the JDK zip filesystem.

title: Add step retry for integration/acceptance test shards
body:
## PR Description

Our integration and acceptance tests are more likely to fail due to unforeseen or external reasons (e.g. pulling Docker images failing, or when ports aren't ready, etc). The idea with this retry is to avoid a whole pipeline failing due to this.

I am keeping the number of retries low because we also don't want to hide flaky tests. Once we get our reporting back online, we will still be able to see individual test cases failures to spot flakyness.

This is not touching unit tests, property tests or reference tests as they are mostly deterministic and shouldn't be subject to the same oscillations that integration and acceptance tests do.

title: Reject UInt64.MAX_VALUE attestation epochs from the beacon node
body:
## PR Description

A beacon node is untrusted per spec, but Teku's validator client did not validate the source/target epochs of the `AttestationData` it received before signing. An epoch value of `UInt64.MAX_VALUE` was signed without complaint, and, if persisted to the slashing-protection record, is indistinguishable from "never signed" on the next read.

This adds a check in `AttestationProductionDuty.validateAttestationData` that rejects `UInt64.MAX_VALUE` as a source or target epoch before an attestation is ever signed.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Internal tracking: Consensys-Incorporated/teku-internal#334

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches validator signing gates and slashing-protection import logic; changes are narrow validation/filtering with low blast radius but protect safety-critical signing floors.
> 
> **Overview**
> Hardens attestation handling against **`UInt64.MAX_VALUE`** source/target epochs, which are invalid on-chain but can corrupt slashing-protection floors because persisted `MAX_VALUE` is treated like **never signed** on reload (teku-internal#334).
> 
> **Validator client:** `AttestationProductionDuty.validateAttestationData` now rejects beacon-node `AttestationData` whose source or target checkpoint epoch is `UInt64.MAX_VALUE` before signing, so malicious or broken nodes cannot get that value into signing records.
> 
> **Slashing interchange / import:** When deriving attestation epoch highs from imported history, `SigningHistory.toValidatorSigningRecord` and `SlashingProtectionImporter.signingHistoryConverter` skip `MAX_VALUE` entries instead of taking them as the max epoch. Tests cover the import conversion path and duty failure when the node returns max epochs.
>

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
 `GET /eth/v1/events` validated its topics only after the SSE handler had committed the `200` response, so an unrecognised topic could not be reported: the client got a stream which stayed open and never delivered anything.
  
Topics are now checked before the stream starts, and an unknown or missing `topics` value is rejected with `400`, matching Prysm, Lighthouse, Lodestar and Nimbus, and letting clients fall back when a topic is not supported.
  
Covered by unit tests on the handler and by integration tests against a running REST API, which are what pin the ordering between validation and the committed response.

See the spec: https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/apis/eventstream/index.yaml#L203-L211

body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

  `head_v2` events reported `payload_status` as `pending` before Gloas, because fork choice models every pre-Gloas block as a base node — but `pending` is not a status the API 
  defines, the spec never yields a pending head, and Prysm and Lodestar both report `full` there.
  A pre-Gloas block always carries its execution payload, so the event now reports `full` for every milestone before Gloas, leaving the empty/full mapping untouched from Gloas 
  onwards.
  Covered by a unit test over every pre-Gloas milestone crossed with all three fork choice statuses, plus an end-to-end case feeding a pending status through a phase0 subscription
  manager.

Fork choice was surfacing **`pending`** for those heads, but that value is not part of the API contract and does not match other clients; pre-Gloas blocks always include their execution payload, so the head should read **`full`**.

title: Log dropped gossip queue parts at debug level
body:
## PR Description

When jvm-libp2p drops the queued RPC parts of a slow peer, the publish promise fails with `DroppedRpcPartsException` and `GossipFailureLogger` logged the first occurrence at WARN. That reads as if we are deliberately not delivering messages we would otherwise have delivered. In reality the peer isn't consuming its outbound queue, so those messages would never have reached it anyway. Also there isn't much value in logging it as warning given that the node operator has nothing they could've done to prevent this. Neither there are any actions they can take to prevent that in the future. We can't control finding bad peers, all we can do is downscore them and eventually disconnect (what we already do).

### Changes

- Log `DroppedRpcPartsException` at DEBUG unconditionally in `GossipFailureLogger`, since the drop is expected handling of a slow peer and the peer is already downscored by gossip scoring.
- Update `GossipFailureLoggerTest` to assert the slow-peer log is DEBUG with and without suppression, and that no WARN or ERROR is emitted.

title: Bound in-flight execution payload gossip validation
body:
## PR Description

Execution payload envelopes can be large and expensive to validate, and the gossip handler had nothing limiting how many of them could be waiting for validation at once. They were decoded on the libp2p thread and then held decoded in the shared P2P queue.

Changes:
- `Eth2TopicHandler` supports an optional limit on in-flight messages per topic. Messages over the limit are ignored before SSZ decoding (libp2p has already decompressed them to compute the message id). `execution_payload` uses a limit of 8 (honest traffic is about one envelope per slot).
- A message holds an in-flight slot for at most one slot. After that it is ignored and the slot is released, even if the validation is still running, so stuck validations can't block the topic. Validations still count until they actually finish, and no new message is admitted while twice the limit (16 for `execution_payload`) are still running, so timed-out work can't pile up either.
- New metrics: `network_gossip_messages_in_flight{topic}` (including validations that timed out but are still running) and `network_gossip_messages_in_flight_limit_discarded_total{topic}`.
- ~~SSZ decoding now happens on the async runner for all topics, so queued messages are not held decoded and the libp2p thread doesn't pay for it.~~ (now done here https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/pull/11447)
- `SnappyPreparedGossipMessage.getDecodedMessage()` reuses the payload already uncompressed for the message id instead of uncompressing again.
- `ExecutionPayloadGossipValidator` ignores envelopes that are not for the current or previous slot when their block state is not cached, instead of regenerating the state before the signature is even checked. Otherwise a few peers could keep every in-flight slot busy with state regenerations and get the builder's envelope ignored.
- `ExecutionPayloadGossipValidator` remembers block root and builder pairs whose envelope failed signature verification, and ignores further envelopes for a pair before hashing the execution requests, looking up the state or checking the signature, once the payload for the block is imported (FULL fork choice node). Requiring the payload to be imported means invalid envelopes sent ahead of the builder's can't get the valid one ignored, and envelopes are still accepted as the spec requires when their payload was imported without a failed signature.
- Envelopes for an unknown block are only queued when they are for the current or previous slot, and the pending pool goes from 64 to 8 entries. When an envelope is evicted from the pool, its block root is remembered and the envelope is fetched by root as soon as that block is imported, so junk envelopes can't push an honest one out for good.
- The `execution_payload` topic is now scored (same shape as the other low-rate topics, no mesh delivery penalty). Its weight is left out of the max positive score, so scoring for existing topics doesn't change.

## Fixed Issue(s)
- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku-internal/issues/326
- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku-internal/issues/341

title: Keep ENR next_fork_version at a BPO fork
body:
## PR Description

The ENR `eth2` field advertises the wrong `next_fork_version` when a BPO fork is scheduled before the next hard fork.

The [Fulu p2p spec](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/82b6e507dc31f6f7052e79b16ecfe3778c1b38f6/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#eth2-field) says that `next_fork_version` "will only change for regular forks, _not BPO forks_". `DiscoveryNetwork.setForkInfo` sets `next_fork_epoch` to the earlier of the next BPO fork and the next hard fork. But it always takes `next_fork_version` from the next hard fork. Example: the current fork is Fulu, with a BPO fork at epoch A and Gloas at epoch B > A. Teku advertises (Gloas, A). The spec requires (Fulu, A).

Prysm's discv5 dial filter (`compareForkENR`, from OffchainLabs/prysm#15604) rejects a peer when `next_fork_epoch` matches and `next_fork_version` does not. Prysm advertises (Fulu, A). So in this window, Prysm does not dial Teku nodes that it finds through discovery. No public network is in this state today.

This PR uses the hard fork's version only when the hard fork is at `next_fork_epoch`. In all other cases it uses the current version. `DiscoveryNetworkTest` gets three cases: a BPO before, at, and after the hard fork. Prysm, Lodestar, and Nimbus already use this rule.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Spec issue: ethereum/consensus-specs#5701

title: Validate full epoch processing in epoch processing reference tests
body:
## PR Description

Epoch processing reference tests only check each sub-transition in isolation (`pre` -> `post`). That can't catch bugs in how sub-transitions depend on each other, e.g. running them in the wrong order or reading stale validator statuses. Since consensus-specs #4155, the vectors also ship `pre_epoch`/`post_epoch` states, the state before and after the full epoch transition. This PR runs `processEpoch` against those states next to the existing per-operation check.

### Changes

- Run the full epoch check in `EpochProcessingTestExecutor` alongside the per-operation check with `assertAll`, so both failures get reported and a full-epoch-only failure points at an interaction between sub-transitions.
- Expect `processEpoch` to throw when `pre_epoch` exists without `post_epoch`, which is how the 9 `registry_updates/invalid_large_withdrawable_epoch` vectors encode invalid cases.
- Report only the names of the differing top-level state fields on a mismatch, instead of rendering both full states. With a bug that fails hundreds of tests at once, the full state dumps exhausted the test JVM heap (`OutOfMemoryError`) and the run hung instead of failing.
- Skip the full epoch check for phase0 `participation_record_updates/updated_participation_record` (minimal and mainnet). The vector puts `PendingAttestation`s with empty aggregation bits in the state, which no valid block can produce. The spec never reads them at epoch 0, but Teku builds validator statuses from them up front and rejects the bitlist size. The skipped vectors must still fail with that exact error, so the entry can't outlive the reason or hide a different failure.
- Add `FullEpochProcessingCoverageTest`, which fails if any config/fork has no vectors with full epoch states (e.g. the file gets renamed in a spec release and the check silently stops running) or if a skip entry no longer matches a vector. Skip entries are only judged when vectors for their fork and config were loaded, so partial local runs (e.g. minimal only) don't fail.
- Include the handwritten tests under `src/referenceTest/java` in the CI shard list. It only picked up generated tests, so `FullEpochProcessingCoverageTest` (and the existing `SszMaxLengthFixturesTest`) never ran in CI.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Fixes https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/issues/11365

## PR Description

Teku has almost no visibility inside libp2p. Of the metrics in the networking module, only peer counts and RPC request counters touch libp2p at all — nothing reports gossip mesh size, duplicate rate, validation outcomes, router misbehaviour or slow peers, which is most of what you want when diagnosing a gossip problem.

jvm-libp2p has exposed `GossipRouterEventListener` for a while and we never registered anything on it. This wires a listener onto the router in `LibP2PGossipNetworkBuilder`, where the `MetricsSystem` was already at hand, and turns those events into metrics. **No jvm-libp2p change is required** — it works against the released 1.3.7.

### Metrics

All under a new `LIBP2P_GOSSIP` category, so they publish as `libp2p_gossip_gossipsub_*`:

| Metric | Type | Label | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gossipsub_topic_msg_recv_counts` | counter | topic | Messages received for the first time |
| `gossipsub_topic_msg_recv_bytes` | counter | topic | Payload bytes of first-seen messages |
| `gossipsub_duplicate_messages_total` | counter | topic | Messages received that were already seen |
| `gossipsub_accepted_messages_per_topic` | counter | topic | First-seen messages that passed validation |
| `gossipsub_invalid_messages_per_topic` | counter | topic | First-seen messages that failed validation |
| `gossipsub_mesh_peer_inclusion_events` | counter | topic | Peer added to a topic mesh |
| `gossipsub_mesh_peer_churn_events` | counter | topic | Peer pruned from a topic mesh |
| `gossipsub_router_misbehaviour_events_total` | counter | - | Router misbehaviour penalties applied |
| `gossipsub_slow_peer_events_total` | counter | - | Peer outbound queue above the slow-peer threshold |
| `gossipsub_mesh_peer_counts` | supplied gauge | topic | Peers currently in the topic mesh |

**Update (Oct 1):** five metrics were renamed after review. `accepted_messages_total` and `invalid_messages_total` are now `accepted_messages_per_topic` and `invalid_messages_per_topic`, matching the rust-libp2p names Lighthouse exposes. The three Teku-only counters (duplicate, router misbehaviour, slow peer) got clearer names, since there is no other client to match. The names in this table are the final ones.

Metric names follow the set rust-libp2p's gossipsub crate exposes, so a Teku dashboard lines up with the equivalent Lighthouse one.

### Off by default

They sit in their own `LIBP2P_GOSSIP` category, deliberately left out of `defaultCategories()`. Enable with `--Xmetrics-additional-categories=LIBP2P_GOSSIP`. This new hidden option adds categories on top of whatever `--metrics-categories` sets, so operators don't have to repeat the full default list just to turn these on. `--metrics-categories=...,LIBP2P_GOSSIP` also works.

A separate category rather than a config flag, because the alternatives are worse. Dropping `LIBP2P` from the defaults would also silence `libp2p_peers` and `libp2p_rpc_requests_total`, which operators have today. Reusing `LIBP2P` with a second enum constant does not work at all: Besu's `MetricsSystem.isCategoryEnabled` matches on `getName()` rather than enum identity, so sharing the name would let `LIBP2P` enable this category too.

The cost is the prefix — `CategorizedPrometheusCollector` builds it from the category name, so series are `libp2p_gossip_gossipsub_*` while experimental. The `gossipsub_` segment is kept in each metric name rather than dropped as redundant, so **promoting these to `LIBP2P` later is a one-line category change** that lands exactly on `libp2p_gossipsub_*`. That promotion will rename every series and break dashboards built against the experimental names — the reason they are experimental.

`attachTo` also checks `isCategoryEnabled` and skips attaching entirely when disabled. A disabled category already makes every metric a no-op, but the listener would still parse a topic per received message and maintain the mesh map; not attaching keeps that off the gossip event thread.

### Two details worth review

**Topic label is the topic shape, not the topic.** A raw topic label is unbounded in practice — the fork digest rotates at every fork and the subnet index multiplies every series by the subnet count. `GossipTopicShape` strips both (`/eth2/<digest>/beacon_attestation_37/ssz_snappy` → `beacon_attestation`) and buckets anything unparseable into `other`. Trade-off: no per-subnet breakdown from these metrics; `subnet_peer_count` still gives that separately. Both go-libp2p and rust-libp2p enforce this kind of bound; Prysm does not, and carries ~64 series per metric per fork digest as a result.

**Mesh membership is mirrored locally** rather than read from `GossipRouter.getMesh()`. That map is a plain `LinkedHashMap` mutated on the event thread, so a scrape would race it. Counting incrementally from meshed/pruned alone would drift upward instead, because `GossipRouter.onPeerDisconnected` removes the peer from every mesh **without** emitting a prune. The listener mirrors that removal on disconnect; there is a named test for it.

No metric carries a peer id.

Fixes #11367

title: Send Eth-Consensus-Version header with proposer preferences
body:
## PR Description

The remote validator client sent gloas proposer preferences to the beacon node without the `Eth-Consensus-Version` header, which the beacon-APIs spec marks as required for `POST /eth/v1/validator/proposer_preferences`. A beacon node that enforces it rejects every submission with 400.

`SendSignedProposerPreferencesRequest` now takes the `Spec`, derives the milestone from the first entry's `proposal_slot` and sends the `Eth-Consensus-Version` header, following the same pattern as `PublishSignedExecutionPayloadBidRequest` and `SendBuilderPreferencesRequest`. The JSON type definition is taken from the schema definitions at that slot. The integration test asserts the header is present.

## PR Description
  Use proposer config for Gloas block proposal

  - The builder config for Gloas blocks now comes from the proposer config and the
    keymanager API, not only from CLI options.
  - Added ProposerConfigManager.resolveBuilderConfig. It returns
    ResolvedBuilderConfig, with every value already filled in, taken in this order:
    proposer config for the key, then keymanager API, then proposer config
    default, then CLI.
  - If the proposer config sets enabled: false, no builders are used.
  - BuilderConfigProvider is now an interface:
    - DefaultBuilderConfigProvider is used when Gloas is supported. It refreshes
      the proposer config before building a config, and passes the builder pubkeys
      through to the beacon node.
    - NOOP is used otherwise.
  - Tests: added DefaultBuilderConfigProviderTest and extended
    ProposerConfigManagerTest.

Modified the hackmd to reflect those changes: https://hackmd.io/W4iNPxjbSAq1yeJTntOS0Q?view#Proposer-config

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how Gloas builder URLs, bids, and pubkeys are chosen at proposal time (layered config with new empty/disabled semantics), which can alter MEV/builder routing for operators who relied on CLI-only defaults.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Gloas block proposal and builder preferences now resolve builder settings from proposer config and Keymanager API**, not only CLI flags. `ProposerConfigManager.resolveBuilderConfig()` produces a fully merged `ResolvedBuilderConfig` (per-validator config → runtime API → default config → CLI), honors `enabled: false` and explicit empty `urls` as “no builders,” and passes per-URL overrides (`auth_data`, `builder_pubkeys`, bids, etc.) through to the beacon node.
> 
> `BuilderConfigProvider` is split into an interface: **`DefaultBuilderConfigProvider`** (Gloas) builds signed builder entries from resolved config, caches by proposer/slot, skips failed builders, and uses **`BuilderConfig.NO_OP`** when proposer config is not ready; **`NOOP`** is used pre-Gloas. Proposer/builder preference publishers **`refresh()` proposer config** before publishing and use a shared async error-handling path.
> 
> **Validation and parsing** move into proposer-config load and shared **`BuilderUrlParser`** (URL length, entry limits, auth/pubkey bounds); CLI `--builder-urls` enforces max entries. Block production **falls back to non-biased `BuilderConfig.NO_OP`** if builder config resolution fails.

title: Replace deprecated log4j builder calls
body:
## PR Description

log4j 2.26 deprecates the `withX()` methods on the layout, appender and policy builders in favour of `setX()`. CodeQL flags each call as `java/deprecated-call`, which accounts for 15 of the open code scanning alerts.

### Changes

- Switch `PatternLayout.Builder` calls in `LoggingConfigurator` and `LogCaptor` to `setPattern`, `setRegexReplacement`, `setAlwaysWriteExceptions`, `setNoConsoleNoAnsi`, `setConfiguration` and `setPatternSelector`.
- Switch `RollingFileAppender.Builder` calls to `setAppend`, `setFileName`, `setFilePattern` and `setPolicy`.
- Switch `TimeBasedTriggeringPolicy.Builder` calls to `setInterval` and `setModulate`.

No behaviour change, each `withX()` in 2.26.1 has the same body as its `setX()` counterpart.

Code scanning alerts #1889 to #1903.

title: Speed up slow property tests
body:
## PR Description

One property test shard has been taking 20+ minutes on every CI run. Almost all of it is `deneb/helpers/CKZG4844PropertyTest.fuzzVerifyBlobKzgProofBatch`, which took between 430s and 1700s across the last ~25 runs (the other three methods in that class take ~10s). The planner assigns the longest class first, so it always lands in shard 0. The variance comes from jqwik's random list sizes.

There were two causes, both in test fixtures.

### Changes

- Build random blobs with `Bytes.concatenate` instead of `Bytes.wrap` in `DataStructureUtil.randomValidBlob()`, because `wrap` produced a `ConcatenatedBytes` of 4096 chunks whose `get(i)` walks the chunk list. jqwik adds every generated list element to a `HashSet`, so hashing each 128KB blob cost ~268M iterations.
- Exclude `EPHEMERY` from the networks picked by `SpecSupplier`, because its config is loaded from `https://ephemery.dev/...` and `DataStructureUtilSupplier` creates a new `Spec` per generated element. That meant many HTTP round-trips per property, and a CI dependency on ephemery.dev being up. Stack samples showed the test worker mostly blocked on SSL reads.

### Results (same machine)

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `fuzzVerifyBlobKzgProofBatch` | 1093s | 32s |

The full `:ethereum:spec:propertyTest` suite passes locally (179 tests). Shard balancing uses timings cached from the last master run, so the plan should even out after the first master build with this change.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Fixes https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/issues/11379

title: Remove Gradle workers.max=4 cap from CI
body:
## PR Description

`GRADLE_OPTS` in `ci.yml` carries `-Dorg.gradle.workers.max=4` from #10011, when CI ran on 4-cpu runners. The test shards have since moved to `ubuntu-latest-128` (32 cpu), and `build.gradle` asks for `maxParallelForks = availableProcessors / 2`, but Gradle clamps that to `workers.max`. The reference test shard log says it plainly:

```
:eth-reference-tests:referenceTest.maxParallelForks (16) is larger than max-workers (4), forcing it to 4
```

The same clamp applies silently to every unit, integration, property and acceptance shard (the message is only printed at `--info`), and to compile parallelism in `assemble`. So we've been paying for 32-cpu runners and running 4 test JVMs on them.

### Changes

- Drop `-Dorg.gradle.workers.max=4` from `GRADLE_OPTS`, so Gradle defaults to the runner's cpu count for both test forks and compile workers.

Memory headroom is fine: 16 forks at `-Xmx4096m` is 64GB on a 128GB runner. Jobs still on `ubuntu-24.04` (spotless, moduleChecks, report jobs) default to 4 workers as before.

This is the first of a series of CI speedups; the rest (method-level sharding, building the acceptance Docker image once, compiling reference tests in `assemble`, trimming the 1.4GB `assemble-output` artifact) will follow in separate PRs.

## Fixed Issue(s)
Part of https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/issues/11381

title: Publish test reports as check runs from a workflow_run workflow
body:
## PR Description

We have had test report jobs in CI for a while, but nothing from them was reaching the PR page. Looking at recent runs (master `8f45734`, PR run 36727382142):

- `dorny/test-reporter` ran with `use-actions-summary: true`, so it only wrote a job summary. No `Combined * tests` check run exists on any recent commit.
- Even with that flag off, 14 of the last 15 PRs came from forks. A `pull_request` job on a fork PR gets a read-only token, so `checks: write` is ignored and no check run can be created.
- `ctrf-io/github-test-reporter` skipped its output on every unit run: `report is 32.29MB, which exceeds GitHub's 1MB output limit. Skipping report output.` It also scanned 400 workflow runs per job looking for previous results and found none.

### Changes

- Add `test-reports.yml`, triggered by `workflow_run` on `ci`. It runs in the base repository with a writable token and dorny resolves the triggering run's PR head SHA, so one check run per suite (`unit tests`, `integration tests`, `property tests`, `acceptance tests`, `reference tests`) shows up on the PR, fork or not. Each job downloads all shard artifacts for its suite via `artifact: /^<suite>-reports-.*$/`.
- Configure dorny for check runs: `use-actions-summary: false`, `list-suites: failed`, `list-tests: failed`, `max-annotations: 50`, `fail-on-empty: false`. Check run output is capped at 65535 bytes, so green runs show totals and red runs list only failures.
- Remove the five `*TestsReport` jobs from `ci.yml` and the `collate-junit-reports` composite action, including the ctrf conversion and reporter steps.

## Fixed Issue(s)
Part of https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/issues/11381
