title: Merge JUnit XML per shard before uploading test reports
body:
## PR Description

First `test-reports` run after #11383 (https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/actions/runs/36833901378): four of five check runs came out fine, `reference tests` died with:

```
Creating check run reference tests
Creating report summary
##[error]RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

dorny builds the summary as one row plus one section per XML file and splices them in with argument spread (`sections.push(...runs)`, `table(..., ...rows)`). Gradle writes one XML per test class, and the reference suite uploads ~8.2k files per shard, ~66k in total, so the spread overflows the Node call stack. Upstream issue dorny/test-reporter#249, fix PR #813 still open. The same per-file rows also filled the 65535-byte check run budget on a green integration run (`Test report summary exceeded limit of 65535 bytes and will be trimmed`), which on a red run would push the failure list out of the report.

### Changes

- Add `merge-junit-xml` composite action that folds every `build/test-results/**/TEST-*.xml` into one `<testsuites>` file, and run it in `matrix-tests-template.yml` and the `referenceTests` job before upload, so each shard artifact carries a single XML. dorny's `java-junit` parser already reads `<testsuites>` roots, and every suite and test case is kept.
- Upload only the merged XML plus the HTML reports, so artifacts shrink and dorny has 8-12 rows per suite instead of hundreds or thousands.
- Switch `capture-test-timings` from `root.findall("testcase")` to `root.iter("testcase")`, since test cases are now nested one level deeper. Without this the per-class timing cache would silently go empty.

Checked locally against the artifacts of that run: `property-reports-0` (6 files, 16 test cases) and `reference-reports-0` (8262 files, 8266 test cases) both merge with all test cases preserved; the reference shard takes 2s and ~220MB RSS. `findall` on the merged root returns 0 test cases, `iter` returns all of them.

title: Speed up CI: prebuilt Docker image, reference tests in assemble, single-tarball artifact, split slow DAS test, faster CodeQL
body:
## PR Description

Follow-up to #11382, which took a PR run from ~21 to ~18.6 minutes. Looking at the job logs of a recent master run, most of what is left is not test time:

- Shards are planned per class. `DasCheckpointSyncAcceptanceTest` (two methods, 307s + 223s) sits alone in a shard while every other acceptance shard finishes under 350s, so the whole run waits on it.
- Every acceptance shard spends ~2m15s running `distTar` -> `dockerDistUntar` -> `distDocker` (both JDK variants, `--pull`) before its first test, because `distTar`'s `repackage` rewrites its own output and is never up to date.
- `referenceTestsPrep` compiles the ~66k generated reference test classes (170s on an 8-cpu runner), and then every reference shard compiles them again (~107s).
- `assemble-output` is 1.4GB and is downloaded by ~57 jobs. 20s per job on master, 99s per shard in the PR run.
- Why the shards recompile at all: two things. `upload-artifact` zips file by file and drops empty directories, which Gradle treats as removed outputs. And `build/tmp/<compileTask>/previous-compilation-data.bin` is a declared output of every `JavaCompile` task, so an earlier revision of this PR that excluded `build/tmp` from the artifact made every compile task fall back to the build cache (`FROM-CACHE` in every shard log), and `compileReferenceTestJava`, with no cache entry, recompiled. Reproduced locally: tar a built checkout, unpack into a fresh clone at the same path, run with `--info`: 146 tasks out of date with the exclude, 0 without.

### Changes

- Split `DasCheckpointSyncAcceptanceTest` into two classes so the two slow scenarios land in different shards. An earlier revision of this PR did method-level shard planning from cached timings instead; dropped because a cache-driven method list can silently skip tests (new methods, parameterized cases, partial reports after a failed shard).
- Build the Docker image once in `assemble`, upload it as a zstd-compressed `docker save` artifact (313MB locally), and have the acceptance shards `docker load` it and run with `-x distDocker`.
- Generate and compile the reference tests inside `assemble` and delete `referenceTestsPrep`. Shards restore the archive cache themselves. Also drop `--info` from the shard run (335k log lines) and replace the undefined `inputs.gradle_args` with the log-level expression the other suites use.
- Trim `assemble-output`: exclude `build/distributions` (always rebuilt by consumers, see above), the reference test archives (shards restore them from cache), javadoc output (423MB, no consumer), and test report directories. `build/tmp` stays in, see above. Shards also stop uploading the Gradle HTML test report (16.5k files and 130MB per reference shard; nothing reads it, and the merged XML keeps each test's captured output); the merged XML is what `test-reports.yml` and `capture-test-timings` consume.
- Ship `assemble-output` as one zstd tarball and unpack it in every consumer, so the upload is one file (the loose upload hit 136s with the generated tests in it) and empty directories survive, which keeps compile tasks `UP-TO-DATE` in the shards. `publish-docker.yml` gets the matching unpack step because it downloads the same artifact; nothing else in the publish jobs changes.
- Fetch tags in `assemble`: the Docker image is built there now, and with a shallow checkout teku reported `UNKNOWN+g<sha>` as its version, which `ExternalMetricPublisherAcceptanceTest` checks. Side effect worth knowing: `publishDocker` builds from `assemble`'s jars, and the published `consensys/teku:develop` has been reporting `teku/vUNKNOWN+g<sha>` since `assemble` went shallow (release images are unaffected, a tag checkout resolves `git describe`). With tags fetched, `develop` will report `v26.9.1+<n>-g<sha>` again.
- Print the assertion message and full stack trace for failed tests in the Gradle output (`testLogging { events "failed"; exceptionFormat "full" }`). Gradle's default printed one line per failure (`java.lang.AssertionError at Foo.java:208`), so the shard log said what failed but not why.
- CodeQL: switch `init` to `build-mode: manual` with `./gradlew --no-daemon compileJava` on `ubuntu-latest-128`, using the `prepare` action for JDK and the read-only Gradle cache. CodeQL took ~21 minutes on every run (18 of them in `autobuild` on a 4-cpu runner, compiling tests, fixtures and JMH too) and became the last check on every PR once `ci` got faster. Same query suites, still build-based for production code; `build-mode: none` rejected because it drops library type resolution.
- Make the shard count a `matrix-tests-template` input and run unit and integration on 8 shards instead of 12. 56 shard jobs hit the large-runner pool within seconds of `assemble`; ~49 start immediately and the rest trickle in over 2-3 minutes, and the ones left waiting are always the acceptance shards (last suite in the file, longest suite, critical path). Unit and integration shards finish in ~3 minutes at 16 forks, so 8 of each frees runners for acceptance at the burst.

Expected PR critical path: `assemble` (~3.5m) -> acceptance shard with the longest single method (~307s + setup) or reference shard (~1m setup + ~1m of tests, which after #11382 is overhead-bound: fork startup and matching 66k classes against 8k `--tests` patterns), about 11-12 minutes. Master adds the publish jobs, untouched here.

Not included: lowering `SECONDS_PER_SLOT` in `fulu-minimal.yaml` for the DAS tests. 3s is flaky (`DasCustodyBackfiller` runs on a fixed 30s wall-clock round and loses the race against a faster chain) and 4s passed 2 of 3 local runs for a ~66s gain. Worth revisiting after making that backfill round configurable.

Things to verify on the first run of this branch:
- compile tasks show as UP-TO-DATE (not FROM-CACHE) in a test shard log
- `compileReferenceTestJava` is UP-TO-DATE in a reference shard
- `assemble` upload step is back under a minute
- `Analyze (java)` well under 21 minutes, and the code scanning alert count for production code matches master
- acceptance shards go from `docker load` straight into `acceptanceTest`
- `DasGetBlobsAcceptanceTest` has no cached timing on the first run, so it gets the average and may share a shard until the next master run records it

## Fixed Issue(s)

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes affect how every test shard restores build state and Docker images; mis-packed artifacts or cache keys could cause flaky or widespread CI failures, though production runtime code is largely untouched.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Restructures CI so `assemble` warms more of the pipeline and downstream jobs spend less time downloading, unpacking, and recompiling.**
> 
> Reference test archive restore/generate/compile and `distDocker` move into **`assemble`** (drops **`referenceTestsPrep`** and the separate reftests artifact). Shards unpack a single **zstd `assemble-output` tarball** (preserves Gradle `build/tmp` for UP-TO-DATE compiles) instead of a huge loose workspace upload. Acceptance shards **`docker load`** a **`teku-docker-image`** artifact and run with **`-x distDocker`**.
> 
> **Sharding and observability:** unit/integration use **8** shards via configurable **`shard_count`**; the slow get-blobs DAS scenario moves to **`DasGetBlobsAcceptanceTest`** so it can land in a different acceptance shard. Test jobs upload **merged JUnit XML only** with **`overwrite: true`**. Gradle **`testLogging`** prints full failure stacks in logs.
> 
> **CodeQL** runs on **`ubuntu-latest-128`** with **`prepare`**, **`build-mode: manual`**, and **`compileJava --no-build-cache`** instead of autobuild. **`assemble`** checkout fetches **tags** so Docker-built Teku reports a real version in acceptance tests.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes block-production bid selection when the flag is disabled; default behavior is unchanged, but misconfiguration could exclude competitive P2P bids from proposals.

title: Fetch tags in the publish jobs so develop artifacts carry a real version
body:
## PR Description

The published `consensys/teku:develop` image reports `teku/vUNKNOWN+g<sha>`:

```
$ docker run --rm consensys/teku:develop --version
teku/vUNKNOWN+g802d5a8/linux-aarch_64/-eclipseadoptium-openjdk64bitservervm-java-25
```

and a jar pulled out of that image has `Implementation-Version: UNKNOWN+g802d5a8` in its manifest.

Cause: `publishDocker` and `publishRelease` check out with the default depth 1 and no tags, so `git describe --tags` fails and `calculateVersion()` falls back to `UNKNOWN+g<sha>`. Both jobs rebuild every jar (the manifest's `Implementation-Version` input differs from what `assemble` recorded, so Gradle re-runs all 67 `jar` tasks; visible in the job logs), and the rebuilt manifests carry the UNKNOWN string into the image and, by the same mechanism, into the `develop` Maven artifacts on Cloudsmith. Release tags are unaffected: a tag checkout resolves `git describe` on the exact commit, and `consensys/teku:latest` reports `teku/v26.9.1`.

This has been the case since `assemble` moved to a shallow checkout with the GHA migration; nobody noticed because the acceptance tests built their own image from a full checkout. #11385 moved that image build into `assemble` and fetched tags there, which fixed the test image but not the published one, since publishing rebuilds the jars.

### Changes

- `fetch-depth: 0` and `fetch-tags: true` on the checkout step in `publish-docker.yml` and `publish-release.yml`, same as `assemble` and the test shards already use. Costs ~10s per job.

Verification after merge: pull `consensys/teku:develop` and run `--version`; expect `teku/v26.9.1+<n>-g<sha>`.

title: VoluntaryExitGossipManager fork validation fix
body:
# Voluntary exit gossip rejection: capture evidence

Teku 26.9.1, mainnet, October 1, 2026 (UTC). Values are sampled every five seconds from the node's metrics and peer-score APIs.

| Time | Exit gossip messages (counter) | Exit pool validations (ACCEPT) | Peers below −8000 | Lowest score |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 12:09:55 | 672 | 5 | 0 | −2,883 |
| 12:10:00 | 692 | 5 | 0 | −3,609 |
| 12:10:05 | 904 | 5 | 24 | −15,480 |
| 12:10:10 | 904 | 5 | 24 | −15,391 |
| 12:31:55 | 921 | 6 | 1 | −8,266 |
| 12:32:00 | 1,204 | 7 | 20 | −49,981 |
| 12:32:05 | 1,204 | 7 | 20 | −49,694 |

Metrics: `libp2p_gossip_messages_total{topic=".../voluntary_exit/ssz_snappy"}` and `beacon_operation_pool_validation_VoluntaryExitPool_total`. −8000 is the gossip publish threshold.

## Interpretation

- Bursts of voluntary exits arrive on gossip (212 at 12:10:05, 283 at 12:32:00), but the exit pool validates almost none of them. `ACCEPT` is the only result label ever recorded, so they are turned away before the validator runs.
- In the same five-second step, many peers drop below the publish threshold. The lowest score at 12:10:05 is exactly 107.5 × 12², the invalid-delivery penalty for twelve messages.
- The exits were valid: batches from these bursts are in finalized blocks (slots 15336049 and 15336158–15336159).
- Nothing is logged. The topic-layer fork check rejects an exit whose `epoch` falls in an earlier fork and returns before any rejection logging.

Net effect: peers that forward valid pre-signed exits are penalised as if they had sent invalid messages, which makes them ineligible for publishing until the penalty decays.

title: Stop rejecting slashings for offences in an earlier fork at the gossip topic layer
body:
The topic handler's milestone check derived an epoch from the offending slot and rejected the slashing when it fell in a different fork than the topic. The spec's gossip rules for proposer_slashing and attester_slashing have no such condition: validity is checked against the head state, and get_domain uses the fork's previous version for epochs before the fork epoch, so a slashing for an offence in the previous fork is valid after a fork boundary.

Disable the fork check for both slashing topics, as already done for BLS to execution changes, and leave validation to the slashing validators.


can cause similar effects of #11392 



## Why the topic-layer fork check on slashings is wrong

**Bug:** `OperationMilestoneValidator` REJECTs a proposer/attester slashing whose offending slot is in a different fork than the topic ("Incorrect spec milestone"), penalising every forwarding peer.

**Spec evidence** (consensus-specs, phase0):

1. **No such gossip rule.** `validate_proposer_slashing_gossip` and `validate_attester_slashing_gossip` (`p2p-interface.md`) list every REJECT condition, evaluated against the head state. None compares the offence's fork with the topic's fork. Electra only changes the `AttesterSlashing` container size.
2. **Slashability uses the current epoch.** `process_proposer_slashing` / `process_attester_slashing` check `is_slashable_validator(validator, get_current_epoch(state))`. The age of the offending messages is not bounded.
3. **Previous-fork signatures verify post-fork.** `get_domain` uses `state.fork.previous_version` when `epoch < state.fork.epoch`, so a slashing for an offence in the immediately previous fork is valid after the boundary.

**Limits:**

- `get_domain` knows only two fork versions, so offences from two or more forks back fail signature verification. That is a legitimate REJECT, now issued by the slashing validator instead of the topic layer.
- Counter-reading: topic names use the fork digest of the message's "context epoch". The spec does not define a context epoch for slashings; reading it as the offending slot's epoch would make previous-fork slashings ungossipable once the old topics are dropped.

**Fix:** `ProposerSlashingGossipManager` and `AttesterSlashingGossipManager` pass `message -> forkInfo.getFork().getEpoch()` (same idiom as `SignedBlsToExecutionChangeGossipManager`), disabling the fork check at the topic layer.

**Proof:** `handleMessage_validSlashingForOffenceInPreviousFork` in both topic handler tests: Altair offence, Bellatrix head, passes spec validation against the head state. The handler returned `Invalid` before the fix and returns `Valid` after.

## PR Description

title: Dial TCP when a discovered peer's QUIC address is unreachable
body:
## PR Description

When a peer's ENR advertises both QUIC and TCP, Teku dialed the QUIC address only. If QUIC did not respond, the TCP address from the same ENR was never tried and the peer was retried over QUIC after every cooldown. Peers behind UDP-blocking firewalls were unreachable entirely.

`MultiaddrPeerAddress` now carries the TCP address as a fallback when the primary is QUIC. `PeerManager` dials the fallback once if the primary dial fails. We went with a sequential fallback rather than dialing both in parallel: it keeps the QUIC preference, costs no extra handshakes, and TCP is likely on its way out anyway. A `PeerAlreadyConnectedException` from the primary dial does not trigger the fallback, since the peer is already connected and the existing duplicate-connection handling takes over.

The second commit fixes a pre-existing race in `PeerManager.connect` found while reviewing the first. Every caller sharing a pending attempt registered an unconditional removal from `pendingConnections`. When one caller's cleanup ran, a new attempt could be inserted before the next caller's cleanup ran, which then removed the new attempt and let a further caller start a third concurrent dial. The entry is now removed only if it is still the attempt that completed.

Both changes come with unit tests that fail on the previous code.

## Fixed Issue(s)

fixes #11397

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes outbound libp2p dial and connection coalescing logic, which affects peer connectivity but is narrowly scoped with new unit tests and no parallel dial behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes unreachable peers when an ENR advertises both QUIC and TCP but QUIC is blocked or fails. Discovered addresses now keep **QUIC as the primary dial** and attach the **TCP multiaddr as a sequential fallback** when they differ; `PeerManager` retries once over TCP after a failed primary dial, and **does not** fall back when the failure is `PeerAlreadyConnectedException`.
> 
> `MultiaddrUtil` exposes `fromDiscoveryPeerAsTcp` for that fallback path. Separately, **`pendingConnections` cleanup** only removes the completed attempt (`remove(id, future)`), fixing a race where a newer in-flight dial could be dropped and trigger extra concurrent dials.
> 
> Unit tests cover fallback selection and connect behavior (including the pending-connection race).

title: Verify the proposer signature before processing a block
body:
## PR Description

The spec's `state_transition` verifies the block signature before `process_block`. Teku queued the proposer signature with the other signatures and only ran the batch after the full transition, so an invalid proposer signature came out as a generic state transition failure and was handled like an invalid block.

### Changes

- `AbstractBlockProcessor.processAndValidateBlock` now checks the proposer index and the proposer signature before `processUnsignedBlock`, and throws `InvalidBlockSignatureException` for a bad signature. The signature is left out of the batch when it was already verified.
- `ForkChoice.onBlock` runs that check before starting the data availability check and maps it to a new `FailureReason.FAILED_INVALID_PROPOSER_SIGNATURE`, so the failure is attributed to that copy of the block rather than to the block root.
- `BlockManager` drops only the offending copy on that reason. It no longer records the root in `invalidBlockRoots`, and descendants waiting on that root keep waiting. A queued copy with a different signature is kept or replaced based on which signature verifies, not on arrival order.
- `BlockGossipValidator` checks the proposer signature against the head state's validator registry and the fork schedule before returning `SAVE_FOR_FUTURE` for blocks with an unknown parent or a future slot, and before the Gloas bid-parent check. A provably invalid signature is a `REJECT`. This matches what Prysm does.
- `PeerSync` treats the new reason as a bad block from the serving peer.

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes ordering and failure handling on the hot block-import, fork-choice, and gossip paths; incorrect handling could stall sync or wrongly blacklist roots, though behavior is spec-aligned and heavily tested.
> 
> **Overview**
> Aligns block import with the spec by **verifying the proposer signature before** state transition, execution payload work, and data-availability checks. Bad signatures now surface as **`InvalidBlockSignatureException`** / **`FAILED_INVALID_PROPOSER_SIGNATURE`** instead of a generic state-transition failure.
> 
> **Block processing:** `AbstractBlockProcessor` adds `verifyProposerSignature` (proposer index check, then BLS) ahead of `processUnsignedBlock`, and skips re-checking the proposer sig in the post-processing batch when already verified.
> 
> **Import & gossip:** `ForkChoice.onBlock` authenticates before DA and payload execution. `BlockManager` does **not** add the block root to `invalidBlockRoots` on signature failure; pooled copies with the same root but different signatures are resolved by which signature verifies. `BlockGossipValidator` rejects provably bad signatures before `SAVE_FOR_FUTURE` (unknown parent / future slot), using head-state proposer keys when parent state is missing. **`PeerSync`** treats the new failure reason like other bad blocks from a peer.
> 
> Tests cover processor, fork choice, block manager, and gossip paths across milestones.
>

title: Settle builder payment before parent requests and sweep remaining builder balance
body:
fixes: #11405

Implement consensus-specs PR 5695 (v1.7.0-beta.3) in Gloas block processing:

- In apply_parent_execution_payload, settle or re-queue the builder payment before processing the parent's execution requests, so a builder exit request is rejected while the payment is pending. Previously, when the parent was older than the previous epoch, the payment had already been evicted from builder_pending_payments, the exit guard saw nothing pending, and the payment was re-added right after the exit went through.
- In get_builders_sweep_withdrawals, sweep only the balance left after withdrawals already selected for the builder in the same payload, via the new get_builder_balance_after_withdrawals helper.

Specrefs are left at v1.7.0-beta.2 until beta.3 is released with test vectors and picked up by ethspecify.

title: Bound the future block queue by size and count
body:
Blocks for future slots (up to 2 slots ahead) are queued before their signature is verified. The queue was limited only to 500 blocks per slot, with no limit on total size, so its memory use was effectively unbounded.

Move future blocks into a dedicated FutureBlocks queue:
- Keep at most 4 blocks per slot, evicting the oldest when full.
- Cap the total SSZ size at 4 x MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE. Evict from the furthest-future slot first; drop the new block instead if evicting can't free enough space.
- Guard the queue with a single lock. BlockManager already serialised every call, so this adds no contention.

FutureItems is unchanged, so attestation and blob sidecar handling is unaffected.

Also:
- Add beacon_future_blocks_total{result} with the results queued, dequeued, evicted and dropped.
- Key gossip-retry roots in BlockManager by slot, so roots of evicted or dropped blocks are cleaned up instead of building up.

Devnet metrics over the last 7 days show the future block queue almost always empty (at most 1 block at a time), so these limits shouldn't affect normal operation.

## Documentation

- [X] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [X] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes future-block buffering and retry bookkeeping in block import; mis-eviction could delay imports under attack, but limits are tight and devnet metrics suggest normal queues stay nearly empty.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces the generic **`FutureItems`** queue for future-slot beacon blocks with a dedicated **`FutureBlockPool`** wired through **`PoolFactory`** and **`BeaconChainController`**.
> 
> The new pool caps memory with **at most 4 blocks per slot** (oldest evicted when full) and a **total SSZ budget of 4× `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE`**, evicting from the **furthest-future slots** first and **dropping** incoming blocks when capacity cannot be freed. Blocks beyond the existing **2-slot tolerance** are dropped without queuing. **`beacon_future_blocks_total{result}`** tracks queued, dequeued, evicted, and dropped events.
> 
> **`BlockManager`**’s **`FutureBlockTracker`** now keys gossip-retry roots **by slot** so evicted/dropped blocks do not leave stale retry state, and only records retry mode when **`add`** actually accepts the block. **`FutureItems`** is unchanged for attestations and other pending pools.
> 
> Tests cover pool eviction/drop behavior, factory defaults, and that blocks too far in the future are not retried on slot advance.

title: Lower pending block pool byte cap and report pool size in bytes
body:
Each of the two pending block pools (blocks waiting for their parent, and blocks waiting for their parent's execution payload) was capped at 10 x MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE (100 MiB) of SSZ. Decoded blocks retain roughly 4-5x their SSZ size on the heap, so together the pools could hold about 1 GB.

- Lower DEFAULT_PENDING_BLOCK_BYTES_MULTIPLIER from 10 to 4, giving 40 MiB of SSZ per pool, at most a few hundred MB of heap. The two pools keep separate budgets.
- Add beacon_pending_pool_bytes{type}, the total SSZ size of blocks in each pending block pool, alongside the existing pending_pool_size. PendingPool takes an optional total-weight gauge; only the block pools, which are weighted by SSZ size, use it.

Checked on a mainnet node:
- After a 15 minute outage the pool peaked at 10 blocks, 1.97 MB (4.7% of the new cap); it drained within 2 minutes.
- After a 30 minute outage it peaked at 2 blocks, 0.33 MB (0.8%).
- A missed slot caused no pending pool activity.
- Pending mainnet blocks averaged 173-183 KB, so 40 MiB holds about 240 of them.

Gloas blocks no longer carry the execution payload and are much smaller, so headroom increases after the fork.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Reduces pending-block retention during outages or parent gaps, which may drop older queued blocks sooner but is bounded by separate per-pool budgets and was validated on mainnet-style catch-up.
> 
> **Overview**
> Tightens how much memory beacon nodes can spend on **blocks waiting for a parent** (and the parallel pool waiting on a parent execution payload) by cutting the SSZ-weighted cap from **10×** to **4×** `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` per pool, targeting a few hundred MB of heap instead of ~1 GB when decoded objects are retained.
> 
> Adds observability via a new **`beacon_pending_pool_bytes`** labelled metric (`type` = `blocks` vs `blocks_waiting_for_parent_execution_payload`), reporting total SSZ bytes in each pool. `PendingPool` now accepts an optional gauge and keeps it in sync on add, remove, and eviction; only SSZ-weighted block pools wire it in. Changelog and unit tests cover the new multiplier and byte tracking.
>

title: Use imported slashing protection for an already loaded key
body:
## PR Description

The protector now owns the record state across an import. `SlashingProtector.importSigningRecord` runs the file update with signing for that key blocked, then drops or reloads the cached copy, so an in-flight signature can't write the pre-import record back over the imported one between the write and the eviction. A plain invalidate call after the import would leave that window open.

`ValidatorLoader` had to start holding the protector to call it, which is the only reason the test-only `create` overload grew an argument. I left the misleading `duplicate` response alone since changing it is an API behaviour change rather than part of this fix.

The import holds the per-validator map lock even when nothing is cached, and `LocalSlashingProtector.getSigningRecord` is now synchronized so a concurrent read cannot re-cache the pre-import record.

## Fixed Issue(s)

fixes #11388

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes slashing-protection caching and concurrency around signing, where incorrect behavior can allow double-signing or wrongly block valid attestations.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a case where **EIP-3076 slashing protection imported through the keymanager API** for a key that was already running was written to disk but **ignored** because the in-memory signing record stayed stale.
> 
> Adds **`SlashingProtector.importSigningRecord`**, which runs the file update while signing for that validator is blocked, then **drops or reloads the cache** so later signatures use the imported history. **`ValidatorLoader`** now calls this on the shared protector instead of updating files only through the importer.
> 
> **`LocalSlashingProtector`** synchronizes **`getSigningRecord`** and evicts the cache after a successful import; the concurrent-access implementation holds per-validator locks and **read-backs** the updated record from disk.

title: Report payload reorgs and payload statuses in reorg events
body:
From Gloas the fork-choice head is a (block root, payload status) node, so the head can change without any block leaving the canonical chain: the payload of the head block becomes non-canonical (FULL to EMPTY). Such a payload reorg produced no ReorgContext at all, so nothing was logged.

RecentChainData is now the single authority on reorgs:
- a payload reorg (same head root, FULL to EMPTY) emits a ReorgContext and increments the new payload_reorgs_total counter
- a block reorg additionally carries the old head payload status, both execution block hashes and the common ancestor payload status along each branch, resolved with the payload-status-aware ancestry (get_ancestor)

ReorgContext is converted to a record and the two kinds are told apart by content: in a payload reorg the old head is the common ancestor, which never holds for a block reorg. Pools, light client pruning and the chain_reorg SSE event act on block reorgs only; a payload reorg is still reported through head_v2.

The event log distinguishes the two and annotates block reorgs with payload statuses when available:

  Reorg Event *** New Head: ... [EMPTY], Previous Head: ... [FULL], Common Ancestor: ... [FULL -> EMPTY]
  Reorg Event *** Payload Reorg, Head: ..., Previous Execution Head: ..., New Execution Head: ...

Pre-Gloas output is unchanged. EMPTY to FULL is the payload arriving after the block and is intentionally not reported as a reorg.

Fixes #10670

title: Verify block signatures before saving blocks for future processing
body:
Gossip blocks from a future slot, or whose parent is not yet known, are saved for future processing before their proposer signature is checked. Any peer could fill the future and pending block pools with blocks nobody signed, without any penalty to its peer score.

Before saving such a block, `BlockGossipValidator` now checks its proposer and signature:
- **Valid signature:** saved for future processing, as before.
- **Invalid signature:** rejected, so it is not queued and the sending peer is penalised.
- **Proposer index in the head state but not yet finalized:** the signature is checked against the head-state pubkey, with the same outcomes as above.
- **Proposer index not in the head state:** ignored and not queued.

The parent state isn't available at this point, so the signing domain is taken from the fork schedule for the block's epoch, and the proposer's pubkey from the latest finalized state, or from the head state for a validator that isn't finalized yet. Whether the block was proposed by the expected proposer is still checked once its parent is known.

For Gloas, the existing signature check now runs before the check on the execution payload bid's parent, which can also save a block for future processing, so only correctly signed blocks wait for their parent's payload.

This follows the existing signature check for future-slot attestations in `AttestationValidator`. The outcomes match Prysm's `verifyPendingBlockSignature`, which Prysm applies before queueing a block whose parent, or parent payload, is unknown: an invalid signature is rejected, and a proposer index the head state doesn't have is ignored.

### Testing
- New `BlockGossipValidatorTest` cases:
  - future-slot and unknown-parent blocks with invalid signatures are rejected;
  - a proposer index not in the head state is ignored;
  - for a proposer index in the head state but not yet finalized, an invalid signature is rejected and a valid one is saved for future processing;
  - a block in the first epoch of a new fork verifies with that fork's signing domain;
  - a Gloas block waiting on its parent's payload is rejected for an invalid signature.
- New `BlockManagerTest` case: a rejected future block is not queued.
- Reference tests pass, including all `gossip/beacon_block` cases. Their future-slot and unknown-parent blocks are correctly signed and are still ignored.
- Ran on mainnet (about 13 hours) and hoodi with gossip reject logging enabled, then on mainnet again from a fresh checkpoint sync after adding the head-state check. 18 blocks arrived before their parent, during catch-up after a restart and during normal operation. All passed the check, were saved for future processing and later imported. No block was rejected.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes consensus gossip validation and peer scoring for deferred blocks; incorrect signature or fork/proposer lookup logic could wrongly reject or accept gossip, though behavior is aligned with Prysm and heavily tested.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Blocks queued for future or pending processing must now pass an early proposer signature check**, closing a gossip abuse vector where peers could fill those pools with unsigned blocks without score penalty.
> 
> When a block would be `SAVE_FOR_FUTURE` (future slot, missing parent, or unknown parent slot), `BlockGossipValidator` calls `checkSignatureBeforeSavingForFuture` instead of queuing immediately. It derives the signing domain from the fork schedule for the block’s epoch and the proposer pubkey from the latest finalized state, or from head state if the validator isn’t finalized yet. **Invalid signatures are rejected**; **unknown proposer indices are ignored**; valid signatures still defer as before.
> 
> For blocks that reach full stateful validation, the **proposer signature check runs before Gloas execution-payload-bid parent validation**, so only signed blocks wait on a parent payload. `GossipValidationHelper` adds `getLatestFinalizedState`, `getHeadState`, and `getForkInfo` to support this path. New unit tests cover rejection, ignore, fork-transition signing domains, and `BlockManager` not queuing rejected future blocks.
>

title: [beacon api] add Gloas fields to payload_attributes and block events
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Brings the `payload_attributes` and `block` SSE events up to date with the Gloas changes in the beacon API spec.

From Gloas onwards:
- **`payload_attributes`** includes `safe_block_hash` and `finalized_block_hash`: the execution block hashes sent in the `forkchoiceUpdated` call when building on `parent_block_hash` ([beacon-APIs#638](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/638)). They are taken from the same `ForkChoiceState` used for that call.
- **`payload_attributes.payload_attributes`** includes `slot_number` and `target_gas_limit`, matching the `PayloadAttributesV4` sent to the execution client. The event's inner object must mirror `PayloadAttributesV<N>` for the fork; the spec example was updated in [beacon-APIs#652](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/652).
- **`block`** includes `builder_index` and `block_hash` from the block's `signed_execution_payload_bid.message`, including for self-builds with `BUILDER_INDEX_SELF_BUILD` ([beacon-APIs#641](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/641)).

Before Gloas these fields are omitted, and the existing fields (including `parent_block_number`) are unchanged.

### Testing
- New `EventSubscriptionManagerTest` cases check the serialized JSON:
  - Gloas `payload_attributes` includes all four new fields;
  - Deneb `payload_attributes` includes none of them;
  - a Gloas `block` event carries the bid's `builder_index` and `block_hash`, including a self-build;
  - a Deneb `block` event carries neither.
- `BlockEvent.json` schema fixture updated with the two optional fields.
- Checked on live networks with `--Xfork-choice-updated-always-send-payload-attributes`:
  - **Sepolia (Gloas):** every `block` event had `builder_index` and `block_hash`, covering self-builds and external builders, and matched the block's bid. `payload_attributes` had the four new fields, with field names matching the dev spec. `slot_number` matched `proposal_slot`. The safe and finalized hashes matched the fork choice state sent to the execution client, including across an epoch boundary.
  - **Mainnet (Fulu):** none of the new fields appeared, and `parent_block_number` was still present.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #11439

title: Decode gossip messages on the async runner instead of the gossipsub thread
body:
## PR Description

`Eth2TopicHandler.handleMessage` SSZ-decoded every gossip message inline on the thread libp2p called it from. In jvm-libp2p that is the single gossipsub event thread (`AbstractRouter` runs on `P2PService`'s one-thread executor).

Split out of #11359 so it can go sooner.

### Changes
- `Eth2TopicHandler` decodes and runs the fork check inside the `asyncRunner` task, ~~so the gossipsub thread only enqueues and queued messages stay compressed until a `p2p` thread picks them up~~ (this it not correct, we need decompression and messageId calculation to happen, this still happens on the gossipsub thread. What has changed is SSZ parsing and the milestone check). A full queue now rejects the message before any decode work.
- `SnappyPreparedGossipMessage.getDecodedMessage()` reuses the payload already uncompressed for the message id instead of uncompressing a second time.
- Tests updated for the async decode, plus a test that decoding does not happen before the async runner runs and one that the uncompressor is called once.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Part (kinda) of https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku-internal/issues/359

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes gossip validation threading and message decode timing on the hot P2P path; behavior should match prior logic but ordering and executor load under congestion could differ.
> 
> **Overview**
> Moves **SSZ deserialization and the fork/milestone check** off libp2p’s single gossipsub thread by running them inside `Eth2TopicHandler.handleMessage`’s `asyncRunner` task (along with the existing processor path), so the gossipsub thread mainly enqueues work instead of parsing payloads inline.
> 
> **`SnappyPreparedGossipMessage`** refactors lazy decode behind a memoized `decodeMessage()` and routes `getUncompressed()` through `getDecodedMessage()`, so snappy decompression is **cached** when `getMessageId()` runs before later decode/SSZ handling—avoiding a second uncompress.
> 
> Tests are updated to drive the stub async runner before assertions, plus coverage that deserialize runs only after the runner executes and that uncompress happens once across message-id and decode calls.
>

title: [beacon api] update fork choice v2 to the final spec
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Brings `GET /eth/v2/debug/fork_choice` (added in #10800) in line with the final spec merged in [beacon-APIs#615](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/615). The node type now matches the spec's `NodeV2`: the same 14 required fields, in the spec's order.

Changes to each fork choice node:
- **`parent_payload_status` (new, required, nullable):** the payload status of the parent fork choice node, or `null` if the parent isn't retained in the fork choice tree. Pre-Gloas parents are reported as `full`, consistent with how pre-Gloas nodes are reported.
- **`parent_root`:** for Gloas `empty` and `full` nodes this is now the block's own root, pointing to the same block's `pending` node. Previously it was the beacon block's parent. Other nodes are unchanged.
- **`justified_checkpoint` and `finalized_checkpoint` (new):** the checkpoints recorded for the node.
- **`extra_data` (now required):** now holds `state_root` and the unrealised justified/finalized checkpoint fields, which were previously flat fields on the node. `justified_root` is dropped in favour of `justified_checkpoint`.
- **`execution_block_hash`:** unchanged. `pending` and `empty` nodes already carry the bid's `parent_block_hash`, and there is now a test for it.

Also:
- `GET /eth/v1/debug/fork_choice` is marked deprecated, with a pointer to v2, as in the spec.
- The v2 summary, description and field descriptions follow the spec text.

Supporting changes:
- **`ReadOnlyForkChoiceStrategy.getBlockDataWithParent()`** pairs each node with its parent node, read under the proto array lock. From Gloas, a block has several fork choice nodes, so the parent node can't be found from the parent root alone. The interface default reports no parent, so test and benchmark implementations are unaffected.
- **`withNullableField`** on the JSON object type builder: a required field written as `null` when empty. In OpenAPI it is described as `nullable: true` around `allOf`, so it also works for referenced types.

**Compatibility:** clients reading the previous v2 node's flat `state_root`, `justified_root` or `unrealised_*` fields need to read `justified_checkpoint` or `extra_data` instead.

### Testing
- **JSON builder:** nullable field with a value, with `null`, and its OpenAPI description.
- **`ForkChoiceStrategyTest`** (Gloas, real insertion path):
  - parent pairing for each link type: anchor with no parent, `empty`/`full` → `pending`, and `pending` → parent block's `full`;
  - `pending` and `empty` nodes carry the bid's `parent_block_hash`.
- **`ChainDataProviderTest` / `ChainDataProviderTestPhase0`:** Gloas parent roots and parent statuses. On a pre-Gloas chain, parents are `full` and only the anchor has none.
- **`GetForkChoiceV2Test`:** fixture covering `full`, `pending` and `null` parent statuses.
- **OpenAPI fixtures:** regenerated from the generated document. The changes are the new `NodeV2` schema, `GetForkChoiceResponseV2` referencing it, and the v1 and v2 path descriptions (with v1 deprecated).
- **Live check on Sepolia (Gloas):**
  - all 471 nodes had exactly the spec's fields;
  - every `empty`/`full` node pointed at its own `pending` node, and every `pending` node at its parent block's `empty` or `full` node;
  - only the anchor had a `null` parent status;
  - `parent_root` and `execution_block_hash` matched the blocks API for the blocks checked;
  - v1 still works and is deprecated in the served OpenAPI document.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #11442

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [ ] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes a debug API response shape and Gloas fork-choice parent semantics; v1 is deprecated but unchanged, while v2 clients must adapt to moved/renamed fields.
> 
> **Overview**
> Aligns **`GET /eth/v2/debug/fork_choice`** with the final beacon-APIs **`NodeV2`** shape: one array entry per `(block_root, payload_status)`, with updated parent linking for Gloas.
>

title: Log in to Docker Hub with OIDC instead of a stored password
body:
## PR Description

Replaces the stored Docker Hub push credential with OIDC. Docker Hub issues a short-lived token, scoped to `consensys/teku`, only to jobs running in the `publish` environment, so there is no long-lived push password in the repo secrets any more.

### Changes

- Bump `docker/login-action` from v4.0.0 to v4.6.0 (`dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f`) in both `publish-docker.yml` jobs and in `matrix-tests-template.yml`, since OIDC login needs >= v4.5.0. The new SHA is already in the repo Actions allowlist; the old one can be removed from the allowlist once this is merged.
- `publishDocker` gets `id-token: write` so the job can mint the GitHub OIDC token. `signAndAttest` already had it for cosign.
- Both publish login steps use `username: consensys` with no `password`, and pass `DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID` from the repo variable of the same name.
- `publishDocker` also sets `DOCKERHUB_OIDC_EXPIREIN: 600`, because login to push takes about 3m10s and the default token lifetime is 5 min.

### Follow-up after the first green publish on master

Delete `DOCKER_USER_RW` and `DOCKER_PASSWORD_RW`. `DOCKER_USER_RO` and `DOCKER_PASSWORD_RO` are not referenced by any workflow on master either, so they can go too if nothing else uses them. Drop `docker/login-action@b45d80f862d83dbcd57f89517bcf500b2ab88fb2` from the Actions allowlist.

title: Update reference tests to v1.7.0-beta.4
body:
## PR Description

Bump reference tests and specrefs to consensus-specs `v1.7.0-beta.4`, and implement the two beta.4 spec changes that affect forks Teku runs reference tests for.

**Exclude slashed validators from `calculate_committee_fraction` (consensus-specs #5679)**

This changes the phase0 fork-choice rule, so it applies to every fork, mainnet included.
- `calculateCommitteeFraction` now uses the effective balance of active, unslashed validators instead of the total active balance.
- `getProposerBoostAmount` (`compute_proposer_score`) now calls `calculateCommitteeFraction`, as the spec does.
- This affects proposer boost and the late-block reorg head and parent thresholds.

Fork choice calls this on every head update with the justified state, so the total is cached per epoch in a new `TransitionCaches.totalActiveUnslashedBalance`. `slashValidator` clears that cache because a slashing changes the total mid-epoch. The cost is one validator-registry scan per justified state per epoch.

**Clear pending builder payments of slashed proposers (consensus-specs #5719, Gloas)**

The clearing moves from `process_proposer_slashing` into a modified `slash_validator`.
- `BeaconStateMutatorsGloas.slashValidator` clears every `builder_pending_payments` entry whose `proposer_index` is the slashed validator.
- This now also covers attester slashings and payments from other slots in the window.
- The old proposer-slashing-only hook is removed from `AbstractBlockProcessor` and `BlockProcessorGloas`.

**Bump**
- `refTestVersion` → `v1.7.0-beta.4`, specrefs version → `v1.7.0-beta.4`, and specrefs regenerated.
- Removed `process_proposer_slashing#gloas`, since it's now identical to phase0, and added `slash_validator#gloas`.
- Heze-only beta.4 changes are added to the specref exceptions: EIP-8015, EIP-8365 `apply_pending_deposit`, and the inclusion-list signing domain. Teku doesn't run Heze reference tests yet, so they'll follow separately.

**Testing**
- Reference tests: all pass against beta.4 (63,880 tests, 3,660 skipped).
- The new `proposer_boost_excludes_slashed_validators` (every fork) and `builder_payment_removed_when_proposer_slashes_itself` (Gloas) cases fail with each fix reverted.
- New unit tests in `BeaconStateAccessorsTest` (slashed exclusion, proposer boost, cache invalidation after a slashing) and `BeaconStateMutatorsGloasTest` (payments cleared or kept on slashing).

title: Keep block reorgs over payload reorgs when coalescing head events
body:
While syncing, CoalescingChainHeadChannel delivers only the last head update and keeps the reorg context with the earliest common ancestor. That rule predates payload reorgs (#11437) and assumed every context was a block reorg. A payload reorg's common ancestor is its own head, so an early FULL to EMPTY flip could outrank a later block reorg forking above it. The flushed event then read as a payload reorg and pools, light client pruning and the chain_reorg event skipped the real block reorg.

Make the merge kind-aware: a block reorg always replaces a pending payload reorg and is never displaced by one; between block reorgs the earliest common ancestor still wins; between payload reorgs the latest wins. A payload reorg displaced this way is not logged once syncing completes, the delivered payload status still reflects the final head.

addresses: https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/pull/11437#discussion_r4225025787

title: Disallow new validators with BLS withdrawal credentials in Heze
body:
## PR Description

Implement [EIP-8365](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8365) for Heze ([consensus-specs#5713](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5713), `v1.7.0-beta.4`).

From Heze, `apply_pending_deposit` no longer creates validators with BLS (`0x00`) withdrawal credentials:
- New `EpochProcessorHeze` (extends `EpochProcessorGloas`) overrides `applyPendingDeposits`.
- When the deposit's pubkey isn't an existing validator and its credentials start with `BLS_WITHDRAWAL_PREFIX`, it returns before the signature check, so no validator is created and nothing is refunded.
- Everything else falls through to the existing logic, so top-ups to existing validators are unchanged.
- The check runs when the deposit is applied, so deposits queued before Heze are skipped too, as the spec requires.
- `SpecLogicHeze` now builds `EpochProcessorHeze`.
- The `apply_pending_deposit#heze` specref moves from the exceptions to the new implementation.

**Testing**

New `EpochProcessorHezeTest`, mirroring the spec's Heze `pending_deposits` cases:
- a new `0x00` validator with a valid signature is skipped, and so is one with an invalid signature;
- a new `0x01` validator is still created;
- a `0x00` top-up to an existing validator is applied, even with an invalid signature;
- a `0x00` deposit followed by a `0x01` deposit for the same key creates one validator, with the `0x01` credentials and only the second amount;
- Gloas still creates new `0x00` validators.

The valid-signature skip and same-key cases fail with the new check disabled.

Not verified against reference tests: the beta.4 Heze `epoch_processing/pending_deposits` fixtures use the EIP-8015 state layout, so Teku can't run Heze reference tests yet.

## Fixed Issue(s)
fixes #11461

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes consensus epoch deposit handling at the Heze fork; incorrect filtering could reject valid validators or accept forbidden BLS credentials.

> **Overview**
> Implements **EIP-8365** for the Heze fork: `apply_pending_deposit` no longer registers **new** validators when withdrawal credentials use the BLS prefix (`0x00`). Deposits are dropped with no refund, including ones already in the pending queue from before Heze.

That processor extends Gloas and short-circuits before the parent logic when the pubkey is unknown and credentials are BLS; eth1-style new validators and balance top-ups for existing keys behave as before. title: Resolve discovered peer addresses against both local transports
body:
A node with TCP disabled built TCP addresses for peers that advertise no QUIC endpoint and attached a TCP fallback after a failed QUIC dial. Both fail immediately, waste a selection slot and put the peer in the dial cooldown.

Pass the TCP flag from the network builder into address creation, so a discovered peer resolves to QUIC when both sides have it, otherwise TCP when both sides have it, otherwise no address. Drop candidates with no dialable address before selection and count them in the new peer_candidate_count_total metric.

title: Use the block's dependent root for inclusion list satisfaction
body:
## PR Description

Align inclusion list satisfaction with the Heze spec (`v1.7.0-beta.4`).

**Satisfaction uses only the block's own inclusion lists**

`record_payload_inclusion_list_satisfaction` checks a payload against `get_inclusion_list_transactions(store, slot - 1, dependent_root, only_timely=True)`, where `dependent_root` is the payload's beacon block's shuffling dependent root for the epoch of `slot - 1`.

Teku merged every timely, non-equivocating list at `slot - 1` across **all** dependent roots. On a fork, lists from another branch could make a valid payload count as unsatisfied, and `should_extend_payload` would then not extend it.

- `ForkChoice` now builds the key `(slot - 1, shuffling dependent root)` from the beacon block's state using `ShufflingDependentRootUtil`, which is also correct in an epoch's first slot, where `slot - 1` belongs to the previous epoch. Both callers (block import and execution payload envelope) use it.
- `ForkChoiceUtil.getInclusionListsForPayloadValidation` takes that key.
- `InclusionListStore.getInclusionLists(UInt64 slot)`, the cross-root lookup, is replaced by `getTimelyInclusionLists(SlotAndBlockRoot key)`.

**Duplicates no longer upgrade timeliness**

In `process_inclusion_list`, an inclusion list already stored for the validator is ignored: the first message and its timeliness are kept, and a different message marks the validator as an equivocator. Teku let an identical timely duplicate upgrade an untimely stored entry. It now ignores it.

**Not changed:** the forkchoice-updated path that records satisfaction stays as it is. The Heze optimistic-sync spec requires recording satisfaction when a payload moves from `NOT_VALIDATED` to `VALID`. Stopping an already-`VALID` payload from flipping needs per-node payload status, so that's left for a follow-up.

**Testing**
- `InclusionListStoreTest`:
  - timely lists are looked up per key, and lists under another dependent root for the same slot aren't mixed in;
  - a timely duplicate doesn't upgrade an untimely entry.
- New `ForkChoiceTest` case: lists stored under the block's dependent root, under another root, and one untimely. Only the first list's transaction reaches `engineNewPayload`. The test fails if the key uses the wrong root.
- `ethereum:spec` and `ethereum:statetransition` unit tests pass.
- There are no beta.4 Heze fork-choice reference tests involving inclusion lists, and Teku doesn't run Heze reference tests yet.

title: Align InclusionListsByIndices with the Heze spec
body:
## PR Description

Align `InclusionListsByIndices v1` with the Heze spec (`v1.7.0-beta.4`).

**Protocol ID**

Teku registered `/eth2/beacon_chain/req/inclusion_list_by_committee_indices/1/`. The spec uses `/eth2/beacon_chain/req/inclusion_lists_by_indices/1/`, so peers following the spec couldn't reach Teku. The constant and its getter in `BeaconChainMethodIds` are renamed to match. The request and handler classes and their metrics keep their names; that has no effect on the wire.

**Requested bits are committee positions**

The spec says `indices` is interpreted against `get_inclusion_list_committee(state, slot)`, where `state` is the `dependent_root` block processed up to `slot`. `InclusionListManager.getInclusionLists` tested each bit with the validator index (`committeeIndices.isSet(validatorIndex)`), so it returned the wrong validators' lists.
- It now retrieves the dependent block's state at `slot`, maps each set position to that committee member's validator index, and returns those validators' lists for the slot and dependent root.
- Equivocators are still excluded.
- The method now returns a `SafeFuture`, because retrieving the state is asynchronous. If the dependent state is unknown, the response is empty.
- The RPC handler waits for that future before streaming responses.
- `NodeDataProvider.getInclusionLists`, which has no callers, follows the new signature.

**Rate limiter refund**

`Eth2Peer.adjustInclusionListsRequest` refunded the blob sidecar rate limiter, even though inclusion list requests are approved against the inclusion list limiter. It now refunds the inclusion list limiter.

**Spec alignment**

The protocol ID, request and response encoding, `MAX_REQUEST_INCLUSION_LIST`, the serving window (Teku keeps 4 slots, more than `MIN_SLOTS_FOR_INCLUSION_LISTS_REQUESTS` = 1), equivocator exclusion, and the fork digest context all match.

One remaining dependency: Teku only serves lists that passed its gossip validation, which is still behind the spec. For example, it accepts empty inclusion lists. That will be fixed separately.

**Testing**
- New `InclusionListByCommitteeIndicesMessageHandlerTest` (the handler had no tests):
  - streaming all lists;
  - waiting for the lookup and refunding the limiter when fewer lists are sent;
  - a failed lookup completing with an error and a refund of 0;
  - both rate-limited paths;
  - request validation.
- `InclusionListManagerTest`:
  - a requested position whose validator index differs from the position returns only that member's list. It excludes the same validator under another root, other committee members, and the validator whose index equals the position;
  - equivocators are excluded;
  - an unknown dependent state, a pre-Heze slot, and out-of-range positions return nothing.
- `Eth2PeerTest`: the adjustment goes to the inclusion list rate limiter.
- `BeaconChainMethodsTest`: Heze registers exactly `/eth2/beacon_chain/req/inclusion_lists_by_indices/1/ssz_snappy`, and Gloas doesn't register it.
- The bit-mapping and rate-limiter tests fail if the fixes are reverted. Every changed line is covered by JaCoCo.
- `ethereum:statetransition`, `networking:eth2` and `data:provider` unit tests pass.

title: Align inclusion list gossip validation with the Heze spec
body:
## PR Description

Align inclusion list gossip validation and `on_inclusion_list` with the Heze spec (`v1.7.0-beta.4`), except the dependent root checks, which follow separately.

**Gossip validation (`SignedInclusionListValidator`)**

The checks now run in spec order:
1. **IGNORE** if two valid inclusion lists have already been seen for `(slot, dependent_root, validator_index)`.
   - The count (`seen.inclusion_list_counts`) is kept in the validator and only counts lists that fully validate. It's capped atomically, so concurrent validations can't let a third list through.
   - Previously it was derived from the manager's pool: keyed by validator only, across all slots and dependent roots, and it allowed a third list (`> 2`).
2. **IGNORE** if the inclusion list isn't for the current slot. This uses `GossipValidationHelper.isSlotCurrent`, the spec's `is_current_slot` with `MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY`. This check was missing, so past and future inclusion lists were accepted and forwarded.
3. **IGNORE** an inclusion list with no transactions. These were previously accepted.
4. **REJECT** transactions over `MAX_TRANSACTIONS_BYTES_PER_INCLUSION_LIST`, then **REJECT** any empty transaction. These used to run first, so peers were penalised for messages the spec only ignores.
5. The existing dependent root, committee and signature checks are unchanged here.

`validate()` no longer needs the manager's inclusion list pool.

**Fork choice (`on_inclusion_list`)**

Adds the spec's retention window (`slot <= current_slot` and `slot + MIN_SLOTS_FOR_INCLUSION_LISTS_REQUESTS >= current_slot`) and `transactions_size > 0`, with new failure reasons `SLOT_OUTSIDE_RETENTION_WINDOW` and `NO_TRANSACTIONS`. As in the spec, a list that arrives within clock disparity before its slot starts is forwarded on gossip but not stored by fork choice.

**Config**
- `MIN_SLOTS_FOR_INCLUSION_LISTS_REQUESTS` is now a Heze networking config value: 1 in mainnet, minimal and swift.
- Its specref is sourced and removed from the exceptions.
- `INCLUSION_LIST_COMMITTEE_SIZE`, a preset that already lives in `presets/*/heze.yaml`, is removed from those three configs.

**Not in this PR:** the spec's dependent root checks. These are: dependent block seen and validated, REJECT if after the shuffling dependent slot, `is_valid_dependent_root`, and the state taken from the dependent root. `validate_inclusion_list_gossip#heze` stays in the specref exceptions until then.

**Testing**
- `SignedInclusionListValidatorTest` (from 2 to 11 tests), mirroring the beta.4 `gossip_inclusion_list` cases:
  - a third message from a validator is ignored;
  - counts are kept per dependent root;
  - invalid lists aren't counted;
  - a third list that was validating concurrently is ignored;
  - a list not for the current slot is ignored;
  - a list with no transactions is ignored;
  - an empty transaction or oversized transactions are rejected;
  - the slot check and the seen count both apply before the transaction REJECTs.
- `ForkChoiceTest`:
  - new tests for no transactions, a future slot, and the retention window boundary;
  - the existing empty transaction test now includes a non-empty transaction, because a list holding only an empty transaction fails `transactions_size > 0` first.
- Disabling any of the new checks fails at least one test. Every changed line in the validator, `ForkChoice` and `InclusionListManager` is covered.
- `ethereum:spec` and `ethereum:statetransition` unit tests pass. The beta.4 Heze reference tests can't run yet; they need EIP-8015.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Part of bringing EIP-7805 on `heze-devnet-0` up to `v1.7.0-beta.4`.

> **Medium Risk**

> 
> **Overview**
> Brings Heze inclusion list handling in line with **v1.7.0-beta.4** gossip and `on_inclusion_list` rules (dependent-root checks are explicitly out of scope).
> 
> **Gossip (`SignedInclusionListValidator`)** reorders and tightens validation: **IGNORE** when two valid lists were already seen for `(slot, dependent_root, validator_index)` using an internal `seen.inclusion_list_counts` map (atomically capped, only after full validation) instead of the manager’s pool keyed only by validator; **IGNORE** non-current-slot messages via `GossipValidationHelper.isSlotCurrent`; **IGNORE** lists with no transactions; **REJECT** oversize or empty transactions only after those IGNORE checks. `validate()` no longer takes the inclusion list pool.

title: Accept inclusion list dependent roots from any branch
body:
## PR Description

Complete `validate_inclusion_list_gossip` for the Heze spec (`v1.7.0-beta.4`) by accepting dependent roots from any valid branch.

**Problem**

`SignedInclusionListValidator` only accepted an inclusion list whose `dependent_root` matched the local head's branch (`spec.getInclusionListDependentRoot` on the state in effect at the slot). It also checked the committee and signature against that state. Inclusion lists for competing branches, which spec-following clients accept, were ignored, which affects inclusion list satisfaction and bid inclusion list bits after reorgs.

**Change**

The spec's dependent root checks, in spec order:
1. **IGNORE** if the dependent block hasn't been seen.
2. **IGNORE** if the dependent block hasn't passed validation (no block state).
3. **REJECT** if the dependent block's slot is after `compute_shuffling_dependent_slot(epoch)`.
4. **IGNORE** if it isn't a possible dependent block for the committee lookahead. This uses the existing `GossipValidationHelper.isPossibleDependentRoot`, the spec's `is_valid_dependent_root`, also used by proposer preferences validation.
5. The committee and signature are checked against the dependent block's state processed to the start of the lookahead epoch: the checkpoint state `(lookahead_epoch, dependent_root)`.

The checkpoint states are cached, and only inclusion lists that already passed the cheap checks (seen count, current slot, transactions, dependent block known and possible) reach the state lookup.

**Also**
- Removes the unreachable `SAVE_FOR_FUTURE` handling from `InclusionListManager`. The validator never returns it.
- `validate_inclusion_list_gossip#heze` moves from the specref exceptions to a sourced entry. With #11468, every gossip check is now implemented in spec order.

**Testing**

`SignedInclusionListValidatorTest` grows from 11 to 19 tests, mirroring the beta.4 `gossip_inclusion_list` dependent root cases:
- `valid_dependent_block_on_fork`: a dependent root on another branch is accepted, and is validated against that root's lookahead checkpoint state;
- the dependent block hasn't been seen, or hasn't passed validation;
- `reject_dependent_block_at_lookahead_epoch_start`;
- `ignore_dependent_block_not_possible`;
- the lookahead state is unavailable;
- `reject_non_genesis_dependent_root_in_genesis_epoch`;
- `reject_includer_not_in_committee`.

The REJECT tests assert the specific reason. Disabling any of the new checks, or using the wrong epoch's state, fails its test. Every changed line is covered. Unit tests across all modules pass. The beta.4 Heze reference tests can't run yet; they need EIP-8015.

title: Skip signing inclusion lists with no transactions
body:
## PR Description

Stop the validator client signing and submitting inclusion lists with no transactions.

**Problem**

The spec IGNOREs inclusion lists where `transactions_size == 0`. Since #11468, Teku's beacon node does too, and `SignedInclusionListPublisher` only publishes accepted lists, so empty lists already don't reach the network. However, `InclusionListProductionDuty` still:
- **signed** every inclusion list the beacon node returned, including empty ones. With a remote signer, that's a signing request per committee member per slot.
- **submitted** it. The beacon node ignores it, and because only REJECTs are reported back as errors, the duty was **counted as a success** even though nothing was published.

This should happen often, whenever the execution layer has no transactions to put in an inclusion list.

**Change**

When the inclusion list has no transaction bytes (the same `transactions_size == 0` condition gossip ignores, so a list of only empty transactions counts too), the duty skips signing and returns `ProductionResult.noop(...)`. No-op results aren't submitted, and the duty reports `NOOP` instead of success. Lists with transactions are handled as before.

**Not in this PR:** the spec says to broadcast by `get_inclusion_list_due_ms()`, built on the current slot's block if it has become head. Teku builds the list at the start of the slot (#11404). That was a deliberate change, so it's left for a separate discussion.

**Testing**

`InclusionListProductionDuty` had no tests. The new `InclusionListProductionDutyTest` covers:
- no validators;
- a list with transactions, which is signed and sent;
- a list with no transactions, and one with only empty transactions, neither signed nor sent;
- a mix of validators, where only the non-empty list is sent;
- an unavailable inclusion list, reported as a failure.

The three empty-list tests fail if the skip is removed. Every changed line is covered. Unit tests across all modules pass.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Part of bringing EIP-7805 on `heze-devnet-0` up to `v1.7.0-beta.4`.

Those cases return `ProductionResult.noop`, so the duty reports **NOOP** instead of a false success and remote signers are not hit every slot when the EL has nothing to include.

title: Record forkchoiceUpdated IL satisfaction only on a payload's NOT_VALIDATED to VALID transition
body:
## PR Description

Only record inclusion list satisfaction from a forkchoiceUpdated response when a payload transitions from `NOT_VALIDATED` to `VALID`, and record it against the block that payload belongs to, as the Heze optimistic sync spec requires.

**Problem**

The spec (`heze/optimistic-sync.md`): *"When a block transitions from `NOT_VALIDATED` -> `VALID`, the response from the execution engine also indicates whether the block's execution payload satisfies the inclusion list constraints. The consensus engine MUST record the result for that block. The recorded inclusion list satisfaction of its ancestors remains unchanged."*

Teku recorded "unsatisfied" from any `VALID` forkchoiceUpdated response, against the head's block root:
1. **Flip:** a later `VALID` response could change an already `VALID`, satisfied payload to unsatisfied. Satisfaction recorded at import must not change.
2. **EMPTY head:** for an EMPTY node, the execution head is the nearest FULL ancestor's payload (usually the parent's). The verdict was recorded against the EMPTY block instead of the block whose payload it describes. That could stop fork choice extending the EMPTY block, and left the parent's payload marked satisfied even though `markNodeValid` had just made it `VALID`, so fork choice could extend an unsatisfied payload.

**Change**

`recordPayloadInclusionListSatisfaction` (forkchoiceUpdated path) now:
- finds the FULL node whose payload is the execution head. For a FULL head that is the head itself. For an EMPTY head it walks up through EMPTY nodes to the nearest FULL ancestor;
- records against that node's block root only if the node is still **optimistic**, which is the `NOT_VALIDATED -> VALID` transition.

The node data is read through `recentChainData.getForkChoiceStrategy()` (the read-only strategy, which takes its own lock), because this runs before `finishAsync` switches to the fork choice thread. `ForkChoice.getForkChoiceStrategy()` can't be used there.

**Tests**
- New: `shouldNotChangeSatisfactionOfAlreadyValidPayload`. A later "unsatisfied" response doesn't change a payload imported as `VALID` and satisfied.
- New: `shouldRecordSatisfactionOfEmptyNodesParentPayload`. With an EMPTY head built on an optimistic FULL parent, a "VALID, unsatisfied" response is recorded against the parent, and not against the EMPTY block.
- New: `shouldNotChangeSatisfactionOfEmptyNodesValidParentPayload`. If the parent payload was already `VALID` and satisfied, an EMPTY head's response changes nothing.
- Updated: `shouldRecordDelayedUnsatisfiedInclusionListResult` was actually exercising the flip. The test harness's automatic forkchoiceUpdated reply (`VALID`, no satisfaction info) validated the payload first, then the test sent a second response. The harness now replies `SYNCING`, so the test's response is the real transition, and it's recorded.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Part of bringing EIP-7805 on `heze-devnet-0` up to `v1.7.0-beta.4`.

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes fork-choice store updates on execution-engine responses, which can affect Heze chain extension and head selection when inclusion lists are unsatisfied; scope is limited to the fcU path with added guards and tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Aligns Heze **inclusion list satisfaction** updates from `forkchoiceUpdated` with optimistic-sync rules: only when a payload first becomes **VALID** from **NOT_VALIDATED**, and only for the block that payload belongs to.
> 
> **`recordPayloadInclusionListSatisfaction` (fcU path)** now takes the fork-choice **head node** instead of a block root. It records “unsatisfied” only if the response is valid with unsatisfied IL **and** the execution-head **FULL** node (walking up through **EMPTY** heads to the parent’s payload) is still **optimistic**. Already-valid payloads keep satisfaction from import; a later fcU cannot flip them. For an **EMPTY** head, satisfaction is applied to the **parent’s** FULL payload root, not the empty block.
> 
> Node status is read via **`recentChainData.getForkChoiceStrategy()`** (`ReadOnlyForkChoiceStrategy`) because this runs before the async hop to the fork-choice thread.
> 
> **Tests:** harness uses **`SYNCING`** so delayed validation is the real transition; new cases cover no flip on already-valid payloads, EMPTY-head parent targeting, and unchanged parent satisfaction when already valid.

title: Create inclusion lists on the current slot's block
body:
## PR Description

Create inclusion lists on the current slot's block, and publish them before the inclusion list due time, as the Heze validator spec requires.

@mehdi-aouadi, this follows up #11404, as we discussed, so you don't need to look at it on holiday. It keeps your fix for late publishing and also builds the list on the current slot's block.

**Background**

The spec (`heze/validator.md`, *Inclusion list proposal*):

> If a validator is in the current inclusion list committee, the validator should create and broadcast the `signed_inclusion_list` to the global `inclusion_list` subnet by `get_inclusion_list_due_ms()` milliseconds into the slot, built against the block for the current slot if it has been processed and confirmed as head, or against the local head returned by `get_head()` otherwise.

`get_inclusion_list_due_ms()` is `INCLUSION_LIST_DUE_BPS = 6667`, about 8 s into a 12 s slot.

| | When the list is created | Built on |
|---|---|---|
| Before #11404 | **At** the inclusion list due time (~8 s) | head at that time |
| #11404 (current) | Slot start (0 ms) | the **previous** slot's head |
| This PR | When the slot's block becomes head; fallback at the attestation due time (3 s on mainnet) | the current slot's block, or the local head |

Creating the list at the due time meant signing and gossip ended after the deadline, so lists were published late. #11404 fixed that by moving creation to the slot start, but then the current slot's block can't have arrived, so the list is always built on the previous slot's head.

**Change**

- **Head event trigger.** When the head moves to a block, `onInclusionListCreationDue(slot)` is called next to the existing early attestation trigger. This happens in both validator client paths: `IndependentTimerEventChannelEventAdapter.chainHeadUpdated` (in-process) and `EventSourceHandler` (remote). It only applies from Heze, and only when `generateEarlyAttestations` is enabled (the default). That flag already means "act on head events" and is the escape hatch for unreliable head events.
- **Timer fallback.** `HezeTimeBasedEventAdapter` schedules creation at the attestation due time instead of 0 ms. That covers a missing or late block (a block after the attestation due time isn't timely), and still leaves about 5 s to publish before the inclusion list due time.
- **No duplicates.** Whichever trigger fires first creates the list. `AbstractDutyScheduler.onProductionDue` already ignores a slot at or before `lastProductionSlot`, so the later trigger, and the second Gloas head event when the payload arrives, do nothing.

**Tests**

- New `IndependentTimerEventChannelEventAdapterTest`: pre-Heze head events trigger only attestations, Heze head events also trigger inclusion lists, and nothing is triggered early when early attestations are disabled.
- `EventSourceHandlerTest`: a Heze head event triggers inclusion list creation; no early duties when disabled.
- `SlotEventVerifierTestUtil`: the Heze timer is expected at the attestation due time.
- Full `./gradlew test` passes, except `:infrastructure:kzg:test`, which fails locally with `UnsatisfiedLinkError` loading the native KZG library. That's unrelated to this change.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Part of bringing EIP-7805 on `heze-devnet-0` up to `v1.7.0-beta.4`. Follows up #11404.

> Changes validator duty timing for HEZE inclusion lists across in-process and remote paths; incorrect timing could cause late or wrong-head lists, though existing per-slot production dedup limits duplicate work.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Heze inclusion lists** are now built against the **current slot’s block when it becomes head**, with a timer fallback if the block is missing or late—so lists can still be published before the inclusion list due time.
> 
> On **chain head** (in-process `IndependentTimerEventChannelEventAdapter` and remote `EventSourceHandler`), `onInclusionListCreationDue` runs alongside early attestation creation when `generateEarlyAttestations` is on and the slot is **HEZE+**. **`HezeTimeBasedEventAdapter`** moves the scheduled fallback from slot start (**0 ms**) to **attestation due time** (~3 s on mainnet), leaving room to gossip before ~8 s. Wiring passes **`Spec`** into the event adapters; tests cover Heze vs pre-Heze, disabled early duties, and the updated timer expectation in `SlotEventVerifierTestUtil`.
