title: Implement EIP-8015 in the Heze state transition
body:
## PR Description

Implement [EIP-8015](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8015) (remove `deposits` and `eth1_data`) in the Heze state transition, as in consensus-specs `v1.7.0-beta.4` ([#5655](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5655)). This is the spec layer; block production and the Eth1 services follow in a separate PR.

**Containers** (progressive containers: removed fields become gaps, so the remaining fields keep their tree positions)
- `BeaconBlockBody`: no `eth1_data` or `deposits`, `active_fields(width=13, gaps=(1, 6))`. New `BeaconBlockBodySchemaHezeImpl`, `BeaconBlockBodyHezeImpl` and `BeaconBlockBodyBuilderHeze`, also used by `SchemaDefinitionsHeze.createBeaconBlockBodyBuilder()`.
- `BeaconState`: no `eth1_data`, `eth1_data_votes`, `eth1_deposit_index` or `deposit_requests_start_index`, `active_fields(width=46, gaps=(8, 9, 10, 28))`. New `BeaconStateHeze`/`MutableBeaconStateHeze` and impls, extending the Gloas ones, and `BeaconStateSchemaHeze` builds its own field list.

**Removed field accessors.** The accessors stay on the shared `BeaconState`, `MutableBeaconState` and `BeaconBlockBody` interfaces. On Heze they return empty values (zero `Eth1Data`, empty lists, `0`) and log an error with a stack trace (`Eip8015RemovedFields`), as Heze logic should never reach them. Writes do nothing. `toString`, `copyCommonFieldsFromSource` and the test state builders skip fields the schema doesn't have, so they never trigger the error.

**State transition**
- `process_block`: `BlockProcessorHeze.processEth1Data` does nothing.
- `process_operations`: no deposit checks or processing (new `processBodyDeposits` hook in `AbstractBlockProcessor`).
- `process_epoch`: `EpochProcessorHeze.processEth1DataReset` does nothing.
- `upgrade_to_heze`: asserts `eth1_deposit_index == deposit_requests_start_index` and drops the removed fields.
- Deposit requests: `ExecutionRequestsProcessorHeze` skips the `deposit_requests_start_index` update (new `updateDepositRequestsStartIndex` hook in Electra). The Heze spec inherits `process_deposit_request` unchanged, but the field is gone, and the Heze `operations/deposit_request` reference tests only append the pending deposit.

**Genesis**
- A Heze genesis skips the removed fields and seeds the RANDAO mixes from the Eth1 block hash directly.
- **Behaviour change outside Heze:** a Fulu or later genesis now sets `deposit_requests_start_index` to the genesis deposit count instead of `UNSET`, as the spec's test genesis does. Otherwise `upgrade_to_heze`'s assert fails for any Teku-generated chain that forks to Heze later. Teku already treats the Eth1 bridge as finished from Fulu (`isFormerDepositMechanismDisabled`), so nothing else depends on the value. Electra genesis is unchanged.

**Specrefs:** `BeaconBlockBody#heze`, `BeaconState#heze`, `process_block#heze`, `process_operations#heze`, `process_epoch#heze`, `upgrade_to_heze#heze` and `verify_block_body_operation_limits#heze` moved from the exceptions to the implementation.

**REST:** the Heze `BeaconBlockBody` and `BeaconState` OpenAPI schemas lose the removed fields.

**Testing**
- Beta.4 Heze reference tests, run locally with Heze temporarily enabled in the reference test finder (not part of this PR, as Heze reference tests aren't enabled yet):
  - `ssz_static` `BeaconState`, `BeaconBlockBody`, `BeaconBlock`, `BeaconBlockHeader`, `SignedBeaconBlock`: 640/640
  - `fork/fork`: 17/17
  - `operations/deposit_request`: 30/30
  - `epoch_processing` (17 suites): 339/339
  - `sanity/slots`: 34/34, `finality`: 10/10, `random`: 32/32
  - `sanity/blocks`: 155/167. The 12 failures are the `invalid_too_many_*` cases, which Teku rejects at decoding, as already allowlisted for Gloas in `SszMaxLengthFixtures`.
- Unit tests: gap layouts and tree positions, removed accessors returning empty values and logging, writes not changing the state, `toString`, SSZ round trips, the body builder, the upgrade assert, deposit requests, and a Heze interop genesis plus `processEpoch` at an Eth1 voting period boundary not touching the removed fields.
- Full `./gradlew test` passes, except `:infrastructure:kzg:test`, which fails locally with `UnsatisfiedLinkError` loading the native KZG library. `OpenApiIntegrationTest` passes.

**Devnet note:** this changes the SSZ layout of Heze blocks and states, so all clients on a Heze devnet need to move to it together. If a devnet forks to Heze after genesis, its genesis state needs `eth1_deposit_index == deposit_requests_start_index`, or the upgrade fails.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Part of #11463 (block production and the Eth1 services follow).

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes Heze SSZ layouts and consensus rules for deposits and Eth1 voting; all nodes on a Heze devnet must upgrade together, and pre-fork chains need a compatible genesis/bridge state for `upgrade_to_heze`.
> 
> **Overview**
> Implements **EIP-8015** for the Heze fork by dropping the legacy Eth1 deposit bridge from consensus containers and state transition, while keeping **progressive SSZ tree positions** via field gaps (same indices as Gloas, absent fields).
> 
> **Containers:** New Heze `BeaconBlockBody` (no `eth1_data` / `deposits`) and `BeaconState` (no `eth1_data`, `eth1_data_votes`, `eth1_deposit_index`, `deposit_requests_start_index`), with schema/builder/impl types wired through `SchemaRegistry` and `SchemaDefinitionsHeze`. Shared interface getters for removed fields are stubbed via `Eip8015RemovedFields` (empty values + error log); copies, `toString`, and test builders skip fields the schema no longer has.
> 
> **State transition:** `BlockProcessorHeze` skips `process_eth1_data`, deposit verification, and body deposit processing; `EpochProcessorHeze` skips `process_eth1_data_reset`; `ExecutionRequestsProcessorHeze` no longer updates `deposit_requests_start_index`. `upgrade_to_heze` requires `eth1_deposit_index == deposit_requests_start_index` before upgrade and does not carry removed state fields.
> 
> **Genesis / cross-milestone:** Heze genesis omits Eth1 state fields and seeds RANDAO from the Eth1 block hash directly. **Fulu+ genesis** now sets `deposit_requests_start_index` to the genesis deposit count (not `UNSET`) so later Heze upgrades satisfy the new assert.
> 
> **API / fixtures:** Beacon REST OpenAPI and produce-block JSON fixtures drop the removed Heze fields. Specrefs document the new containers and fork functions.
>

title: Tighten the CI publish path and drop the Docker Hub login from acceptance tests
body:
## PR Description

Follow-up to #11455 from a security review of the workflows. The publish job ran Gradle while holding `id-token: write` for the `publish` environment, and the acceptance shards logged in to Docker Hub with a credential committed to the repo.

### Changes

- `publishDocker` no longer runs Gradle, the prepare action or the assemble-output unpack, so none of the build dependency tree executes in a job that can mint a Docker Hub push token. It downloads the `distribution-tar` artifact that `assemble` already uploads and untars it into `build/docker-teku/teku` with plain `tar`, the same layout `dockerDistUntar` produced. The checkout is shallow again since nothing there calls `git describe`.
- The tag script in `publishDocker` reads `github.ref_name`, `inputs.jdk_version`, `inputs.include_hash_in_docker` and friends from `env:` and quotes them, so a crafted ref name or `workflow_dispatch` input cannot inject shell into that job. Ran the script locally for release, RC, master and dispatch inputs and the computed tags are unchanged.
- The acceptance shards stop logging in to Docker Hub and instead merge `registry-mirrors: ["https://mirror.gcr.io"]` into `/etc/docker/daemon.json` and restart the daemon. No credential, no rate limit, and forked PRs keep working. The daemon falls back to docker.io when the mirror misses.
- Remove `secrets: inherit` from `publishDockerJDK25` and `publishDockerJDK26`. `publish-docker.yml` only uses `vars.DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID` and `github.token`, neither of which needs it. `publishRelease` keeps it.
- Move the `# vX.Y.Z` comments onto the `uses:` line so Renovate tracks them, and add the missing ones for `gradle/actions` and `softprops/action-gh-release`. Bump `setup-buildx-action` v4.0.0 to v4.4.1, `build-push-action` v7.0.0 to v7.4.0 and `cosign-installer` v4.1.0 to v4.1.2.
- Point `CODEOWNERS` at `@Consensys-Incorporated/protocols-teku`. The old teams are in the previous org and GitHub reports them as unknown owners.

The publish path only runs on master and tags, so the first master push after merge exercises the new untar step and the bumped actions. The removed Docker Hub account still needs to be revoked on the Docker Hub side, since the credential stays in git history.

## Fixed Issue(s)

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes affect master/tag Docker publishing and acceptance CI; publish behavior should match prior tags but the new artifact-only path needs a successful master run to validate end-to-end.
> 
> **Overview**
> Hardens CI after a security review: the Docker publish job no longer runs Gradle or the full build tree while holding `id-token: write` for Docker Hub OIDC push.
> 
> **`publish-docker`** now downloads the `distribution-tar` artifact from `assemble`, unpacks it with `tar` into the same layout `dockerDistUntar` used, and only checks out the repo for the JDK-specific Dockerfile. Tag computation reads ref and workflow inputs via `env` so malicious ref or dispatch values cannot inject shell. **`ci.yml`** drops `secrets: inherit` on the JDK25/JDK26 publish workflow calls since OIDC uses `vars` and `github.token` only.
> 
> **Acceptance test shards** stop using a committed Docker Hub login; they configure `registry-mirrors` to `https://mirror.gcr.io` and restart Docker so pulls avoid Hub rate limits and forked PRs still work.
> 
> Also pins Renovate-friendly `# vX.Y.Z` comments on several actions (with minor bumps for buildx, build-push, cosign), and updates **CODEOWNERS** for `.github/workflows/` to `@Consensys-Incorporated/protocols-teku`.

title: Stop using Eth1 data and deposits from Heze
body:
## PR Description

Stop the node using Eth1 data and deposits from Heze. Follows #11473, which removed `eth1_data` and `deposits` from the Heze block body and the Eth1 fields from the Heze state (EIP-8015). On Heze, the removed field accessors return empty values and log an error, so these paths would otherwise log errors on every block and every finalization.

**Changes**
- **Block production.** `BeaconBlockBodyBuilder` gets `supportsEth1DataAndDeposits()` (default `true`, `false` for `BeaconBlockBodyBuilderHeze`), like the other `supports*` checks. `BlockOperationSelectorFactory` only asks `Eth1DataCache` for an Eth1 vote and `DepositProvider` for deposits when the builder supports them.
- **`DepositProvider.onNewFinalizedCheckpoint`** returns early when the finalized state is Heze or later. There are no more bridge deposits to prune or deposit tree to finalize, and it read `eth1_deposit_index` and `eth1_data` from the finalized state without a guard.
- **Teku REST** `GET /teku/v1/beacon/state/{state_id}/eth1voting` and `GET /teku/v1/beacon/pool/eth1data` return 400 ("Eth1 data was removed in Heze (EIP-8015)") for a Heze state. Every endpoint already declares a 400 response, so the OpenAPI spec doesn't change. `GET /teku/v1/beacon/pool/deposits` doesn't read the state and is unchanged.

`DepositProvider.getDeposits` and `Eth1DataCache.updateMetrics` already return early from Fulu, because `isFormerDepositMechanismDisabled` is `true`. `Eth1DataCache.getEth1Vote` returns `state.getEth1Data()` from Fulu, which is a removed field read on Heze, but its only callers are block production and the `eth1data` endpoint, which no longer call it for Heze.

**Tests**
- `BlockOperationSelectorFactoryTest`: a builder that supports Eth1 data gets the Eth1 vote and deposits, and one that doesn't makes no calls to `Eth1DataCache` or `DepositProvider`.
- `DepositProviderTest`: a Heze finalized state logs no removed field errors, prunes nothing and doesn't write to storage.
- `GetEth1DataTest`, `GetEth1VotingSummaryTest`: a Heze state gets a 400, without calling the Eth1 data provider.
- `BeaconBlockBodyHezeTest`: Heze's body builder doesn't support Eth1 data and deposits.
- Full `./gradlew test` and `:data:beaconrestapi:integrationTest` pass locally, except two environment failures on my machine: `:infrastructure:kzg:test` (`UnsatisfiedLinkError` loading the native KZG library) and `RestApiInterfacesIntegrationTest.shouldOnlyListenOnLocalhostByDefault` (connect timeout instead of refusal).

## Fixed Issue(s)

Fixes #11463 (with #11473). This PR targets `heze-devnet-0`, so GitHub won't close the issue automatically.

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes block production and deposit finalization on a consensus fork boundary; mistakes could omit pre-Heze behavior or mishandle Heze blocks, but scope is guarded by milestone checks and builder capability flags.
> 
> **Overview**
> Aligns Teku with **Heze (EIP-8015)** after Eth1 bridge fields were removed from block bodies and state, so the node no longer touches removed accessors on every block or finalization.
> 
> **Block production** gates Eth1 voting and deposit inclusion on a new `supportsEth1DataAndDeposits()` hook on `BeaconBlockBodyBuilder` (default `true`, `false` on `BeaconBlockBodyBuilderHeze`). `BlockOperationSelectorFactory` only calls `Eth1DataCache` and `DepositProvider` when the builder supports those fields.
> 
> **Deposit finalization** skips `onNewFinalizedCheckpoint` work when the latest finalized state is Heze or later, avoiding reads of removed `eth1_deposit_index` / `eth1_data` and unnecessary prune/storage updates.
> 
> **Teku REST** returns **400** with a shared message for `GET /teku/v1/beacon/pool/eth1data` and `GET /teku/v1/beacon/state/{state_id}/eth1voting` when the resolved state is Heze+, without calling `Eth1DataProvider`.
> 
> Tests cover the gated block path, Heze finalization, REST behavior, and the Heze body builder flag.

title: Fetch envelopes by range from canonical chain
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
The fix has three parts, each test-first.

- Serving (the reported bug). 
A new payload-status-aware walk, ForkChoiceUtil.getAncestorNodes, is exposed through Spec, RecentChainData.getAncestorNodesOnHeadChain and CombinedChainDataClient.getAncestorNodes. The handler now serves a hot slot only when its node on the head chain is FULL, so EMPTY ancestors and a PENDING head are skipped. The “all finalized” shortcut now compares against the finalized block’s slot rather than the finalized epoch, so the finalized block’s own payload status comes from the head chain instead of the database.
- Persistence. 
Orphaned envelopes are detected in KvStoreDatabase.findOrphanedExecutionPayloadRoots at finalization by walking the finalized chain pairwise and comparing each child’s bid against its parent’s bid, reading block bodies from the database. Fork choice is not used because the checkpoint-sync anchor has no FULL variant, so its child always attaches to EMPTY. Detection is skipped while Gloas is only scheduled. Envelopes already persisted for finalized orphaned payloads by earlier versions are not removed, which only affects Gloas devnet nodes upgraded in place.
- Sync import. 
SyncSourceBatch drops an envelope when the next block in the batch did not build on it, including across requests within a batch, instead of importing it. The last block of a batch cannot be resolved within the batch, so that boundary is not covered. This matches the issue’s “optional” scope and is documented in the Javadoc.

## Fixed Issue(s)
<!-- Please link to fixed issue(s) here using format: fixes #<issue number> -->
<!-- Example: "fixes #2" -->
Fixes #11246 

## Documentation

- [ ] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [ ] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes Gloas P2P envelope serving, forward sync import, and finalized envelope pruning; incorrect payload-status logic could omit valid envelopes or serve wrong forks, but scope is EPBS/Gloas rather than core auth or payments.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes Gloas **ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesByRange** so peers only receive envelopes for execution payloads on the **current head chain** (fork-choice node **FULL**), not orphaned payloads from EMPTY/PENDING variants.
> 
> The RPC handler walks the head chain via new **`getAncestorNodes`** plumbing (`ForkChoiceUtil` → `Spec` → `RecentChainData` / `CombinedChainDataClient`) instead of block roots alone, and skips hot slots whose payload is not on-chain. Finalized slots before the finalized block still use the DB; the finalized block’s payload status is resolved from the head chain.
> 
> **Sync** drops execution payload envelopes when the following block did not build on the parent’s payload (`validateAndPruneNewExecutionPayloads`), with **`dropExecutionPayload` / `restoreExecutionPayload`** at batch boundaries when forks are re-downloaded. **`isParentBlockFull`** moves to **`MiscHelpersGloas`**.
> 
> **Persistence** deletes blinded envelopes at finalization when a finalized child built on the parent’s EMPTY variant (`findOrphanedExecutionPayloadRoots` in **`KvStoreDatabase`**). Envelopes already on disk from older releases are not migrated away (noted in the changelog).
>

title: Fix Heze block import reading removed deposits, cover gaps, drop dead code
body:
## PR Description

Running the Heze reference tests (#11476) and the `ethereum/spec` and `ethereum/statetransition` unit tests with JaCoCo found a bug, a few untested paths, and dead code.

**Bug: every Heze block import logged an EIP-8015 error**

`BlockProcessorCapella.validateBlockPreProcessing` reads `body.getDeposits()` for every block, in case a failed BLS to execution change check needs retrying with the block's deposits applied. Heze inherits it, and the Heze body's `getDeposits()` returns an empty list but logs `Accessed deposits, which was removed in Heze (EIP-8015)` with a stack trace. The node takes this path on every block import (`ForkChoice` → `processAndValidateBlock` → `validateBlockPreProcessing`), so the result was correct but each Heze block logged an ERROR. It showed up in 843 Heze reference test results.

Deposits are now read only when the BLS change check fails, through a protected `getDepositsForBlsChangeRetry` hook, which `BlockProcessorHeze` overrides to return no deposits. Behaviour is unchanged for every fork.

**Tests for code neither suite ran**
- `BlockProcessorHezeTest`: a Heze block through `processAndValidateBlock` doesn't access removed fields. It fails without the fix.
- `InclusionListManagerTest`: `onSlot` keeps lists for `SLOTS_TO_RETAIN` slots and prunes them after. It fails without pruning.
- New `InclusionListDutiesGeneratorTest`: duties match the spec's `get_inclusion_list_committee_assignment` (computed independently), unknown validators get none, and the dependent root is right for the current and next epoch.
- `BeaconStateHezeTest`: the two remaining removed-field accessors.

The duties generator maps each validator to the last slot it's assigned to in the epoch, while the spec function returns the first. They always agree: the inclusion list committee for a slot comes from that slot's beacon committees, and a validator is in exactly one slot's beacon committees per epoch. The new test checks this against the spec definition.

**Dead code removed**
- `InclusionListUtil.getInclusionListCommitteeRoot`, `hasCorrectCommitteeRoot` and `getInclusionListCommitteeAssignment`, their `Spec` wrappers, and the committee vector schema they used. The committee root was replaced by the dependent root.
- `ValidatorsUtilHeze` (Heze uses `ValidatorsUtilGloas`) and `ValidatorsUtil.getValidatorIndexToILCommitteeAssignmentMap`. Nothing called them.
- `ExecutionRequestsProcessorHeze`, its test, and Electra's `updateDepositRequestsStartIndex` hook, from #11473. Fulu's `processDepositRequests` already doesn't set `deposit_requests_start_index`, so they never ran. Electra's inline code is restored.

**Testing**
- Heze reference tests: 12222 pass, and none logs a removed-field access (843 results did before).
- Full `./gradlew test` and `spotlessCheck` pass, except `:infrastructure:kzg:test`, which fails locally with `UnsatisfiedLinkError` loading the native KZG library.
- `ethspecify check` passes.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Follow-up to #11473 and #11476.

title: Test inclusion list duties run once per slot
body:
## PR Description

Test that inclusion list duties run once per slot.

Since #11472, both the head event for a slot's block and the fallback timer at the attestation due time trigger inclusion list creation for the same slot. That relies on `AbstractDutyScheduler.onProductionDue` ignoring a slot at or before `lastProductionSlot`, which is tested for attestation and block duties (`shouldNotPerformDutiesForSameSlotTwice`) but wasn't for inclusion lists.

`InclusionListDutySchedulerTest.shouldNotPerformDutiesForSameSlotTwice` loads epoch 0's duties, triggers creation for slot 1 twice, and checks the duty runs once. It fails if the `lastProductionSlot` check is removed.

Test only, no production code changes. `:validator:client:test` (725 tests) and `spotlessCheck` pass.

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [gradle/actions](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions) | action | major | `v5.0.2` → `v6.4.0` |
| [softprops/action-gh-release](https://redirect.github.com/softprops/action-gh-release) | action | major | `v2.6.1` → `v3.0.3` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>gradle/actions (gradle/actions)</summary>

### [`v6.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/releases/tag/v6.4.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/compare/v6.3.0...v6.4.0)

#### Highlights

##### Gradle version support status in the Job Summary

The actions now report the support status of every Gradle version used in a workflow, as job
annotations and in the Job Summary ([#​1057](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/issues/1057)). Thanks to [@​ov7a](https://redirect.github.com/ov7a) for the contribution.

| version kind                                                                            | job annotation | version table         | below the table                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **End-of-life** — two or more major versions behind the latest release                  | warning        | :warning:             | expandable section naming the affected release lines, pointing at the [Gradle Security Subscription](https://gradle.org/security-subscription/) |
| **Out of date** — one major behind, or more than two minors behind on the current major | notice         | :information\_source: | one-line legend pointing at the [Gradle release lifecycle](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/feature_lifecycle.html#eol_support) docs   |
| **Current**                                                                             | none           | —                     | —                                                                                                                                               |

Deliberately *not* reported: patch releases (being on `9.7.0` when `9.7.1` exists is not flagged) and
pre-releases (release candidates, milestones and snapshots never produce annotations). The latest
Gradle release is determined from the wrapper checksum data already bundled with the action, so no
network access is required.

Note that these annotations are emitted independently of the `add-job-summary` setting: setting
`add-job-summary: 'never'` suppresses the Job Summary itself, but the warning and notice annotations
remain.

##### Gradle itself is now reported in the dependency graph

The `dependency-submission` action now applies **v1.5.0** of the
[GitHub Dependency Graph Gradle Plugin](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/github-dependency-graph-gradle-plugin)
(up from v1.4.2) ([#​1069](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/issues/1069)).

The headline change is that the Gradle Build Tool running the build is now reported as an
`org.gradle:gradle-core` dependency, so that **GitHub can surface known vulnerabilities in the version
of Gradle used to run your build**. These are the coordinates that GitHub advisories for the Gradle
Build Tool are published against.

Details worth knowing:

- The entry is always reported as a **direct** dependency with **development** scope.
- It is **not** affected by the project, configuration or scope filters, so it appears even in graphs
  that filter aggressively.
- Expect dependency graphs to gain this one new entry the first time a build runs after upgrading.

##### A new Gradle signing key, if you use dependency verification

> \[!IMPORTANT]
> If your build has [dependency verification](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/dependency_verification.html#sec:signature-verification)
> enabled, you must add a **second** trusted key before upgrading, or Dependency Graph generation will
> fail signature verification.

`github-dependency-graph-gradle-plugin` `1.5.0` is signed with a new Gradle signing subkey, and the
key previously documented in our setup guide has been revoked upstream:

| Artifact                                                             | Signing key                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `org.gradle:github-dependency-graph-gradle-plugin` `1.5.0` and later | `E2879931BCA1A42E55F2D64DD9B2DFBD9F3298BA` (new)          |
| `org.gradle` plugin versions before the rotation                     | `7B79ADD11F8A779FE90FD3D0893A028475557671` (old, revoked) |
| `com.gradle` Develocity Gradle plugin, including `4.5.0`             | `7B79ADD11F8A779FE90FD3D0893A028475557671` (old, revoked) |

Because the Develocity Gradle plugin is still signed with the old key, you should trust **both** keys
rather than swapping one for the other — replacing the old key outright will break Develocity
injection. The documented snippet in
[docs/setup-gradle.md](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/blob/3f5f9adaf7d9fecd50b5935e54106014257a94e6/docs/setup-gradle.md#dependency-verification)
has been updated accordingly ([#​1071](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/issues/1071)):

```xml
<trusted-keys>
   <trusted-key id="7B79ADD11F8A779FE90FD3D0893A028475557671">
      <trusting group="com.gradle"/>
      <trusting group="org.gradle"/>
   </trusted-key>
   <trusted-key id="E2879931BCA1A42E55F2D64DD9B2DFBD9F3298BA">
      <trusting group="org.gradle"/>
   </trusted-key>
</trusted-keys>
```

##### `cache-provider: external` for externally managed Gradle User Home

Builds that save and restore Gradle User Home by some other mechanism (Develocity Artifact Cache, for
example) previously had to set `cache-disabled: true`, which was misleading: caching wasn't disabled,
it just wasn't managed by this action, and the Job Summary reported it as "Disabled".

`cache-provider: external` skips Gradle User Home restore/save exactly as `cache-disabled` does, but
reports a distinct **External** status in the Job Summary explaining that caching is handled by
another provider ([#​1059](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/issues/1059)).

```yaml
- uses: gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v6
  with:
    cache-provider: 'external'
```

##### Develocity access keys containing OIDC tokens now work

Short-lived-token handling validated the `server=key[;server=key]*` access key format with a regex
whose `key` portion was too strict, so an access key holding an OIDC token value was rejected
outright. Worse, had it passed the regex, parsing split each entry on `=` and kept only the second
field — silently **truncating** any key containing `=` (as JWT padding does) and sending the mangled
key to the server. Both problems are fixed ([#​1061](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/issues/1061)).

##### Job Summary attribution

Job summaries produced by `setup-gradle` and `dependency-submission` now carry a top-level heading
naming the action, so the block stays attributable when another action's summary content lands in the
same job ([#​1058](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/issues/1058)).

##### Updated defaults

- GitHub Dependency Graph Gradle Plugin: **1.4.2 → 1.5.0**
- 5 new known-good wrapper checksums for `wrapper-validation` (368 → 373 entries)

#### What's Changed

- Bump the github-actions group across 3 directories with 6 updates by [@​dependabot](https://redirect.github.com/dependabot)\[bot] in [#​1039](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1039)
- Bump the npm-dependencies group in /sources with 3 updates by [@​dependabot](https://redirect.github.com/dependabot)\[bot] in [#​1038](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1038)
- Add action heading to Gradle job summary by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1058](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1058)
- Add cache-provider: external to skip Gradle User Home caching by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1059](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1059)
- Relax Develocity access key format validation by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1061](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1061)
- Use the root-qualified `:wrapper` task by [@​cobexer](https://redirect.github.com/cobexer) in [#​1064](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1064)
- Report EOL and maintenance status for Gradle versions by [@​ov7a](https://redirect.github.com/ov7a) in [#​1057](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1057)
- Update dependencies by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1065](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1065)
- Update .tool-versions: node 24.18.0, gradle 9.7.1, java 17 by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1068](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1068)
- Combined automated updates: wrapper checksums, npm dependencies, setup-java by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1070](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1070)
- Bump dependency-graph-gradle-plugin to 1.5.0 by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1069](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1069)
- Document the new Gradle signing key for dependency verification by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1071](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1071)

### [`v6.3.0`](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/releases/tag/v6.3.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/compare/v6.2.0...v6.3.0)

#### Highlights

##### Enhanced Caching: Windows fixes and a cache-protocol bump

This release updates `gradle-actions-caching` to **v1.0.0** (up from v0.7.0), which fixes two significant caching defects, both most visible on Windows:

- **Cache entries failed to store at all on Windows.**. Every entry failed
  with `Path Validation Error: Path(s) specified in the action for caching do(es) not
    exist`, even though the Gradle User Home was fully intact. Nothing was stored, so
  every downstream job ran against an empty Gradle User Home. The cause was a nested,
  unpatched copy of `@actions/glob` combined with a silently swallowed `require()` in
  the bundle, which left Windows path separators unnormalized.
- **Cache cleanup deleted instrumented jars that were in use.** A bug in key
  hashing for paths shorter than 64 characters made cleanup judge freshly created
  `caches/jars-9` entries as unused and remove them, so the `instrumented-jars` entry
  was never saved and every job re-instrumented its classpaths.

  Also included: cache entry names are now consistent between the save and restore
  reports — restore previously fell back to showing the raw glob pattern (e.g.
  `/home/runner/.gradle/caches/modules-*/files-*/*/*/*/*/`) instead of `dependencies`.

> \[!IMPORTANT]
> **Existing cache entries are invalidated by this release.** The cache protocol
> version was bumped to `v2`, so the first run after upgrading will be a cache miss
> and will repopulate the cache. No configuration changes are required.

##### Basic caching warns instead of failing silently

The basic (open-source) caching provider now emits a warning and reports
`(Entry not saved: save failed)` in the Job Summary when a cache save fails, rather
than reporting success ([#​1028](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/issues/1028)).

##### Dependency submission works with Isolated Projects

`dependency-submission` now disables Isolated Projects via a promoted property, so
dependency graph generation works on builds that enable it ([#​1025](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/issues/1025)). Thanks to [@​reinsch82](https://redirect.github.com/reinsch82) for the contribution.

- Injected Develocity Gradle plugin: **4.4.2 → 4.5.0**

- Disable Isolated Projects via promoted property in dependency-submission by [@​reinsch82](https://redirect.github.com/reinsch82) in [#​1025](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1025)
- Add Windows coverage for caching via a new smoke-test suite by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1027](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1027)
- Fix basic caching smoke test on Windows, and warn on save failure by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1028](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1028)
- Move non-smoke restore-gradle-home tests back to the integ-test suite by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1032](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1032)
- Bump npm-dependencies group with TypeScript 6.0.3, [@​types/node](https://redirect.github.com/types/node) 24.x, and security fixes by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1033](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1033)
- Bump Gradle Wrapper to 9.6.1, wrapper checksums, and Develocity plugin to 4.5.0 by [@​bigdaz](https://redirect.github.com/bigdaz) in [#​1034](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/pull/1034)

### [`v6.2.0`](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/releases/tag/v6.2.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/compare/v6.1.1...v6.2.0)

#### Highlights

This release brings significant behaviour improvements to **Enhanced caching**, improvements to the generated Job Summary, and a number of correctness and security fixes.

1. **Improved cache-cleanup mechanism.** Cleanup of stale files from the Gradle User Home is now faster, and no longer depends on Gradle or a JVM. It works by inspecting the local file state directly, removing the Gradle invocation from the post-build step.
2. **More granular, more stable caching.** The local build cache is stored as a separate cache entry, so it can be restored and invalidated independently of the main Gradle User Home entry. Transient Gradle housekeeping files are excluded from the cache, reducing its size and improving stability.
3. **Hide obsolete Job summaries in PR commments**: When a new Job summary comment is added to a PR, previous outdated Job summaries are now hidden.
4. **Improved caching report in the job summary.** The cache report now uses a single, consistent layout across all cache states and providers. Provider information is integrated directly into the report, and per-entry details are available in an expandable section. ([#​985](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/issues/985))
5. **Correctness and security fixes.** A unique cache key is now used per run attempt, so re-runs no longer collide; the job summary shows the cache key string rather than an internal id; and bundled dependencies have been updated, including a ReDoS fix and a fast-xml CVE fix.

### [`v6.1.0`](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/releases/tag/v6.1.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/gradle/actions/compare/v6.0.1...v6.1.0)

#### New: Basic Cache Provider

A new MIT-licensed **Basic Caching** provider is now available as an alternative to the proprietary **Enhanced Caching** provided by `gradle-actions-caching`. Choose Basic Caching by setting `cache-provider: basic` on `setup-gradle` or `dependency-submission` actions.

- Built on `@actions/cache` -- fully open source
- Caches `~/.gradle/caches` and `~/.gradle/wrapper` directories
- Cache key derived from build files (`*.gradle*`, `gradle-wrapper.properties`, etc.)
- Clean cache on build file changes (no restore keys, preventing stale entry accumulation)

**Limitations vs Enhanced Caching:** No cache cleanup, no deduplication of cached content, cached content is fixed unless build files change.

#### Revamped Licensing & Distribution Documentation

title: Accept gossip subscription RPCs carrying up to 500 topics
body:
## PR Description

A peer announces every topic it is subscribed to in one RPC when a stream opens. `MaxCountTopicSubscriptionFilter` throws above `MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_MESSAGE = 200` and `AbstractRouter` then ignores the whole RPC, so Teku never learned a single subscription of that peer. A Lodestar supernode with `--subscribeAllSubnets` announces 205 topics (128 column + 64 attestation + 4 sync committee + core), which made it invisible to Teku's gossip.

### Changes

- Raise the inbound per-RPC subscription limit to 500 (`MAX_INBOUND_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_RPC`). Prysm accepts 500 and Lighthouse 424, and a node subscribed to all subnets announces two forks worth of topics (~432) around a fork, so 500 covers that too.
- Keep our own outbound batches at 200 (`MAX_OUTBOUND_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_RPC`), so a Teku supernode on this release still fits inside the filter of every earlier Teku release. jvm-libp2p splits the announcement into several RPCs.
- `GossipTopicsTest` now also asserts that two forks worth of Teku's own topics fit in one inbound RPC, so a fork that adds topics fails CI instead of reopening this.
- `GossipSubscriptionLimitTest` feeds subscription RPCs through the production router pipeline: 201 and 500 topics are accepted, 501 is dropped whole, `MAX_SUBSCRIBED_TOPICS` still caps a peer across RPCs, and irrelevant topics are still filtered. The 201 case fails on master.

### Verification

Kurtosis devnet, minimal preset, Fulu at genesis, 2x Lodestar v1.50.0 supernodes with `--subscribeAllSubnets` (205 topics each) and one Teku with `--p2p-subscribe-all-subnets-enabled=true`.

| | Teku master | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `No peers for message topics` warnings by slot 38 | 168 | 0 |
| Teku view of subscribed peers per subnet | none | 2 |
| Lodestar mesh peers per topic | - | 2 of 2 |

Thanks to @nflaig for the report and diagnosis.

## Fixed Issue(s)

fixes #11482

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes libp2p gossip subscription handling and peer visibility on the mesh; scope is limited to RPC size limits with new integration tests and backward-compatible outbound batching.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes peers being invisible on gossip when they announce more than 200 topic subscriptions in a single RPC (e.g. Lodestar supernodes with `--subscribeAllSubnets`). Teku previously dropped the **entire** announcement via `MaxCountTopicSubscriptionFilter`, so it never learned any of that peer’s subscriptions.
> 
> The inbound cap is raised to **500** (`MAX_INBOUND_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_RPC`) and wired into the production gossip router filter. Outbound announcement batching stays at **200** (`MAX_OUTBOUND_SUBSCRIPTIONS_PER_RPC`) so upgraded Teku nodes still interoperate with older Teku releases that only accept 200 per RPC.
> 
> `GossipTopicsTest` now checks that two forks’ worth of worst-case Teku topics fit in one inbound RPC. **`GossipSubscriptionLimitTest`** exercises the real router pipeline (accept up to 500, drop 501+, `MAX_SUBSCRIBED_TOPICS` cap, irrelevant-topic filtering).

title: Read SSZ byte lists in bulk instead of one element per tree walk
body:
## PR Description

Reading the content of an SSZ byte list (`SszByteList.getBytes()`) walked the backing merkle tree once per byte: the interface default looped over `getElement(i)`, and `SszByteListImpl` had an equivalent `IntStream` override. The SSZ encoding of a byte list is exactly its content, so `getBytes()` now delegates to `sszSerialize()`, which copies whole 32-byte leaf chunks.

For progressive lists (EIP-7916) `sszSerialize()` itself was not bulk either: the packed-primitive branch of `AbstractSszProgressiveListSchema.sszSerializeFixed` did a root-to-leaf `get()` per chunk. It now does a single in-order leaf traversal from the first to the last chunk, like the regular list fast path.

### Flows affected

**Historical backfill on Gloas (`HistoricalBatchFetcher.validateExecutionPayloadBlockHash`).** After checkpoint sync Teku backfills `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` worth of blocks and, on Gloas, their execution payload envelopes. Historical payloads are never sent to the EL, so the fetcher recomputes the EL block hash in Java for every envelope. That reads every transaction (`Transaction::getBytes`) and the whole block access list (`getBlockAccessList().getBytes()`). In a CPU profile of a freshly checkpoint-synced Sepolia node this chain was 17.5% of all samples, with 14% in SSZ tree navigation and under 2% in Keccak.

**Block import and head following (`engine_newPayload`), all forks since Bellatrix.** `ExecutionPayloadV1`..`V4.fromInternalExecutionPayload` read every transaction, the extra data and (Gloas) the block access list through `getBytes()` to build the Engine API request. This runs for every imported block on the import critical path. Not visible in the profile because it was taken with the EL stub, which skips payload serialization.

**Gloas SSZ serialization** of progressive primitive lists benefits from the second change wherever states, blocks or envelopes are encoded for storage, gossip or RPC: transactions and block access lists in payloads, and `previous_epoch_participation`, `current_epoch_participation` and `inactivity_scores` in the state.

Not affected: element access (`get(i)`), deserialization, hash tree roots, progressive bitlists (own serializer), progressive lists of containers, and lists already backed by a packed byte-lists node. Byte vectors are untouched since `SszByteVectorImpl` already returns cached bytes.

### Measurements

First call on a freshly deserialized instance, best of N, Apple M-series:

| Size | Regular `getBytes()` | Progressive `getBytes()` | Progressive `sszSerialize()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 KiB | 33 µs → 2.6 µs | 51 µs → 2.6 µs | 6.7 µs → 2.7 µs |
| 64 KiB | 563 µs → 35 µs | 876 µs → 35 µs | 149 µs → 35 µs |
| 1 MiB | 10.3 ms → 0.51 ms | 14.9 ms → 0.55 ms | 3.6 ms → 0.55 ms |

### Testing

New `SszByteListTest` (162 cases): regular and progressive schemas, `BYTE` and `UINT8` elements, 18 sizes crossing chunk and progressive level boundaries, random and all-zero content (zero chunks use shared zero leaf nodes), lists built from bytes and from elements. Full `infrastructure:ssz` suite and the spec tests for execution payloads, transactions, blobs and cells pass.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core SSZ serialization/read paths used for large byte lists (e.g. execution payloads); behavior is covered by new tests but incorrect bulk reads would corrupt consensus data.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`SszByteList.getBytes()`** no longer reads one byte at a time via `getElement()` (and the `SszByteListImpl` override is removed). It now returns **`sszSerialize()`**, since SSZ byte-list encoding is the raw bytes and serialization can copy whole merkle leaf chunks.
> 
> For **progressive lists** with packed primitives, fixed-size SSZ serialization replaces a per-chunk `dataNode.get(gIdx)` loop with a **single in-order leaf traversal** (`TreeUtil.iterateLeavesData` from the first to the last chunk), which also speeds other progressive primitive lists.
> 
> Adds **`SszByteListTest`** parameterized coverage across regular and progressive (EIP-7916) schemas, chunk/level boundary sizes, deserialize vs `createFromElements`, and all-zero shared leaf nodes.
>

title: Resend forkChoiceUpdated when a reused block production result failed
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

If the `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` call that prepares a payload for block production fails (EL error or timeout), block production can't recover for that slot.

`ValidatorApiHandler.createUnsignedBlock` clears its per-slot caches on failure, so a retried request calls `prepareForBlockProduction` again. That re-pins the same `ForkChoiceUpdateData`: its payload future has already failed, and its resend guard stops a new fcU going out. Every retry gets the original error, and even after the resend window the failed future is never replaced, so the proposal is missed.

**Fix:** in `ForkChoiceNotifierImpl.pinForkChoiceStateForBlockProduction`, the reused-result path already retried once when the reused fcU returned no payloadId. It now also retries once when the reused fcU failed. Both cases go through one handler, `retryPinnedBlockProductionIfPayloadIdIsUnavailable` (renamed from `retryPinnedBlockProductionIfPayloadIdIsMissing`), which uses `forResend()` (new future, resend guard cleared) to send a new fcU.
- This covers a failed fcU from an earlier block production attempt, from an ordinary fcU that sent the same attributes first, and from an ordinary fcU that was still in flight when block production pinned it (that request recovers by itself).
- A result with a payloadId is still reused as is.
- When the reused result is already known to be unusable, only the retry is sent. The reused data is not resent as well, because once the resend window has passed that would be a duplicate fcU with its result dropped. This also applied to the existing missing-payloadId retry.
- A reused result gets at most one retry: a single handler means a failed retry can't set off the missing-payloadId retry, or the other way round. If the retry fails too, that request fails, and the next block production request for the slot gets one more attempt. Nothing is scheduled, and the pin is still cleared when the head advances or the slot expires.

**Other clients:** Lighthouse, Prysm and Lodestar only cache payloadIds they actually received. On a cache miss during block production they send fcU with attributes again, so a failed fcU is retried on the next request. This brings Teku in line with them.

**Tests** (`ForkChoiceNotifierTest`), all failing on master:
- `getPayloadId_shouldResendForkChoiceUpdatedWhenBlockProductionIsRetriedAfterFailure`: the block production fcU fails, then a second request for the slot recovers.
- `getPayloadId_shouldResendForkChoiceUpdatedWhenReusedOrdinaryResultFailed`: an ordinary fcU with the same attributes failed before block production pinned it.
- `getPayloadId_shouldResendForkChoiceUpdatedWhenReusedInFlightResultFails`: an ordinary fcU fails after the pin, and the same `getPayloadId` recovers.
- `getPayloadId_shouldNotResendUnusableReusedResultAfterResendWindow` (failed and no-payloadId cases): after the resend window, exactly one retry fcU is sent.
- `getPayloadId_shouldResendForkChoiceUpdatedOnlyOnceWhenReusedResultFails`: the EL keeps failing, exactly two fcUs are sent and the EL error is returned.

title: Exclude pending dials from peer selection and reserve their slots
body:
Selection excluded connected peers but not peers with a dial in progress, so a candidate could be selected again while its dial was pending: the slot was spent, both callers received the result, and the attempt and failure counters counted one dial twice.

Expose the pending dials from PeerManager through the network, exclude them from both selection stages, and count each as a reserved slot in the total and random budgets until it completes or times out. Budgets derive from one connected-peer snapshot read after the pending dials, so a dial completing in between is counted once. Pending repair dials are not usable coverage, so the subnet deficit is still measured against connected peers; outstanding score-based dials cap each search's repair dials so overlapping searches do not accumulate them.

Fixes #11422

Alternative to #11488

A block production request that reuses a ForkChoiceUpdateData whose forkChoiceUpdated already failed (EL error or timeout) got the original failure back on every attempt: the resend guard suppressed a new fcU and the failed future was never replaced, so the proposal was missed.

title: Re-pin block production after a failed attempt for the same slot
body:
## PR Description

The early return added in `pinForkChoiceStateForBlockProduction` with the inclusion list payload attributes (#11211) kept any existing pin for the same parent and slot, on every post-merge milestone. If the first attempt failed (no payloadId even after the resend, or an EL error), the pin stayed. `ValidatorApiHandler.createUnsignedBlock` clears its per-slot caches on failure so the next request can retry, but that retry got the same failed result back and never sent a new forkChoiceUpdated, so the proposal was missed. Master always re-pinned here.

The early return also skipped the re-pin path where #11491 handles a failed forkChoiceUpdated, so `getPayloadId_shouldResendForkChoiceUpdatedWhenBlockProductionIsRetriedAfterFailure` currently fails on `heze-devnet-2`.

Changes:
- Keep an existing pin only while it is still being prepared or already has a payloadId (`canReusePinnedBlockProduction`). Otherwise fall through to the normal re-pin path, which resends the attributes, including inclusion list transactions.
- Only reuse a pin once Heze is active. Before Heze every repeated request re-pins, as on master, so pre-Heze behaviour is unchanged. That also keeps the Bellatrix validator guide's recommendation to call `prepare_execution_payload` again when its inputs (for example the safe block hash) change. Whether the reuse should also apply before Heze for robustness is tracked in #11493.

Tests:
- `ForkChoiceNotifierTest.getPayloadId_shouldRecoverWhenBlockProductionIsRequestedAgainAfterNoPayloadId` (Bellatrix): a retried request after no payloadId sends a new forkChoiceUpdated.
- New `ForkChoiceNotifierBlockProductionRepinTest` runs on Bellatrix and Heze and asserts each fork's behaviour: recovery after no payloadId, recovery that keeps the inclusion list attributes, reuse of a pin with a payloadId (Heze only), and keeping an in-flight inclusion list pin (Heze only; before Heze it is replaced as on master). The two inclusion list tests moved here from `ForkChoiceNotifierTest`.

I checked the tests against variants of the reuse check: without the Heze gate the Bellatrix cases fail; with the original early return the recovery tests (including #11491's) fail; with no reuse at all the Heze cases fail.

`:ethereum:statetransition:test` and `:beacon:validator:test` pass.

consensus-specs #4704 ("Remove support for old deposit mechanism in Fulu", in v1.7.0-beta.4) removed the Eth1 deposit bridge in Fulu. It also changed the reference genesis helper (`test/helpers/genesis.py`) to set `deposit_requests_start_index = eth1_data.deposit_count` for Fulu and later.

It also adds `GenesisGeneratorDepositRequestsStartIndexTest` (ELECTRA/FULU/GLOAS). Before the fix, the test fails for FULU and GLOAS (expected 16, got UNSET).

title: Stop fetching execution payload envelopes on every block import
body:
## PR Description

The focil devnet-0 changes (#11139) made `RecentExecutionPayloadsFetchService` a `ReceivedBlockEventsChannel` listener. As a result, every imported Gloas block queues an execution payload envelope fetch straight away, with exponential retry and no cap. Fetch tasks for empty or withheld payloads are never removed, so on Gloas networks these tasks leak and RPC traffic goes up. This applies before Heze is active, so it would change Gloas behaviour once `heze-devnet-2` merges to master.

Envelopes are already fetched on demand, as on master: when a block's parent payload is required (`blockManager.subscribeRequiredParentExecutionPayload`) and when an attestation needs the full payload (`pendingAttestationPool.subscribeRequiredFullPayload`). The spec has no requirement to fetch every envelope on import.

This change:
- restores `RecentExecutionPayloadsFetcher`, `RecentExecutionPayloadsFetchService` and `RecentExecutionPayloadsFetchServiceTest` to match master exactly
- removes only the `ReceivedBlockEventsChannel` subscription for the fetcher from `BeaconChainController`

Nothing else in the repo depended on fetches being triggered by block import.

cc @mehdi-aouadi: was this a devnet-0 workaround, e.g. for nodes missing envelopes? If devnet-2 still needs something like it, we can add a bounded version that only runs under Heze.

`:beacon:sync:test` and `:services:beaconchain:test` pass.

title: Set Gloas attestation index from fork choice payload status
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Gloas spec conformance fix for the attestation `data.index` payload signal.

The rule is in `specs/gloas/validator.md` › Attestation; it's unchanged in v1.7.0-beta.4 and beta.5:
- if `block.slot == data.slot`, set `data.index = 0`
- otherwise, set it from the attested block's payload status in the validator's fork choice: `0` if `EMPTY`, `1` if `FULL`

On master, `ForkChoiceUtilGloas.computeCommitteeIndexForAttestation` returned `isPayloadVerified(store, root) ? 1 : 0`, which means "the payload was received and verified locally", not "fork choice selected FULL". So we voted `1` when we had the payload but fork choice picked the EMPTY variant, for example because the PTC voted it not timely or not data-available.

Changes:
- `ValidatorApiHandler` takes the attestation head node, including its payload variant, from fork choice (`getAttestationHeadNode`). It loads that block and state, and passes the node to `computeCommitteeIndexForAttestation`. Pre-Gloas keeps the existing `getSignedBlockAndStateInEffectAtSlot` path unchanged.
- When attesting to a slot earlier than the head, the new `ReadOnlyForkChoiceStrategy.getAncestorNodeData` returns the ancestor variant chosen by the canonical descendant. `ForkChoiceStrategy` resolves it under one read lock.
- `ForkChoiceUtilGloas.computeCommitteeIndexForAttestation` maps FULL → 1 and EMPTY → 0. PENDING is accepted only for a pre-Gloas block at the fork boundary.

This is the attestation part of #11396 (thanks @mehdi-aouadi), ported from `heze-devnet-2`. That PR's inclusion-list part stays on `heze-devnet-2` because it is Heze-only. That covers the `satisfiesInclusionList` predicate in `ForkChoiceModelGloas`/`ForkChoiceModelFactory`, `onUnsatisfiedInclusionList` tracking in `ForkChoiceStrategy`, the related `Store` changes and the `ForkChoiceTest` IL cases. The ported code matches the current `heze-devnet-2` versions, so the next master → heze-devnet-2 sync should resolve by taking the branch side.

Tests:
- New `ValidatorApiHandlerTest$LocallyVerifiedPayloadAttestationDataTest` runs on FULU and GLOAS. The payload is verified locally and the fork choice head is EMPTY, so the expected index is 0. It fails on master with `expected: 0 but was: 1` for GLOAS. The FULU case asserts the attestation data is unchanged and that the fork choice head is never consulted.
- Ported from #11396: the `ValidatorApiHandlerTest` canonical-variant and pre-Gloas cases, `ForkChoiceUtilGloasTest` PENDING handling, `ForkChoiceStrategyTest` `getAncestorNodeData`, and the `ValidatorApiHandlerIntegrationTest` Gloas index assertion.

cc @mehdi-aouadi

title: Bound memory held by gossip blocks waiting for validation
body:
## PR Description

Gossip messages wait for validation in the shared P2P async runner queue, which is only bounded by its number of tasks. Each queued message kept its uncompressed payload, cached when gossipsub computed the message id, so a burst of large blocks that compress well could fill the heap while waiting. Every block was then hashed inside the synchronized equivocation check before the future-slot check, so blocks that were about to be dropped were hashed one at a time.

Changes:
- **Queued messages keep only the compressed payload.** `SnappyPreparedGossipMessage` uncompresses once to compute the message id and a `DecodedMessagePrefix` (decoded size and first 128 bytes), then drops the payload. The worker uncompresses it again to decode it, as Prysm does. This reverses the payload reuse added in #11447.
- **Byte-weighted in-flight limit per topic.** `Eth2TopicHandler` takes a `GossipInFlightLimiter` (unlimited by default), which limits the total uncompressed size of the topic's messages that are queued or being validated. A message over the limit is ignored before it is queued. `beacon_block` uses 4 × `MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE` (40 MiB). Discards are logged at most once every 12 seconds per topic, with the number discarded since the last warning.
- **Far-future blocks are ignored before decoding.** `Eth2TopicHandler` takes a `DecodedPrefixFilter`, which runs on the gossipsub thread against the kept prefix. For `beacon_block`, `FarFutureBlockFilter` reads the slot from its fixed position in the SSZ bytes, as Lodestar does. Malformed messages are left to the decoder, which rejects them.
- **`BlockGossipValidator`** ignores far-future blocks before the equivocation check, and computes the block root before taking the lock so blocks are hashed in parallel.
- The pool, the validator and the filter share one far-future rule, `FutureBlockPool.isBeyondFutureSlotTolerance`, applied to `GossipValidationHelper.getMaxCurrentSlot()` (the current slot with the gossip clock disparity allowance).
- New metrics: `network_gossip_messages_in_flight_limit_discarded_total{topic}` (same name as in #11359) and `network_gossip_far_future_blocks_ignored_total`.

Notes:
- There is no in-flight gauge. Every fork's gossip managers are created at startup, and Besu replaces a supplied gauge's collector when it is registered again, so only the last fork's gauge would survive. Counters are cached by name, so they're safe.
- #11359 also changes `SnappyPreparedGossipMessage` to reuse the cached payload; that hunk should be dropped when it is rebased. Its count limit and timeout could be added to `GossipInFlightLimiter` later.
- Current-slot junk blocks can still use up the `beacon_block` budget, so an honest block arriving then is ignored and fetched by RPC instead. The admitted junk blocks fail validation, which penalises the sending peers.

### Testing
- Unit tests for each change: `DecodedMessagePrefix`, `SnappyPreparedGossipMessage`, `GossipInFlightLimiter`, `FarFutureBlockFilter` (slot offset across all milestones), `Eth2TopicHandler`, `BlockTopicHandler`, `BlockGossipValidator` (root not computed for far-future blocks, computed outside the lock), `GossipValidationHelper` and `FutureBlockPool`.
- Heap held per queued message, using a Fulu block with 1,048,576 empty transactions (4.2 MB SSZ, 207 KB snappy): 6.20 MiB on master, 0.20 MiB with this change. Of 2,000 copies sent to the `beacon_block` handler at the current slot, 9 were queued; at a far-future slot, none.
- Reporter's Kurtosis PoC (minimal preset, Fulu from genesis, target and control Teku nodes with `-Xmx4g`, 12 libp2p peers × 150 of those blocks with a zero signature):

  | Build | Block slot | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | master | far future | target killed by `OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`; control stayed up |
  | this PR | far future | target stayed up; all 1,800 ignored before decoding; heap back to baseline after GC |
  | this PR | current | target stayed up and kept pace with the control's head; 1,234 of 1,800 discarded by the in-flight limit |
  | this PR | current, 3 more bursts | old gen settled at 479, 474 and 486 MB (control ~60 MB), no growth between bursts; head kept pace |

## Fixed Issue(s)
- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku-internal/issues/357

## Documentation

- [ ] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes hot-path gossip and block validation behavior (early ignores, in-flight drops, re-uncompress on decode); mis-tuned limits could drop honest blocks under load, but scope is defensive memory/DoS mitigation on P2P.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Bounds memory and CPU spent on gossip beacon blocks** before and during validation, addressing heap exhaustion from bursts of large compressed blocks.
> 
> Queued snappy gossip messages now keep only the compressed payload: message id and a small `DecodedMessagePrefix` (size + first 128 bytes) are computed once, then the uncompressed bytes are dropped and re-uncompressed when the worker decodes. For `beacon_block`, a byte-weighted `GossipInFlightLimiter` (4× max gossip payload) drops messages that would exceed the in-flight budget before they are queued, and `FarFutureBlockFilter` reads the slot from fixed SSZ offsets to ignore blocks beyond `FutureBlockPool`’s future-slot tolerance without full decode.
> 
> `BlockGossipValidator` applies the same far-future rule before the equivocation check (avoiding expensive `getRoot()` on junk) and computes the block root outside the equivocation lock so hashing can run in parallel. `GossipValidationHelper.getMaxCurrentSlot()` centralizes clock-disparity handling for these checks. New counters track in-flight discards and pre-decode far-future ignores.
>

title: Faster gossip signature verification: batch gathering and same-message grouping
body:
### Problem

On a mainnet node subscribed to all subnets, BLS verification of gossip signatures was two thirds of total CPU. Two causes:

1. Verification batches were mostly size one. Eight workers raced on the same queue and each took whatever was there, so nothing was ever batched.
2. Every signature paid its own hash-to-curve and pairing, even though nearly all attestations in a slot sign the same message.

### What changes

- **Batches now form.** One worker gathers at a time, waiting up to 10 ms (or 64 tasks) after the first task arrives.
- **Same-message signatures are verified together.** Signatures over one message are scaled by independent random multipliers, summed, and paired once.
- **Distinct-message signatures are verified in chunks.** Signatures that share their message with nothing else in the batch (aggregate-and-proof wrappers, selection proofs, sync contributions, backfill) are prepared 8 at a time in one blst pairing context, so one multi-pair Miller loop replaces 8 separate ones. Chunks run in parallel; each signature keeps its own random multiplier and subgroup check. This saves 13–28 % CPU per distinct-message signature and supersedes the old `doublePairing` path in the new mode.
- **Single-key aggregation is skipped.** Almost every gossip signature (unaggregated attestations, sync committee messages, selection proofs) comes with one public key, and aggregating a one-element list used to cost a point addition plus an affine conversion. `BlstPublicKey.aggregate` now returns the key itself after the usual validity check. This benefits every batch path, legacy included.
- **Failed batches are handled in one place.** Small failed batches and the exception fallback share one loop that isolates a throwing task and respects `--Xp2p-batch-verify-signatures-strict-thread-limit-enabled`.

### The BLS optimisation, for non-cryptographers

Verifying one BLS signature means checking an equation with two "pairings", a pairing being an expensive
function of two curve points. For a signature `S` from public key `P` over message `m`:

```
e(P, H(m)) == e(G, S)
```

`H(m)` is the message hashed onto the curve (expensive on its own), and `G` is a fixed generator. Before
this PR, every signature paid its own `H(m)` and its own two pairings, no matter how many signatures the
batch held or how many of them were over the same message.

Two properties of pairings let us do better:

1. **Pairings are bilinear**: `e(A, X) · e(B, X) = e(A + B, X)`. Several signatures over the *same*
   message, with keys `P1 … Pn`, can be checked with one hash and one pairing on the key side:
   `e(P1 + … + Pn, H(m))`, with the signatures summed on the other side. This is the same algebra that
   makes BLS aggregation possible.
2. **A batch of checks can be folded into one** by multiplying each check by an independent random
   number before summing. Without the random numbers an attacker could craft two invalid signatures whose
   errors cancel in the sum; with them, such a pair passes only with probability about 2^-64. This is
   the standard randomised batch verification technique and the code already used it; this PR keeps it
   intact and tests the cancelling-pair attack explicitly.

So for a batch, the verifier now:

- groups signatures by message; each group is hashed and paired **once**, with every signature scaled by
  its own fresh random number and its own subgroup check (a cheap sanity check that the point is a
  legitimate signature, which stops a class of malformed-input attacks);
- prepares the remaining signatures, those whose message nobody else in the batch shares, in **chunks**
  (see below);
- runs one final exponentiation for the whole batch, as before.

**Chunking, for the signatures grouping cannot help.** Aggregate-and-proof wrappers, selection proofs,
sync contributions and backfill tasks each sign a message of their own, so there is nothing to group them
with. A pairing's dominant cost is the Miller loop, a fixed sequence of ~64 steps; each step has a part
that depends on the pair being checked and a part that is the same no matter how many pairs are in flight.
blst can run up to 8 pairs through a single loop, paying the shared part once. Before this PR each of these
signatures got its own loop. Now `SameMessageBatchVerifier` cuts them into chunks of 8, prepares each chunk
sequentially inside one blst context (`BLS12381.prepareBatchVerifyChunk`), and runs the chunks in parallel.
Every signature in a chunk still gets its own random number and subgroup check, and one bad member fails
the whole chunk, which the normal split-and-retry then isolates. Measured gain: 13–28 % less CPU per
distinct-message signature. The trade-off is that a chunk is one sequential job, so a very small batch of
distinct messages takes slightly longer in wall-clock than when each signature ran on its own thread; at
the service level that difference disappeared into the gather window (valid p99 within ±10 %). This
replaces the previous `doublePairing` code path in the new mode, which prepared two signatures in two
separate contexts and merged the results, so it never shared any Miller-loop work despite its name.

Why it pays off on gossip: nearly every attestation in a slot votes for the same head and target, so its
signing message is identical. A batch of 64 gossip attestations used to cost 64 hashes and 128 Miller
loops; it now costs about one hash, a handful of Miller loops, and 64 cheap scalar multiplications.
Measured on this machine, a same-message signature went from ~330 µs to ~95 µs of CPU, and a
distinct-message one dropped a further 13–28 % through chunking.

One small change does reach the legacy path too: `BlstPublicKey.aggregate` on a one-element list now
returns that key instead of adding it to zero and converting back to affine coordinates, which on the
profiled node was about 2 % of total CPU for no cryptographic effect. The validity check (infinity,
subgroup) runs exactly as before.

What did **not** change: `BLS.java` itself, the single-signature path used for blocks, and the
randomisation and subgroup checks that make batch verification safe. The new logic lives in
`SameMessageBatchVerifier` and two additive blst preparation methods, and only the gossip verification
service calls it.

### Effect

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| CPU, all-subnets mainnet node | ~3.6 cores | ~1.7 cores |
| BLS share of node CPU | ~67 % | ~25 % |
| Gossip validation latency, p99 | ~3 ms | ~15 ms |

Block import, block gossip validation and block production are unaffected: they never use this service.

### Operator controls

- `--Xp2p-batch-verify-signatures-mode`: `GATHER_AND_GROUP` (default) or `LEGACY`, which restores the previous behaviour exactly.
- `--Xp2p-batch-verify-signatures-gather-timeout-ms`: the wait window, default 10 (new mode only).
- New metrics: `signature_verifications_batch_gather_time_micros`, plus the existing batch-size histogram.

### Safety

- Random multipliers, per-signature subgroup checks and infinity-key rejection are retained; a crafted pair of signatures that only verify in aggregate is rejected (tested).
- `BLS.java` is unchanged; the grouped path lives in a new `SameMessageBatchVerifier` used only by the gossip verification service.
- Under 10 % invalid gossip traffic, CPU is on par with master (bigger batches fail more often and are re-verified), and gossip p99 rises to ~50 ms in bursts. Peer scoring already penalises senders of invalid messages.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes gossip-only BLS batching and cryptography prep paths; correctness relies on existing randomised batch checks and extensive tests, but default behaviour and latency trade-offs affect all P2P gossip validation.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Gossip BLS verification** is reworked to cut CPU by forming larger batches and verifying signatures that share a message together, at the cost of up to ~10 ms extra validation latency (default).
> 
> `AggregatingSignatureVerificationService` gains **`GATHER_AND_GROUP`** (new default) vs **`LEGACY`**: one worker holds a gather lock, waits up to the configured timeout (default 10 ms) or until ~64 tasks, then verifies via **`SameMessageBatchVerifier`** instead of plain `BLS.batchVerify`. Failed or throwing batches now re-verify per task through a shared path that respects **`--Xp2p-batch-verify-signatures-strict-thread-limit-enabled`** without failing unrelated tasks in the batch.
> 
> The BLS layer adds **`SameMessageBatchVerifier`** plus blst **`prepareBatchVerifySameMessage`** and **`prepareBatchVerifyChunk`** (8 distinct-message signatures per pairing context). **`BlstPublicKey.aggregate`** skips work for a single-key list (helps legacy mode too).
> 
> Operators can tune behavior with hidden flags **`--Xp2p-batch-verify-signatures-mode`** and **`--Xp2p-batch-verify-signatures-gather-timeout-ms`** (max 100), wired through **`P2PConfig`** into the beacon chain signature service. New metric: **`signature_verifications_batch_gather_time_micros`**.

title: Verify validator deposit signatures lazily at Gloas builder onboarding
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

At the Gloas fork, `GloasStateUpgrade.onboardBuildersFromPendingDeposits` needs to know, for each builder (`0xB0`) deposit, whether its pubkey is already a pending validator, i.e. an earlier queued deposit without builder credentials has a valid signature. Master answers that by verifying the signature of **every** such deposit as it is queued, even though most pubkeys never get asked about. With a large pending queue that verification dominates the upgrade.

This change keeps the loop as it is and only swaps the eager `Set<BLSPublicKey>` for a small `PendingValidatorTracker`:

- validator deposits are recorded per pubkey, unverified
- `isPendingValidator(pubkey)` verifies that pubkey's recorded deposits only when a builder deposit asks, each deposit at most once, and caches a positive answer

No behaviour change: the answer still considers only deposits queued ahead of the builder deposit, and the output queue order still comes solely from the `pendingDeposits` list.

### Performance

New JMH benchmark `GloasBuilderOnboardingBenchmark` (Fulu→Gloas upgrade, N signed new-validator deposits + 100 signed builder deposits for new keys):

| Validator deposits | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 748 ms | 73 ms |
| 10,000 | 6,812 ms | 81 ms |

```
./gradlew :eth-benchmark-tests:jmh --args="GloasBuilderOnboardingBenchmark"
```

### Testing

- New `GloasStateUpgradeTest` cases pin the number of signature checks (validator deposits for keys with no builder deposit are never verified; each deposit verified at most once; builder deposits for a pending-validator pubkey stay queued).
- All 72 Gloas `fork/fork` reference tests (v1.7.0-beta.4, minimal and mainnet) pass, including the builder-onboarding cases.

title: Reject Heze slot duration changes until EIP-8198 is supported
body:
## PR Description

ethereum/consensus-specs#5718 (and ethereum/consensus-specs#5743, which carries it with review fixes) folds EIP-8198 (quick slots) into Heze. It adds two config values, `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE` and `MIN_BLOB_DATA_RETENTION_MS`. Teku doesn't implement variable slot timing yet. The default config loader only warns on unknown keys, so a network that shortened the Heze slot would start Teku on the old timing and fork off.

This PR adds a guard and nothing else:

- Both values are parsed as **optional** Heze config. When absent they default to the current timing:
  - `SLOT_DURATION_MS`
  - `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH * SLOT_DURATION_MS`
- When Heze is **scheduled**:
  - Startup fails if `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE != SLOT_DURATION_MS`, with the message "changing the slot duration at the Heze fork (EIP-8198) is not supported yet".
  - A warning is logged if `MIN_BLOB_DATA_RETENTION_MS` differs from the epoch-based window. Serving and pruning still use the epoch window. That's a p2p difference only, not consensus, so it doesn't stop startup.
- When Heze is **not scheduled**, the values are stored and ignored, matching the spec.

While the guard passes (Heze slot duration equal to `SLOT_DURATION_MS`), every EIP-8198 change in both spec PRs reduces to current behaviour: piecewise clock, reward and churn scaling, deadlines. So current Teku stays spec-correct for those configs.

Not changed:
- The bundled network yamls. Upstream's minimal value (5000) or #5718's mainnet value (10000) would trip the guard in `TestSpecFactory` Heze specs, which schedule Heze at genesis.
- `/eth/v1/config/spec` output for existing networks.
- Any pre-Heze path.
- specrefs. The pinned beta.4 spec doesn't define these keys; the entries come with the ref-test bump.

The full EIP-8198 implementation will land separately once the spec PR merges and test vectors exist. That work removes the equality check and keeps the parsing.

Testing: new `SpecConfigHezeTest` cases cover defaults (mainnet, minimal, gnosis), accepted matching values, a rejected slot-duration change, the change being ignored when Heze is unscheduled, and a different retention value. They go through `SpecConfigLoader` with the yaml key names. `:ethereum:spec:test` and `spotlessCheck` pass.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes Heze network startup validation for fork scheduling; misconfiguration now fails fast instead of risking consensus divergence, but runtime timing and blob retention behavior are unchanged.

> **Overview**
> Adds **optional Heze spec config** for upcoming EIP-8198: `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE` and `MIN_BLOB_DATA_RETENTION_MS`, exposed on `SpecConfigHeze` / `NetworkingSpecConfigHeze` and built via `HezeBuilder`. When keys are omitted, they default to the current `SLOT_DURATION_MS` and the retention implied by `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS`.

title: Reject slot duration changes in SLOT_DURATION_SCHEDULE
body:
## PR Description

Follow-up to #11512.

Heze devnet configs generated from the earlier form of EIP-8198 (ethereum/consensus-specs#5592) carry a `SLOT_DURATION_SCHEDULE` list rather than `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE`. For example, `ethpandaops/heze-devnets` devnet-1 has:

```yaml
SLOT_DURATION_SCHEDULE:
  - EPOCH: 0
    SLOT_DURATION_MS: 12000
```

Teku only warned about the unknown key. A schedule that shortened slots would therefore bypass the guard from #11512, and Teku would keep running on the old timing.

This PR:
- Parses `SLOT_DURATION_SCHEDULE` (`EPOCH` / `SLOT_DURATION_MS` entries), following the existing `BLOB_SCHEDULE` / `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE` parsers.
- Fails at startup if any scheduled entry differs from `SLOT_DURATION_MS`, with the message "changing the slot duration (EIP-8198) is not supported yet".
- Ignores entries at `FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH`.
- Rejects malformed entries.
- Applies whether or not Heze is scheduled, because in the old format the schedule isn't tied to a fork.

A schedule that keeps the current duration loads as before, which covers devnet-1's single 12000 ms entry. Nothing else reads the schedule, and no bundled config changes.

Testing: new `SpecConfigLoaderTest` cases load yaml files with strict loading:
- devnet-1's shape (Heze at epoch 5, a single 12000 entry) is accepted.
- A 10000 ms entry at epoch 5 is rejected.
- A far-future entry is ignored.
- A malformed entry is rejected.

`:ethereum:spec:test` and `spotlessCheck` pass.
