title: Implement EIP-8198 quick slots in Heze
body:
## PR Description

**Draft, CI only.** Don't merge until the spec PR lands and a release with test vectors is available.

This implements EIP-8198 (quick slots) in Heze, following ethereum/consensus-specs#5743, which carries #5718 with its review fixes. Nothing changes unless a network sets the new config values: they default to today's timing, and with Heze unscheduled or the same slot duration every computation reduces to the current one.

### Changes
- **Config**
  - `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE` is on the base config. It defaults to `SLOT_DURATION_MS` and must be a positive multiple of 1000 when Heze is scheduled.
  - `MIN_BLOB_DATA_RETENTION_MS` is on the Heze config. It defaults to the `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS` window.
  - The guard from #11512 that rejected a different Heze slot duration is removed.
- **Clock**
  - `MiscHelpers` slot/time conversions are piecewise across the Heze fork. They keep the linear path when the duration doesn't change.
  - This fixes `ForkSchedule`, `Spec.getCurrentSlot` and the time conversions in the other spec versions.
  - Slot-length consumers updated: `Spec.getSlotDurationMillis(slot)`, `AttestationUtilPhase0` time checks, inclusion list timeliness (time since slot start instead of `mod slotDuration`), the validator timing adapter period, and the gossip `seenTTL`, which uses the longer duration.
- **Deadlines:** Heze slot component deadlines use `get_slot_duration_ms(HEZE_FORK_EPOCH)`.
- **Rewards and churn**
  - Scaled by `get_slot_duration_ms(epoch) / SLOT_DURATION_MS`, so Heze at genesis is still scaled.
  - Flag deltas use the previous epoch. The inactivity penalty scales by the square of the ratio.
  - The attestation proposer reward uses the target epoch, and sync aggregate rewards use the current epoch.
  - Activation, exit and consolidation churn are scaled before rounding.
  - The REST ideal attestation rewards and the attestation sorter's base reward cache follow the same epochs.
- **Retention:** the Heze data column sidecar retention window is wall-clock (`compute_blob_data_retention_start_epoch`). It's used for availability checks, the minimum custody slot (Status `earliest_available_slot`) and pruning.
- **Reference tests:** `TransitionTestExecutor` applies a test's `config.yaml`, and the `fork_choice/slot_duration` test type is registered.
- **Not changed:** gossip scoring parameters keep the genesis slot duration, because they are fixed when the router starts.

### Validation
- Full beta.4 `referenceTest` passes (76,098 tests), and `ethspecify check` passes.
- Unit tests cover the piecewise clock, the fork boundary, deadlines, Heze at genesis, rewards, churn, the inactivity penalty, retention, inclusion list timeliness, attestation time checks, the proposer reward target epoch, the validator timing adapter, `seenTTL` and the minimum custody slot.
- Heze minimal vectors generated locally from #5743 pass, except:
  - 45 `gossip_inclusion_list` / `gossip_proposer_preferences` cases, which also fail on plain `heze-devnet-2` (spec changes since beta.4);
  - 31 `transition/core` cases, which need `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE: 5000` in Teku's bundled minimal config (to do with the spec bump);
  - `fork_choice/slot_duration`, which disagrees on the head after a mid-chain anchor (still being investigated).
- Kurtosis on ethrex `heze-devnet-2` with 3 Teku nodes each: no missed slots and finality across the change for 12 s -> 10 s (mainnet preset) and 6 s -> 4 s (minimal preset).
- The SlotProcessor double node-slot increment in Heze, which these runs found, was fixed separately in #11515.

### To do before merge
- Rebase on the merged spec PR and update to its final form.
- Specrefs for the new and changed `#heze` entries, with the spec version bump.
- Bundled minimal config `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE: 5000`, with the ref-test harness defaulting it to `SLOT_DURATION_MS` for vectors that don't schedule Heze.
- Resolve the `fork_choice/slot_duration` anchor difference.

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Touches consensus-critical timing, reward/churn math, fork choice, and blob retention; incorrect scaling or clock math would cause network splits or wrong validator economics.
> 
> **Overview**
> Implements **EIP-8198 (quick slots)** for the Heze fork so networks can change slot duration at Heze without changing behavior when `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE` matches the legacy duration or Heze is unscheduled.
> 
> **Config:** `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE` moves to base spec config (defaults to `SLOT_DURATION_MS`, validated as whole seconds when Heze is scheduled). The prior rejection of a different Heze slot duration is removed. `HezeBuilder` no longer owns that field.
>

title: Fix Heze slot processor advancing the node slot twice per slot
body:
## PR Description

From Gloas, `SlotProcessor` increments `nodeSlot` at the payload attestation (PTC) deadline. The Heze inclusion list deadline handling (#11177) also called `nodeSlot.inc()` unconditionally, without an `isProcessingDueForSlot` guard, measuring from the node slot start. This advanced the node slot twice per Heze slot:

- `INCLUSION_LIST_DUE_BPS` 6667 (IL before PTC): after the IL increment the PTC check measures from the next slot, so payload attestation processing (`onPayloadAttestationsDue`, "PTC Event") never ran.
- 7500 (equal, as in consensus-specs #5718 and current master configs): both fire on the same tick, the node slot runs a slot ahead and every other slot's slot start / attestation-due / IL / PTC processing is skipped.
- IL after PTC: the IL refresh never ran.

Fix:
- Track the IL deadline with its own processed-slot field (`onTickSlotInclusionList`), like the attestation and PTC deadlines.
- Stop incrementing `nodeSlot` there; the Gloas+ PTC increment already does it.
- Measure the IL due time from the start of the calculated (wall-clock) slot, matching the spec's `get_time_into_slot_ms`, so it fires once per slot regardless of its order relative to the PTC deadline.

Pre-Heze behaviour is unchanged (the Heze gate still returns false). Validator duties were unaffected, as they are timed by the VC.

Tests: `SlotProcessorTest` ticks a Heze minimal spec every 100 ms through three slots and asserts slot start, attestation-due, IL-due and PTC-due each run exactly once per slot at the right offset, with IL due at 6667, 7500 and 8500 bps; plus a Gloas case asserting the IL path never runs. All three Heze cases fail on the current branch.

## Fixed Issue(s)

> **Overview**
> Fixes **Heze** `SlotProcessor` advancing **`nodeSlot` twice per slot** because the inclusion-list path both incremented the node slot and used node-slot-relative timing without a once-per-slot guard.
> 
> The inclusion-list deadline now tracks **`onTickSlotInclusionList`** (same pattern as attestation and payload attestation), **no longer calls `nodeSlot.inc()`** there (Gloas+ still advances at the payload attestation deadline), and computes due time from the **wall-clock slot start** via `genesisTimeMillis` so inclusion-list refresh runs **once per slot** whether it falls before, at, or after the PTC deadline.

body:
## PR Description

We used to scan our Docker images with Trivy every night in a CircleCI `dockerScan` job (#4267). When CI moved to GitHub Actions only (#10266), that job wasn't ported, so the images haven't been scanned since January.

This restores it as a GHA workflow.

- Add `docker-scan.yml`, which runs nightly at the same time as the old job (`0 19 * * *`) and on `workflow_dispatch`, and scans `consensys/teku:develop-jdk25` and `develop-jdk26` for HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerabilities.

title: Record fcU inclusion list satisfaction on the fork choice thread
body:
## PR Description

In `ForkChoice.onForkChoiceUpdatedPayloadResult`, `recordPayloadInclusionListSatisfaction(node, ...)` ran a store transaction inside `thenCompose` on whichever thread completed the EL response, before `finishAsync(..., forkChoiceExecutor)`. A failure there also stopped the forkchoiceUpdated result from being applied.

- The satisfaction write now runs via `forkChoiceExecutor.executeFuture(...)`, with `checkOnEventThread()` before `startStoreTransaction`.
- Its failure is logged separately (`handleException`), so the forkchoiceUpdated result is still applied.
- Ordering is unchanged: the write commits before the node is marked VALID, which matters because it's only recorded while the payload node is still optimistic.

Pre-Heze behaviour is unchanged: nothing is written unless the EL reports `inclusionListSatisfied: false`.

Tests: two `ForkChoiceTest` cases, one completing the EL response off the fork choice thread and asserting the write happens on it, and one with a failing commit asserting the payload result is still applied. Both fail without the fix.

title: Add end-to-end test for inclusion lists by indices RPC
body:
## PR Description

#11520 registered `InclusionListsByIndices` (`/eth2/beacon_chain/req/inclusion_lists_by_indices/1/`), but its unit test only checks that the method is registered. Teku never sends this request, and no other client does either (Lodestar, Prysm, Lighthouse and Nimbus only serve it), so serving it had no end-to-end coverage on devnets.

This adds `InclusionListsByCommitteeIndicesIntegrationTest`. Two connected peers make the request over libp2p, and the responder serves it from a real `InclusionListManager` on a chain that forks from Gloas to Heze. It covers:

- lists returned in committee-bit order, not insertion order; a list for a different dependent root is not returned
- missing indices left out of the response
- empty request → empty response
- pre-Heze slot → `3: ResourceUnavailable`, and the peer stays connected
- more than `MAX_REQUEST_INCLUSION_LIST` indices → `1: InvalidRequest`, and the peer stays connected. The test lowers the limit to 4, because with the default presets a 16-bit committee bitvector can't exceed 16.
- Heze not scheduled locally: the request fails locally and is never sent
- Heze not scheduled remotely: protocol negotiation fails (`NoSuchRemoteProtocolException`), and the peer stays connected

The test builds both peers itself instead of using `AbstractRpcMethodIntegrationTest`. That base class always creates the local node with 8 validators at slot 0, so a remote that is already in the Heze epoch is rejected as `IRRELEVANT_NETWORK`.

To check the test catches the #11520 bug, I removed the method from `BeaconChainMethods.allMethods`; 6 of the 7 tests then fail.

Test only; no production code changes.

## Fixed Issue(s)

title: Keep inclusion list gossip across Heze BPO forks and reject pre-Heze ILs
body:
## PR Description

Fixes two Heze (FOCIL) bugs that the Heze test-coverage work turned up.

**1. A BPO fork during Heze dropped the inclusion_list topic.**
- `Eth2P2PNetworkBuilder.createBpoSubscriptions` mapped `case GLOAS, HEZE` to `GossipForkSubscriptionsGloasBpo`, which has no `InclusionListGossipManager`.
- Once a BPO epoch activated during Heze, the node stopped subscribing to `inclusion_list` and `publishSignedInclusionList` silently did nothing.
- Fix: add `GossipForkSubscriptionsHezeBpo`, which extends `GossipForkSubscriptionsHeze` and overrides `getActivationEpoch`, and use it for Heze BPO entries.

**2. A pre-Heze inclusion list made the validator API return 500.**
- `SignedInclusionListValidator` called `toVersionHeze().orElseThrow()` without a fork check.
- A current-slot pre-Heze inclusion list submitted via the validator API (`ValidatorApiHandler` → `SignedInclusionListPublisher` → `InclusionListManager`) threw `NoSuchElementException`, and the REST call returned 500.
- Gossip is not affected, because the topic is fork-checked.
- Fix: reject before the config lookup.

### Tests
- `GossipForkSubscriptionsHezeBpoTest`: the subscription activates at the BPO epoch, adds the IL gossip manager, and publishes on the BPO-digest `inclusion_list` topic.
- `Eth2P2PNetworkBuilderTest`: with Heze at epoch 1 and a BPO entry at epoch 2, the built `GossipForkManager` subscribes to and publishes on `inclusion_list` after the BPO epoch. It fails with the old mapping.
- `SignedInclusionListValidatorTest.shouldRejectInclusionListForCurrentPreHezeSlot`: fails with `NoSuchElementException` without the fix.

## Fixed Issue(s)

> **Overview**
> Fixes two Heze inclusion-list gaps: **BPO gossip** stopped subscribing to `inclusion_list` when a blob-parameter-only fork activated during Heze, and the **validator API** could 500 on pre-Heze slots.
>

It now uses new **`GossipForkSubscriptionsHezeBpo`**, which extends the Heze subscriptions (including `InclusionListGossipManager`) and activates at the BPO epoch.

body:
## PR Description

`ForkChoiceNotifierTest` only runs on Bellatrix. This PR adds `ForkChoiceNotifierGloasHezeTest`, which uses `@TestSpecContext(milestone = {GLOAS, HEZE})` (12 tests, 24 runs). This PR only adds tests.

The setup uses a real in-memory chain with a FULL head node, a spied real `ProposersDataManager`, and a real `InclusionListStore`. The store holds overlapping lists plus decoys for another dependent root and another slot.

- **Inclusion lists reach forkChoiceUpdated.** On Heze, the deduplicated inclusion-list transactions are in the payload attributes for a prepared proposer, for `preparePayloadAttributes`, and for a pinned block production refreshed after pinning. On Gloas there are none.
- **`onPayloadAttestationsDue`.** It keeps the inclusion-list attributes stable on Heze and recalculates on Gloas.
- **Error path, `completePendingPayloadAttributesPreparationExceptionally`.**
  - A failed calculation fails both the pending preparation and the pinned `getPayloadId`.
  - A later prepare, and a retried block production, still succeed.
  - A preparation replaced by a newer preparation, or by pinned production for another slot, fails with the matching message.
  - A stale calculation that completes late is ignored.
  - Two prepares for the same parent and slot share one calculation.
- **Expiry, `clearPinnedBlockProductionIfExpired`.**
  - The pin is not cleared at the pinned slot, and not by `onAttestationsDue` at the next slot.
  - It is cleared by `onPayloadAttestationsDue` at the next slot, and by `preparePayloadAttributes` for slot+1.
  - A prepare for the same slot refreshes the pin.

title: Only pay Gloas fee recipients that came from signed proposer preferences
body:
## PR Description

`sendSignedProposerPreferences` validated every submitted entry and then cached
the whole list, failures included. The response reported the failure while the
rejected fee recipient was already cached, and the next payload the node built
paid it.

A Gloas fee recipient now only comes from a signed preference that passed
validation.

- Cache an entry only when it is identical, by hash tree root, to one in the
  accepted preferences pool.
- Resolve it at payload build time from the accepted preferences for the
  proposal slot and dependent root, the way `getTargetGasLimit` already does.
- Ignore `prepare_beacon_proposer` from Gloas onwards. beacon-APIs deprecates it
  there and makes beacon node support optional, and our validator client already
  stops sending it.
- Refuse a cached fee recipient that did not come from signed preferences for a
  Gloas proposal, since entries written in the last pre-fork epoch live for three
  epochs.

Honest submissions still land when they are accepted on a retry, when a gossip
copy beat them to validation, and when an identical gossip copy wins validation
while ours is queued.

Known gap: payload attributes are not recomputed when preferences are accepted
after the last head update before a proposal. With
`forkChoiceUpdatedAlwaysSendPayloadAttributes` enabled, pinned block production
can reuse attributes built with the default address. That flag is off by default.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Fixes #11518

## Testing

New tests in `ProposersDataManagerGloasTest`, `ProposerDataManagerTest`,
`ProposersDataManagerTest` and `DefaultProposerPreferencesManagerTest`. Each one
was run with the logic under test disabled and fails there.

## Documentation

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes where Gloas blocks send execution-layer fees and when payload attributes are built; mistakes could misroute validator rewards or delay block production.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes incorrect Gloas execution payload fee recipients when invalid or unsigned proposer data was cached.
> 
> **Gloas fee recipients** now come only from **accepted** signed proposer preferences for the proposal slot and shuffling dependent root. Rejected submissions are no longer cached, `prepare_beacon_proposer` is ignored once Gloas is active, and validator-index caches are not used as a fallback for Gloas blocks. Payload preparation for local proposers waits until matching preferences are accepted (including after retry or when an identical gossip copy validates first).
> 
> **`DefaultProposerPreferencesManager`** tracks pending local submissions so acceptance notifications stay **local** when gossip validates the same preferences first, with slot-based cleanup and refined `REJECT` / `IGNORE` handling.
> 
> **Wiring:** locally accepted preferences update the prepared-proposer cache via `LocalOperationAcceptedFilter` in `BeaconChainController`.

title: Keep imported slashing protection from being overwritten by cache
body:
## PR Description

A keymanager import (`POST /eth/v1/keystores` with `slashing_protection`)
wrote the merged EIP-3076 history to the key's record file, but the
slashing protector kept using the record it had cached for that key and
wrote values derived from it back over the file on the next signature.

- **Delete, then re-import:** `SlashingProtectedSigner.delete()` now
  evicts the key's cached record via a new
  `SlashingProtector.evictSigningRecord`. `DeletableSigner` calls it
  with in-flight signing drained and further signing blocked, so the
  eviction needs no extra locking. A key that is deleted, run on
  another client and imported back with that history now reloads the
  imported record.
- **Re-import of a loaded key:** `ValidatorLoader` checks for a
  duplicate before applying imported slashing protection. History sent
  with a keystore that is already loaded is no longer applied, so the
  `duplicate` response means nothing changed. To raise a running key's
  protection, delete and re-import it.

Tests cover eviction for both local protectors, the delete hook, the
duplicate check for both import modes, and an end-to-end keymanager
delete and re-import against real record files.

Alternative to #11436, which keeps applying history to loaded keys by
routing the import through the protector under its locks.

## Fixed Issue(s)

fixes #11388

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

## Changelog

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes slashing-protection caching and keymanager import semantics; incorrect behavior could affect whether slashable signatures are blocked, though the change aligns enforcement with on-disk imported history.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes keymanager slashing-protection imports being **ignored on disk** because the in-memory `SlashingProtector` cache still held an older record and wrote it back on the next signature.
> 
> **Delete → re-import:** `SlashingProtectedSigner.delete()` now calls new `SlashingProtector.evictSigningRecord()` so a removed key’s cache entry cannot survive deletion. `LocalSlashingProtector` also stops caching records loaded via `getSigningRecord()` (only signing paths populate the cache), which avoids stale entries when protection summaries read records before delete/re-import.
> 
> **Duplicate import:** `ValidatorLoader` returns `duplicate` and **skips** applying bundled EIP-3076 history when the pubkey is already loaded, since the running protector owns that record.
> 
> Tests cover both protector implementations, delete/eviction ordering, loader duplicate behavior, and end-to-end keymanager delete/re-import flows.
>

title: Add CombinedChainDataClient.getForkChoiceNodeInEffectAtSlot
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Follow-up to #11498, addressing tbenr's non-blocking design comment (https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/pull/11498#discussion_r4319206227): resolving the canonical fork choice node at a slot is moved out of `ValidatorApiHandler`.

- New `RecentChainData.getForkChoiceNodeInEffectBySlot(slot)`, next to `getBlockRootInEffectBySlot`, with `CombinedChainDataClient.getForkChoiceNodeInEffectAtSlot(slot)` delegating to it. Both return `Optional<ProtoNodeData>`: the head node if the head is at or before `slot`, otherwise the head chain's ancestor at that slot. One `ForkChoiceStrategy.getAncestorNodeData` call covers both cases, so root, payload variant and optimistic status come from a single locked snapshot.
- **Fork choice only, unlike its siblings.** `getSignedBlockAndStateInEffectAtSlot` and the other "in effect at slot" client methods fall back to finalized storage. This one doesn't, because only fork choice knows a block's payload variant. The javadoc says so explicitly. It returns empty when there is no chain head, when the slot is before the fork choice anchor, or when the head node is no longer tracked: an INVALID payload result drops the node until the head is re-selected.
- **`ValidatorApiHandler`:** a single fork check picks the pipeline.
  - Pre-Gloas is unchanged: `getSignedBlockAndStateInEffectAtSlot`, then `isOptimisticBlock`.
  - Gloas uses the new method, rejects an optimistic node, then loads block and state for the node's root and computes the index.
  - When the Gloas node is missing while the chain head is optimistic (e.g. a just-invalidated head), it fails with `NodeSyncingException` (503) instead of returning empty (404). That keeps the old head-path behaviour, so validator clients can fail over.
- Added `ProtoNodeData.getForkChoiceNode()`.

One small Gloas difference: when the head is at or before the slot, the optimistic flag used to come from the cached `ChainHead`. It now comes from the current fork choice node data, the same source the ancestor case already used.

### Tests
- `CombinedChainDataClientForkChoiceNodeTest` (`@TestSpecContext` FULU/GLOAS/HEZE, real in-memory storage):
  - no chain head
  - pre-Gloas base node
  - head at the slot, and head before the slot
  - FULL ancestor (including a skipped slot)
  - EMPTY ancestor even though the payload was imported
  - slot before the fork choice anchor (initialised from a non-genesis anchor)
  - head node invalidated before the head is re-selected
  - ancestor and head with different optimistic status
- `ValidatorApiHandlerTest`:
  - attestation tests stub `getForkChoiceNodeInEffectAtSlot`
  - new: Gloas missing node with an optimistic head → `NodeSyncingException`
  - new: pre-Gloas optimistic block in effect → `NodeSyncingException`

### Other callers that might need the canonical payload variant at a slot (not migrated)
None of these was a trivial migration, so they are listed here and left alone. The REST slot selectors in particular **cannot** switch to this method by analogy with `getSignedBlockAndStateInEffectAtSlot`: it has no finalized-storage fallback, so historical slot queries would break.
- `ExecutionPayloadSelectorFactory.headSelector` / `slotSelector` (`/eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelope/{head|slot}`): these return the envelope for the block at the head or slot even when the canonical chain builds on its EMPTY variant. Changing that is an API decision.
- `StateSelectorFactory.headSelector` / `slotSelector`: these return the block post-state. Choosing the FULL or EMPTY state is also an API decision.
- Sync committee message production (`SyncCommitteeStateUtils`, the VC head block root): signs a block root only, so the variant doesn't matter.
- Block production parent selection (`BlockProductionContext`): uses the proposer head (`getProposerHead`), which is a different question.
- `ValidatorApiHandler.createUnsignedExecutionPayload`: matches the exact block root at the slot, so the variant doesn't matter.

> **Medium Risk**

title: Seed the Gloas genesis execution payload only for a genesis anchor committing to it
body:
## PR Description

`ForkChoice.applyGenesisExecutionPayloadForGloas` seeds a synthetic execution payload envelope so that a Teku-generated Gloas genesis, whose bid commits to the EL genesis block, has a FULL fork-choice node for the slot-1 block to build on. It ran on every startup, keyed the envelope by the best block root and used a zero parent hash. That caused three problems:

- After a restart the head is already selected when it runs, so the envelope was written for the head root and persisted over the head's real blinded envelope.
- A checkpoint-state start marked the anchor FULL with the parent's block hash.
- The persisted blinded envelope is validated against the block bid on every store rebuild (`StoredBlockMetadata.getValidatedPayloadHeader`: parent hash, block hash, gas limit). With `parent_hash = 0` that check failed, so a Gloas-genesis node restarting while the genesis block was still hot could not start.

The seeding now runs only while the finalized anchor is the genesis block and no payload is cached for it, keys the envelope by the anchor root, and mirrors the genesis bid's `parent_block_hash` and `gas_limit` so the persisted envelope validates on rebuild. It is skipped entirely when the genesis bid does not commit to the EL genesis block (`latest_block_hash != latest_execution_payload_bid.block_hash`), which is what the pyspec genesis helper and ethpandaops/eth-beacon-genesis (Kurtosis) produce: there the genesis block is EMPTY per the spec, the slot-1 block builds on EMPTY(genesis) and no genesis payload is required. Teku's own `GenesisGenerator` convention, where the bid block hash is the EL hash, keeps the FULL seeding, so interop and acceptance-test genesis behave as before.

Independent of #11450, which relies on the seeding happening before any block import for the Teku convention; that still holds.

## Fixed Issue(s)

fixes #11555

## Testing

- New `ForkChoiceTest` cases: seeding mirrors the genesis bid and survives a restart; no seeding for a genesis whose bid commits to no block, with a slot-1 block imported on EMPTY(genesis) and a restart; re-seeding only the genesis payload on a restart before finalization; no-op on a restart after finalization; a checkpoint-state anchor is not marked FULL.
- `ethereum:statetransition` tests green on master ddd05510d1, spotless clean.

## Documentation

## Changelog

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes Gloas fork-choice startup and genesis payload persistence; mistakes could break restarts, checkpoint sync, or interop with non-Teku genesis, but behavior is heavily regression-tested.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Tightens Gloas genesis execution-payload seeding** so it no longer runs on every startup or overwrites real envelopes.
> 
> `ForkChoice.applyGenesisExecutionPayloadForGloas` now seeds a synthetic payload **only** when the finalized anchor is still genesis, no payload is cached for that root, and the genesis bid commits to the EL genesis block (`latest_block_hash == bid.block_hash`). It skips **EMPTY** genesis layouts (pyspec / eth-beacon-genesis) where slot 1 builds on EMPTY(genesis). The synthetic envelope is keyed by the **genesis anchor root** (not chain head) and copies **`parent_block_hash`** and **`gas_limit`** from the genesis bid so persisted blinded envelopes pass validation on store rebuild.
>

title: Key the gossip seen cache by a cheap SHA-256 fast id
body:
## PR Description

The gossip seen cache (`FastIdSeenCache` in jvm-libp2p) is keyed by a "fast id" computed from every inbound copy of every subscribed message, duplicates included, on the single `GossipRouter-event-thread`. It holds every message seen within the seen TTL (1115 heartbeats, about 13 minutes), so millions of entries on a well connected node.

The fast id was `Bytes.wrap(msg.messageSha256())`. Tuweni's `AbstractBytes.hashCode` and `equals` walk the 32 digest bytes one virtual `get(i)` call at a time, and in a JFR of the event thread at ~340 peers those frames (`AbstractBytes.equals`, `ArrayWrappingBytes.get`, `AbstractBytes.computeHashcode`) were about 16% of the thread's samples.

This PR adds `FastMessageId`, a small key holding the digest:
- `hashCode()` is the big-endian int of the first four digest bytes, computed once in the constructor (a SHA-256 needs no extra mixing);
- `equals()` is a class check plus `Arrays.equals` (intrinsified);
- it is `Comparable` (unsigned lexicographic `Arrays.compareUnsigned`) so a `HashMap` bin that treeifies under 32-bit hash collisions stays logarithmic.

The digest and the seen-cache semantics are unchanged; collision resistance still comes from the full SHA-256. A JMH benchmark (`SeenCacheKeyBenchmark`) runs the real `FastIdSeenCache` with both keys:

| path | entries | tuweni `Bytes` | `FastMessageId` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| duplicate (hit) | 100k | 64.6 ns | 16.0 ns |
| duplicate (hit) | 2M | 132.1 ns | 44.7 ns |
| first delivery (miss) | 2M | 73.0 ns | 40.2 ns |

**Measured on a mainnet node** (AWS m6a.2xlarge, all subnets, full custody), together with the matching jvm-libp2p seen-cache restructuring in libp2p/jvm-libp2p#545 (both on top of jvm-libp2p #542, #543, #544). CPU of `GossipRouter-event-thread` per peer-count bin:

| peers | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| 250-299 | 25.0 % | 18.8 % |
| 350-399 | 27.7 % | 22.9 % |
| 450-499 | 30.9 % | 24.2 % |
| 550-599 | 30.4 % | 26.0 % |

title: Envelopes by range follow ups
body:
## PR Description
Follow-ups agreed in the review of #11477, for the two findings both sides marked as follow-ups rather than blockers.

**Orphaned envelope deletion is atomic with the finalized block write** (review thread 6).
The finalization storage update used to write the finalized blocks in batched `FinalizedUpdater` transactions and only then delete the blinded envelopes of orphaned payloads in a separate transaction. A failure between the two left those envelopes in the finalized database for good, where the finalized-range handler would serve them. The orphaned roots are now resolved before `updateFinalizedData` runs and each one is deleted inside the same updater batch that writes its block, in both prune and archive mode. Two edges are kept correct: an orphaned root the update does not write as a finalized block (the parent of the oldest pair, finalized earlier) is still deleted in the trailing envelope transaction, and an envelope that arrives in the same update as the finalization of its orphaned block is filtered out of the additions so it cannot be resurrected.

**The payload-status-aware ancestor walk runs under a single protoarray lock** (review thread 8).
`ForkChoiceUtil.getAncestorNodes` took and released the protoarray read lock twice per step, so a prune running concurrently could truncate the walk and push the remaining slots onto the database path. The walk is now `ReadOnlyForkChoiceStrategy.getAncestorNodes`, an interface default holding the generic implementation so test fixtures are untouched, with `ForkChoiceStrategy` overriding it to walk the protoarray under one read lock. `ForkChoiceUtil` delegates to the strategy. No behaviour change for callers.

Not included, as discussed in the same review: the anchor FULL variant for checkpoint-sync anchors needs the payload's execution block number, which neither the bid nor the anchor state carries, and raw-SSZ extraction of the bid hashes is an optimisation to revisit if the finalization scan shows up in a profile.

**Tests**
- `KvStoreDatabaseTest`: drives `update()` with mocked updaters and verifies that the finalized block write, the envelope deletion and the commit happen on the same updater, with a single finalized commit.
- `DatabaseTest`: an envelope arriving with the finalization of its orphaned block is not retained, across all storage contexts.
- `ForkChoiceStrategyTest`: payload statuses along a chain whose child built on EMPTY, the FULL branch, and the empty-result cases of the single-lock walk.

## Fixed Issue(s)
Follow-up to #11477 (fixes #11246). No new issue.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches finalized DB write ordering for Gloas blinded envelopes and fork-choice locking during ancestor walks; behavior is tightened rather than broadened, with focused tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Follow-ups to Gloas finalized-range envelope handling and fork-choice ancestor walks.
> 
> **Finalized storage:** Orphaned blinded execution payload envelopes are now resolved before finalized data is written, and each finalized block’s envelope is added or deleted in the **same** `FinalizedUpdater` transaction as that block (prune and archive). Envelopes that arrive in the same update as finalization of an orphaned block are filtered out so they are never stored. A separate envelope-only transaction still handles pruned non-canonical roots and orphaned roots that are not rewritten as finalized blocks.
> 
> **Fork choice:** Payload-status-aware `getAncestorNodes` moves to `ReadOnlyForkChoiceStrategy` (default walk); `ForkChoiceUtil` delegates to the strategy. `ForkChoiceStrategy` overrides it to skip down to the requested slot without holding the lock, then walks the bounded range under one protoarray read lock so concurrent prunes cannot truncate the walk mid-range.
> 
> Tests cover same-transaction envelope updates, orphaned envelopes at finalization, and Gloas EMPTY/FULL ancestor maps.
>

title: Keep the finalized anchor DAS tracker alive while its payload is recovered
body:
## PR Description

Follow-up to #11450. Starting from a state-only Gloas checkpoint, ForkChoice recovers the anchor's `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` and runs its data availability check at the anchor block slot. That slot is always at or below the finalized epoch start, so `DasSamplerBasicImpl.onSlot` pruned the sampling tracker on the next slot tick and completed it exceptionally with "DAS sampling expired while slot finalized".

The failure is not a `TimeoutException`, so the out-of-window rescue in `DataColumnSidecarAvailabilityChecker` does not apply. The envelope import fails with `NOT_AVAILABLE`, `BatchImporter` reports `DATA_NOT_AVAILABLE`, and each retry creates a fresh tracker that the next tick prunes the same way. A node checkpoint-synced onto a Gloas network with blobs in the anchor block could never import its first child block.

`onSlot` now exempts exactly one tracker from the finalized-range pruning: the one whose root is the store's latest finalized anchor, on a fork where DA is deferred to the execution payload envelope, while the store has no execution payload for that root. Everything else is pruned as before. The tracker is removed by `onExecutionPayloadImported` once the payload lands, or by the normal rule once finalization advances past the anchor.

Tests in `DasSamplerBasicTest`:
- the anchor tracker survives `onSlot` while the payload is missing, a sibling tracker at the same slot is still pruned, and the anchor tracker is pruned once the store has the payload
- on Fulu the anchor tracker is pruned as before
- a `checkDataAvailability` call at the anchor slot survives a slot tick mid-fetch and completes once the columns arrive

The first and third tests fail without the fix.

## Fixed Issue(s)

Follow-up to #11450.

title: Fix restart of a Gloas-at-genesis node before finalization
body:
## PR Description

With Gloas active at genesis, the genesis execution payload envelope is synthesized locally (`ForkChoice.applyGenesisExecutionPayloadForGloas`) from the genesis EL block hash instead of being committed to by the genesis bid, so its payload header (zero parent hash, genesis block hash) never matches the genesis block's bid. On restart before finalization moves past genesis, rebuilding fork choice from the hot DB validated that envelope against the bid and the node failed to start. For the slot 0 block this now only checks the envelope's block root and rebuilds the FULL node from the envelope's payload (genesis block hash, number, gas limit) with the bid's parent block hash, matching what the live path imported. Verified with kurtosis (Gloas at genesis, teku + lighthouse on ethrex): a teku restart at slot 5 with finalized epoch 0 now starts, follows the same head as lighthouse and proposes blocks again, where master crash-loops.

title: Make the Gloas genesis block EMPTY and drop the synthetic genesis payload
body:
Teku's GenesisGenerator set the genesis execution payload bid's block_hash to the EL genesis hash, which made the genesis block FULL: the slot-1 block built on FULL(genesis) and could only be imported once a payload for genesis was known, so ForkChoice seeded a synthetic genesis envelope at every startup. The consensus-specs genesis helper and eth-beacon-genesis (Kurtosis) leave that block_hash zero: the genesis block is EMPTY, the slot-1 block builds on EMPTY(genesis) whose execution hash is the EL genesis hash, and no genesis payload is ever needed.

Follow that layout. The genesis bid now commits to no payload, and applyGenesisExecutionPayloadForGloas and its callers are removed. One of those callers was GenesisHandler, the deposit-log genesis path that has had no production caller since the deposit log fetching was removed (#10937); it is deleted together with its test and the ethereum:pow:api dependency only it used in the module. Teku-generated Gloas genesis states are now interchangeable with those produced for Kurtosis. Genesis states and databases written by earlier Teku versions use the old layout and must be regenerated: a node started on one is refused at startup with a message saying so, instead of never importing the slot-1 block. BuilderBidValidator no longer treats a zero parent bid block hash as a payload a bid can extend. The state-side test behind both checks is the spec's is_parent_block_full, added to MiscHelpersGloas and used by the withdrawals processing as well.

Test fixtures build on the EMPTY variant when the parent bid commits to no payload. New tests cover a slot-1 import on a fresh Gloas genesis without any genesis payload, a restart while the genesis block is still hot, the zero attestation payload index for genesis targets, the startup check and the bid validator guard.

Fixes #11545

title: Verify attestation signatures before saving them for future processing
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
  Attestations saved for future processing got a penalty-free Ignore at gossip and were then BLS verified in fork choice, so any peer could load the shared signature verifier with bogus signatures for free. They are now verified at gossip, so invalid ones are rejected, and valid signatures are cached so fork choice doesn't verify them again. Attestations dropped because the verification queue is full are also no longer logged as errors.

  - Aggregates from a future slot
  - Gloas full payload votes waiting for their payload
  - Attestations for a block that hasn't been seen yet, if the target block is known
## Fixed Issue(s)
https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku-internal/issues/375

## Documentation

- [x] I thought about documentation and added the `doc-change-required` label to this PR if updates are required.

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core gossip validation and aggregate batching for attestations (signature timing, deferral, and peer scoring), which affects network-facing behavior under load and Gloas payload rules.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Deferred attestations are now BLS-checked at gossip** instead of being saved with a penalty-free outcome and verified later in fork choice. That closes an abuse path where peers could flood the signature verifier with invalid signatures for free.
> 
> Gossip validation now runs signature verification (and caches valid results) before `SAVE_FOR_FUTURE` for **future-slot** attestations, **votes for blocks not yet in the store** (using an already-available target checkpoint state when the voted block is unknown), and **Gloas full-payload votes** waiting on execution payload. Provably bad messages are **rejected** early (wrong subnet, out-of-range committee index, invalid target timing, bad signature); when no state is available, deferral is unchanged and fork choice still verifies later.
> 
> The aggregate path is updated so deferred attestations can carry a short-lived **state** for aggregate checks, batch flush happens before deferring when signatures were queued, and **SAVE_FOR_FUTURE** aggregates are not marked seen. **`GossipValidationHelper.getCheckpointStateIfAvailable`** avoids regenerating checkpoint state from attacker-chosen targets.
> 
> **`AttestationManager`** downgrades log noise when processing fails due to a full executor or signature queue (`RejectedExecutionException` / `ServiceCapacityExceededException`) from error to trace.
>

title: Move payload bodies request to a separate EL request queue
body:
## PR Description

Moves `engine_getPayloadBodiesByHash` onto its own Engine API queue and makes serving `ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesByRange` and `ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesByRoot` requests cheaper and more bounded.

Envelopes that are no longer in memory are stored blinded, so serving them needs an `engine_getPayloadBodiesByHash` call. Until now those calls shared a queue with `engine_newPayload` and `engine_forkchoiceUpdated`, were made one envelope at a time, and were not limited by how many requests were being served.

### Changes

**Separate Engine API queue**
- `ThrottlingExecutionEngineClient` serves `engine_getPayloadBodiesByHash` from its own queue: 2 concurrent calls, 128 queued, then rejected.
- New metrics: `beacon_ee_payload_bodies_request_queue_size` and `beacon_ee_payload_bodies_request_queue_rejected`.

**Batched lookups**
- New `CombinedChainDataClient.getExecutionPayloadsByBlockRoots`: serves what is in the hot store and resolves the rest with one provider call.
- Both handlers load envelopes in batches of up to 32, so each batch costs at most one EL call. By-range resolves head-chain roots from fork choice and finalized roots from the database. Responses keep slot order (by-range) or request order (by-root).

**Request handling**
- New `ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesRequestLimiter`, shared by both handlers: at most 16 requests served at once, 2 per peer. Excess requests get `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`.
- The envelope rate limiter is charged for every slot or root looked up, not only for envelopes returned.
- `ResponseCallback.isClosed()` lets handlers stop serving once the peer closes the stream. It is checked before each batch.

**Refactor**
- Shared logic is in `AbstractExecutionPayloadEnvelopesMessageHandler` and `ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesRequestState`: rate limiting, the concurrency limit, charging, completion, and the batched load.

### Testing
- Unit tests for the new queue, limiter, request state, batched client lookup, stream-close plumbing, and both handlers. These cover batching and ordering, charging, stopping on close, and the total and per-peer limits.
- `./gradlew :networking:eth2:test :ethereum:executionclient:test :storage:test`, the envelope RPC integration tests, and `spotlessCheck` pass.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes peer-driven Engine API and Gloas req/resp serving under load; mis-tuning could affect sync peers or delay critical EL calls if queues were wrong (mitigated by separate queues and limits).
> 
> **Overview**
> Peer-driven **`engine_getPayloadBodiesByHash`** traffic no longer shares the main Engine API throttle with **`newPayload`** / **`forkchoiceUpdated`**. **`ThrottlingExecutionEngineClient`** routes payload-body calls through a dedicated queue (2 concurrent, 128 queued) with new **`ee_payload_bodies_request_*`** metrics.
> 
> **`ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesByRange`** and **`ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesByRoot`** are reworked around shared **`AbstractExecutionPayloadEnvelopesMessageHandler`** logic: envelopes are **unblinded in batches** (up to 32) via **`CombinedChainDataClient.getExecutionPayloadsByBlockRoots`**, and concurrent serving is capped by **`ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesRequestLimiter`** (16 global, 2 per peer, bounded wait queue). Peers are charged for slots/roots **looked up**, not only envelopes returned; handlers **stop when the RPC stream closes** using new **`ResponseCallback.isClosed()`** / **`getStreamClosedFuture()`** plumbing.

title: Close inbound RPC streams whose response cannot be written
body:
## PR Description

Close an inbound RPC stream when its response cannot be written, instead of leaving it half-closed or open.

### Why

A Hoodi supernode on master served **zero inbound RPC** (status, ping, metadata, by-range, everything) for ~40 minutes, three times in one day. Peers that got no answer dropped it one by one (Nimbus first), its own dials never stuck, and each episode ended the instant one specific Prysm-over-QUIC peer disconnected.

The DEBUG log showed every inbound stream being refused with `Rejecting inbound RPC stream ... because the global active stream limit of 128 has been reached`. The limit itself is fine; the problem is that one peer could hold all 128 permits with streams that never ended:

1. A QUIC requester that gives up on a request closes it with FIN **and** `STOP_SENDING` (that is what go-libp2p's `Close()` does, so Prysm on a cancelled request).
2. Once `STOP_SENDING` has been received, quiche refuses every further write on that stream. If our reply has not gone out yet, the reply write itself fails (or, when quiche has already collected the stream, hangs until the 10 s write timeout). Netty does not close the channel on that failure, and it closes a QUIC stream channel on its own only once both FINs are exchanged, so from then on only an explicit `close()` ends it.
3. Teku's `RpcResponseCallback` never fully closed a stream after a failed write. The single-response path (status, ping, metadata, goodbye, light client) logged the failure and did nothing else; the error-response path (every error reply, including rate-limited by-range) logged and then half-closed, which cannot complete either since our FIN is refused as well. By then the request had been decoded, so the 10 s receive timeout was already disarmed.

Result: the stream stayed open until the peer disconnected, holding one permit each. A peer with a laggy path (its requests arrived late, so it cancelled before our reply) leaked 128 permits in about two minutes. Reproduced deterministically against this exact build with a small QUIC client that sends `STOP_SENDING` before the reply: 130 abandoned ping streams and the node rejects everyone's streams until that client disconnects.

The by-range success path was already safe because its write failures reach `completeWithUnexpectedError`, which closes abruptly. Yamux is not affected by this particular path: a local half-close completes the stream once the remote side is closed.

### What changes

- `respondAndCompleteSuccessfully`: a failed write now closes the stream abruptly.
- `completeWithErrorResponse`: half-closes only after the error reply was actually written; a failed write closes the stream abruptly.
- `completeSuccessfully`: a failed half-close closes the stream abruptly.
- The existing benign-failure log levels are unchanged (`STOP_SENDING`, closed channel, closed stream stay at TRACE).

Nine new unit tests cover the failing and succeeding paths.

### What this does not fix: a peer that never sends its FIN

This PR closes the hole that was hit in production, not every way to hold a permit. A peer that sends a complete request and then simply never closes its write side gets its reply, we half-close, and the stream then waits for a remote FIN that never comes. That holds the permit until the peer disconnects, on QUIC and on yamux alike, with no timeout left to catch it: the receive timeout is disarmed once the request is decoded, and nothing bounds the lifetime of an accepted stream. 130 such requests give the same outcome as the incident, against a merged version of this PR.

Closing that needs the inbound stream limiter to stop trusting peers: a per-peer cap well below the global 128, a lifetime deadline on accepted inbound streams, and metrics for active and rejected streams (the rejection path has none today). That is a separate PR, and it should land soon after this one rather than be treated as nice-to-have.

## Fixed Issue(s)

## Documentation

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core inbound eth2 RPC stream lifecycle on QUIC; behaviour change is narrowly scoped to error paths but affects peer connectivity under load or cancelled requests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a **QUIC req/resp leak** where inbound RPC streams stayed open (and held one of the **128 global permits**) after a peer cancelled with `STOP_SENDING`, because half-closing could not complete and failed writes did not fully close the stream.
> 
> **`RpcResponseCallback`** now routes successful completions through `closeWriteStream()` and, on any failed response or error-reply write—or a failed half-close—calls **`closeStreamAbruptly()`** so permits are released instead of waiting for the peer to disconnect. Write-failure logging is consolidated in `logWriteFailure` without changing TRACE vs ERROR behaviour for benign churn.
>

## PR Description

This PR stores light client bootstraps in the database and fixes a few cases where a checkpoint synced node could not serve light client data. The PR:

- builds the bootstrap for each new finalized checkpoint and keeps it in two new database columns, so `LightClientBootstrap` and the `bootstrap` endpoint are served from storage instead of rebuilt from a state each time
- returns the anchor state for a state-only finalized anchor when the state is the block's post-state, so the bootstrap at the checkpoint sync anchor can be built
- retries an update whose finalized block was not yet in the database on the next finalized checkpoint, so the update gets its finality branch once the block is backfilled
- runs the finalized checkpoint and head through the light client server on startup

title: Reject RPC data column sidecars whose fork digest doesn't match their slot fork
body:
The response decoder picked the SSZ schema from the peer's fork digest alone, so a peer could label a Gloas-slot sidecar with the Fulu digest and have it decoded as a Fulu sidecar. Validation then dispatched by slot, where the Gloas rules skip the inclusion proof, and the commitments provider trusted the commitments embedded in the sidecar, so sender-chosen cells verified against sender-chosen commitments and the column was accepted into custody and the sampling tracker.

- RpcContextCodec gains verifyPayloadMatchesContext, called by RpcResponseDecoder after each decoded payload. The fork-digest codec rejects a chunk whose digest names a fork other than the one active at the payload's slot with the new, penalised ContextPayloadMismatchException. ForkDigestPayloadContext.rejectsContextSlotMismatch enables the check per payload type; only data column sidecars enable it, so blocks, blob sidecars and envelopes keep their behaviour at fork boundaries.
- MiscHelpersGloas.verifyDataColumnSidecar rejects sidecars that are not Gloas sidecars.
- BlobKzgCommitmentsProvider ignores commitments carried by a sidecar at a Gloas or later slot and resolves them by block root instead.

title: Remove the compromised eMudhra roots from the Docker images
body:
## PR Description

The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs were found to be recoverable in October 2026 ([OpenJDK guidance](https://openjdk.org/emudhra)). Java does not check revocation by default, and the `eclipse-temurin:25` and `:26` base images (last rebuilt 2026-10-17) still trust the root they chain to. So our Docker images accept certificates signed with the compromised keys on any outbound HTTPS connection, such as an external signer, remote beacon node, builder or checkpoint sync.

This removes the four roots that OpenJDK removed in its fix ([openjdk/jdk@8e492bf50b](https://github.com/openjdk/jdk/commit/8e492bf50b)) from the jlinked runtime's `cacerts` in the jdk25 and jdk26 images: emSign ECC Root CA - G3, emSign Root CA - G1, emSign Root CA - G2 and AAA Certificate Services.

- Roots are matched by SHA-256 fingerprint, so it doesn't depend on Temurin's alias names.
- The build fails if any of them is still present afterwards.
- A root the base image doesn't ship is skipped, so the step is safe to leave in.

In the current Temurin images this removes emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and emSign Root CA - G1; G2 and AAA aren't shipped by Temurin. Temurin's trust store follows Mozilla, which still trusts G1, so that removal will keep applying after Temurin's images are updated. emSign Root CA - C1 and emSign ECC Root CA - C3 stay trusted, as in OpenJDK's guidance.

Testing:

- Built the `jre-build` stage for both variants: ECC G3 and G1 are removed, 116 roots remain, none of the four among them, and C1 and C3 are kept.
- Broke the delete step: the build fails with "A distrusted root is still in cacerts".
- Ran the step twice: the second run finds nothing and passes.
- `./gradlew distDocker`: `develop`, `develop-jdk25` and `develop-jdk26` contain none of the four roots, run as `teku`, and load Hoodi's checkpoint state over HTTPS.

## Fixed Issue(s)

N/A

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the JVM trust store for all outbound HTTPS from official Docker images; legitimate peers still presenting chains to the removed roots will fail TLS until they rotate certificates.
> 
> **Overview**
> Hardens **Teku Docker images** against the October 2026 eMudhra CA compromise by stripping four OpenJDK-distrusted roots from the **jlinked** runtime `cacerts` in the `jdk25` and `jdk26` image builds (emSign G1/G2/G3 and AAA Certificate Services). A new post-`jlink` step uses `keytool` to delete entries by **SHA-256 fingerprint** (not alias) and **fails the image build** if any of those roots remain, so Temurin bases that still ship Mozilla-trusted G1 are corrected until upstream catches up.
> 
> The **changelog** documents this under bug fixes and adds an upcoming notice that **`-jdk26` images** will stop being published in favor of `-jdk25`.

title: Inbound rpc stream backstops
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

A single peer could stop Teku from serving req/resp. An inbound RPC stream only gives back its slot in the node-wide limit of 128 once it is fully closed, and the peer decides when that happens. On Hoodi, one peer connected over QUIC held all 128 slots by leaving its streams open.

This PR adds three backstops:

- **Per-peer cap:** a single peer can hold at most 16 of the 128 inbound stream slots.
- **Lifetime deadline:** an inbound stream still open two minutes after it started is closed.
- **Shorter deadline after our response:** once we half-close an inbound stream, it gets five more seconds. The transport normally closes the stream straight away at that point, so this only catches streams the peer or the transport left open.

The deadlines run on the stream's event loop, so closing a stream removes its timer instead of keeping the stream in memory until the timer would have fired.

New metrics: `rpc_inbound_streams_active`, `rpc_inbound_streams_rejected_total{reason}` and `rpc_inbound_streams_expired_total{reason}` (exported with the `libp2p_` prefix).

Trade-off: a response that takes longer than two minutes to send is cut off.

These are backstops. The QUIC STOP_SENDING cause is handled by #11569 and libp2p/jvm-libp2p#548.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core libp2p inbound RPC lifecycle and limits; mis-tuned deadlines could disrupt slow peers or long responses, but scope is defensive networking rather than consensus or keys.
> 
> **Overview**
> Stops a single peer from monopolizing inbound req/resp by leaving streams open (notably over QUIC), which could fill the node-wide **128** stream cap and reject everyone else’s RPCs.
> 
> **Inbound limits and metrics:** `InboundRpcStreamLimiter` now tracks permits **per peer** (max **16** per peer, **128** global), returns explicit reject reasons, and exposes `rpc_inbound_streams_active`, `rpc_inbound_streams_rejected_total{reason}`, and `rpc_inbound_streams_expired_total{reason}`.
> 
> **Deadlines on inbound streams:** `RpcHandler` schedules a **2 minute** lifetime close on the stream’s Netty event loop, then shortens it to **5 seconds** after the node half-closes its write side; overdue streams are closed abruptly and permits released. Half-close completion triggers the shorter deadline via `LibP2PRpcStream`.
> 
> **Response path hardening:** `RpcResponseCallback` times out stuck half-closes (same bound as response writes) and fully closes the stream; failed writes already avoid half-close so permits are not leaked on STOP_SENDING.
> 
> **Trade-off:** RPC responses still sending after **2 minutes** can be cut off.
>

title: Publish the bare Docker release tags from the jdk25 job only
body:
## PR Description

Both release jobs in `ci.yml` (`publishDockerJDK25` and `publishDockerJDK26`) call `publish-docker.yml`, and on a release tag its `get workflow_details` step gave each of them the bare `X.Y.Z`, `X.Y` and `latest` tags. Whichever job finished last owned them, so 6 of the 10 releases since the default moved to Java 25 (#10567) ended up with the bare tags on the jdk26 image, including `latest` today. The workflow comment, the `develop` branch of the same step and Gradle's `uploadDocker`/`manifestDocker` all say the bare tags track jdk25; the release branch never had that check.

### Changes

- The release-tag branch of `get workflow_details` adds `X.Y.Z`, `X.Y` and `latest` only when `JDK_VERSION` is `jdk25`, matching what the `develop` branch already does. The jdk26 job pushes only its `-jdk26` tags.

Verified by running the step's script for both variants:

| Run | jdk25 job | jdk26 job |
|---|---|---|
| Tag `26.10.3` | `26.10.3-jdk25`, `26.10.3`, `26.10-jdk25`, `latest-jdk25`, `26.10`, `latest` | `26.10.3-jdk26`, `26.10-jdk26`, `latest-jdk26` |
| Tag `26.10.3-RC1` | `26.10.3-RC1-jdk25`, `26.10.3-RC1` | `26.10.3-RC1-jdk26` |
| Push to `master` | `develop-jdk25`, `develop` (unchanged) | `develop-jdk26` (unchanged) |

The older bare tags already pointing at jdk26 are not touched by this PR.

title: Route pending deposits by credentials at Gloas builder onboarding
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description

Implements [consensus-specs#5736](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5736)
("Separate builder and validator deposits at the Gloas fork", merged
2026-10-26 as `8b374fa81b`) in `onboard_builders_from_pending_deposits`.
At the Gloas fork, pending deposits are now routed by withdrawal
credentials, so the builder and validator registries stay independent,
as they are after the fork.

> [!NOTE]
> **5 Gloas fork reference tests are expected to fail until the reference
> tests are bumped.** Teku runs the v1.7.0-beta.4 vectors, which were
> generated before ethereum/consensus-specs#5736 merged and encode the old routing. No spec
> release includes it yet. The failing vectors are exactly the cases
> whose routing the spec change alters; see [Reference tests](#reference-tests).
> Against vectors generated from consensus-specs master, all Gloas fork
> tests pass.

| Deposit at the fork | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Non-builder credentials | Topped up a builder if one used the pubkey, otherwise stayed queued | Always stays queued |
| Builder credentials, valid signature, pubkey is an existing or pending validator | Stayed queued | Registers or tops up the builder |
| Builder credentials, existing builder | Tops up, signature ignored | Unchanged |
| Builder credentials, invalid signature, no builder | Stayed queued for an existing or pending validator, otherwise dropped | Unchanged |

`PendingValidatorTracker` from #11511 is unchanged. It is now only
consulted for builder deposits with an invalid signature, so validator
deposit signatures are checked even less often. Each builder deposit's
own signature is checked first, and no deposit is checked more than once.
The two #11511 tests that pin signature-check counts are updated (2 → 5
and 3 → 5); what ends up queued or created is the same in both.

### Tests

- New differential test in `GloasStateUpgradeTest` that compares the
  upgrade with a direct Java port of the spec function. It covers every
  sequence of up to 4 deposits for one new pubkey (340 cases) and 200
  seeded sequences mixing two new pubkeys and an existing validator with
  a known key. It varies credential prefixes, padding, amounts and slots,
  and checks that no signature is checked more than once.
- Injecting a bug into either "stays queued" condition (existing
  validator, pending validator) fails 56 and 73 cases.

### Reference tests

The v1.7.0-beta.4 vectors still encode the old routing. **CI will fail 5
`gloas/fork/fork` vectors on both presets until the reference tests move
to a release that includes ethereum/consensus-specs#5736.** Each one fails on `pending_deposits`,
and each is a case the spec change deliberately alters:

| Vector (beta.4) | Why it now differs |
|---|---|
| `fork_builder_deposit_followed_by_non_builder_credentials` | The non-builder deposit now stays queued instead of topping up the builder |
| `fork_validator_deposit_followed_by_builder_credentials` | A valid builder deposit now registers even though the pubkey is a pending validator |
| `fork_valid_then_invalid_validator_then_builder_deposit` | Same: the valid builder deposit registers despite the pending validator |
| `fork_invalid_then_valid_validator_then_builder_deposit` | Same |
| `fork_mixed_validity_validator_deposits_surrounding_builder_deposits` | Same |

ethereum/consensus-specs#5736 renames or rewrites these vectors (for example to
`..._then_invalid_builder_deposit`) and adds 13 new onboarding cases, so
they go away with the reference test bump. No exclusion is added here.

Checked locally against `gloas/fork/fork` vectors generated from
consensus-specs master (`0216d01ba`, which includes the change) via
`-Dteku.ref-test.root-dir`: all 86 pass (44 minimal, 42 mainnet). As a
control, the current master implementation fails 11 of them on both
presets.

### Networks that have already forked

Sepolia and plataberget have already run the Gloas fork under the old
rule. Before this ships, we should confirm that no pending deposit at
either fork falls into a case whose routing changed. Otherwise nodes
syncing through the fork would compute a different state. The
consensus-specs discussion only covered Sepolia, where builder deposits
were token-gated.

title: Bound RocksDB range seeks and skip pruned data column slots
body:
Ranged RocksDB streams applied the end of the range only as a Java predicate, so a seek into a pruned range stepped over every deletion tombstone up to the first live key. On Sepolia, by-range data column requests for long-pruned slots took minutes and filled all RPC storage throttle slots.

- Give ranged `stream`/`streamKeys` iterators an exclusive `iterate_upper_bound`. Every iterator owns and closes its `ReadOptions` and, for ranged streams, the bound `Slice`.
- Start `streamDataColumnIdentifiers` above the prune watermark and skip the database when the range is fully pruned. The pruner and `getEarliestDataColumnSidecarSlot` rely on this instead of computing the watermark themselves.
- Merge `RocksDbKeyIterator` into a generic `RocksDbIterator`.

In a local benchmark with production column family options, a 32-slot request inside a band of 1M–4M tombstones went from 41–167 ms to ~1.5 µs for data columns (no seek) and ~0.2 ms for other ranged tables (bound only). Reads of live ranges are unchanged or slightly faster.

Fixes #11584

title: Accumulate decoded snappy frames into a single buffer
body:
SnappyFramedDecompressor now copies each decoded frame into one growable buffer sized from the advertised payload length, instead of retaining every frame and summing their sizes after each one. Per-frame work is constant and each frame is released as soon as it is copied.

Eth2OutgoingRequestHandler now releases its response decoder in closed(), which runs on the stream's event loop, rather than in abortRequest(), which may run on the timeout thread. The threading contract is documented on RpcRequestHandler.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes hot-path P2P decompression and RPC stream lifecycle threading; mistakes could cause leaks, double-close, or cross-thread decoder use under timeouts.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **Snappy framed decompression** performance and **thread-safety** when tearing down outgoing RPC response decoders.
> 
> **SnappyFramedDecompressor** no longer keeps a list of every decoded frame and rescans their lengths on each chunk. It **copies each frame into one growable `ByteBuf`** capped at the advertised uncompressed size, **releases frames immediately**, and returns that buffer when the payload is complete. That makes per-frame work **O(1)** instead of scaling with frame count (important for many small or fragmented frames). New tests cover large frame counts, fragmented input, linear-time behavior, and oversize payloads.
> 
> **Eth2OutgoingRequestHandler** stops calling **`responseDecoder.close()` from `abortRequest()`** (which can run on the timeout thread). Cleanup now happens only in **`closed()`** on the stream event loop, aligned with **`Eth2IncomingRequestHandler`** and documented on **`RpcRequestHandler`**. Tests assert abort/timeouts do not close the decoder until `closed()`, that repeated `closed()` is safe, and that state still reaches `CLOSED` if `close()` throws.

## PR Description

A Gloas `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` that passes gossip validation but whose payload content does not hash to its declared block hash poisoned three things keyed on identifiers that assumed the envelope was the committed one: the gossip seen-set (`block_root`, `builder_index`), the invalid-payload set used by attestation validation, and the by-root fetch gate that reused the seen-set. The builder's correct envelope for the same block was then ignored as a duplicate, never fetched, and the block root stayed marked as having an invalid payload.

- Gossip validation computes the block hash from the envelope content after the signature check and IGNOREs on mismatch, before marking the envelope as seen. IGNORE rather than REJECT because this is not a spec rule and compliant peers relay such envelopes.
- The invalid-payload set is only written for envelopes that went through gossip validation. A REST broadcast with `broadcast_validation=NOT_REQUIRED` therefore no longer marks the block root on an EL rejection (behaviour change, matching the `importExecutionPayload` contract). The mark is cleared once a payload for the root imports.
- The by-root fetch is gated on the payload being imported or its import being in flight, instead of on the gossip seen-set.
- `Spec.computeExecutionPayloadBlockHash` is the single entry point for the hash; the requests hash is delegated to Besu's EIP-7685 implementation. A real Sepolia envelope and its EL header are test fixtures, so the calculator is checked against a hash produced by a real execution client. The stub EL now stamps content-consistent Gloas hashes.

Design notes and the alternatives considered are in #11568. Verified end-to-end on a kurtosis devnet with a builder revealing a tampered envelope before the correct one on every won slot.

## Fixed Issue(s)

fixes #11568
related to https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5770

- [x] I thought about adding a changelog entry, and added one if I deemed necessary.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes Gloas gossip validation, payload import caching, and block-hash computation on the critical path for builder payloads; incorrect hashing or dedup logic could drop valid envelopes or fetch duplicates.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes Gloas handling when an **execution payload envelope** declares a block hash that does not match the hash computed from its payload content (a Teku-side check, not a consensus-spec rule).
> 
> **Gossip** now **IGNORE**s such envelopes instead of accepting them into the seen cache, so a forged envelope that reuses the bid’s block hash can no longer block the builder’s real envelope or prevent RPC fetch/import. **Invalid-payload** marking for attestation validation is tied to verified imports only (`BroadcastValidationLevel.NOT_REQUIRED` no longer poisons the cache), and the invalid mark is **cleared** when a payload for that block imports successfully.
> 
> **Block hash computation** is centralized on `Spec.computeExecutionPayloadBlockHash`, with `ExecutionPayloadBlockHashCalculator` aligned to Besu’s `BodyValidation.requestsHash` and covered by a Sepolia mainnet fixture test. The execution-layer stub and test utilities produce Gloas payloads whose declared hash matches computed content.
> 
> **RPC deduplication** replaces “recently seen on gossip” with **`isExecutionPayloadImportedOrImporting`** (fork-choice FULL node or import in flight), so failed gossip imports can still trigger fetches.
>

title: Buffer pending RPC bytes in a single growable buffer
body:
## PR Description

`AbstractByteBufDecoder`, the base of the RPC `ByteBuf` decoders, kept bytes that had not yet completed a message in a `CompositeByteBuf`, adding one component per input. Netty merges the components of such a buffer every 16 additions, copying all pending bytes each time, so a message that arrives in many small reads was copied over and over.

- Pending bytes now go into one growable buffer. When nothing is pending, the input is decoded in place, with no extra buffer and no copy. Bytes after a decoded message stay in the caller's input, as before.
- A guard checks that a decoded message never leaves earlier bytes behind. If it does, the decoder releases the message and fails instead of skipping a negative number of bytes.
- `SnappyFrameDecoder` limits a `COMPRESSED_DATA` chunk to snappy's worst-case encoded length of a 64 KiB block plus its checksum (76,494 bytes), instead of 16 MiB. A chunk can never decompress to more than 64 KiB, and standard snappy encoders stay within this length.
- The worst-case length formula now lives in `SnappyUtil` and is shared by the payload limit and the chunk limit.

Tests cover:
- decoding a message delivered one byte at a time;
- bytes after a message staying in the input;
- `complete()` reporting leftover bytes;
- the leftover guard;
- the chunk limit.

## Fixed Issue(s)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core libp2p RPC/Snappy decode paths and buffer lifecycle; behavior is heavily tested but any decoder edge-case bug could affect peer message handling.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`AbstractByteBufDecoder`** no longer accumulates partial RPC reads in a Netty **`CompositeByteBuf`** (which could re-copy all pending bytes every 16 chunks). Pending bytes now live in a **single growable buffer**, with **in-place decoding** when nothing is buffered yet; trailing bytes after a message still remain in the caller’s input. A new **invariant check** releases a decoded message and fails if decoding would leave more unread bytes in the cumulation than the current input contributed.
> 
> **Snappy RPC framing** tightens **`COMPRESSED_DATA`** chunk acceptance from a 16 MiB cap to **76,494 bytes** (checksum plus worst-case Snappy encoding of a 64 KiB block), with **`SnappyUtil.maxCompressedLength`** shared by the chunk limit and **`SnappyFramedCompressor`**. Oversize chunk errors use **`CompressionException`** instead of Netty’s **`DecompressionException`**.
> 
> Tests add linear-time accumulation coverage, leftover-byte behavior, the invariant guard, chunk-limit cases, and adjust partial-stream buffer refcount expectations (copy vs retain).
>

title: Compute snappy frame checksums with bulk CRC32C updates
body:
## PR Description

`SnappyUtil.calculateChecksum` fed `CRC32C` one byte at a time (`crc32.update(data.getByte(i))`), and that loop was most of the cost of decoding `ssz_snappy` RPC payloads. It now passes the buffer's NIO views (`ByteBuf.nioBuffers(offset, length)`) to `CRC32C.update(ByteBuffer)`, so the JDK's CRC32C intrinsic does the work. A composite buffer yields one view per component, nothing is copied, and the buffer's indices are not moved.

The checksum is used by the snappy frame encoder and, for both chunk types, by the frame decoder.

Measured on an M-series laptop, best of 5 runs, 1 MB payload:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| checksum, heap buffer | 5.7 ms | 95 µs |
| checksum, direct buffer | 3.9 ms | 95 µs |
| checksum, composite of 32 KiB components | 5.2 ms | 93 µs |
| decode, incompressible data | 3.5 ms | 0.17 ms |
| decode, 2:1 compressible data | 3.9 ms | 0.65 ms |

`SnappyUtilTest` checks the result against masked CRC32C values computed independently of this code, for these inputs:
- empty input
- the `"123456789"` check string
- large heap and direct buffers
- a composite mixing heap and direct components
- a sub-range, checking that the indices are left untouched
- a checksum mismatch, which must be rejected

## Fixed Issue(s)

> **Overview**
> **Replaces per-byte CRC32C in `SnappyUtil.calculateChecksum` with bulk `CRC32C.update(ByteBuffer)` over `ByteBuf.nioBuffers(offset, length)`**, so snappy frame checksums on `ssz_snappy` RPC encode/decode use the JDK CRC32C intrinsic instead of a tight byte loop. Composite buffers are handled component-by-component without copying or shifting reader/writer indices.
>

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes DAS custody satisfaction logic and concurrent storage archival/backfill behavior; mistakes could cause unnecessary RPC backfill or incorrect custody reporting, but scope is storage/DAS rather than auth or funds.
> 
> **Overview**
> Makes **custody backfill** and **sidecar-to-proof archival** safe to run at the same time by separating *physical* column IDs from *custody* column IDs.
> 
> **Custody counting** now uses new `getCustodyDataColumnIdentifiers` APIs (per slot and batched ranges). `ChainStorage` expands physical first-half columns plus a complete proof archive into a full canonical column set for custody only, so archived extension columns are not re-downloaded. `DasCustodyBackfiller` and `DataColumnSidecarCustodyImpl` switch to these APIs for batch planning and slot completeness checks.

> 
> **Robustness**: stricter KV deserialization for proof/UInt64 payloads with `KvStoreDeserializationException`, plus broad unit and integration tests (including supernode restart and no-download when custody is already satisfied via archive).
