title: Read the validator registry from packed bytes in epoch processing
body:
## PR Description

Whole-registry scans in epoch processing read every validator through `validators.get(i)`, which builds a `Validator` view and caches it in the list for the life of the state. On the mainnet registry (2.39M validators) the first such scan on a freshly loaded state adds about 1.2 GB of heap and spends seconds building views that are read once; and because committing a post-state transfers the pre-state list's view cache, every epoch transition rebuilt them.

This PR reads the registry from its packed SSZ bytes instead, in five commits, each independently revertable:

1. **`SszList.forEachElementSsz`**: visits the serialized bytes of a list's elements in index order without creating views. Elements packed in a supernode are handed out as a range of the supernode's own content; others are serialized from their tree node. One in-order tree walk serves bounded and progressive lists. A mutable list overlays its uncommitted changes, with the size and changed indices taken before the walk, so a visitor may update the element it is visiting. `ValidatorFields` decodes validator fields at an offset, with the offsets derived from the validator schema.
2. **Statuses, active indices and fork-choice effective balances** are decoded from the bytes (statuses in parallel over index ranges, by one builder shared with the view-based path).
3. **`process_registry_updates`** (pre-Electra and Electra) and the Electra **`process_effective_balance_updates`** walk the bytes while keeping the spec's single loop. `is_eligible_for_activation` and the compounding-credential check gain raw forms that the existing methods delegate to; `get_max_effective_balance` is computed from the credentials prefix.
4. **`ValidatorIndexCache`** fills from the bytes and builds each key over a copy of its 48 bytes, so cache entries no longer pin the supernode arrays. The LRU, seeding and stale-index filter are unchanged.
5. **`createValidatorExitContext`** reads the exit epochs from the bytes (the last whole-registry view scan on a running node).

### Measured

Epoch transition `processSlots` over one empty-slot epoch on the mainnet finalized state at epoch 483376 (12 GB heap, Java 25, median of 10 runs; same post-state root):

| | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| cold transition (fresh state) | 7,442 ms | 4,041 ms |
| warm transition (same pre-state) | 4,432 ms | 1,668 ms |
| `createValidatorStatuses`, cold | 3,072 ms, +660 MB | 599 ms, +0 MB |
| `getActiveValidatorIndices`, cold | 709 ms, +591 MB | 69 ms, +3 MB |
| cold pubkey lookup (unknown key) | 1,765 ms | 667 ms |
| heap growth of a cold transition | 1,970 MB | 930 MB |

Two mainnet nodes side by side on the same machine (checkpoint sync, EL stub, minimal storage, 10 GB heap), read at the same head slot after the same two epoch transitions, heap after a forced full GC: used heap 5.56 GB → 3.80 GB, cached `Validator` views 7.19M → 2.46M, RSS 12.2 GB → 10.0 GB. The views that remain come from per-attester reads during block processing (base reward and pubkey lookups, the total-active-balance sum), about one per active validator per retained state; single-element byte reads for those paths are a follow-up.

### Verification

- Full consensus reference suite (v1.7.0-beta.4, mainnet and minimal, all milestones): 63,880 cases, 0 failures, run on the four-commit tree and again on the five-commit tree.
- Module suites green: `:infrastructure:ssz` (28,414), `:ethereum:spec` (2,123), `:ethereum:statetransition` (3,063), `:storage` (976); `ethspecify check` passes (1,200 references).
- A local mainnet node built from the branch ran from checkpoint sync through epochs 485625 to 485633 across three restarts, with finality and block roots matching a public beacon API and no errors.

Not included on purpose: a process-wide pubkey table replacing the per-lineage index cache (measured separately at 642 MB per lineage → 127 MB per process; a follow-up PR), and moving pubkeys out of the supernode content.

title: Tolerate a pruned previous balance source in fast confirmation
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! Please check out our contribution guidelines: -->
<!-- https://github.com/Consensys-Incorporated/teku/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

## PR Description
Fast confirmation no longer falls back to finality for a whole slot when the previous observed justified checkpoint state has been pruned, a Teku-only cause of an extra warmup epoch found in hoodi logs.
- `FastConfirmationStateLoader` still fetches the previous balance source at epoch-start slots but no longer requires it, so a stale checkpoint observed while catching up after a restart, and pruned two epochs later, no longer empties the source states.
- `isConfirmedChainSafe` only needs it after its checkpoint check and when there are blocks to score, as in the spec, and returns false if it is missing, so the rule reverts to finality and can still restart from the observed justified checkpoint in the same slot.
- Tests: loader without the previous source, reconfirmation with and without blocks to score, and an epoch-start restart without it.


## Fixed Issue(s)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes epoch-boundary fast confirmation behavior when checkpoint states are pruned; impact is localized to reconfirmation and state loading, with conservative fallbacks to finality when safety cannot be proven.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fast confirmation no longer **skips an entire slot** when the previous epoch’s observed-justified checkpoint state has been pruned (e.g. stale checkpoint after restart). **`FastConfirmationStateLoader`** still tries to load that state at epoch-start slots but treats it as optional: only the current balance source and pulled-up head state must be present for a successful load.
> 
> **`isConfirmedChainSafe`** now matches spec ordering: it loads the previous balance source only after the checkpoint check and only when there are blocks to reconfirm. An empty chain to score returns **true** without that state; if scoring is needed but the state is missing, it returns **false** so **`getLatestConfirmed`** can revert to finalized and still restart from the observed justified checkpoint in the same slot.
> 
> Tests cover the loader, reconfirmation with/without blocks to score, and epoch-start restart without the previous source.
